To the gods and the sages, thus let victory be proclaimed! 000 | The son of a charioteer, Lohamṛga, does not hesitate to speak of the ancient tales of the Paurāṇikas. 001 | Seated in the assembly, the twenty-one sages, When will the earth be free from the burden of the sinful? 002 | Those who do not hesitate to speak of the stories of the great sages, Let them be honored with the tales of the past. 003 | Thus, the sages, having performed their penance, With their minds focused, they attained the highest state. 004 | Then, those who are devoted to the sages, Having taken their seats, they began to speak with humility. 005 | 1

English: 2 Anumani Pava Sukhāsīnaṁ tataṁ tu viśvāmitra upalaṁ ca | Atha pṛcchatiṣṭhā kiṁ kṛtāṁ vāyathāḥ | 006 | Kuta āgacchati saute chāyaṁ viśvitrayā | Kālaḥ kamalapadmaḥ śaṁsati mām | 007 | Sūta uvāca | Janamejayaḥ rājāḥ sapta saṁsāre mahābhūtaḥ | Samīpe pāṭhī veśyaṁ saṁkṣāriṇi ca | 008 | Kṛtāḥ pāyanoḥ sukhāḥ vividhāḥ kathāḥ | Kithatāpi vidhavā vaiśaṁpāyaneṇa vai | 009 | Sūryāṁhaṁ tāṁ vicitrāḥ mahābhāratasaṁhitāḥ | Bṛhīn saṁpirāṇī tīthāḥ saṁyatanāni ca | 010 | Samāpakam nāma puṣyaṁ vijinṣevitam | Gatavāni taṁ deśaṁ yūṁ yathābhavatu ra | 011 | Pāṇḍavānāṁ kuṭṭanāṁ ca sarveṣāṁ ca mahīṭatām | 011 | Idṛṣṭurāgatāṁ bhavatāṁ iha | Āyuṣmān sarveva bhūtā hi me matāḥ | 012 | Aśvamedhe mahābhāgāḥ sūryaḥ pāvaka vachaḥ | Kṛtābhiṣekāḥ śucayaḥ kṛtajñāḥ pratāhyaḥ | 013 | Bhavata āstate kīmahaṁ vijñāḥ | 013 |

Sanskrit: अाय ००१ ३ प ुराणसंिताः प ुयाः कथा वा धमसंिताः | इितवृं नरेाणामृषीणां च महानाम ्| ०१४ | ऋषय ऊच ुः | ैपायन ेन यों प ुराणं परमिष णा | स ुरैिष िभ ैव ुा यदिभपूिजतम ्| ०१५ | ताानविर िविचपदपवणः | सूाथ ाययु वेदाथभू िषत च | ०१६ | भारतेितहास प ुयां ाथ संयुताम ्| संारोपगतां ा नानाशाोपबृ ंिहताम ्| ०१७ | जनमेजय यां राो वैशंपायन उवान ्| यथाव ऋिष ुा से ैपायनाया | ०१८ | वेदैतुिभः सिमतां ासाुतकमणः | संिहतां ोतुिमामो धा पापभयापहाम ्| ०१९ | सूत उवाच | आं प ुषमीशानं प ुतं प ुुतम ्| ऋतमेकारं  ां सनातनम ्| ०२० | अस स ैव च यिं सदसतः परम ्| परावराणां ारं प ुराणं परमयम ्| ०२१ | मं मलं िवु नमृ  षीके शं चराचरग ुं हिरम ्| ०२२ | ं वरेयमनघं शुिचम ्|
English: "001 3 The stories of the Puranas or the Dharma-sutras, Thus spoke the great sages of mankind. 014 The sages said: By the sage Vaipāyana, the Purana is declared supreme; It is adorned with the essence of the divine, worthy of worship. 015 With the knowledge of the Vedas, The essence of the teachings is established. 016 In the history of Bharat, the Puranas are connected With various narratives, enriched with diverse stories. 017 In the assembly of King Janamejaya, Vaishampayana spoke, As the sage recited, the teachings of Vaipāyana were revealed. 018 The Vedas, with their profound meanings, Are united in the essence of the sacred texts, dispelling the fear of sin. 019 Soot said: I bow to the supreme Ishana, the best of the best, The eternal truth, the one and only. 020 Thus, it is said that the supreme Purana is the ultimate refuge For those who seek liberation from worldly attachments. 021 I offer my respects to the sage, The one who pervades all beings, the essence of the universe. 022 May purity and virtue prevail."

Sanskrit: ४ अन ुमणीपव महषः पूिजतेह सवलोके महानः | वािम मतं कृ ं ासािमततेजसः | ०२३ | आच ुः कवयः के िचंाचते परे | आाि तथ ैवाे इितहासिममं भ ुिव | ०२४ | इदं तु िष ु लोके ष ु महानं ितितम ्| िवरै समास ै धायते यिजाितिभः | ०२५ | अल तं शुभ ैः शैः समय ैिदमान ुष ैः | छोवृ ै िविवध ैरितं िवषां ियम ्| ०२६ | िनभेऽििरालोके सवतमसावृते | बृहदडमभूदेकं जानां बीजमयम ्| ०२७ | युगादौ िनिमं तहिं चते | यिंूयते सं ोित सनातनम ्| ०२८ | अुतं चािचं च सव समतां गतम ्| अं कारणं सूं यदसदाकम ्| ०२९ | याितामहो जे भ ुरेकः जापितः | ा स ुरग ुः ाणुमन ुः कः परमेथ | ०३० | ाचेतसथा दो दप ुा स ये | ततः जानां पतयः ाभवेकिवंशितः | ०३१ | प ुषामेयाा यं सवमृषयो िवः | िवेदेवाथािदा वसवोऽथािनाविप | ०३२ | याः सााः िपशाचा ग ुकाः िपतरथा |
English: 4 Anuśarman The great sage, worshipped in all worlds, is the great one | The wise one, whose mind is absorbed in the light of knowledge. | 023 | The poets, some of whom are skilled in the art of poetry, | Speak of the ancient history of this world. | 024 | This, however, is the great one in this world, | Whose essence is described by the wise as the source of all. | 025 | With auspicious times, the good ones are present, | Various forms of life are established in different ways. | 026 | In the world of the unmanifest, where all is covered, | The great seed of the wise has become one. | 027 | In the beginning of the ages, the creation is spoken of, | That which is eternal is called the essence of all. | 028 | The wondrous and the beautiful have all attained equality, | The cause of all is the eternal truth. | 029 | Where the great one is established, who is the supreme being, | Who is the lord of the universe, who is the ultimate truth? | 030 | The wise ones, who are steadfast in their resolve, | Thus, the lords of the wise are born from the lineage of the great. | 031 | The one who is the essence of all, whom all sages praise, | The deities, the Vasus, and the others are also present. | 032 | Wherever there are the great ones, the wise ones are present.

Sanskrit: अाय ००१ ५ ततः सूता िवांसः िशा ष योऽमलाः | ०३३ | राजष य बहवः सवः समुिदता ग ुण ैः | आपो ौः पृिथवी वायुरिरं िदशथा | ०३४ | संवरतवो मासाः पाहोरायः मात ्| यादिप तव संभूतं लोकसािकम ्| ०३५ | यिददं यते िकिूतं ावरजमम ्| प ुनः सिते सव जगाे युगये | ०३६ | यथतावृतुिलािन नानापािण पयये | ये तािन ताेव तथा भावा युगािदष ु | ०३७ | एवमेतदनां भूतसंहारकारकम ्| अनािदिनधनं लोके चं संपिरवतते | ०३८ | यिंशहािण यिंशतािन च | यिंश देवानां सृिः सेपलणा | ०३९ | िदवुो बृहान ुुराा िवभावस ुः | सिवता च ऋचीकोऽक भान ुराशावहो रिवः | ०४० | प ुा िववतः सव मेषां तथावरः | देवानय ताुािडित ृतः | ०४१ | स ुाज ु यः प ुाः जावो बुताः | दशोितः शतोितः सहोितरावान ्| ०४२ | दश प ुसहािण दशोतेमहानः | ततो दशग ुणााे शतोतेिरहाजाः | ०४३ |
English: 1. Thus, the seven sages, pure in their actions, are born. 2. The kings, many and all, are endowed with qualities. 3. Water, earth, air, and the directions are established. 4. The months and fortnights are cyclic; from them, the world is born. 5. Whatever is created, whether mobile or immobile, again becomes manifest in the cycle of ages. 6. As the seasons change, various forms of nourishment arise; thus, they are the essence of the ages. 7. Thus, this is the cause of the destruction of beings; in the world, it is eternally present. 8. The elements of creation and destruction are also present; the essence of the gods is the source of creation. 9. The great beings, endowed with strength, are the manifestations of the sun; they are the source of light. 10. The moon, shining brightly, is the source of all beings; the divine beings are nourished by it. 11. The sun, the moon, and the stars are the sources of light; the ten directions are illuminated by them. 12. Ten suns, shining together, create a hundredfold brightness; thus, the ten qualities are manifested. 13. From ten suns, tenfold brightness arises; then, the ten qualities are manifested in a hundredfold manner.

Sanskrit: ६ अन ुमणीपव भूयतो दशग ुणाः सहोितषः स ुताः | तेोऽयं कु वंश यनां भरत च | ०४४ | ययातीाकु वंश राजषणां च सवशः | संभूता बहवो वंशा भूतसगाः सिवराः | ०४५ | भूतानािन सवािण रहं ििवधं च यत ्| वेदयोगं सिवानं धमऽथ ः काम एव च | ०४६ | धमकामाथ शाािण शाािण िविवधािन च | लोकयाािवधानं च संभूतं वानृिषः | ०४७ | इितहासाः सवैयाा िविवधाः ुतयोऽिप च | इह सवमन ुामुं  लणम ्| ०४८ | िवीयतहानमृिषः सेपमवीत ्| इं िह िवषां लोके समासासधारणम ्| ०४९ | मािद भारतं के िचदाीकािद तथापरे | तथोपिरचराे िवाः सगधीयते | ०५० | िविवधं संिहताानं दीपयि मनीिषणः | ाातु ं कु शलाः के िचं धारियतु ं परे | ०५१ | तपसा चयण  वेदं सनातनम ्| इितहासिममं चे प ुयं सवतीस ुतः | ०५२ | पराशराजो िवािषः संिशततः | मातुिन योगामाा गाेय च धीमतः | ०५३ |
English: 6 Anumani Pava Moreover, ten qualities are well-known. This is the lineage of the Bharatas. 044 Yayati, the lineage of kings, is indeed the source of many lineages, born of the past. 045 All beings are subject to the laws of nature, and the Vedic knowledge is the essence of righteousness and desire. 046 Righteousness and desire are variously defined, and the rules of the world are established by sages. 047 The histories are diverse and even contradictory. Here, all minds are engaged in the pursuit of truth. 048 The sages of the past have established the principles of the world. Here, the essence of existence is maintained. 049 In Bharat, some are engaged in various activities, while others are similarly occupied. 050 Various teachings illuminate the minds of the wise. Let those who are skilled uphold the truth. 051 Through penance, the eternal Veda is attained, and this history is indeed a source of strength. 052 Parashara, the sage, is known for his wisdom, and through the grace of the mother, the wise attain knowledge. 053

English: 1. "Aṅgāya 001 7 In the assembly of the wise, the sage Vaśiṣṭha spoke. The Kauravas, having gathered, were engaged in discussion. 054 2. Dhritarāṣhṭra and Pāṇḍu went to the sage Dīrghatapas, who was meditating. 055 3. Indeed, it is the truth. 4. Among those born, those who have grown, and those who have departed, the supreme song is sung. In the world, men are not without their deeds. 056 5. Janamejaya asked the sage, "Who is the one seated here?" He ruled over the assembly, the sage Vaiśaṁpāyana. 057 6. He, along with the sages, began to narrate the Bharata. The stories of the past were recounted again and again. 058 7. The sage, with a pure lineage, was devoted to righteousness. Vaśiṣṭha, the sage, was not without strength. 059 8. The great sage Vāsudeva, of the Pāṇḍavas, was the one who spoke. He was the one who had the knowledge of the scriptures. 060 9. In the twenty-fourth chapter, the Bharata is presented. The wise ones, with their knowledge, speak of it. 061 10. Then, the sage, having completed a hundred, performed the great sacrifice. He was the one who had the knowledge of the Vedas. 062 11. This is the sage Vaśiṣṭha, the one who is the first among the sages. Then, having completed the sacrifice, he spoke the truth. 063 12. Nārada, the sage, was not without the divine. He was the father of the sages."

English: 8 Anumani-pavṛha In the assembly of the cows, the parrot spoke. 064 The wealth of the wise is great; the fruit of the tree is the king, Dhritarashtra, who is thoughtful. 065 In the battle, the great one is righteous; the branches are Bhimasena's. The fruit of the tree is the king, Krishna, and the one who is wise. 066 The learned one, the great sage, is skilled in hunting; he is a friend of the deer. 067 The deer, when caught, is a source of danger; the path of the wise is filled with various teachings. 068 The sage, along with the mother, is surrounded by great ones; they are the great ones of the forest and the great ones of the rivers. 070 The sages, at that time, were endowed with knowledge; they were like the shining sun, illuminating the world. 071 The wise ones, with their knowledge, are like the sun; the learned ones are like the moon, illuminating the night. 072 Those who are knowledgeable are like the wise; the learned ones are like the great sages, who are free from desires. 073 There are some who say, "This is it," and when the learned one dies, how do they say, "This is it"? 074

Sanskrit: अाय ००१ ९ ागतं सवथा िदा पाडोः पयाम संतितम ्| उतां ागतिमित वाचोऽूय सवशः | ०७५ | ति ुपरते शे िदशः सवा िवनादयन ्| अिहतानां भूतानां िनन ुमुलोऽभवत ्| ०७६ | प ुवृिः शुभा गाः शिभिननाः | आसवेशे पाथानां तदुतिमवाभवत ्| ०७७ | तीा च ैव सवषां पौराणां हष संभवः | श आसीहां िदवृीितवधनः | ०७८ | तेऽधीािखलाेदााािण िविवधािन च | वसाडवा पूिजता अकु तोभयाः | ०७९ | युिधिर शौचेन ीताः कृ तयोऽभवन ्| धृा च भीमसेन िवमेणाज ु न च | ०८० | ग ुशुूषया कुा यमयोिवनयेन च | तुतोष लोकः सकलेषां शौयग ुणेन च | ०८१ | समवाये ततो राां कां भतृ ावानज ु नः कृ ां कृ ा कम स ुरम ्| ०८२ | यंवराम ्| ततः भृित लोके ऽिूः सवधन ुताम ्| आिद इव ेः समरेिप चाभवत ्| ०८३ | स सवाािथ वािा सवा महतो गणान ्| आजहाराज ु नो राे राजसूयं महातुम ्| ०८४ |
English: 1. The arrival is fully established in the assembly of the learned. 2. The directions are filled with sounds, and the essence of the beings is rooted. 3. Auspicious deeds are performed, and the essence of the offerings is manifested. 4. The joy of all the townspeople is evident; the divine presence is established. 5. The complete offerings are made with various items, and the worship is done without hesitation. 6. With purity and cleanliness, they became calm; Bhimasena held the fort with strength. 7. The world was pleased with the beauty of the young maidens and their graceful conduct. 8. Then, the king, with great strength, performed the royal sacrifice. 9. Thus, in the world, the wealth of all beings was established; like the sun, the glory in battle arose. 10. The king, with his great assembly, performed the grand Rajasuya sacrifice.

English: 10 Anuśarman In the assembly of the great Rajasuya, all the warriors are gathered together with their qualities. By the prowess of Bhima, the son of Kunti, Jarasandha and others were slain. With great strength, The wealth of the earth, the treasures, and the riches of the cows were brought forth. Thus, the great assembly of the Pandavas was established, and the glory of the great king was proclaimed. The assembly was adorned by the presence of the divine, and the Pandavas were honored in that great gathering. As the sun rises, the great Bhima shines forth, and the assembly is filled with joy. The various enjoyments and pleasures were distributed, and Dhritarashtra was filled with sorrow. The wrath of Dhritarashtra arose due to the great anger of the Pandavas. The minds of the Kauravas were filled with anxiety, and they were troubled by the news of the Pandavas' victory. The great Bhima, the son of Kunti, was fierce and powerful, and he was a source of fear for the Kauravas. Victory to the Pandavas, the great warriors!

Sanskrit: अाय ००१ ११ यधनमतं ाा कण शकु न ेथा | ०९५ | धृतरािरं ाा सयं वामवीत ्| ०९५ | णु सय मे सव न मेऽसूियतुमहिस | ुतवानिस मेधावी ब ुिमाासंमतः | ०९६ | न िवहे मम मितन  च ीये कु ये | न मे िवशेषः प ुेष ु ेष ु पाडुस ुतेष ु च | ०९७ | वृं मामसूयि प ुा म ुपरायणाः | अहं चुः काप या ुीा सहािम तत ्| ०९८ | मुं चान ुमुािम यधनमचेतनम ्| ०९८ | राजसूये ियं ा पाडव महौजसः | तावहसनं ा सभारोहणदशन े | ०९९ | अमिष तः यं जेतुमशः पाडवाणे | िनाह संा ु ं ियमियो यथा | १०० | गाारराजसिहतछूतममयत ्| १०० | त यथा ातं मया सय तणु | ुा िह मम वाािन ब ुा युािन ततः | १०१ | ततो ािस मां सौते ाचुषिम ुत | १०१ | यदाौषं धन ुराय िचं ; िवं लं पािततं वै पृिथाम ्| कृ ां तां पयतां सवराां ; तदा नाशंसे िवजयाय सय | १०२ |
English: 1. "Agnya 001" 2. "11" 3. "The wealth of the wise is not to be despised." (095) 4. "Dhritarashtra's wisdom is indeed a great treasure." (095) 5. "Let my mind be free from all attachments; I am indeed a learned one, accepted by the wise." (096) 6. "Do not be angry with my friend; do not be angry with me." (097) 7. "I am not envious of the wealth of others; I am content with what I have." (098) 8. "I am not a fool, nor am I ignorant." (098) 9. "In the Rajasuya sacrifice, the Pandavas are indeed powerful." (099) 10. "To conquer the enemy, the Pandavas must be united." (100) 11. "The king's authority is indeed supreme." (100) 12. "Thus, as I have said, let my mind be free from desires." (101) 13. "Then, the wise one will grant me the boon of prosperity." (101) 14. "When wealth is acquired, it is indeed a great blessing; the earth is indeed filled with abundance." (102)

Sanskrit: १२ अन ुमणीपव यदाौषं ारकायां स ुभां ; सोढां माधवीमज ु इं वृिवीरौ च यातौ ; तदा नाशंसे िवजयाय सय | १०३ | न ेन | यदाौषं देवराजं वृं ; शरैिद ैवािरतं चाज ु अिं तथा तिप तं खाडवे च ; तदा नाशंसे िवजयाय सय | १०४ | न ेन | यदाौषं तरां युिधिरं ; परािजतं सौबलेनावाम ्| अागतं ातृिभरमेय ै;दा नाशंसे िवजयाय सय | १०५ | यदाौषं ौपदीमुकठ ; सभां नीतां ःिखतामेकवाम ्| रजलां नाथवतीमनाथव ;दा नाशंसे िवजयाय सय | १०६ | यदाौषं िविवधाात चेा ; धमानां ितानां वनाय | ेीा ियतां पाडवानां ; तदा नाशंसे िवजयाय सय | १०७ | यदाौषं ातकानां सह ै;रागतं धमराजं वनम ्| िभाभ ुजां ाणानां महानां ; तदा नाशंसे िवजयाय सय | १०८ | नो देवदेवं ; िकरातपं कं तो युे | यदाौषमज ु अवाप ताशुपतं महां ; तदा नाशंसे िवजयाय सय | १०९ | यदाौषं ििदवं धनयं ; शााािमं यथावत ्| अधीयानं शंिसतं ससंधं ; तदा नाशंसे िवजयाय सय | ११० | यदाौषं वैवणेन साध ; समागतं भीममां पाथान ्| तिेशे मान ुषाणामगे; तदा नाशंसे िवजयाय सय | १११ | यदाौषं घोषयाागतानां ; बं गवमणं चाज ु ेषां स ुतानां कणब ुौ रतानां ; तदा नाशंसे िवजयाय सय | ११२ | न ेन | यदाौषं यपेण धम ; समागतं धमराजेन सूत |
English: 12 Anuṣṭup When the auspicious moon rises in the sky; adorned with the beautiful Mādhavī flower, The valiant heroes will depart; then victory will be assured in the destruction. 103 When the auspicious moon rises for the king of gods; with arrows and the chariot, And the great bow is drawn; then victory will be assured in the destruction. 104 When the auspicious moon rises in the battlefield; with the Parājita flower by the Soubala, And the uninvited guests are driven away; then victory will be assured in the destruction. 105 When the auspicious moon rises with the Pāṇḍava; the assembly is well-governed and united, The lord of the earth is without a lord; then victory will be assured in the destruction. 106 When the auspicious moon rises with various signs; in the forest of the righteous, The great ones will be honored by the wise; then victory will be assured in the destruction. 107 When the auspicious moon rises with the great ones; the righteous king arrives in the forest, The great ones will be honored by the wise; then victory will be assured in the destruction. 108 When the auspicious moon rises for the god of gods; the great one is worshipped, When the auspicious moon rises; then victory will be assured in the destruction. 109 When the auspicious moon rises for the wealthy; as the righteous are properly honored, The learned will be respected; then victory will be assured in the destruction. 110 When the auspicious moon rises with the great assembly; the mighty Bhīma is present, In the presence of men of great honor; then victory will be assured in the destruction. 111 When the auspicious moon rises with the sound of drums; the great gathering of the cows and the herds, Of those who are devoted to their children; then victory will be assured in the destruction. 112 When the auspicious moon rises with the righteous; the righteous king is present with the charioteer.

Page 25, Segment 1

Sanskrit: अाय ००१ १३ ान ुािुवं च स ;दा नाशंसे िवजयाय सय | ११३ | यदाौषं मामकानां विरा ;नयेन ैकरथेन भान ्| िवराटराे वसता महाना ; तदा नाशंसे िवजयाय सय | ११४ | यदाौषं सृ तां मराा ; स ुतां दामुरामज ु तां चाज ु नः गृाुताथ ; तदा नाशंसे िवजयाय सय | ११५ | नाय | यदाौषं िनिजताधन ; ािजत जनाुत | अौिहणीः स युिधिर ; तदा नाशंसे िवजयाय सय | ११६ | यदाौषं नरनारायणौ तौ ; कृ ाज ु अहं ा लोके सदेित ; तदा नाशंसे िवजयाय सय | ११७ | नौ वदतो नारद | यदाौषं माधवं वास ुदेवं ; सवाना पाडवाथ िनिवम ्| येमां गां िवममेकमा ;दा नाशंसे िवजयाय सय | ११८ | यदाौषं कणयधनाां ; ब ुिं कृ तां िनहे के शव | तं चाानं बधा दशयानं; तदा नाशंसे िवजयाय सय | ११९ | यदाौषं वास ुदेवे याते; रथ ैकामतिमानाम ्| आता पृथां साितां के शवेन ; तदा नाशंसे िवजयाय सय | १२० | यदाौषं मिणं वास ुदेवं ; तथा भीं शांतनवं च तेषाम ्| भाराजं चािशषोऽन ुुवाणं ; तदा नाशंसे िवजयाय सय | १२१ | यदाौषं कण उवाच भीं ; नाहं योे युमान े यीित | िहा सेनामपचाम च ैव ; तदा नाशंसे िवजयाय सय | १२२ | यदाौषं वास ुदेवाज ु ीयुवीयािण समागतािन ; तदा नाशंसे िवजयाय सय | १२३ | नौ तौ ; तथा धन ुगािडवममेयम ्|
English: "Invocation 001 13 With the sound of the conch and the drum, victory is assured; for the destruction of the enemy, victory is certain. 113 When the army of my kin is assembled; with the chariot of the great warrior, then for the destruction of the enemy, victory is certain. 114 When the army is led by the great charioteer; with the auspicious banner, then for the destruction of the enemy, victory is certain. 115 When the army is led by the noble ones; with the auspicious weapons, then for the destruction of the enemy, victory is certain. 116 When the army is led by the divine Narayana; I, the lord of the world, am present; then for the destruction of the enemy, victory is certain. 117 Thus spoke Narada. When the army is led by Madhava, the Lord of Vāsudeva; with the great warriors assembled, then for the destruction of the enemy, victory is certain. 118 When the army is led by the one with the conch and the bow; with the great charioteer, then for the destruction of the enemy, victory is certain. 119 When the army is led by Vāsudeva, the Lord of the chariot; with the chariots of the warriors assembled, then for the destruction of the enemy, victory is certain. 120 When the army is led by the Lord of Vāsudeva; and also by Bhishma and Shantanu, then for the destruction of the enemy, victory is certain. 121 When the army is led by the conch, Bhishma speaks; I am not one to be defeated in battle; thus, for the destruction of the enemy, victory is certain. 122 When the army is led by the divine Vāsudeva; with the auspicious gathering, then for the destruction of the enemy, victory is certain. 123 Thus, the wealth of the great warriors is assured."

Page 26, Segment 1

Sanskrit: १४ अन ुमणीपव यदाौषं कमलेनािभपे; रथोपे सीदमान ेऽज ु कृ ं लोकाशयानं शरीरे ; तदा नाशंसे िवजयाय सय | १२४ | न े वै | यदाौषं भीमिमकशनं; िनमाजावयुतं रथानाम ्| न ैषां किते यप ;दा नाशंसे िवजयाय सय | १२५ | यदाौषं भीमशूरं ; हतं पाथनाहवेधृम ्| िशखिडनं प ुरतः ापिया ; तदा नाशंसे िवजयाय सय | १२६ | यदाौषं शरते शयानं; वृं वीरं सािदतं िचप ुैः | भीं कृ ा सोमकानशेषां ;दा नाशंसे िवजयाय सय | १२७ | यदाौषं शांतनवे शयान े; पानीयाथ चोिदतेनाज ु भूिमं िभा तिप तं त भीं ; तदा नाशंसे िवजयाय सय | १२८ | न ेन | यदाौषं शुसूय च युौ ; कौेयानामन ुलोमौ जयाय | िनं चााापदा ाभष ;दा नाशंसे िवजयाय सय | १२९ | यदा ोणो िविवधानमागा;िदशयमरे िचयोधी | न पाडवाेतमािहि ; तदा नाशंसे िवजयाय सय | १३० | यदाौषं चादीयाहारथा ;वितानज ु संशकािहतानज ु न ेन ; तदा नाशंसे िवजयाय सय | १३१ | नाकाय | यदाौषं ूहमभेम ै;भाराजेनाशेण ग ुम ्| िभा सौभं वीरमेकं िवं ; तदा नाशंसे िवजयाय सय | १३२ | यदािभम ु ं पिरवाय बालं ; सव हा पा बभूवुः | महारथाः पाथ मशुव ;दा नाशंसे िवजयाय सय | १३३ |
English: 14 Anumani Pava When the charioteer, seated on the chariot, is afflicted by the lotus of the herb; then, in the body of the victorious, there is no destruction. 124 Again, When the charioteer, terrified by the fierce enemy; is surrounded by the chariots of the enemy; then, in the body of the victorious, there is no destruction. 125 When the charioteer, struck down in battle; is defeated by the arrows of the enemy; then, in the body of the victorious, there is no destruction. 126 When the charioteer, lying in the autumn; is a hero, steadfast in battle; when the enemy is terrified by the remaining warriors; then, in the body of the victorious, there is no destruction. 127 When the charioteer, lying in the peaceful; is questioned by the water; when the earth is shaken by the terrified enemy; then, in the body of the victorious, there is no destruction. 128 Again, When the charioteer, with a calm mind, is victorious; in the battle of the Kauravas; when the enemy is defeated by the words of the wise; then, in the body of the victorious, there is no destruction. 129 When the charioteer, in the midst of the battle; is struck by the arrows of the enemy; then, in the body of the victorious, there is no destruction. 130 When the charioteer, with a clear mind, is victorious; in the battle of the wise; then, in the body of the victorious, there is no destruction. 131 Again, When the charioteer, with a strong heart; is surrounded by the enemy; when the hero is alone, steadfast in battle; then, in the body of the victorious, there is no destruction. 132 When the charioteer, with a fierce heart; is surrounded by the enemy; when the great warriors are defeated; then, in the body of the victorious, there is no destruction. 133

Page 27, Segment 1

Sanskrit: अाय ००१ १५ यदाौषमिभम ु ोधं मुं स ैवे चाज ु ं िनह ; हषाूढाोशतो धातराान ्| न ेन ; तदा नाशंसे िवजयाय सय | १३४ | यदाौषं स ैवाथ ितां ; ितातां तधायाज ु सां िनीणा शुमे च तेन ; तदा नाशंसे िवजयाय सय | १३५ | न ेन | यदाौषं ाहये धनये; मुा हयाायियोपवृान ्| प ुनयु ा वास ुदेवं यातं ; तदा नाशंसे िवजयाय सय | १३६ | यदाौषं वाहन ेासु; रथोपे ितता गािडवेन | सवाोधाािरतानज ु न ेन ; तदा नाशंसे िवजयाय सय | १३७ | यदाौषं नागबलैहं ; ोणानीकं युयुधानं म | यातं वायं य तौ कृ पाथ ; तदा नाशंसे िवजयाय सय | १३८ | यदाौषं कणमासा मुं ; वधाीमं कु िया वचोिभः | धन ुोा तु कणन वीरं ; तदा नाशंसे िवजयाय सय | १३९ | यदा ोणः कृ तवमा कृ प ; कण ौिणमराज शूरः | अमष यैवं वमानं; तदा नाशंसे िवजयाय सय | १४० | यदाौषं देवराजेन दां ; िदां शिं ंिसतां माधवेन | घटोचे रासे घोरपे; तदा नाशंसे िवजयाय सय | १४१ | यदाौषं कणघटोचाां ; युे मुां सूतप ुेण शिम ्| यया वः समरे ससाची ; तदा नाशंसे िवजयाय सय | १४२ | यदाौषं ोणमाचायमेकं ; धृ ुेनाित धमम ्| रथोपे ायगतं िवशं ; तदा नाशंसे िवजयाय सय | १४३ | यदाौषं ौिणना ैरथं ; माीप ुं नकु लं लोकमे |
English: 1. When the auspicious moment arrives, the auspiciousness of the moon and the sun is established; then, victory is assured without doubt. 2. When the auspicious moment is established, the auspiciousness of the sun and moon is confirmed; then, victory is assured without doubt. 3. When the auspicious moment is established for the wealthy; the auspiciousness of the moon is confirmed; then, victory is assured without doubt. 4. When the auspicious moment is established for the chariots; the auspiciousness of the horses is confirmed; then, victory is assured without doubt. 5. When the auspicious moment is established for the elephant forces; the auspiciousness of the army is confirmed; then, victory is assured without doubt. 6. When the auspicious moment is established for the brave; the auspiciousness of the warriors is confirmed; then, victory is assured without doubt. 7. When the auspicious moment is established by the king of gods; the auspiciousness of the moon is confirmed; then, victory is assured without doubt. 8. When the auspicious moment is established for the chariots; the auspiciousness of the horses is confirmed; then, victory is assured without doubt. 9. When the auspicious moment is established for the teacher of the moon; the auspiciousness of the chariots is confirmed; then, victory is assured without doubt. 10. When the auspicious moment is established for the brave; the auspiciousness of the warriors is confirmed; then, victory is assured without doubt.

Sanskrit: १६ अन ुमणीपव समं युे पाडवं युमानं; तदा नाशंसे िवजयाय सय | १४४ | यदा ोणे िनहते ोणप ुो ; नारायणं िदमं िवकु वन ्| न ैषामं गतवााडवानां ; तदा नाशंसे िवजयाय सय | १४५ | यदाौषं कणमशूरं ; हतं पाथनाहवेधृम ्| तिातृणां िवहे देवग ुे; तदा नाशंसे िवजयाय सय | १४६ | यदाौषं ोणप ुं कृ पं च ; ःशासनं कृ तवमाणमुम ्| युिधिरं शूमधष यं ; तदा नाशंसे िवजयाय सय | १४७ | यदाौषं िनहतं मराजं ; रणे शूरं धमराजेन सूत | सदा सामे धते यः स कृ ं ; तदा नाशंसे िवजयाय सय | १४८ | यदाौषं कलहूतमूलं ; मायाबलं सौबलं पाडवेन | हतं सामे सहदेवेन पापं ; तदा नाशंसे िवजयाय सय | १४९ | यदाौषं ामेकं शयानं; दं गा िया तदः | यधनं िवरथं भदप ; तदा नाशंसे िवजयाय सय | १५० | यदाौषं पाडवांिमाना ;ादे वास ुदेवेन साध म ्| अमष णं धष यतः स ुतं मे; तदा नाशंसे िवजयाय सय | १५१ | यदाौषं िविवधांात मागा;दायुे मडलं सरम ्| िमा हतं वास ुदेव ब ुा ; तदा नाशंसे िवजयाय सय | १५२ | यदाौषं ोणप ुािदिभ ै;हतााालाौपदेयां स ुान ्| कृ तं बीभमयशं च कम; तदा नाशंसे िवजयाय सय | १५३ | यदाौषं भीमसेनान ुयातेन ; अाा परमां युम ्| ुेन ैषीकमवधीेन गभ ; तदा नाशंसे िवजयाय सय | १५४ |
English: 16 Anuśarmanīpava When the equal army is engaged in battle; then victory is assured in destruction. 144 When the elephant is slain by the elephant hunter; Narayana, the divine light, is invoked. When the warriors have not retreated; then victory is assured in destruction. 145 When the fierce warrior is slain; in the battle of the path of the brave. For the victorious, the divine is invoked; then victory is assured in destruction. 146 When the elephant is slain, the bowman and the archer; the command is given to the brave. In the battle, the strong are victorious; then victory is assured in destruction. 147 When the king of elephants is slain; in battle by the brave king. He who is always victorious in battle; then victory is assured in destruction. 148 When the root of conflict is slain; the illusionary strength of the mighty Pandava. Slain in battle by Sahadeva, the sinful; then victory is assured in destruction. 149 When the single elephant is lying down; the great one is struck by the mighty. The wealth of the brave is rendered useless; then victory is assured in destruction. 150 When the Pandavas are engaged in battle; with the divine Vasudeva as their guide. The great one is struck by the divine; then victory is assured in destruction. 151 When the various armies are engaged; the great one is struck by the divine. The mighty is slain by Vasudeva; then victory is assured in destruction. 152 When the elephant is slain by the bowman; the great one is struck by the mighty. The deed is done by the powerful; then victory is assured in destruction. 153 When Bhimasena is engaged in battle; the great one is struck by the mighty. With the strength of the great, victory is assured; then victory is assured in destruction. 154

Sanskrit: अाय ००१ १७ यदाौषं िशरोऽज ु अाा मिणरं च दं ; तदा नाशंसे िवजयाय सय | १५५ | न ेन ; मुं ीमेण शाम ्| यदाौषं ोणप ुेण गभ ; वैराा वै पामान े महाे | ैपायनः के शवो ोणप ुं ; पररेणािभशाप ैः शशाप | १५६ | शोा गाारी प ुपौैिवहीना ; तथा वः िपतृिभातृिभ | कृ तं काय रं पाडवेय ैः ; ां रामसपं प ुन ैः | १५७ | कं युे दश शेषाः ुता मे; योऽाकं पाडवानां च स | ूना िवंशितराहताौिहणीनां ; तिामे िवहे ियाणाम ्| १५८ | तमसा वीण मोह आिवशतीव माम ्| सां नोपलभे सूत मनो िवलतीव मे | १५९ | इ ुा धृतराोऽथ िवल बःिखतः | मूितः प ुनराः सयं वामवीत ्| १६० | सय ैवते ाणांु िमािम मािचरम ्| ोकं िप न पयािम फलं जीिवतधारणे | १६१ | तं तथावािदनं दीनं िवलपं महीपितम ्| गाविणिरदं धीमाहाथ वामवीत ्| १६२ | ुतवानिस वै राो महोाहाहाबलान ्| ैपायन वदतो नारद च धीमतः | १६३ | महु राजवंशेष ु ग ुण ैः समुिदतेष ु च | जातािािवषः शितमतेजसः | १६४ |
English: 1. When the medicinal herb is prepared, then the victory is assured; thus, there is no destruction. 2. With the help of the wise, peace is attained. 3. When the medicinal herb is prepared with the essence of the earth, the enemies are vanquished. 4. The sage, having prepared the medicinal herb, curses with the curse of the other. 5. The beautiful flower, devoid of fragrance; thus, the father is bereft of sons. 6. What has been done by the wise is the essence of the body; the king is adorned with the essence of the earth. 7. How many remain, my ten; the wise are not without sorrow. 8. The one who is afflicted by the darkness of ignorance does not perceive; my mind is indeed troubled. 9. Thus, the son of Dhritarashtra, having been defeated, is indeed troubled; the one who is wise is not without sorrow. 10. The wise do not engage in the fruit of life; they do not desire sorrow. 11. Thus, the one who speaks thus, the king, is indeed troubled; the wise are not without sorrow. 12. The one who has spoken is indeed a great sage; the wise Narada speaks. 13. Among the great royal lineages, the qualities are indeed united; the one born of the noble lineage shines with great brilliance.

Sanskrit: १८ अन ुमणीपव धमण पृिथव िजा य ैिरादिण ैः | अि.ोके यशः ा ततः कालवशं गताः | १६५ | वैं महारथं वीरं सृयं जयतां वरम ्| स ुहों रिदेवं च कीवं तथौिशजम ्| १६६ | बाीकं दमनं शैं शयाितमिजतं िजतम ्| िवािममिममरीषं महाबलम ्| १६७ | मं मन ुिमाकु रामं दाशरिथं च ैव शशिबं भगीरथम ्| १६८ | ं गयं भरतमेव च | ययाितं शुभकमाणं देवैय यािजतः यम ्| च ैयूपािता भूिमयेयं सवनाकरा | १६९ | इित राां चतुिवशारदेन स ुरिष णा | प ुशोकािभताय प ुरा शैाय कीितताः | १७० | तेाे गताः पूव राजानो बलवराः | महारथा महाानः सवः समुिदता ग ुण ैः | १७१ | पूः कु यः शूरो िवगो महाधृितः | अन ेना युवना ककुो िवमी रघ ुः | १७२ | िविजती वीितहो भवः ेतो बृह ुः | उशीनरः शतरथः को िलहो ुमः | १७३ | दोवः परो वेनः सगरः स ितिन िमः | अजेयः परशुः प ुः श ुदवावृधोऽनघः | १७४ | देवायः स ुितमः स ुतीको बृहथः |
English: 18 Anumani (a type of gem) The earth, knowing the truth, is filled with various qualities. From the glory of the scriptures, those who are subject to time have passed away. Victory to the great charioteer, the hero, the best among the victorious! Also to the auspicious Ridhadeva and the great physician! The conqueror of the demon, the one who is victorious in the bed of death, Mighty and powerful, the one who is the best among the strong! Rama, the son of Dasharatha, and Bhagiratha, And also Bharata. By the auspicious deeds of Yayati, the one who is worshipped by the gods, The earth is made prosperous by the offerings of the great sages. Thus, with the fourteenth chapter, the great sage Surishi Has sung the glories of the ancient kings who were powerful and virtuous. The kings of the past, who were strong and valiant, The great charioteers, all gathered together with their qualities. The one who is a great warrior, who is fearless and has great strength, With the young and brave Kaku, the one who is known as Raghu. The victorious, the one who has conquered fear, the great one, Ushinar, the one with the bow, the one who is known as Shuma. The one who is the son of the ocean, Sagara, the one who is invincible, The one with the axe, the one who is the protector, the one who is sinless. The gods are pleased with the one who is the best, the one who is the greatest.

Sanskrit: २० अन ुमणीपव भिवतं तथा त नातः शोिचतुमहिस | दैवं ािवशेषेण को िनविततुमहित | १८६ | िवधातृिविहतं माग न किदितवतते | कालमूलिमदं सव भावाभावौ स ुखास ुखे | १८७ | कालः पचित भूतािन कालः संहरित जाः | िनदहं जाः कालं कालः शमयते प ुनः | १८८ | कालो िवकु ते भावावा.ोके शुभाशुभान ्| कालः सिपते सवाः जा िवसृजते प ुनः | १८९ | कालः सवष ु भूतेष ु चरिवधृतः समः | १८९ | अतीतानागता भावा ये च वति सांतम ्| ताालिनिमता ुा न सां हातुमहिस | १९० | सूत उवाच | अोपिनषदं प ुयां कृ ैपायनोऽवीत ्| भारतायना ुयादिप पादमधीयतः | १९१ | धान पूये सवपापाशेषतः | १९१ | देवष यो  प ुया राजष यथा | की े शुभकमाणथा यमहोरगाः | १९२ | भगवाास ुदेव की तेऽ सनातनः | स िह समृतं च ैव पिवं प ुयमेव च | १९३ |
English: 20 Anumani-pavṛha Thus, the one who is not to be grieved is not to be grieved by the divine, due to the special nature of fate. 186 The one who is bound by the creator does not become liberated. The root of time is the existence and non-existence of all beings, which is happiness and sorrow. 187 Time cooks the beings; time gathers the created. The one who is bound by time, time again calms. 188 Time differentiates between auspicious and inauspicious states. Time, the lord of all, again releases the created. 189 Time is equal to all beings, maintaining their movement. 189 The states of the past, present, and future are not to be grasped by the one who is bound by time. 190 Soot spoke: Even though the Upanishads are pure, they are not to be disregarded. The Bharatiya tradition is to be honored in the footnotes. 191 In the purest of the pure, all sins are completely removed. 191 The divine beings, the great sages, and the kings of the earth, who are engaged in auspicious deeds, are indeed the great serpents. 192 The blessed one, the eternal god, is indeed the one who grants eternal life and pure liberation. 193

English: 1. "The supreme truth, eternal, is spoken of by the wise." 2. "The unchanging is indeed the source of all beings." 3. "That which is spoken of as the ultimate is indeed the supreme." 4. "Those endowed with the strength of knowledge are steadfast." 5. "The one who is devoted to righteousness, a virtuous person, does not suffer." 6. "In this world, the one who is devoted to truth is always protected." 7. "Both are indeed the same; the one who is devoted to truth is a king." 8. "India is like nectar, and it is indeed immortal." 9. "As butter is churned from milk, so is India from its people." 10. "The giver of gifts is like a cow; it is indeed the source of abundance." 11. "As they are revered, so is India honored." 12. "Thus, the history and the Puranas should be studied."

English: 22 The essence of purity Having taken the form of the sacred, I am the essence of the mind. | 204 | What is the meaning of this knowledge, which is the essence of the Vedas? | The doubt arises that sin is also created by the mind. | 205 | Whoever reads this pure text, with a pure mind, | That person will attain the essence of Bharat. | 206 | Whoever follows this path with devotion, | They will have a long life, fame, and a good end. | 207 | The Vedas are one, and Bharat is one. | Gathered together, they are the essence of the ancient texts. | 208 | In the great and the small, the essence is more. | 208 | The Mahabharata is the essence of the great epic. | Whoever knows the Vedas, all sins are removed. | 209 | There is no end to penance, nor is there an end; the essence of the Vedas is not limited. | There is no end to the essence of the scriptures; the essence is not hindered by worldly attachments. | 210 | The essence of purity Anaya 002 The sages said.

English: "Thus 002 23 In the assembly, the one who speaks, We shall proclaim this as it is! 001 The speaker said: If auspicious tales are heard by you, We shall proclaim the assembly's auspiciousness! 002 In the confluence of the white and red, Rama, the best of the beautiful, Repeatedly struck the one who was questioned. 003 He, with a great bow, having taken the fire, In the assembly, performed the act of giving. 004 He, in that assembly, with the best of gifts, Having taken the seat, spoke to us. 005 Then, from the beginning, the fathers of the questioned, That one, having been instructed, was the great Rama. 006 Near them, the land of gifts, Is indeed the most excellent of assemblies. 007 By which means that land is attained, By that, indeed, the land is made prosperous. 008 In the end, indeed, there was a great assembly, In the assembly, the one who is the best of the best. 009 In the middle of the assembly, in the land of the wise."

English: 24 Pavansamāhāpava In the eleventh society of the great sages, you shall be united. | 010 | Thus, the name of the newly established beautiful land is known to you. | 011 | This land is indeed glorious. Thus, I have made this statement to you, O sages, as the land is indeed manifest in the world. | 012 | The sages said: The great sage said, "Thus, the name of the great sage is known. Let it be proclaimed as it is." | 013 | The measure of the great sage is known by the name of the charioteer. As it is, it is known to all. | 014 | The charioteer spoke: One chariot, one elephant, one man, and foot soldiers; the swift horses are bound together. | 015 | But the name of the army is known as the chief of the army. The chief of the army is indeed bound together. | 016 | The army is known as the group, and the army is indeed a multitude. The chariots are indeed drawn by the multitude. | 017 | The army is indeed a multitude of chariots, and the ten groups are indeed bound together. | 018 | The measure of the great sage is known by the chariots.

English: 1. "Aṅgāya 002" 2. "25" 3. "With the assembly of the warriors, the lineage of the united." 4. "A hundred times, and also more, thus it is established." 5. "The measure of elephants is indeed defined." 6. "This is a hundredfold assembly, and also nine." 7. "Among men, the qualities of the righteous are indeed pure." 8. "The assembly of birds and also of beasts, a hundredfold." 9. "The tenfold measure of the sixfold assembly is defined." 10. "These are the knowledgeable people of the assembly." 11. "What you have spoken, O wise ones, is indeed clear." 12. "By this measure, the assembly of the two is established." 13. "The assembly of the wise is indeed defined by the ten." 14. "In the land, they have indeed gone to their end." 15. "The Kauravas, having been defeated, have indeed perished." 16. "In the battle, the Bhīṣma was indeed the supreme." 17. "In the battle, the son of Pṛthā was indeed the leader." 18. "In the battle, the Kauravas were indeed defeated by the might." 19. "Thus, in the day, the Gautamas were indeed victorious." 20. "The strength of the night is indeed the victory of the wise." 21. "O you, the sons of Śaunaka, the Bharatas are indeed victorious." 22. "In the assembly, the Pāṇḍavas are indeed supreme."

English: 26 Pavansamāhāra In the beginning, the words of the wise are spoken by men with great effort. 030 The knowledge of the Vedas is the essence of life. History is the foundation of all knowledge. 031 History is the essence of the wise; it is the speech of the people, like the Vedas. 032 The wise, having understood the essence of the words, proclaim the history of Bharat. 033 The sacred gem of the wind is the first among the sacred texts; it reveals the lineage of the Pauravas. 034 Then, the divine being, born of the wind, is worshipped; the fire is offered in the house of the sage. 035 Then, the killing of the crane and the wind is performed; thereafter, the swayamvara of the princess is celebrated. 036 The sacred marriage is then performed; the departure of the bride is marked by the wind. 037 Then, the abode of the sage is established; the auspicious signs are then revealed, bringing forth the harbinger of good fortune. 038 Then, the great sacrifice is performed, and the assembly of the wind is established, followed by the supreme. 039

English: "Jarasandha's killing, O wind, O wind, as in the victory of Diti. O wind, in the victory of Diti, the Rajasuya sacrifice is performed. Then, the carrying of the burden of Shishupala's killing. The wind, then, is the supreme essence of the great sound. Then, the wind, the killing of the Kirmira demon, the king of the elephants, O wind, is the best among the Kiratas. The wind, the supreme essence of the sight of the world, then, the wind, the wise king of the earth. The wind, the supreme essence of the killing of the Jatila, and the wind, the distinguished one, is the one that follows. The wind, the one who is like a monkey, is the one that follows. Then, the wind, the conversation of the two, is the one that follows. Then, the wind, the sound of the announcement, is the one that follows. The wind, the fear of the deer, is the one that follows. The wind, the taking of the princess, is the one that follows. The wind, the great one, is the one that follows. Then, the wind, the one who is in the forest, is the one that follows. The killing of the Kichaka, the wind, the gathering of the cows, is the one that follows. By the power of the wind, the great one, the one who is in the marriage, the wind, the supreme essence of the great sound, is the one that follows. Then, the wind, the supreme essence of the great sound, is the one that follows."

The wind, which is the supreme essence, is the one that brings forth the auspiciousness. | 054 | 6. The wind, which is the one that brings forth the great sound, is the earth's wind, then, the one that brings forth the essence. | 055 | 7. The wind, then, is the essence of the supreme sound, the one that brings forth the great essence. | 059 | 11. The essence of the wind is the one that brings forth the qualities of the lineage. | 060 |

English: 1. The auspicious wind, the great purifier, is the source of all good. 2. The wind of the waters, the wind of the earth, is supreme. 3. The wind of the sacred fire, the wind of the divine, is the essence of all. 4. The wind of the earth, the wind of the heavens, is the king of all. 5. The wind of the sky, the wind of the stars, is the supreme ruler. 6. The wind of the mountains, the wind of the forests, is the source of wisdom. 7. The wind of the rivers, the wind of the oceans, is the destroyer of all sins. 8. The wind of the seasons, the wind of the cycles, is the great teacher. 9. The wind of the storms, the wind of the tempests, is the source of all power. 10. The wind of the universe, the wind of the cosmos, is the ultimate truth.

English: 30 Pavansamāhā In the context of the Pava, it is not to be said that the Pava is the twelfth. The compound is the Pava of the Bharata. 071 In the Pava, the great Mahāmaṇu is the one who is the Pava. The lineage of Puloma is described. 072 The possibility of all serpents and the gathering of the Gṛdhras. The churning of the ocean is indeed established by the wise. 073 For the one who sacrifices, the king is the Pārīcī and the one who is to be spoken of is the great name of the Bharatas. 074 Various possibilities of the kings are indeed possible in the Pava. And for all the seers, the great names are indeed the means of salvation. 075 The descent of the portions is indeed the most described of the gods. Of the divine beings, the demons, and the great powerful ones. 076 Among the serpents and the great ones, the husbands of the Gṛdhras. And for all beings, the various possibilities are indeed established. 077 Among the Vasu, the great name of the Punarbhava is indeed the great name. The chariot of the Punarāṣa is indeed in the sky. 078 The gathering of the Tejas is indeed possible. The one who is the king is indeed the one who is established in the assembly. 079 The protection of the Ṛtā is indeed the one who is the Chitrā. When the Chitrā is slain, the Ṛtā is indeed the one who is the great one. 080 The one who is indeed the wise and the one who is established in the assembly.

English: 1. Dharma is the foundation of the world. 2. The path of righteousness is the way of the wise. 3. The strength of the righteous is like a mountain. 4. The forest of the righteous is filled with great wealth. 5. The abode of the righteous is a refuge for the distressed. 6. The wise are like the sun, illuminating the world. 7. The wise are free from attachment and desire. 8. The wise are like the moon, bringing peace to the hearts. 9. The wise are like the ocean, vast and deep. 10. The wise are like the stars, guiding the lost. 11. The wise are like the wind, ever-moving and free. 12. The wise are like the earth, stable and nurturing. 13. The wise are like the fire, purifying and transformative. 14. The wise are like the lotus, rising above the mud. 15. The wise are like the tree, providing shelter and sustenance. 16. The wise are like the river, flowing towards the sea. 17. The wise are like the mountain, unshaken by storms. 18. The wise are like the flower, spreading fragrance everywhere. 19. The wise are like the bird, soaring high in the sky. 20. The wise are like the jewel, precious and rare. 21. The wise are like the bridge, connecting hearts and minds. 22. The wise are like the song, bringing joy to all. 23. The wise are like the book, filled with knowledge and wisdom. 24. The wise are like the teacher, guiding others on the path. 25. The wise are like the friend, always there in times of need. 26. The wise are like the parent, nurturing and protective. 27. The wise are like the healer, mending wounds and bringing peace. 28. The wise are like the light, dispelling darkness and ignorance. 29. The wise are like the compass, showing the right direction. 30. The wise are like the anchor, providing stability in turbulent times. 31. The wise are like the mirror, reflecting truth and clarity.

English: 32 The gathering of the wind In the body of the wind, there is beauty and desire, and the beloved is pleasing. In the opinion of the Lord of the Universe, there is a great delight. 092 The taking of the house is a gathering of the divine. The gathering of the divine is the burning of the body and the destruction of the body. 093 In the beauty of the divine, the light of the sun is pleasing. My mind is absorbed in the light of the moon and the moonlight. 094 The great sage is the protector, born of the lineage of the sage. 094 This is the first of the great gatherings. Among the hundreds of the unworthy, the supreme offering is the best. 095 The one who is the same as the one who is the light of the sun. 095 Thus, the gathering of the world and the nine hundred. The gathering of the four and eighty is the great gathering. 096 The second is the assembly of the wind, the great gathering of the assembly. The assembly is the gathering of the learned and the wise. 097 From the assembly of the guardians of the world, Narada speaks of the ten. The Rajasuya and the killing of Jarasandha. 098 In the gathering of the mountains, the kings are absorbed in the light. In the Rajasuya, the dialogue of the killing of Shishupala. 099 Wherever there is glory, there is the great gathering of the divine, and the laughter of Bhima in the assembly hall. 100

Sanskrit: अाय ००२ ३३ या म ुूतो येन ूतमकारयत ्| य धमस ुतं ूते शकु िनः िकतवोऽजयत ्| १०१ | य ूताणवे माौपदी नौिरवाणवात ्| तारयामास तांीणााा यधनो नृपः | १०२ | प ुनरेव ततो ूते समायत पाडवान ्| १०२ | एतव सभापव समाातं महाना | अायाः सितयाथा ौ चा संया | १०३ | ोकानां े सहे तु प ोकशतािन च | ोका ैकादश ेयाः पवयिकीितताः | १०४ | अतः परं तृतीयं तु ेयमारयकं महत ्| पौरान ुगमनं च ैव धमप ु धीमतः | १०५ | वृीनामागमो य पाालानां च सवशः | य सौभवधाानं िकमरवध एव च | १०६ | अहेतोिववास पाथ ािमततेजसः | १०६ | महादेवेन युं च िकरातवप ुषा सह | दशनं लोकपालानां गारोहणमेव च | १०७ | दशनं बृहद महषभािवतानः | युिधिर चात सन े पिरदेवनम ्| १०८ | नलोपाानमैव धिमं कणोदयम ्| दमयाः िितय नल सनागमे | १०९ |
English: «Agnaya 002 33 By whom the sacrifice was performed, that is the one who made the offering. The one who is righteous, by that offering, the powerful one was victorious. 101 The one who is the essence of the offerings, the one who is the great wind of liberation, the king saved the one who was in distress. 102 Again, then, the one who is learned performed the sacrifice. 102 Thus, the assembly of the great ones was established, by the auspiciousness of the Agnaya and the auspiciousness of the assembly. 103 In the verses, there are indeed a hundred verses, the verses are eleven in number, and they are well composed. 104 Therefore, the third one is indeed a great offering, the going of the townspeople is also righteous, by the wise. 105 The arrival of the Vrishnis and the complete offerings of the Palas, the one who is of the nature of auspiciousness, and the one who is of the nature of the great. 106 By the cause of the unbroken offerings, the one who is of the nature of brilliance is indeed established. 106 With Mahadeva, you are indeed to be worshipped, along with the one who is the great protector of the ten directions. 107 The ten are the great ones, the ones who are endowed with the essence of the great, the one who is the protector of the world, and the one who is the great deity. 108 The one who is not to be neglected, indeed, the wise one is the one who rises. The offerings are indeed established in the arrival of the ten directions. 109»

Sanskrit: ३४ पवसंहपव वनवासगतानां च पाडवानां महानाम ्| ग वृिरााता लोमशेनाज ु न वै | ११० | तीथ याा तथ ैवा पाडवानां महानाम ्| जटास ुर तैव वधः समुपवयते | १११ | िनयुो भीमसेन ौपा गमादन े | य मारप ुाथ निलन तामधष यत ्| ११२ | या स ुमह ुमभवह रास ैः | य ैािप महावीयमिणममुख ैथा | ११३ | आगमिप चाानं य वातािपभणम ्| लोपामुािभगमनमपाथ मृषेरिप | ११४ | ततः येनकपोतीयमुपाानमनरम ्| इोऽिय धम अिजासििबं नृपम ्| ११५ | ऋय चिरतं कौमारचािरणः | जामद राम चिरतं भूिरतेजसः | ११६ | कातवीयवधो य हैहयानां च वयते | सौकमिप चाानं वनो य भागवः | ११७ | शयाितये नासौ कृ तवाोमपीिथनौ | ताां च य स मुिनयवनं ितपािदतः | ११८ | जूपाानमैव य प ुेण सोमकः | प ुाथ मयजाजा लेभे प ुशतं च सः | ११९ |
English: 34 The gathering of the wind Of those who have gone to the forest and the great ones of the Pandavas, the sage Lomasha speaks. Thus, the great ones of the Pandavas, with matted hair, are indeed present. The mighty Bhimasena, having taken the path of the great, does not abandon his duty. Wherever the great ones are, there the mighty ones are also present. The arrival of the wind, the departure of Lopāmuda, is indeed a matter of great importance. Then, the sage Kapotika, having approached the king, speaks of righteousness. The sage Chyavana, for a long time, and Jamadagni, for a long time, are of great radiance. The killing of the Kaatviiya, and the great ones of the Hayas, are indeed significant. The sage, having taken the path of the great, is indeed a great one among the sages. The one who is called Jatuka, having performed the sacrifice, received a hundredfold.

Sanskrit: अाय ००२ ३५ अावीयमैव िववादे य बिनम ्| िविज सागरं ां िपतरं लवानृिषः | १२० | अवा िदाािण ग ुवथ ससािचना | िनवातकवच ैयु ं िहरयप ुरवािसिभः | १२१ | समागम पाथ  ातृिभगमादन े | घोषयाा च गवय युं िकरीिटनः | १२२ | प ुनरागमनं च ैव तेषां ैतवनं सरः | जयथेनापहारो ौपाामारात ्| १२३ | यैनमयाीमो वायुवेगसमो जवे | माक डेयसमायामुपाानािन भागशः | १२४ | संदशनं च कृ  संवाद ैव सया | ीिहौिणकमाानमै ुं तथ ैव च | १२५ | सािवौालकीयं च वैोपाानमेव च | रामायणमुपाानमैव बिवरम ्| १२६ | कण पिरमोषोऽ कु डलाां प ुरंदरात ्| आरणेयमुपाानं य धमऽशाुतम ्| १२७ | जमुलवरा य पाडवाः पिमां िदशम ्| १२७ | एतदारयकं पव तृतीयं पिरकीिततम ्| अाायशते े तु संाते परमिष णा | १२८ | एकोनसित ैव तथाायाः कीितताः | १२८ |
English: 002 35 In the debate of the unlearned, those who are ignorant, The ocean of knowledge is like a father to the wise. | 120 | The one who is knowledgeable, with a firm foundation, Is like a shield against the winds of ignorance. | 121 | The gathering of paths leads to the division of the wise, With the proclamation of the great, they are like the sun. | 122 | The return is indeed their source of joy, With the victory of the wise, the best of the best is achieved. | 123 | Those who are like the wind in speed, In the realm of knowledge, they are part of the whole. | 124 | The communication of the learned is indeed a conversation, With the wise, they are like the sun and the moon. | 125 | The teachings of the great and the knowledge of the wise, The Ramayana is indeed a source of great wisdom. | 126 | The one who is knowledgeable is like a jewel among the ignorant, The teachings of the forest are indeed the most profound. | 127 | The one who is wise knows the paths of the ten directions. | 127 | This is the third of the teachings, In the hundred verses, the supreme knowledge is revealed. | 128 | The one who is not learned is indeed like the wise. | 128 |

Sanskrit: ३६ पवसंहपव एकादश सहािण ोकानां षतािन च | चतुःषिथा ोकाः पवतिरकीिततम ्| १२९ | अतः परं िनबोधेदं वैराटं पविवरम ्| िवराटनगरं गा मशान े िवप ुलां शमीम ्| १३० | ा संिनदध ु पाडवा आयुधा ुत | १३० | य िवय नगरं छिभवस ते | रानो वधो य कीचक वृकोदरात ्| १३१ | गोहे य पाथन िनिजताः कु रवो युिध | गोधनं च िवराट मोितं य पाडवैः | १३२ | िवराटेनोरा दा  ुषा य िकरीिटनः | अिभम ु ं समुिय सौभमिरघाितनम ्| १३३ | चतुथ मेतिप ुलं वैराटं पव विणतम ्| अािप पिरसंातमायानां महाना | १३४ | सषिरथो पूणा ोकामिप मे णु | ोकानां े सहे तु ोकाः पाशदेव तु | १३५ | पवयिमााताः संया परमिष णा | १३५ | उोगपव िवेयं पमं वतः परम ्| उपे िनिवेष ु पाडवेष ु िजगीषया | १३६ | यधनोऽज ु न ैव वास ुदेवमुपितौ | १३६ | साहामिमरे भवाौ कतु महित |
English: 36 Pavansamāhā Eleven companions of the verses, six in number; Four verses are most glorified in the Pavanatirikīrtitam. 129 Therefore, understand this Vairāta Pavanivṛtam; Vairātanagara is a great cremation ground. 130 The sound of the conch is heard, O warriors! 130 Where the city of Śivāya is, There, the slaughter of the Bhīma and Kīchaka occurs. 131 In the house where the Pāṇḍavas are established, The wealth of cows is indeed Vairāta's, as desired by the Pāṇḍavas. 132 Vairāta's daughter is known as the one who is glorious; Abhimanyu is the one who is most beautiful. 133 The fourth is the one who is Vairāta's, Even if it is a great festival of the assembled warriors. 134 The chariot of the Sātvatas is full; Among the verses, the verses are indeed the best. 135 The Pavanapratyaya is the supreme knowledge. 135 The usage of Pavan is indeed the first among the supreme. In the assembly, the Pāṇḍavas desire victory. 136 The wealth of the Bhīma is indeed The divine abode of the gods. 136 May there be auspiciousness in the great deeds!

Sanskrit: अाय ००२ ३७ इ ुे वचने कृ ो योवाच महामितः | १३७ | अयुमानमाानं मिणं प ुषष भौ | अौिहण वा स ै क वा िकं ददाहम ्| १३८ | वे यधनः स ैं माा य मितः | अयुमानं सिचवं वे कृ ं धनयः | १३९ | सयं ेषयामास शमाथ पाडवाित | य तं महाराजो धृतराः तापवान ्| १४० | ुा च पाडवा वास ुदेवप ुरोगमान ्| जागरः संजे धृतरा िचया | १४१ | िवरो य वाािन िविचािण िहतािन च | ावयामास राजानं धृतरां मनीिषणम ्| १४२ | तथा सनुजातेन याामन ुमम ्| मनापाितो राजा ािवतः शोकलालसः | १४३ | भाते राजसिमतौ सयो य चािभभोः | ऐकां वास ुदेव ोवानज ु न च | १४४ | य कृ ो दयापः संिधिमहायशाः | यमागामं कतु  नगरं नागसायम ्| १४५ | ाानं च कृ  राा यधन ेन वै | शमाथ याचमान पयोभयोिहतम ्| १४६ | कणयधनादीनां ं िवाय मितम ्| योगेरं कृ ेन य राजस ु दिशतम ्| १४७ |
English: 002 37 In response to the words of the sage, Mahāmita spoke. 137 What is the use of a person who is not endowed with longevity? What can he give, whether he is a king or a beggar? 138 The one who is endowed with wealth, even if he is a beggar, is considered wealthy. The one who is endowed with longevity is indeed wealthy. 139 He established peace and tranquility, the great king Dhritarashtra was steadfast. 140 The sage also established peace, the divine sage was free from ailments. Dhritarashtra was vigilant and attentive. 141 The king Dhritarashtra, who was wise, was also discerning and insightful. 142 Thus, with the son of the sage, the king was filled with sorrow. The king, who was afflicted by grief, was in a state of lamentation. 143 In the royal assembly, the king was present, and the sage was also there. 144 Those who are compassionate and have a good reputation, they are indeed the ones who are worthy of respect. 145 The king, who was endowed with wealth, was indeed a seeker of peace. 146 Among the wealthy and the learned, the one who is wise is indeed the best. 147

Sanskrit: ३८ पवसंहपव रथमारो कृ ेन य कणऽन ुमितः | उपायपूव शौडीयााात तेन सः | १४८ | ततािभिनयाा रथानरदिनाम ्| नगराािनप ुरालसंानमेव च | १४९ | य राा उक ेषणं पाडवाित | ोभािविन महायुे ेन ू रवािदना | १५० | रथाितरथसंानमोपाानमेव च | १५० | एतुबवृां पमं पव भारते | उोगपव िनिदं संिधिवहसंितम ्| १५१ | अायाः संया  षडशीितशतं ृतम ्| ोकानां षहािण तावेव शतािन च | १५२ | ोका नवितः ोाथ ैवाौ महाना | ासेनोदारमितना पवयिंपोधनाः | १५३ | अत ऊ िविचाथ भीपव चते | जूखडिविनमाणं यों सयेन ह | १५४ | य युमभूोरं दशाहाितदाणम ्| य यौिधिरं स ैं िवषादमगमरम ्| १५५ | कमलं य पाथ  वास ुदेवो महामितः | मोहजं नाशयामास हेतुिभमदशन ैः | १५६ | िशखिडनं प ुरृ  य पाथ महाधन ुः |
English: 38 Pavansamāhāpava With the chariot of the sun, the one who is like a jewel, He, having approached the means, is a great sage. 148 By the distinction of the chariots, In the city of the charioteers, and also in the assembly of the city. 149 When the king is engaged in the great sacrifice, With the great wealth of the sun, he shines like the sun. 150 The chariot and the charioteer are indeed the means of assembly. 150 This is the first of the great powers in Bharata, The power of the sun, the supreme among the assemblies. 151 The doubt of the uninvited is indeed six hundred and sixty. The verses are indeed a hundred in number. 152 The verses are nine, the great wealth is indeed the great treasure, With the generous measure of the sun, they are the means of gathering. 153 Thus, the one who is wise, the one who is a great sage, With the knowledge of the sun, he is indeed the one who is wise. 154 When the one who is like a great mountain is engaged in the ten sacrifices, He, the one who is a warrior, indeed becomes the one who is sorrowful. 155 When the lotus is offered, the great god, the great one, Destroys the delusion, the one who is the cause of the great destruction. 156 The one who is like a great treasure, when offered, He, the great wealth, indeed shines.

Page 51, Segment 1

Sanskrit: अाय ००२ ३९ िविनििशत ैबाण ै रथाीमपातयत ्| १५७ | षमेतहापव भारते पिरकीिततम ्| अायानां शतं ों सदश तथापरे | १५८ | प ोकसहािण संयाौ शतािन च | ोका चतुराशीितः पवयिकीितताः | १५९ | ासेन वेदिवषा संाता भीपविण | १५९ | ोणपव ततिं बवृामुते | य संशकाः पाथ मपिनू रणािजरात ्| १६० | भगदो महाराजो य शसमो युिध | स ुतीके न नागेन सह शः िकरीिटना | १६१ | ं बहवो ज ुलकमहारथाः | यािभम ु जयथमुखा बालं शूरमायौवनम ्| १६२ | हतेऽिभमौ ुेन य पाथन संयुगे | अौिहणीः स हा हतो राजा जयथः | १६३ | संशकावशेषं च कृ तं िनःशेषमाहवे | १६३ | अलुसः ुतायु जलसंध वीयवान ्| सौमदििवराट ुपद महारथः | १६४ | घटोचादयाे िनहता ोणपविण | १६४ | अामािप चाैव ोणे युिध िनपाितते | अं ाकारों नारायणममिष तः | १६५ |
English: 1. "The charioteer of the king is skilled in the art of warfare." 2. "In Bharat, the great epic is recited." 3. "The number of verses is a hundred, and there are others as well." 4. "The verses are eighty-four in number." 5. "By the Vedic tradition, the great epic is recited." 6. "The charioteer is skilled in the art of battle." 7. "When the king Bhagadatta, equal to the gods in battle, fought with the Nagas." 8. "Many great charioteers were present." 9. "When the brave youth, Jayathama, faced the battle." 10. "In the battle, when the brave Jayathama was slain." 11. "The remnants of the battle were completely destroyed." 12. "The mighty warrior, Alakusa, was victorious." 13. "The charioteer was slain in the battle." 14. "Even the great charioteer, Narayana, was defeated in battle."

Sanskrit: ४० पवसंहपव समं भारते पव महदेतदातम ्| अ ते पृिथवीपालाः ायशो िनधनं गताः | १६६ | ोणपविण ये शूरा िनिदाः प ुषष भाः | १६६ | अायानां शतं ोमायाः सितथा | अौ ोकसहािण तथा नव शतािन च | १६७ | ोका नव तथ ैवा संातादिशना | पाराशयण मुिनना सि ोणपविण | १६८ | अतः परं कणपव ोते परमाुतम ्| सारे िविनयोग मराज धीमतः | १६९ | आातं य पौराणं िप ुर िनपातनम ्| १६९ | याणे पषा संवादः कणशयोः | हंसकाकीयमाानमैवाेपसंिहतम ्| १७० | अों ित च ोधो युिधिरिकरीिटनोः | ैरथे य पाथन हतः कण महारथः | १७१ | अमं पव िनिदमेतारतिचकैः | एकोनसितः ोा अायाः कणपविण | १७२ | चायव सहािण नव ोकशतािन च | १७२ | अतः परं िविचाथ शपव कीिततम ्| हतवीरे स ैे तु न ेता मेरोऽभवत ्| १७३ |
English: 40 Pavansamāhāpava In Bharat, the great Pava has now become prominent. The guardians of the earth have gone to the abode of fame. 166 The brave ones among the Pava warriors are indeed the best of men. 166 Among the hundred of the great Pava, there are also those who are strong. And also nine hundred who are of great strength. 167 Nine are the strong ones, and thus they are known as the Pava warriors. By the sage Parāśara, they are described as such. 168 Therefore, the supreme Pava is the best among the Kāṇa. All are engaged in the service of the wise king. 169 The one who is a descendant of the ancient lineage is indeed a great warrior. 169 In the dialogue of the Kāṇa, there is a conversation about the swan-like beings. The great warriors are indeed united in their efforts. 170 In the battle, the one who is skilled and wise is the one who prevails. When the great charioteer is defeated, he is indeed a great warrior. 171 The Pava has indeed become prominent among the warriors of Bharat. The one who is the best among the hundred is the Pava warrior. 172 With the Kāṇa, there are also nine hundred strong warriors. 172 Therefore, the wise ones among the Pava are indeed the most skilled. In the presence of the slain heroes, they did not become weak. 173

Sanskrit: अाय ००२ ४१ वृािन रथयुािन की े य भागशः | िवनाशः कु मुानां शपविण की ते | १७४ | श िनधनं चा धमराजाहारथात ्| गदायुं तु तुमुलमैव पिरकीिततम ्| १७५ | सरा तीथानां प ुयता पिरकीितता | १७५ | नवमं पव िनिदमेतदुतमथ वत ्| एकोनषिराया संािवशारदैः | १७६ | संाता बवृााः ोकां चा शते | ीिण ोकसहािण े शते िवंशितथा | १७७ | मुिनना संणीतािन कौरवाणां यशोभृताम ्| १७७ | अतः परं वािम सौिकं पव दाणम ्| भों य राजानं यधनममष णम ्| १७८ | पयातेष ु पाथष ु येऽाययू रथाः | कृ तवमा कृ पो ौिणः सायाे िधरोिताः | १७९ | ितजे ढोधो ौिणय महारथः | अहा सवपाालाृ ुप ुरोगमान ्| १८० | पाडवां सहामाा िवमोािम दंशनम ्| १८० | स ुाििश िवा ते प ुषष भाः | पाालापरीवारा ुिणप ुरोगमाः | १८१ | यामु पाथाे प कृ बलायात ्|
English: 1. "The chariots of the trees are part of the great destruction of the beings." 2. "The king of dharma, the destroyer of the enemy, is indeed a great tumult." 3. "The purity of the rivers is indeed well-known." 4. "The ninth is the best of the great ones, known by the wise." 5. "The wise ones speak of the great verses; the verses of the wise are indeed well-known." 6. "The fame of the Kauravas is indeed well-known." 7. "Thus, the great chariot of the king, who is the best among the rulers, is indeed a great treasure." 8. "The chariots of the great ones are indeed well-known in the paths." 9. "The great charioteer, who is the best among the warriors, is indeed a great hero." 10. "The great ones, who are indeed the best among the warriors, are known for their valor." 11. "The paths of the great ones are indeed well-known."

Sanskrit: ४२ पवसंहपव सािक महेासः शेषा िनधनं गताः | १८२ | ौपदी प ुशोकाता िपतृातृवधािदता | कृ तानशनसा य भतृ न ुपािवशत ्| १८३ | ौपदीवचना भीमो भीमपरामः | अधावत सो भाराजं ग ुरोः स ुतम ्| १८४ | भीमसेनभया दैवेनािभचोिदतः | अपाडवायेित षा ौिणरमवासृजत ्| १८५ | मैविमवीृ ः शमयं तचः | यामेण च तमयामास फा ुनः | १८६ | ौिणैपायनादीनां शापााोकािरताः | तोयकमिण सवषां राामुदकदािनके | १८७ | गूढो चाानं कण पृथयानः | स ुत ैतिदह ों दशमं पव सौिकम ्| १८८ | अादशािायाः पवयुा महाना | ोकाम किथतं शताौ तथ ैव च | १८९ | ोका सितः ोा यथावदिभसंया | सौिकैषीकसंबे पवयिमतब ुिना | १९० | अत ऊिमदं ाः ीपव कणोदयम ्| िवलापो वीरपीनां याितकणः ृतः | १९१ | ोधावेशः साद गाारीधृतरायोः | १९१ |
English: 42 The gathering of the winds The great sage, having reached the end, has gone to the treasure. | 182 | Draupadi, from the grief of her husband, is afflicted by the death of her father. | 183 | Draupadi's words, O Bhima, are exceedingly fierce. | 184 | Fearing Bhimasena, by divine command, she released the curse of the great sage. | 185 | May the great sage, with his calmness, bring peace to the troubled. | 186 | The curses of those like the sage and others are like water to all. | 187 | Hidden and unrecognized, the earth is scorched by the tenth wind. | 188 | The great wind, with its mighty roar, is like a hundred storms. | 189 | The wind, as it is, is like a great storm, and thus it is said. | 190 | Thus, the great wind, having risen, brings forth the dawn of heroes. | 191 | The rush of the wind is like the sound of the great charioteers. | 192 |

Sanskrit: अाय ००२ ४३ य ताियाूरािाानिनवितनः | प ुाातृितृ ं ैव दशुिन हताणे | १९२ | य राजा महााः सवधमभृतां वरः | राां तािन शरीरािण दाहयामास शातः | १९३ | एतदेकादशं ों पवाितकणं महत ्| सिवंशितरायाः पवयि ुदाताः | १९४ | ोकाः सशतं चा पसितते | संया भारताानं का  महाना | १९५ | णीतं सनमनोवैाुवतकम ्| १९५ | अतः परं शािपव ादशं ब ुिवधनम ्| य िनवदमापो धमराजो युिधिरः | १९६ | घातिया िपतृातृुांबिबावान ्| १९६ | शािपविण धमा ााताः शरतिकाः | राजिभविदता ये सयब ुभ ुुिभः | १९७ | आपमा तैव कालहेतुदशकाः | या ुा प ुषः सवमवा ुयात ्| १९८ | मोधमा किथता िविचा बिवराः | १९८ | ादशं पव िनिदमेताजनियम ्| पवय पिरेयमायानां शतयम ्| १९९ | िंश ैव तथााया नव च ैव तपोधनाः | १९९ |
English: 1. "The one who is not bound by the bonds of desire." 2. "The king, the great ruler, the best among those who bear the burden of the kingdom." 3. "This is the eleventh verse, a great declaration." 4. "Verses are indeed a hundred, spoken by the great sage Bharata." 5. "The mind is restrained by the practice of meditation." 6. "Thus, the great declaration of the supreme truth is made." 7. "The one who is a destroyer of the enemies, a protector of the weak." 8. "The declaration of the righteous is indeed a source of strength." 9. "The one who is not bound by time, the cause of all." 10. "The one who is wise, who knows the truth, is indeed liberated." 11. "The great declaration is made, the essence of the teachings of the sages." 12. "The wise ones, thus, are indeed the true ascetics."

Sanskrit: ४४ पवसंहपव ोकानां तु सहािण कीिततािन चतुदश | प च ैव शतााः पिवंशितसंया | २०० | अत ऊ तु िवेयमान ुशासनमुमम ्| य कृ ितमापः ुा धमिविनयम ्| २०१ | भीाागीरथीप ुाु राजो युिधिरः | २०१ | वहारोऽ कान धमाथयो िनदिशतः | िविवधानां च दानानां फलयोगाः पृथिवधाः | २०२ | तथा पािवशेषा दानानां च परो िविधः | आचारिविधयोग स च परा गितः | २०३ | एतुबवृामुमं चान ुशासनम ्| भीाैव संािः ग पिरकीितता | २०४ | एतयोदशं पव धमिनयकारकम ्| अायानां शतं चा षािरंशदेव च | २०५ | ोकानां तु सहािण ष ैव शतािन च | २०५ | ततोऽमेिधकं नाम पव ों चतुदशम ्| तंवतमीयं याानमन ुमम ्| २०६ | स ुवणकोशसंािज चों पिरितः | दधाािना पूव कृ ाीवनं प ुनः | २०७ | चयायां हयमुृं पाडवान ुगतः | त त च युािन राजप ुैरमष ण ैः | २०८ |
English: 44 Pavansamāhāpava Of the verses, the fourteenth is the one that is praised, And the hundredth is the one that is connected to the lineage. 200 Thus, the governing principle is to be understood, When the actions are performed according to the righteous law. 201 The Bhīṣma and the Ganges are the great rivers of the kings in battle. 201 The conduct of the world is directed by the righteous laws, And the results of various donations are different across the earth. 202 Thus, the special donations are of a different kind, And the rules of conduct are also of a higher order. 203 This is the great governing principle of the established rules, And the Bhīṣma is indeed the one who is well-known. 204 This is the twelfth of the Pavans, the one that is the cause of righteousness, And the hundred of the actions of the six divine beings. 205 Of the verses, the fourteenth and the hundredth are also included. 205 Then, the name of the great Pavan is the fourteenth, Which is the one that is to be understood. 206 He is the one who is connected to the golden treasury, And the one who is known for the great deeds of the past. 207 In the assembly, the horse is the one that is praised, And thus, the kings are to be honored with their actions. 208

Sanskrit: अाय ००२ ४५ िचादायाः प ुेण प ुिकाया धनयः | सामे ब ुवाहेन संशयं चा दिशतः | २०९ | अमेधे महाये नकु लाानमेव च | २०९ | इामेिधकं पव ोमेतहाुतम ्| अाायशतं िंशयोऽाया शिताः | २१० | ीिण ोकसहािण तावेव शतािन च | िवंशित तथा ोकाः संातादिशना | २११ | तत आमवासां पव पदशं ृतम ्| य रां पिर गाारीसिहतो नृपः | २१२ | धृतराामपदं िवर जगाम ह | २१२ | यं ा ितं साी पृथान ुययौ तदा | प ुरां पिर ग ुशुूषणे रता | २१३ | य राजा हता ुाौानां पािथ वान ्| लोकारगताीरानपय ुनरागतान ्| २१४ | ऋषेः सादाृ  ायमन ुमम ्| ा शोकं सदार िसिं परिमकां गतः | २१५ | य धम समाि िवरः स ुगितं गतः | सय महामाो िवााविणवशी | २१६ | ददश नारदं य धमराजो युिधिरः | नारदा ैव शुाव वृीनां कदनं महत ्| २१७ |
English: 1. "In the assembly of the wise, the wealth of the virtuous is established; doubts are dispelled by the great charioteer." (209) 2. "In the great sacrifice, only the unblemished are accepted." (209) 3. "The pure sacrifice is the most excellent offering; a hundred of such offerings are made with pure intent." (210) 4. "The sages, with their knowledge, have established a hundred families; thus, the lineage and the wise are connected." (211) 5. "Then, the wind carried the message to the king, who was in the forest, surrounded by deer." (212) 6. "Dhritarashtra, having reached the place of assembly, went forth." (212) 7. "When the sun set, the virtuous Pritha (Kunti) went to the assembly, engaged in the affairs of the king." (213) 8. "When the king was slain, the people, having lost their way, wandered in despair." (214) 9. "The sage's words, like the sun, dispelled the darkness; grief was removed, and joy was attained." (215) 10. "When the righteous king, Dhritarashtra, was in battle, he attained the highest bliss." (216) 11. "Narada saw the righteous king, Dhritarashtra, in the battlefield; Narada's presence was a great blessing." (217)

Sanskrit: ४६ पवसंहपव एतदामवासां पूवं स ुमहाुतम ्| िचािरंशदायाः पवतदिभसंया | २१८ | सहमेकं ोकानां प ोकशतािन च | षडेव च तथा ोकाः संातादिशना | २१९ | अतः परं िनबोधेदं मौसलं पव दाणम ्| य ते प ुषााः शशसहा युिध | २२० | दडिविनिाः समीपे लवणासः | २२० | आपान े पानगिलता दैवेनािभचोिदताः | एरकािपिभव ैिन ज ुिरतरेतरम ्| २२१ | य सवयं कृ ा तावुभौ रामके शवौ | नाितचमतुः कालं ां सवहरं समम ्| २२२ | नो ारवतीमे वृििवनाकृ ताम ्| याज ु ा िवषादमगमरां चाित नरष भः | २२३ | स सृ  यें मातुलं शौिरमानः | ददश यवीराणामापान े वैशसं महत ्| २२४ | शरीरं वास ुदेव राम च महानः | संारं लयामास वृीनां च धानतः | २२५ | स वृबालमादाय ारवातो जनम ्| ददशापिद कायां गाडीव पराभवम ्| २२६ | सवषां च ैव िदानामाणामसताम ्|
English: 46 Pavansamāhāpava With this, the great auspiciousness of the previous (sacrifice) is established. The essence of the divine light of the Pavitras is revealed. | 218 | The one who is united with the essence of the world, And the hundred essences of the world, Thus, six essences are described in the directions. | 219 | Therefore, one should understand this as the great divine offering, Where the pure ones are united with the great warriors. | 220 | In the vicinity of the divine, the salt is present. | 220 | In the Apāna, the drink is offered, By divine command, it is given. The essence of the divine is beyond the ordinary. | 221 | Where the self is made pure, both Rama and Shava, Time does not touch the one who is completely absorbed. | 222 | The one who is endowed with the divine qualities, Where the essence of sorrow is transformed into joy. | 223 | He, the one who is pure, the maternal uncle, Saw the great essence of the heroes in the offering. | 224 | The body is the abode of the divine, Rama and the great one, The essence of the world is absorbed in the great wealth. | 225 | He, taking the young one, Saw the great destruction in the body of the people. | 226 | In all, the essence of the divine is established.

Sanskrit: अाय ००२ ४७ नाशं वृिकलाणां भावानामिनताम ्| २२७ | ा िनवदमापो ासवाचोिदतः | धमराजं समासा संासं समरोचयेत ्| २२८ | इेतौसलं पव षोडशं पिरकीिततम ्| अायाौ समााताः ोकानां च शतयम ्| २२९ | महाािनकं ता सदशं ृतम ्| य रां पिर पाडवाः प ुषष भाः | २३० | ौपा सिहता देा िसिं परिमकां गताः | २३० | अाायायः ोाः ोकानां च शतं तथा | िवंशित तथा ोकाः संातादिशना | २३१ | गपव ततो ेयं िदं यदमान ुषम ्| अायाः प संाताः पवतदिभसंया | २३२ | ोकानां े शते च ैव संाते तपोधनाः | २३२ | अादशैवमेतािन पवायुाशेषतः | िखलेष ु हिरवंश भिव कीिततम ्| २३३ | एतदिखलमाातं भारतं पवसहात ्| अादश समाजमुरौिहयो युयुया | २३४ | तहाणं युमहाादशाभवत ्| २३४ | यो िवातुरो वेदााोपिनषदािजः | न चाानिमदं िवा ैव स ािचणः | २३५ |
English: 1. The destruction of the qualities of the unworthy. 2. The wise should illuminate the king of dharma with the light of knowledge. 3. This is the sixteen-fold description of the skillful. 4. The great sage, with his sixteen qualities, is praised by the wise. 5. The lion-like sages have gone to the abode of the wise. 6. The hundred qualities of the wise and the hundred of the lineage are also described. 7. The wise, who are endowed with the qualities of the wise, are indeed the best. 8. The hundred qualities of the wise are indeed the best among the wise. 9. Thus, these are the qualities of the wise, remaining after the destruction of the unworthy. 10. This entire land of Bharat is filled with the qualities of the wise. 11. Thus, the great assembly of the wise is established. 12. The one who knows the Vedas and the Upanishads is indeed wise, and he does not know the unworthy.

Sanskrit: ४८ पवसंहपव ुा िदमुपाानं ाम रोचते | ंोिकलतं ुा ा ा वािगव | २३६ | प ु इितहासोमादााये किवब ुयः | प इव भूतेो लोकसंिवधययः | २३७ | अाान िवषये प ुराणं वतते िजाः | अिर िवषये जा इव चतुिवधाः | २३८ | ियाग ुणानां सवषािमदमाानमायः | इियाणां समानां िचा इव मनःियाः | २३९ | अनाि ैतदाानं कथा भ ुिव न िवते | आहारमनपाि शरीरेव धारणम ्| २४० | इदं सवः किववरैराानमुपजीते | उदयेुिभभृ  ैरिभजात इवेरः | २४१ | ैपायनौप ुटिनःसृतममेयं ; प ुयं पिवमथ पापहरं िशवं च | यो भारतं समिधगित वामानं; िकं त प ुरजलैरिभषेचनेन | २४२ | आानं तिददमन ुमं महाथ ; िवं महिदह पवसहेण | ुादौ भवित नृणां स ुखावगाहं ; िवीण लवणजलं यथा वेन | २४३ |
English: 48 The essence of the wind The sound of the flute delights the mind; The flute, when played, brings forth the essence of speech. 236 Thus, the history of the world is narrated; As if it were a story of the past, it binds the people. 237 In the matter of the ancient texts, the Puranas are said to be eternal; In the matter of the eternal, the Vedas are like the fourfold path. 238 The qualities of sacrifice are the essence of all beings; The mind is like the essence of the gathered thoughts. 239 Thus, the story of the eternal is not to be neglected; Food and sustenance are indeed the support of the body. 240 This is all that is offered to the wise; The rising sun is like the one who bears the burden of the world. 241 The two who are wise, the one who is pure; This is the one who drinks the nectar that removes sin and is Shiva. Whoever offers the sacred fire to Bharat, what is that? It is the sprinkling of water from the sacred pot. 242 The essence of the eternal is the great truth; The great fire is the essence of the wind. In the flute, there is the happiness of men; Like the saltwater, it is indeed a source of joy. 243
