Sanskrit: पौपव ४९ पौपव अाय ००३ सूत उवाच | जनमेजयः पािरितः सह ातृिभः कु ेेदीघसमुपाे| त ातरयः ुतसेन उसेनो भीमसेन इित | ००१ | तेष ुतमुपासीन ेष ुत ाागारमेयः | स जनमेजय ातृिभरिभहतो रोयमाणो मातुः समीपमुपागत ्| ००२ | तं माता रोयमाणमुवाच | िकं रोिदिष | के नािभहत इित | ००३ | स एवमुो मातरं  ुवाच | जनमेजय ातृिभरिभहतोऽीित | ००४ | तं माता  ुवाच | ं या तापरां येनािभहत इित | ००५ | स तां प ुनवाच | नापराािम िकित ्| नावेे हविष नाविलह इित | ००६ | तुा त माता सरमा प ुशोकाता तमुपाग स जनमेजयः सह ातृिभदघसमुपाे | ००७ | स तया ुया तोः | अयं मे प ुो न िकिदपराित | िकमथ मिभहत इित | याायमिभहतोऽनपकारी तादं ां भयमागिमतीित | ००८ | स जनमेजय एवमुो देवशुा सरमया ढं संाो िवषणासीत ्| ००९ | स तिेसमाेहािनप ुरं े प ुरोिहतमन ुपमिमानः परं यमकरोो मेपापकृ ां शमयेिदित | ०१० | स कदािचृगयां यातः पािरितो जनमेजयः किंििवषयोेशे आममपयत ्| ०११ | त कििषरासां चे ुतवा नाम | तािभमतः प ु आे सोमवा नाम | ०१२ | त तं प ुमिभग जनमेजयः पािरितः पौरोिहाय वे | ०१३ | स नमृ  तमृिषमुवाच | भगवयं तव प ुो मम प ुरोिहतोऽिित | ०१४ | स एवमुः  ुवाच | भो जनमेजय प ुोऽयं मम सा जातः | महातपी ाायसंपो मपोवीयसंभृतो मं पीतवााः कु ौ संवृः | समथऽयं भवतः सवाः पापकृ ाः शमियतुमरेण महादेवकृ ाम ्| अ ेकमुपांशुतम ्| यदेनंकिाणः किदथ मिभयाचें त ै दादयम ्| येतहसे ततो नयैनिमित | ०१५ | तेन ैवमुो जनमेजयं  ुवाच | भगवंथा भिवतीित | ०१६ | स तं प ुरोिहतमुपादायोपावृो ातृन ुवाच | मयायं वृत उपाायः
English: **Pauṇḍavā** 49 **Pauṇḍavā** **Ānāya 003** Sūta said: Janamejaya, surrounded by his brothers, approached the sage. The brothers were Ṛṣabha, Ṛṣabha, and Bhīma. 001. They were seated in meditation, and Janamejaya, distressed by the loss of his mother, went to her. 002. The mother, seeing him distressed, spoke: "Why are you crying? Who has caused you pain?" 003. He, thus addressed, spoke to his mother: "I am distressed by the loss of my brothers." 004. The mother replied: "What is the reason for your distress? Who has caused you pain?" 005. He then spoke to her: "I do not know what to do; I am unable to bear it." 006. Thus, the mother, named Śarmā, approached Janamejaya, who was accompanied by his brothers. 007. She, with great affection, said: "This is my son; he has not done anything wrong. What has caused you pain?" 008. Janamejaya, thus addressed, became calm and said: "I have been afflicted by the curse of the sage." 009. He, in that state, was not able to speak; he was overwhelmed by grief. 010. Once, while hunting, Janamejaya, surrounded by his brothers, became lost in the forest. 011. There, he encountered a sage named Ṛṣabha. 012. He then, with great respect, approached the sage. 013. He bowed down and spoke: "O revered one, your son is my brother." 014. Thus addressed, the sage replied: "O Janamejaya, this son of mine has been born from great penance, and he is endowed with divine qualities. May he relieve you of your afflictions." 015. Thus, Janamejaya spoke to the sage: "O revered one, I am afraid." 016. He then took the sage's hand and spoke to his brothers: "Let us proceed."

English: 50 Pauṇḍapadma 1. This is like a great river flowing. 017. By this, the divine being is established. 2. Thus, he spoke. He then established the divine being in the land. 018. This great river is called the river of the divine. 3. The divine beings became like the great river. 019. He established a single divine being. 4. The great river is bound. 020. By this means, he did not perish. 021. 5. The divine being, having established the great river, is now bound. 022. He then entered the great river. 6. He lay down in the water. 023. Then, at some time, the divine being, having established the great river, 024. went away. 7. They spoke. The divine being, having bound the great river, 025. thus spoke. 8. "This is the great river where he is." 026. He then spoke to them for the purpose of knowledge. 9. "O divine being, what shall I do?" 027. He, having spoken, went to the great river. 10. Thus, he went to the land. 031. Then, another divine being, like the great river, 032. established himself. 11. He spoke to the great river. 033. He, having spoken, said, "O great river, 12. what shall I do?" 034. He spoke to him. "O great river, what is your nature?" 035. 13. He spoke to the great river. "I shall not use your nature." 037. 14. Thus, he spoke again. "I shall not use your nature." 038. 15. The divine being then spoke. "O great river, I shall go to the land." 039. 16. Thus, he spoke to the divine being. "I shall go to the land."

English: 003 51 | Thus, he said, "I will take the milk." | 040 | The teacher spoke, "This is not the milk of the cow." | The teacher, being present, said, "Let there be no obstruction to the milk of all." | 041 | He then spoke to the teacher, "I will take the milk." | 042 | The teacher, being present, said, "I will take the milk." | "I am not a thief." | "I will take the milk." | 043 | He spoke to the teacher, "O, I will take the milk of these cows." | 044 | The teacher spoke, "This milk is not suitable." | 045 | Thus, he said, "The teacher, being present, said, 'Let there be no obstruction to the milk of all.'" | 046 | The teacher then said, "I am not a thief." | "I will not drink the milk." | 047 | He then spoke to the teacher, "O, I will drink this milk that is from the mothers." | 048 | The teacher spoke, "These fruits are the best among the fruits." | "Thus, let there be no obstruction to the milk of the fruits." | 049 | Thus, he said, "The teacher, being present, said, 'Let there be no obstruction to the milk of the fruits.'" | 050 | He, at some time, was in the presence of the teacher. | 051 | He was then in the presence of the teacher, and he was struck by the teacher. | He fell down. | 052 | Then, the teacher spoke, "I am like the snake." | "I am indeed the teacher." | 053 | Thus, he said, "O teacher, I am like the teacher." | 054 | Then, the teacher spoke, "O, I am like the snake." | 055 | The teacher spoke, "How am I like the snake?" | 056 | He then spoke to him, "I am indeed a teacher." | "Thus, I am like the snake." | 057 | The teacher spoke, "I am indeed a teacher." | "Thus, I am like the snake." | 058 | Thus, he spoke to the teacher, "O teacher, I am like the teacher." | 059 | | The sun rises in the east; it shines brightly. | The moon shines at night; it is beautiful. | The stars are numerous in the sky; they are shining. | The earth is filled with beings; it is full of life. | 060 |

Sanskrit: ५२ पौपव िहरमयौ शकु नी सांपरायौ ; नासदौ स ुनसौ वैजयौ | शुं वयौ तरसा स ुवेमा ;विभ याविसतं िववत ्| ०६१ | ां स ुपण बलेन वितका ;ममुतामिनौ सौभगाय | तावुवृावनम मायया ; समा गा अणा उदावहन ्| ०६२ | षि गाविशता धेनव ; एकं वं स ुवते तं हि | नानागोा िविहता एकदोहना ;ाविनौ हतो घममुम ्| ०६३ | एकां नािभं सशता अराः िताः ; िधा िवंशितरिप ता अराः | अन ेिम चं पिरवततेऽजरं ; मायािनौ समनि चष णी | ०६४ | एकं चं वतते ादशारं िध ;षणािभमेकाममृत धारणम ्| यिेवा अिध िवे िवषा ;ाविनौ मुतो मा िवषीदतम ्| ०६५ | अिनािवममृतं वृभूयौ ; ितरोधामिनौ दासपी | िभा िगिरमिनौ गामुदाचरौ ; तृमा िथता वल | ०६६ | युवां िदशो जनयथो दशाे; समानं मूि रथया िवयि | तासां यातमृषयोऽन ुयाि ; देवा मन ुाः िितमाचरि | ०६७ | युवां वणािकु थो िवपां ;ेऽिधियि भ ुवनािन िवा | ते भानवोऽन ुसृतारि ; देवा मन ुाः िितमाचरि | ०६८ | तौ नासाविनावामहे वां ; जं च यां िबभृथः प ुर | तौ नासावमृतावृतावृधा ;वृते देवापदेन सूते | ०६९ | मुखेन गभ लभतां युवानौ ; गतास ुरेतपदेन सूते | सो जातो मातरमि गभ;ाविनौ मुथो जीवसे गाः | ०७० |
English: 52 The son of the plant; The two of them, like the sun and moon; Not born of the unworthy, but of the worthy, the victorious. Pure, they are born swiftly; The manifestation of the universe is revealed. With the strength of the sun, the moon is adorned; I am blessed with auspiciousness. The two of them, with the power of illusion; The auspicious one rises, the moon. The cowherd, with the strength of the herd; One calf is born, that is the one. Various cows are milked, one milker; The one who is skilled is the one who milks. One who is born, the unworthy are cast away; The one who is skilled is the one who is born. The one who is born is eternal; In the illusion, the one who is skilled is the seer. One who is born is the one who holds the essence; The one who is skilled is the one who holds immortality. If the one who is skilled is born, do not be distressed; The one who is skilled is the one who does not grieve. The one who is skilled in the essence of immortality; The one who is skilled is the servant of the divine. The one who is skilled is the one who speaks; The one who is skilled is the one who is established. You two, generate the directions; The same charioteer drives the chariot. The sages travel in the same direction; The gods, with their minds, act in accordance. You two, with the strength of the sun; In the same way, the worlds are created. They are born from the sun; The gods, with their minds, act in accordance. Thus, the unworthy are not born; The one who is born is the one who is worthy. Thus, the unworthy are born, and the worthy are nourished; The gods give birth through the essence of the divine. With the mouth, let the young ones be born; The one who has gone is born through the essence of the divine. The one who is born is the mother of the young; The one who is skilled is the one who lives.

Sanskrit: अाय ००३ ५३ एवं तेनािभुताविनावाजमतुः | आहतु ैनम ्| ीतौ ः | एष तेऽपूपः | अशान ैनिमित | ०७१ | स एवमुः  ुवाच | नानृतमूचतुभवौ | न हमेतमपूपमुपयोु मुहे अिनवे ग ुरव इित | ०७२ | ततमिनावूचतुः | आवाां प ुरावत उपाायेन ैवमेवािभुताामपूपः ीताां दः | उपयु स तेनािनवे ग ुरवे | मिप तथ ैव कु  यथा कृ तमुपाायेन ेित | ०७३ | स एवमुः प ुनरेव  ुवाच ैतौ | न ुनये भवाविनौ | नोहेऽहमिनवेोपाायायोपयोु िमित | ०७४ | तमिनावाहतुः | ीतौ वानया ग ुवृा | उपााय ते काायसा दाः | भवतो िहरमया भिवि | चुां भिविस | ेयावासीित | ०७५ | स एवमुोऽिां लचुपाायसकाशमागोपाायमिभवााचचे | स चा ीितमानभूत ्| ०७६ | आह च ैनम ्| यथािनावाहतुथा ं ेयोऽवासीित | सव च ते वेदाः ितभाीित | ०७७ | एषा तािप परीोपमोः | ०७८ | अथापरः िश ैवायोद धौ वेदो नाम | ०७९ | तमुपाायः संिददेश |
English: "Thus, by that which is spoken, the sound of the mother is struck. In the cold, there is a sound. This is your offering. It is the cause of hunger. Thus, he spoke again: He did not speak falsely. I do not use this offering, O great one, for the sake of the heavy burden. Then, they spoke: The offering is indeed made by the one who is struck, And the offering is made by the one who is heavy. Thus, it is done as it has been done. He spoke again, the great one: The offering is not to be made by the one who is heavy. To him who is struck, The sound is made by the one who is heavy. What is the offering to you, O great one? Your fear is made of the fear of the great. The fear of the great is made. Thus, he spoke: The offering is indeed made by the one who is heavy. And he is indeed the one who is made. Thus, it is done. As the one who is struck, so is the sound made. All the Vedas are made by the one who is heavy. This is indeed a comparison of the two. Then, the other is the Veda named 'the one who is heavy.' This offering is a command."

English: 54 Pauṇḍav The one who is endowed with the qualities of restraint, coolness, and gentleness, is a true sage. The Vedas are indeed here. By you, the house is made pure with the one who is being worshipped. The worship is performed with reverence. 080 Thus, he who is endowed with long-lasting qualities remained in the house. The great one, after a long time, attained satisfaction. Satisfaction is indeed the essence of all. 081 This is the true knowledge of the Vedas. 082 He, by means of the right approach, was engaged in the house of the sage. Thus, the sages who resided in the house became renowned. 083 The sage spoke thus: What is the use of the house if it is not adorned? Let the one who is adorned be connected with the sage. Then, at some time, Janamejaya, the son of Paṇḍu, performed a sacrifice with the right approach. 085 At some time, he, having been instructed by the sage, named the sage Uḍḍhā. "O Uḍḍhā, if you are not engaged in the house, then you are indeed not engaged." 086 Thus, the Vedas went to the abode of the sage. 087 Then, Uḍḍhā, adorned with the qualities of the sage, was indeed engaged in the right approach. The one who is engaged in the right approach is indeed wise. As the seasons change, so let it be. 089 Thus, the sage spoke: "Not by my words is the body made. I am not engaged by the right approach. The body is indeed made by the essence of the body." 090 Then, he, having gone to the house of the sage, returned from the abode. The one who is endowed with qualities resides in the house. 088 Not to be neglected. 084

Sanskrit: ५६ पौपव ग पौं राजानम ्| िभ त ियया िपने कु डले | ते आनय | इततुथऽहिन प ुयकं भिवता | ताामाबाां ाणािरवेुिमािम | शोभमाना यथा ताां कु डलाां तिहिन संपादय | ेयो िह ते ाणं कु वत इित | १०० | स एवमु उपाािया ािततोः | स पिथ गपयषभमितमाणं तमिधढं च प ुषमितमाणमेव | १०१ | स प ुष उमभाषत | उैत ुरीषम ऋषभ भयेित | १०२ | स एवमुो न ैत ्| १०३ | तमाह प ुषो भूयः | भयो | मा िवचारय | उपाायेनािप ते भितं पूविमित | १०४ | स एवमुो बाढिम ुा तदा तषभ प ुरीषं मूं च भियोः ते य स ियः पौः | १०५ | तमुपेापय आसीनम ्| स तमुपेाशीिभरिभनोवाच | अथ भवमुपगतोऽीित | १०६ | स एनमिभवाोवाच | भगवौः खहम ्| िकं करवाणीित | १०७ | तमुवाचोः | ग ुवथ कु डलाामागतोऽीित येतेियया िपने कु डले तेभवाातुमहतीित | १०८ | तं पौः  ुवाच | िवयाःप ुरं िया यातािमित | १०९ | स तेन ैवमुः िवयाःप ुरं ियां नापयत ्| ११० |
English: 56 Pauṇḍav The king said: "Bring the Pauṇḍava! Let him be brought with great honor! He is worthy of respect. Let him be brought! Thus, let the Pauṇḍava be honored. As he is honored, let him be adorned with garlands. Let him be made to shine like a garland of flowers. Indeed, he is the one who is worthy of respect." 100 Thus, he is honored with great respect. He is indeed the one who is worthy of respect. 101 He speaks with great eloquence. He speaks with the eloquence of a sage. 102 Thus, he is indeed worthy of respect. 103 The king said: "Let the worthy one speak." "Do not think ill of him. By the means of respect, he is indeed worthy of honor." 104 Thus, he is indeed the one who is worthy of respect, and he is the one who speaks with great eloquence. 105 He was seated in a respectful manner. He spoke to him with great respect. Then he said: "O revered one, I have come to you." 106 He spoke to him with great respect: "O revered one, what should I do?" 107 He replied: "Let the worthy one be honored with great respect, and let him be adorned with garlands of flowers." 108 The Pauṇḍava said: "With great respect, let the worthy one be honored." 109 Thus, he did not speak with disrespect towards the worthy one. 110

Sanskrit: अाय ००३ ५७ स पौं प ुनवाच | न युं भवता वयमनृतेनोपचिरतुम ्| न िह ते ियाःप ुरे संिनिहता | न ैनां पयामीित | १११ | स एवमुः पौं  ुवाच | संित भवान ुिः | र तावत ्| न िह सा िया उिेनाशुिचना वा शा ुम ्| पितताादेषा नाशुचेदशनमुप ैतीित | ११२ | अथ ैवमु उः ृोवाच | अि ख मयोिेनोपृं शीं गता चेित | ११३ | तं पौः  ुवाच | एतदेवं िह | न गतोपृं भवित न ितेन ेित | ११४ | अथोथे ुा ा ुख उपिवय स ुािलतपािणपादवदनोऽशािभर ् दयमािभरिपृय िः पीा िः पिरमृ खािपृयाःप ुरं िवय तां ियामपयत ्| ११५ | सा च ैवोमुायािभवाोवाच | ागतं ते भगवन ्| आापय िकं करवाणीित | ११६ | स तामुवाच | एते कु डले ग ुवथ मे िभिते दातुमहसीित | ११७ | सा ीता तेन त सावेन पामयमनितमणीयेित मा ते कु डले अवमुा ै ायत ्| ११८ | आह च ैनम ्| एते कु डले तको नागराजः ाथ यित | अमो नेतुमहसीित | ११९ | स एवमुां ियां  ुवाच | भवित स ुिनवृ ता भव | न मां शको नागराजो धष ियतुिमित | १२० |
English: 003 57 He spoke thus: "Do not be entangled in falsehood. Indeed, you are not bound by the truth. I do not perceive you as being bound." 111 Thus he spoke again: "Your nature is indeed pure. As long as it is so, the truth does not become impure by any means." The father does not become impure by the son. 112 Then, indeed, he spoke: "Even if I am bound by the truth, I will not be affected." 113 The sage spoke: "Thus it is indeed. You will not be affected by the truth." 114 Then, the sage, with a serene countenance, spoke with a gentle voice: "With a pure heart, the truth is indeed pure. The one who is pure will not be affected by the truth." 115 And she, indeed, spoke: "Welcome, O Lord! What should I do?" 116 He replied: "These jewels are to be given to me." 117 She, pleased by this, with a joyful heart, said: "These jewels are indeed yours." 118 And she said: "These jewels belong to the king of serpents. I will not give them." 119 Thus he spoke: "May you be free from all entanglements. Let not the king of serpents harm me." 120

Sanskrit: अाय ००३ ५९ िवपरीतमेतभयं िय ; वाावनीती दयं तीधारम ्| १३२ | म ्| इित | तदेवं गते न शोऽहं तीदयां शापमथा कतु गतािमित | १३३ | तमुः  ुवाच | भवताहमाशुिचभावमागम न ुनीतः | ा तेऽिभिहतम ्| यादमं षयिस तादनपो भिवसीित | े चाे न ैष मम शापो भिवतीित | १३४ | साधयामाविद ुा ािततोे कु डले गृहीा | १३५ | सोऽपयिथ नं मणमागं मुमु अथोे कु डले भूमौ िनिोदकाथ चमे | १३६ | एतिरे स मणरमाण उपसृ ते कु डले गृहीा ावत ्| तमुोऽिभसृ जाह | स तू पं िवहाय तकपं कृ ा सहसा धरयां िववृतं महािबलं िववेश | १३७ | िवय च नागलोकं भवनमगत ्| तमुोऽािववेश तेन ैव िबलेन | िवय च नागानुवदेिभः ोकैः | १३८ | यमानमयमानं च | य ऐरावतराजानः सपाः सिमितशोभनाः | वष  इव जीमूताः सिव ुवनेिरताः | १३९ | स ुपा िवपा तथा काषकु डलाः | आिदवाकपृे रेज ुरैरावतोवाः | १४० | बिन नागवािन गायाीर उरे | इेोऽकाशुसेनायां चतु मैरावतं िवना | १४१ | शताशीितरौ च सहािण च िवंशितः |
English: "Unfathomable 003 59 The fear of the opposite is the essence of the path; the path of speech is the essence of the heart. 132 Thus it is! Therefore, having gone thus, I do not know the heart of the curse, how it has come to be. 133 The great one spoke: You are indeed the one who has come with the essence of purity; the essence of the heart is spoken to you. As long as the curse does not arise, it will not be my curse. 134 I will accomplish the task; the essence of the heart is taken in the pot. 135 He also, having taken the gem, is in the pot, and in the pot, the water of the earth is stirred. 136 Thus, the gem is taken in the pot, and the essence of the heart is established. The great one spoke thus: He, having abandoned the form, suddenly entered the great strength. 137 He entered the serpent world, having become the great one. The great one entered with that strength. 138 The one who is both the essence and the essence of the essence. The king of the Airavata, surrounded by the beautiful ones, is like the clouds in the sky. 139 He is the one who is both the great and the small, as well as the black pot. In the essence of the great, the Airavata shines. 140 The great serpent, the one who is the great one, is without the Airavata. 141 The hundred-headed one and the companions are indeed the ones who are born."

Sanskrit: ६० पौपव सपाणां हा याि धृतराो यदेजित | १४२ | ये च ैनमुपसप ि ये च रं परं गताः | अहमैरावतेातृोऽकरवं नमः | १४३ | य वासः कु ेे खाडवे चाभवदा | तं कावेयमौषं कु डलाथाय तकम ्| १४४ | तकासेन िनं सहचरावुभौ | कु ेे िनवसतां नदीिमुमतीमन ु | १४५ | जघजक ुतसेन ेित यः ुतः | अवसो मह ुि ाथ यागमुताम ्| १४६ | करवािण सदा चाहं नम ै महान े | १४६ | एवं  ुविप नागादा ते कु डले नालभदथापयियौ ते अिधरो पटं वयौ | १४७ | तिं ते कृ ाः िसता तवः | चं चापयिः कु मारैः पिरव मानम ्| प ुषं चापयशनीयम ्| १४८ | स तावा ुाव एिभमवादोकैः | १४९ | ीयिप ता शतािन मे; षि िनं चरित ुवेऽिन ्| चे चतुिवशितपवयोगे; षु माराः पिरवतयि | १५० | तं चेदं िवपं युवौ ; वयतूततं वतयौ | कृ ाितां ैव िववतयौ ; भूताजं भ ुवनािन च ैव | १५१ | व भता भ ुवन गोा ; वृ हा नमुचेिन हा | कृ े वसानो वसन े महाा ; सानृते यो िविवनि लोके | १५२ |
English: 60 Pauṇḍav The one who was conquered by Dhṛtarāṣhṭra, the son of the Sāpaṇas. 142 And those who approach him, and those who have gone to the supreme realm, I bow to the one who is on Airāvata. 143 Wherever the abode is, in the Kachchha, That is the place of the great sage, the one who is the master of the Kachchha. 144 With the two companions, the one who is with the Kachchha, In the river Nīmutī, they reside. 145 The one who is known as Jaghanyajñā, He who is the great sage, is the one who is the master of the great path. 146 I always wish to serve the great sage. 146 Thus, the Nāgas, having been instructed, In the Kachchha, they do not abandon the path of the great sage. 147 Thus, you should perform your duties; The bow and the arrows, the great weapons, The one who is a man should be skilled in archery. 148 He who is a great warrior should be known by the wise. 149 The one who is skilled in archery, With hundreds of arrows; The one who is skilled in the art of archery, In the twenty-fourth chapter of the great epic. 150 If this is the great bow, Then the one who is skilled in archery is the one who is worthy. The one who is skilled in archery is the one who is worthy; The beings of the world are also worthy. 151 The one who is a great sage, In the world of the cows; The one who is a great sage, He who is the master of the great path. 152

English: "0.003 61 He who rides the great elephant; the vehicle of the divine being. Salutations always to the Lord of the Universe; to the Lord of the worlds, the great Purandara. 153 Then he, the man, spoke. I am cold; I have come with a desire. What do you wish to do? 154 He said to him, The serpents have come under my control. 155 Then he, the man, spoke again, This is the essence of the teachings. 156 He spoke the essence of the teachings. Thus, having been instructed, the great sage, with a pure mind, spoke. 157 The world of the sages is purified. 158 Then the sage, with a radiant form, suddenly spoke to the assembled beings, These are the great beings who have come here. 159 He was then addressed by the great beings. The great beings have come here to fulfill their purpose. I have come here for a reason. How can I not consider this? 160 Then he, with a pure mind, spoke to him, O great one, this is the essence of the teachings. This is the great deity who fulfills the purpose of the teachings. 161 Thus, he went to the great essence of the teachings. The purpose of the teachings is to establish the mind. 162 Then the great one, with a pure mind, began to speak the teachings. They are indeed great beings. 163 And she spoke to him."

English: 62 Pauṇḍav In that country, at that time, he arrived. Your arrival is known. I am not at fault. Even the best of the best. The great sage is here. 164 Then he began to speak about the means. That means he said. Your arrival is known. How long has it been since you were created? 165 He spoke that means. O great one, by the king of serpents, the creation was done. Thus, he was taken to the serpent world. 166 And I, with great effort, have brought you here. What is that? 167 And I also have brought the great sage. The young ones are in the mountain. What is that? 168 I have brought the sage. Who is that sage? 169 The one who is not to be neglected. Who is he? 170 The one who is revered by me, the sage. He is also a great one. Thus, with offerings, The revered sage is honored. By means of offerings, you are also honored. What is that which is to be honored by the sage? What is that which is to be honored by you? 171 Thus, the means spoke. Those who are the creators and the ordainers.

English: 003 63 Those who are righteous, they are the rulers of the earth. 172 If the twelve months are completed, then the seasons will be established. That man is a true sage. He who is, he is indeed. 173 That great bull, the king of serpents, is Airavata. He who is firmly established is he. If you are afraid of the bull, then that is nectar. 174 Thus, the king does not abandon the abode of the righteous. He is also my friend. 175 Then, having been seized by the great serpent, he returns. Let him go. Do not allow it. He is indeed a great sage. 176 He, the great sage, is the one who is not to be disturbed. The king has gathered the people, Janamejaya. 178 The ancient one, having been freed from the bondage of ignorance, is the one who is truly wise. 179 Thus, the victorious one, as it is said, spoke to him with words of wisdom at the right time. 180 In the assembly of the wise, the king spoke: "Let the king be honored, for he is the protector of the people." 181 Thus, the king spoke to the sage, Janamejaya, with great respect, addressed him. 182

English: 64 The guardian of the plants; by their care, the lowly are nurtured. What is the use of a king who does not protect the weak? The wise speak of the king's duty; the virtuous are honored. Thus, the king, with a mind of wisdom; the wise one, having performed his duty, spoke to the king, who was distressed; "Only this body is yours, O king." Those who are not kings, by whom the father is indeed protected; the wise are like the sun, illuminating the world. I am the one who knows the time of death; the great one, having taken the path of righteousness. Thus, the one who is guilty is like a snake; the one who has committed a sin is like a heavy burden. The strong, having taken the path of righteousness, is not without a body; he who is more than ten times your worth. The king, of the lineage of kings, is indeed a protector; he who has killed the wicked is a destroyer of sin. The great sin is indeed destroyed by the one who is righteous; the great king is indeed honored in the world. Thus, having gone to the king, I have been honored; my wish is that the great king is indeed honored. O protector of the earth, by whom I am honored; the great king, having performed his duty, walks without sin. Thus, the king is indeed angry.

English: "0.005 67 Thus, the great lineage of the family is praised. Tell me this story, O sage, of your great glory. 0.003 Soot spoke: What was learned in the ancient texts by the great sage Vaishampayana, is indeed told in the ancient lore. 0.004 What I have learned, O sage, is that the divine beings are indeed the ones who are the bestowers of knowledge. 0.005 The lineage of the revered Bhṛgus is indeed glorious. 0.005 This great lineage, O great sage, I shall narrate, connected with the ancient stories. 0.006 From Bhṛgu, the son of the sage, is the name of the divine being, the heir of the great sage, endowed with wisdom. 0.007 The great sage, the son of the sage, is indeed the one who is the bestower of knowledge. 0.007 The son of the sage, who is learned in the Vedas, is indeed the great sage of your family. 0.008 And the one who is both glorious and famous, is indeed the one who is wise and disciplined. 0.009 Shaunaka spoke: O Soot, as the great sage of the family, the lineage of the divine beings is indeed praised. 0.010"

English: **Pauḷomapaṇa** 68 Soot said: By the grace of Bhṛgu's mother, who is endowed with the qualities of Pauḷoma, Bhṛgu was born as a great sage. 011 When the time was right, Bhṛgu, who is of good character, was born in Pauḷoma. 012 For the purpose of anointing, Bhṛgu, the best among those who bear the dharma, then went to Pauḷoma. 013 He, endowed with the qualities of wisdom, was born as Bhṛgu, and with great effort, he was made to shine. 014 However, when Pauḷoma was born, the great sage was also born. At that time, he was nourished by fruits and roots. 015 Then, with great effort, he was made to shine, and he was born as Bhṛgu, who was endowed with wisdom. 016 Then, in the refuge of the sacred fire, the one who is the knower of all was born. 017 Tell me, O sage, what is the truth? Without it, indeed, I cannot speak. 018 I have indeed come here, having been born of the mother of the great sage, to speak the truth. 019 This one, if she is the daughter of Bhṛgu, is indeed hidden.

Sanskrit: अाय ००६ ६९ तथा सं समाािह िजहीषाामािदमाम ्| ०२० | म ुिह दयं मेऽ दहिव ितित | म ुवभाया यिदमां भृग ुः ाप स ुममाम ्| ०२१ | त एवमाम िलतं जातवेदसम ्| शमानो भृगोभाया प ुनः प ुनरपृत | ०२२ | मे सवभूतानामरिस िनदा | सािव ुयपापेष ु सं ूिह कवे वचः | ०२३ | मूवभायापता भृग ुणानृतकािरणा | सेयं यिद तथा मे ं समाातुमहिस | ०२४ | ुा ो भृगोभाया हिराहमामात ्| जातवेदः पयते वद सां िगरं मम | ०२५ | त तचनं ुा सािचःिखतो भृशम ्| भीतोऽनृता शापा भृगोिरवीन ैः | ०२६ | अाय ००६ सूत उवाच | अेरथ वचः ुा तः जहार ताम ्| राहपेण मनोमातरंहसा | ००१ | ततः स गभ िनवसु ौ भृग ुकु लोह |
English: 1. Thus, the one who is to be worshipped, the one who is to be desired, is the great one. 2. My heart is filled with joy; may the one who is the son of Bhrigu grant me happiness. 3. Thus, having been born, the one who knows all, may he again and again be invoked. 4. In the midst of all beings, the one who is the essence of all, may the poet's words be fulfilled. 5. The son of Bhrigu, who is the embodiment of truth, may this be my prayer to him. 6. The one who is the son of Bhrigu, may he speak my words in the assembly. 7. Thus, the one who is the son of Bhrigu, having been greatly frightened, is indeed very much afraid. 8. The sage spoke: "O son of Bhrigu, may your words be fulfilled in the assembly." 9. Then he, the great one, dwelled in the abode of Bhrigu.

English: 70 Pauḷomapa In anger, he became a great serpent. 002 That one, having taken the form of a mother, fell down, shining like a great jewel. 003 She, taking him, the beautiful one, went to the abode of Bhṛgu. 004 Seeing her, the lord of all worlds, the great father, was filled with joy. 005 She became the blessed one, the great father of the world. 005 The great river, flowing with great force, is the source of Bhṛgu's fame. 006 That river, having flowed, became the great one, then at that time. 007 The lord of the world, having taken the form of a bride, is the one who shines. 007 Thus, the abode of Bhṛgu became the source of great heat. 008 He saw the father, and the abode, and also the shining one. 008 That Pauḷomā, then, the sister of Bhṛgu, was not known to anyone. 009 Indeed, the wise do not know the one who is bound by illusion. 009 In this way, she, the great one, having taken the form of a serpent, was cursed. 010 Who does not know the one who is cursed by the great curse? 010

What is this audacity that you have shown?" 001 "While the righteous are speaking, who among them is my equal?" 002 "Indeed, he who knows the truth and speaks otherwise, is a fool; he is indeed a wretched one among men." 003 "Those who, knowing the truth, do not speak, are indeed the most wretched."

The deities and the fathers are satisfied by that. 007 The waters, the divine beings, all the waters, With the fathers, during the full moon of the month. 008 The deities and the fathers, The deities are indeed united, In the offerings, both on earth and in the sky. 009 The deities and the fathers are indeed connected; When they are united, I am indeed the face. 010 The fathers of the new moon and the deities of the full moon, By the face, they indeed dwell in the sky. 011 How can I, who am all-pervading, Be afraid of them? 011 Then, the one who is deluded, I know indeed the deluded ones, And those who are in the state of confusion. 012 The beings who are without protection, Are indeed distinguished by their actions; The ones who are without protection are indeed written. 013

English: "Thus, the gods, having gathered together, are the protectors of the worlds. The unblemished ones are the inhabitants of the worlds. As the various paths are not obstructed, Thus, the gods, having approached the divine knowledge, The great sage Bhrigu, indeed, is the cause of this. How can the divine face be without a portion? In the world of the great, all beings are connected. But, having spoken the words of the creator of beings, Among all beings, who is the one that sustains the worlds? Thus, in the world, as the sun does not set, When the deluded one, having consumed the essence, Does not sustain the world with all beings, The material cause is the one that is the source of all beings. As the sun, shining brightly, illuminates all, Thus, the essence of all beings is also pure. Therefore, the great light is the source of all beings."

The divine beings rejoiced, the worldly beings were liberated; They attained the highest bliss, having been freed from bondage. | 025 | 6. Thus is this ancient history, born of a curse; The destruction of Pauḷoma and the possibility of the forest. | 026 | Anaya 008 Soot spoke: 1. English: 1. "The constellation of the sages, having performed austerities, is pleased with the one who is devoted to the welfare of all beings." 2. "At that time, the king of the cows, having been born in Menaka, was endowed with great strength." 3. "Then Menaka, that beautiful one, gave birth to him at the appropriate time." 4. "And he, having grown up, went to the forest, resembling a deer in beauty." 5. "The great sage saw her, who was beautiful and radiant, by the riverbank." 6. "He then, with great desire, approached her, resembling a beautiful flower." 7. "She blossomed, being endowed with auspicious qualities." 8. "That beautiful one, indeed, was adorned with all virtues." 9. "Then the great sage, named Shambharama, was born in that auspicious place." 10. "In that auspicious place, Shambharama became a great sage, endowed with all virtues." 11. "Then, having been born, he became a great sage, endowed with the essence of Dharma." 12. "Then, having been instructed, he spoke the words of the sage Shambharama." 13. "Then, having been instructed, he went to the forest, that Shambharama."

English: 76 Pauḷomapaṇa The marriage is not to be performed for the divine being. | 013 | Then, when the marriage is about to take place, the friends are eagerly waiting for the bride. | 014 | The serpent does not approach the bride, as she is adorned with a beautiful form. | 015 | She, having suddenly fallen to the ground, lost her consciousness, resembling a lifeless body. | 016 | She, being overwhelmed by the time of death, was struck by the poison of the serpent. | 017 | Even though she was in a state of unconsciousness, her beauty became even more enchanting. | 018 | Her father saw her, and so did the others, as they were lamenting on the ground. | 019 | Then, all the assembled people, being filled with compassion, were distressed. | 020 | Bharata, Kaṇṭaka, and Gautama, along with the others, were in the forest. | 021 | O you, who are beautiful, please show mercy and revive her! | 022 | The serpent, having been struck by poison.

Sanskrit: अाय ००९ ७७ अाय ००९ सूत उवाच | तेष ु तोपिवेष ु ाणेष ु समतः |  ुोश गहनं वनं गा स ुःिखतः | ००१ | शोके नािभहतः सोऽथ िवलपणं ब | अवीचनं शोचियां िच मराम ्| ००२ | शेते सा भ ुिव ती मम शोकिवविधनी | बावानां च सवषां िकं न ु ःखमतः परम ्| ००३ | यिद दं तपं ग ुरवो वा मया यिद | सगारािधताेन सीवतु मम िया | ००४ | यथा जभृित वै यतााहं धृततः | मरा तथा ैव समुितु भािमनी | ००५ | देवत उवाच | अिभधे ह याचा रो ःखेन तृषा | न तु म  धमाायुरि गतायुषः | ००६ | गतायुरेषा कृ पणा गवारसोः स ुता | ताोके मनात मा कृ थां कथन | ००७ | उपाया िविहतः पूव देवैमहािभः | तं यदीिस कतु  ं ासीमां मराम ्| ००८ | वाच |
English: 1. The sage said: Among them, the trees are abundant, the forest is dense, and the river flows. 2. In grief, he did not speak; then he lamented, the lamentation is a source of sorrow. 3. She lies there, my beloved, afflicted by grief; what is not unbearable for all beings? 4. If I have committed a sin, may my suffering be alleviated by the strength of my penance. 5. As the earth bears the burden, so may my grief be borne by the earth. 6. The deity said: By the power of the vow, one should not be afflicted by grief; for the one who has departed, life is not to be lamented. 7. This life is indeed miserable, do not grieve for the departed, do not be troubled. 8. The means of overcoming grief are known; if one is wise, let them be free from sorrow.

English: 78 Pauḷomapaṭha What means have been made by the gods? Thus, may you, O Lord, grant me the ability to understand. 009 With that, the sky-dweller spoke. The deity said: "By the life of the Bhrigus, Thus, may your sister be blessed with longevity." 010 The sky-dweller spoke: "By the life of the sky-dweller, May the ornament of the moon grant me my wish." 011 The sage spoke: Then, the king of cows, To the deity, spoke this word. 012 To the king of dharma, By the life of the cowherd, May the sister be blessed, If she is dead, may she be revived. 013 The king of dharma spoke: "O deity, if the sister is dead, By the life of the cowherd, She will indeed be revived." 014 The sage spoke: Thus, with that, the king of dharma, The sister of the cowherd, Was indeed granted the boon of longevity. 015

Sanskrit: अाय ०१० ७९ एतं भिवे िह रोमतेजसः | आयुषोऽितवृ भायाथऽध सिित | ०१६ | तत इेऽहिन तयोः िपतरौ चतुमु िववाहं तौ च रेमाते पररिहत ैिषणौ | ०१७ | दा | स ला लभां भाया पिकसभाम ्| तं चे िवनाशाय िजगानां धृततः | ०१८ | स ा िजगावाीकोपसमितः | अिभहि यथासं गृ हरणं सदा | ०१९ | स कदािचनं िवो रागमहत ्| शयानं त चापयडुभं वयसाितम ्| ०२० | तत उ दडं स कालदडोपमं तदा | अुिषतो िवमुवाचाथ डुडुभः | ०२१ | नापराािम ते िकिदहम तपोधन | संरािमथ मामिभहंिस षाितः | ०२२ | अाय ०१० वाच | मम ाणसमा भाया दासीुजगेन ह | त मे समयो घोर आनोरग वै कृ तः | ००१ |
English: 1. In this world, the one who is endowed with the brilliance of the sun, the life span of the one who is devoted to the goddess is indeed long. 2. Thus, the two parents of those who are united in marriage, they are indeed filled with love for each other. 3. He who is endowed with a beautiful wife, the one who is like a precious gem, is indeed destined for destruction by the one who is strong. 4. The one who is endowed with a beautiful wife, who is like a precious gem, is always engaged in the act of taking her. 5. At no time does the wise one, who is like a great sage, lie down in a place that is unfit for a young man. 6. Then, that great sage, who is like a great mountain, spoke to the one who is like a great sage. 7. Do not be afraid, O ascetic, of what I have said; protect me from the one who is like a serpent. 8. My sister, who is like a great treasure, has indeed been afflicted by the terrible serpent of time. 9. Thus, my time is indeed terrible, like a fierce serpent.

English: 80 Pauḷomapaṇa "Always, the serpent that I desire, I shall kill. Then, I shall be freed from life." 002 Duḍḍubha said: "Those serpents of yours, O man, do not harm the one who is not to be harmed." 003 "Those who are without a protector, do not harm the one who is not to be harmed." 004 Soot said: "Thus, the serpent spoke, 'Do not harm the sage who is not to be harmed.'" 005 The Blessed One spoke to him, "O serpent, who has come to this subject with desire?" 006 Duḍḍubha said: "I am the ancient one, the sage who fell from grace. I have come here due to a curse." 007 The serpent said: "What is the reason for your fall, O serpent? What is the time of your return?" 008

Sanskrit: अाय ०११ ८१ अाय ०११ डुडुभ उवाच | सखा बभूव मे पूव खगमो नाम वै िजः | भृशं संिशतवाात तपोबलसमितः | ००१ | स मया ीडता बाे कृ ा ताणमथोरगम ्| अिहोे सः सीिषतः मुमोह वै | ००२ | ला च स प ुनः सां मामुवाच तपोधनः | िनदहिव कोपेन सवांिशततः | ००३ | यथावीयया सप ः कृ तोऽयं मिभीषया | तथावीय भ ुजं मम कोपािविस | ००४ | ताहं तपसो वीय जानमानपोधन | भृशमुिदयमवोचं वनौकसम ्| ००५ | यतः संमा ैव ािलः णतः ितः | सखेित हसतेदं ते नमाथ वै कृ तं मया | ००६ |  ुमहिस मे ापोऽयं िविनव ताम ्| सोऽथ मामवीा भृशमुिचेतसम ्| ००७ | मुं िविनः स ुसंापोधनः | नानृतं वै मया ों भिवतेदं कथन | ००८ | य ु वािम ते वां णु ते धृतत |
English: 1. The sage spoke: My friend was named Khagam, a bird of great wisdom, endowed with the power of austerity. 2. I was greatly troubled by the strength of my own actions; indeed, I was completely bewildered. 3. Then the sage spoke to me again: "Do not be angry; you have been afflicted by the wrath of the river." 4. "As it is, this is the result of your fear; thus, my anger is also justified." 5. "Therefore, I, knowing the power of austerity, spoke with a heart full of compassion." 6. "Thus, I bow to you, who are a friend; this is what I have done." 7. "This great sorrow of mine is indeed a result of my own actions; it has greatly disturbed my mind." 8. "What can I say to you, who are steadfast in your resolve?"

English: 82 Pauḷomapaṅga 1. O sage, you who are endowed with wisdom, may you be blessed with the knowledge of the truth. 009 2. The one who is pure and wise, may he be free from the curse of ignorance. 010 3. The one who is pure and wise, may he attain the highest bliss. 011 4. Non-violence is the supreme dharma, the essence of all beings. 012 5. The one who is non-violent is truly blessed, and he is the protector of all beings. 013 6. Non-violence is the essence of all teachings, and it is the foundation of the Vedas. 014 7. The dharma that is non-violent is indeed the highest, and it is the support of all beings. 015 8. This non-violence is the essence of my being, O Janamejaya, the protector of dharma. 016 9. The one who is afraid and seeks refuge, may he find safety in non-violence. 017 10. The one who is endowed with tapas and strength, may he attain the knowledge of the Vedas. 017

English: Chapter 12 83 Chapter 12 Thus spoke: How indeed did Janamejaya, the son of Maharaja, perform the sacrifice? What was the reason for the great sacrifice? 001 What is the reason for the great sacrifice? Please tell me. I do not wish to hear anything else. 002 The sage spoke: The great sacrifice has been performed for a long time, and it is said that the stories of the sages are endless. 003 The Soot spoke: The forest is indeed the place where all the waters flow. It is the abode of the great sages. 004 The great sages, having gathered there, performed the sacrifice, and the father of all beings then narrated everything. 005 Thus ends Chapter 13 Shounaka spoke.

English: 84 Aśīkapava King Janamejaya, the son of King Mahāśala, has gone to the place of the great sacrifice with the assembled sages. 001 Aśīka, the best among the sages, is the one who chants the hymn. He was enchanted by the serpent goddess. 002 What is the king who brings forth the great sacrifice? Tell me, O best among the sages. 003 Sūta said: O great sage, tell me about the Aśīka that is praised by the wise. Speak to me about all this in detail. 004 Śaunaka said: With the essence of the story, let me hear this delightful tale. Aśīka is the best among the Purāṇas. 005 Sūta said: This history is called the Purāṇa, which is narrated by the wise. It is not to be disregarded by those who are learned. 006 When questioned by the sage, my father Lomahaṣa, the wise and learned one, spoke with great clarity. 007 Then I will narrate it as it is. This Aśīka is indeed for you, O Śaunaka. 008

Sanskrit: अाय ०१३ ८५ आीक िपता ासीजापितसमः भ ुः | चारी यताहारपुे रतः सदा | ००९ | जरािरित ात ऊरेता महानृिषः | यायावराणां धमः वरः संिशततः | ०१० | अटमानः कदािच ादश िपतामहान ्| लमानाहागत पादैरधोमुखान ्| ०११ | तानवी ैव जराः िपतामहान ्| के भवोऽवले गतऽिा अधोमुखाः | ०१२ | वीरणके लाः सवतः पिरभिते | मूषके न िनगूढेन गतऽििवािसना | ०१३ | िपतर ऊच ुः | यायावरा नाम वयमृषयः संिशतताः | संतानयाधो गाम मेिदनीम ्| ०१४ | अाकं संतितेको जरािरित ुतः | मभायोऽभायानां तप एव समाितः | ०१५ | न स प ुानियतु तेन लामहे गत संतानयािदह | ०१६ | ं दाराूढिकीष ित | अनाथाेन नाथेन यथा ृ ितनथा | कं ब ुिरवााकमन ुशोचिस सम | ०१७ | ातुिमामहे ो भवािनह िधितः | िकमथ च ैव नः शोानन ुकितुमहिस | ०१८ |
English: 1. "The father of the wise is like a great sage." 2. "The one who eats moderately is always joyful." 3. "The aged one, having attained great wisdom, is a great sage." 4. "The dharma of wanderers is to be always humble." 5. "The one who is self-controlled, even when faced with difficulties, is a great father." 6. "The aged one, having attained great wisdom, is humble in demeanor." 7. "The wise are always engaged in the welfare of all." 8. "The mouse does not hide when it has a good meal." 9. "The father speaks:" 10. "We, the sages, are called wanderers." 11. "With the blessings of our descendants, may we attain the heavenly realm." 12. "The aged one, having attained great wisdom, is indeed a sage." 13. "He does not have a fixed abode; thus, he wanders with his descendants." 14. "The one who is bound by the ties of family is indeed a sage." 15. "The orphaned one, by the master, is like a child without a protector." 16. "Why should one lament for the one who is bound by the ties of family?" 17. "The one who is wise, having attained great wisdom, is indeed a sage." 18. "What is the use of lamenting for the one who is bound by the ties of family?"

English: 86 Aśīkapavaḥ Jaraṭācuṭavāca | My ancestors, indeed, are the fathers of the family. What can the old age do to me? 019 | The father said: Whatever is born from the lineage for the sake of progeny, That is indeed the dharma, and also the wealth. 020 | Indeed, without the fruits of dharma, without austerities, That which is sung is the supreme good, which is attained by the wise. 021 | In the destruction of the mind, The supreme good is attained through the practice of yoga. 022 | Jaraṭācuṭavāca | The mind is always attached to the wives. But your good is indeed the attachment to the wives. 023 | In due time, I have not been able to fulfill the prescribed duties. Thus, when the fruit is ripe, I do not know what to do. 024 | The woman who is my beloved, and who is indeed my life, I am indeed the one who is bound by the rules of love. 025 | Indeed, who is the one who has given me a special gift? If the wise one is indeed the one who has given me a gift. 026 |

English: 1. Thus, for the sake of the marriage, the grandfathers said: "By this arrangement, I shall become a husband." 027 2. Therefore, to save the one who is in distress, the wise ones have given me knowledge and joy, my fathers. 028 3. The sage spoke: 4. Then, for the purpose of the arrangement, he, having been instructed, wandered greatly, not returning to the house. 029 5. At some time, the sage, having heard the words of the father, spoke: "What is the purpose of this arrangement?" 030 6. He, the one who is wise, having been instructed, then did not return to that place, nor did he choose to stay. 031 7. The wise one, having been instructed, said: "I shall go to the house, for the mind is restrained by the fear of the great." 032 8. The great sage spoke: "What is the purpose of this arrangement for you, O serpent, who is in distress?" 033 9. The wise one replied: "The distress of old age is my burden; I have been afflicted by the past." 034 10. The sage spoke: "Indeed, the serpents are wise, for they are the best among those who know."

English: Shounaka said: O Sauti, tell us again the story of that great sage, the best of poets. Madhura, having been asked, O son, speak about the great sage Bhṛgu. In the matter of the sage, indeed, speak as your father has told you. Soot said: I will narrate the story of the great sage, as it has been told to me. In the ancient age of the gods, the auspicious sage was born. He, the son of the sage, was indeed a great sage, like the father of the gods.

English: The celestial beings, having gathered there for the sake of immortality, were engaged in austerities. There, the deity Narayana spoke to Brahmā, contemplating thus among the gods. The assembly of gods and demons should churn the ocean, for the future nectar will arise from the great ocean being churned. Having gathered the herbs and all the ingredients, the gods will know the nectar from the churning of the ocean. Sūta said: Then, the mountain Mandara, resembling a peak of clouds, was covered by the wind and surrounded by a net. It was filled with various flocks of birds and crowded with diverse creatures, served by the celestial beings and the nymphs. Rising to an elevation of eleven thousand yojanas, it was established above the earth among thousands of mountains. The gods were unable to approach Vishnu, who was seated there, along with Brahmā.

English: The infinite Lord, from whom Narayana arises, raised the head of the serpent and repeatedly cast it down. From the serpent Vāsuki, the gods, with their smoke and winds, were driven away from the face of the serpent. Those clouds, born from the gathering of smoke, with lightning, overwhelmed the host of gods, causing them distress. From the peaks of the mountain, the flowers rained down, showering the hosts of gods and demons with garlands. A great roar arose here, comparable to the sound of a great storm, as the ocean churned with the gods and demons. There, various aquatic creatures, driven by the great ocean, came to their end in the waters by the hundreds. The beings of Varuna, diverse and dwelling in the depths, were brought to their end. As the mountain was being churned, the beings, filled with joy, fell like birds from the heights of the great trees. From their clash, a fire blazed forth, enveloping the mountain like a blue cloud. The elephants and lions that had emerged were burned, and all beings of various kinds lost their lives.

English: Then the sun, like the ocean, arose with a thousand rays, bright and shining, the moon, the cool and radiant one. After that, the goddess Surā, born from ghee, appeared, and the horse, too, was born, pale in color. The jewel Koṣṭubha, born from the nectar, and the illustrious Nārāyaṇa, emerged from the ocean. From that place, the goddess Śrī, Surā, and the moon, as well as the swift horse, went to the path of the sun. Then the deity Dhanvantari, endowed with a divine form, appeared, holding a white pot where the nectar resides. This is indeed wonderful, as the great roar arose from the demons, speaking of the nectar. Then Nārāyaṇa, assuming a form of illusion, created a marvelous female form, taking refuge among the demons. Then they, with foolish minds, gave him the nectar, all the demons who were intent on that.

English: Tomarāś ca sutīkṣṇāgrāḥ śasrāṇi vividhāni ca. Tato'surāś ca karabhinnā vamanto rudhiraṃ bahu. Asiṅśaktigadāru gṇā nipetur ghaṭanītale. Chinnāni paṭṭiśeśvāpi rirāṃsi yudhi dāruṇe. Taptakāñcanajālāni nipetur anirāṃ tadā. Rudhiraṇāvaliptād gā nihatāś ca mahāsurāḥ. Adrīṇām iva kūṭāni dhāturaktāni rorate. Hāhākāraḥ samabhavattatra tatra sahasraśaḥ. Anyonaṃ chindatāṃ śasare rāditye lohitāyati. Parigheś ca āyaseḥ pīteḥ saṃnikarṣe ca muṣṭibhiḥ. Nipnatāṃ samare anyonaṃ śabdo divam ivāspṛtāt. Chindhi bhic pradhāvadhvaṃ pātayābhisareti ca. Cintayāmāsa ve cakraṃ viṣṇudānavasūdanaṃ. Tato'ambarā cintitamātram āgataṃ; mahāprabhaṃ cakramamitratāpanaṃ. Vibhāvasoḥ tulyaṃ akuṇṭhamanḍalaṃ; sudarśanaṃ bhīmaṃ ajayyam uttamam. English: The sage said: Thus, I have narrated everything to you, the nectar churned as it is, where the illustrious horse, the mighty Tukhavikrama, was born. Hearing this, Kadru then spoke: O Bhadrā, what color is the horse, Uccaiḥśravā? Please tell me quickly. The one who is bowed down said: This horse is indeed white; do you think otherwise, auspicious one? Please tell me its color, so that it may be brought to the market. Kadru replied: I think this horse is black as a dark cloud; come, let us gamble, O beautiful one, for the sake of the maidservant. The sage said: Thus, having made an arrangement for the maidservant, they went to their own homes, thinking they would see the corpse. Then, desiring a thousand sons, she commanded, having become a messenger, the one with the dark luster. "Quickly bring forth the horse; I shall not be a maidservant as before." That statement was not heeded by the indifferent serpents.

English: The fearsome one, like a great bird, suddenly arose from the sky. Seeing him, the people took refuge, bowing to the universal form seated there. "O Agni, may you not grow fierce; indeed, this great mass is your lord." Agni spoke: "Do not think that you are like the Asuras; Garuḍa is powerful, equal to my own radiance." Thus addressed, they went to Garuḍa, praising him with words. "You are a sage, a great being, a god, the lord of birds; you are the sun, renowned for your brilliance." "O strength, you are indeed a great being; you are the one who has attained prosperity." "You are the best among all beings, illuminating the mobile and immobile like the sun." "Just as the sun, angry, burns the offspring, so do you burn with the power of the fire." "Fearsome, like Agni, you rise, destroying the cycles of time."

English: Salutations to the Lord of Lords, Salutations to the Mighty One. Salutations to Namuci, Salutations to the Thousand-Eyed, Lord of Śacī. You are the shade of the sun-scorched serpents, You alone are our supreme refuge, O Immortal. You are indeed the essence of milk, O Purandara, You are the wind, the cloud, and the sky. You are the one who causes the rain to fall, They call you the source of wealth, the terrible Vajra, O Balāhaka. You are the conqueror of the worlds, You are the light of all beings, you are the sun, the illuminator. You are the great wonder, the king, the best of the gods, You are Viṣṇu, the Thousand-Eyed, the God, the ultimate refuge. You are the essence of all, O God, you are the supreme Soma, You are the moment, the instant, the fleeting time. You are the great year, the seasons, the months, the nights, and the days. You are the best, the earth with mountains; the sun dispelling darkness in the sky. The great ocean, the source of all, You are the great fish, the abode of fish. You are always worshipped, Delighting the wise with your presence, praised by the great sages. You drink the sweet Soma at the sacrifice, And you are the offering for the beings.

English: The Sūta said: The birds, urged by the Suparṇa, quickly went to that land, surrounded by the ocean's waters, resounding with the cries of flocks. It was adorned with the colorful flowers of various trees, and also with beautiful lotuses, enveloping the abode. It was embellished with clear waters, like a heart adorned with white jewels, and fragrant with divine scents, blessed by the breeze. The sky was fragrant, even with the scent of the Malaya mountain, and it was beautified by the flowers and the winds. There, it seemed as if the Nagas were showering flowers and water, a delightful place for the minds of the celestial beings and Apsaras. Various birds were singing beautifully, delighting in the playful sounds of the water lilies. Having reached that forest, the serpents joyfully departed, and spoke to the great hero, the excellent bird Suparṇa. "Indeed, you carry us to a beautiful land, where you fly in the sky." Thinking thus, the bird then spoke to his mother Vinatā, "What should I do, mother, that is worthy of discussion?" Vinata spoke.

English: The invincible one among all beings, indeed, is like fire to the Brahman. The angry Brahman becomes like poison to the cloud, the foremost among beings, the father and teacher. Garuda said: As I know the external one, O Mother, you should ask the reason for this. Vinatā said: He who has reached your throat, like a hidden stick, burns like a blazing fire; he should be known as the external one. Sūta said: Vinatā spoke this word to her son, knowing that it is unparalleled and accompanied by great strength. May the wind protect you, and the moon from behind, and may the sun, the great illuminator, protect you. I am always for you, O son, for peace and well-being. May the path be free from obstacles for the sake of achieving your purpose. Then, upon hearing the words of his mother, he spread his wings and soared into the sky. Then, the great time, like the mighty Yama, approached the hungry Nishadas. He then gathered the Nishadas; raising the dust, he greatly stirred the sky, causing the waters of the ocean to surge, contemplating the earth-dwellers nearby.

English: The sage said: Then that Brahmin, having departed with the Nishāda, went to the land after killing the desired Garuḍa. With his wife having departed, that Brahmin, the king of birds, soared into the sky. Then he saw his father and, having inquired, spoke of his father. "I have indeed been sent by my father to bring the moon from the rising." "I will bring him today to free my mother from servitude." "I have been instructed by my mother to eat the Nishādas, but I have not been satisfied after killing thousands." "Therefore, O Lord, it should be declared that I may become capable of consuming the nectar of sacrifice." HATZ said: There was a great sage named Vibhāvasu, who was angry. He had a brother and a younger brother named Supratīka, who was a great ascetic. The great sage did not desire wealth from his brother, who was residing with him. The brother Supratīka, being Vibhāvasu, was indeed very much attached to the division of wealth. Then the brothers, being deluded, did not divide among themselves.

English: He, agitated, caused the lake to be filled with many trees. The tortoise, too, with great vigor, approached for battle. The elephant, cut into six parts, is thus measured from the tip of the trunk. The tortoise's measure is a circle of ten yojanas. These two are prepared for battle, each seeking victory over the other. Using this quickly, let one accomplish the desired task for oneself. Sūta said: Hearing this, Bhīma, swift as the wind, with a single claw, struck the elephant and the tortoise. Then, the bird, having taken flight, approached the divine tree. They, frightened, trembled, struck by the wind from his wings, thinking, "Let us not be harmed," those divine golden branches. The sky-dweller, having moved the other beings, brought forth the desires of the mind. In the golden and silver branches, the ocean's water was reflected, shining great trees. The best of birds spoke to the great Rohiṇī tree, which was very large and descending swiftly. "Here is my great branch, extending a hundred yojanas. Taking this, you should eat, O tortoise."

English: The fire of Indra, accompanied by suffering, blazed forth. The clouds, like the flames of a fire, fell from the sky. Thus, among the Vasus, Rudras, and Ādityas, and the Maruts, as well as other groups of deities, each wielded their respective weapons, clashing with one another. In that unprecedented assembly, even among the gods and demons, the winds gathered, and the meteors fell all around. Even without disturbance, the sky resounded with a great sound. The deity among the gods also became manifest. The divine beings' offerings were like the rays of light, and the clouds of calamity poured forth much blood. The crowns of these beings were raised. Along with the gods, Śatakratu, observing the terrible calamities, spoke to Bṛhaspati. "Why, O Lord, have such great calamities arisen? I do not see any enemy who could defeat us." Bṛhaspati replied, "Due to your offense, O Indra, and your negligence, O Śatakratu, the beings of the Valakhilyas have become agitated by austerity."

English: Upon hearing this, Prajāpati approached the Devarāja and asked about the accomplishment of the ritual. Thus, they replied to him, the truthful ones, saying, "Let it be so." This is Indra's command in the world, created by the power of the gods. The words of the Brahman are not false; the resolve of you all and my own is not false. May Indra, the most powerful among the birds, grant favor as requested by the Devarāja. Thus addressed by Kaśyapa, the ascetics of the forest replied, worshipping the foremost sage, Prajāpati. This endeavor is for Indra; may it be fulfilled for all of us, O Prajāpati. Therefore, this fruitful offering should be accepted by you, and may you arrange it in a way that you see the best outcome. At that very moment, the auspicious goddess Dākṣāyaṇī, known as Vinatā, who desires a son, appeared. Having performed austerities, she approached her husband and spoke to him. This endeavor is indeed meant for you, O goddess, as you desire.

English: The sage said: Then, in that great assembly, the mighty Garuḍa arrived before the gods. He, being exceedingly powerful, caused the surroundings to tremble. There was an immeasurable being, shining like lightning, a great protector of the moon. He, having engaged in battle with the king of birds, was defeated in combat. Shaking off the dust with a great wind, the bird caused the gods to scatter. The gods, covered by the dust, fell into confusion, and they could not see the one who was protecting them. Thus, Garuḍa began to agitate the gods with his beak and wings. Then the god commanded the wind: "O Marut, let this dust storm be dispersed." Then the wind blew away that dust with great force, and the gods regained their clarity.

English: The god spoke to him, "I am the boon-giver, O Khecara." He desired that you may remain above, O one who moves in the sky. He then spoke again to Narayana, "I am imperishable and I shall be like the amṛta even without you." Receiving the boon, Garuḍa spoke to Viṣṇu, "May you also grant a boon; let it be chosen, O Lord." Kṛṣṇa desired that Garuḍa, the mighty one, be his vehicle, and the Lord said, "You will remain above the flag and the discus." Indra struck the bird with a boon, the one who takes away the nectar by force, the friend of the gods. Garuḍa spoke to Indra, "O lord of the falling ones," with a voice that laughed like thunder. "I will perform the vow of the sage, from whom the bones will arise, and I will also perform the vow of the thunderbolt for you, O Rātkṛta." "I abandon this one leaf, for you will not be disturbed by it; for I have no pain at any time from the fall of the thunderbolt." Then all the beings were astonished, seeing the beautiful leaf, "May this one, O Suparṇa, be." "O wondrous one, I wish to know the strength that is your supreme and unparalleled."

English: Garuda said: "Indeed, this moon is being taken by me for some reason. I will not give the moon to anyone." "Wherever I place this thousand-eyed one, you should quickly take it, O Hari." Vākya said: "By this statement, I am pleased, as you have spoken here, O best of birds. Whatever boon you desire from me, I shall grant." Sūta said: "Thus addressed, he replied, remembering the cause of the mother's servitude." "I am indeed the lord of all; I will fulfill your request. The serpents will be my great food." Thus spoken, the slayer of the demons went, saying, "I will take the moon that has been placed." Then, the swift Suparṇa came to the mother, and he spoke this to her, like a great sage: "I will place this nectar that has been brought here among you."

English: Shonaka said: "Are those serpents born, O father, who are difficult to conquer? Knowing that curse, what else did they do?" Soot said: "Having abandoned the fault of those, the great renowned Kadru performed penance, a vow of eating air." "Having reached Gandhamādana and engaged in penance at Vadaya, at Gokarna, at Pushkarāranya, and at the banks of the river." "In those sacred places, in the holy places, being solitary, self-controlled, and constantly conquering the senses." "Seeing the severe penance being performed, the grandfather, the lord with matted hair, addressed him." "The grandfather said to the one performing penance, 'What is this you are doing, O Shesha? Ensure the welfare of the beings.'" "For indeed, by your intense penance, you are tormenting the beings, O sinless one. Speak to me what is in your heart that has long been there." Rage said: "All my brothers are indeed of dull intellect. I do not have the strength to bear this; let it be permitted."

English: Brahmā said: "I am pleased with you; control your anger and act with restraint. This speech of yours is for the welfare of all, as per my instruction." Rage said: "As the god Varada, the lord of creatures, the king of the earth, I shall uphold this steady earth; grant it to me, O Prajāpati, as you desire." Brahmā said: "Descend to the earth, O best of serpents; it will grant you a passage. By holding this earth, you will indeed fulfill my great purpose." Sūta said: "Thus agreeing, the lord, the elder brother of the serpent, stood firm, holding the goddess and this earth, embracing the ocean's edge." Brahmā said: "You are the best of serpents, as you uphold this earth alone; holding the infinite enjoyment, as I have said, you will be powerful." Sūta said: "Thus, the serpent, the infinite one, powerful, descended to the earth."

English: Thus, let us be united here in the name of the serpents. As their honor may be, time has passed. Even if united, the cause of liberation is RATA. As the gods of old have perished, they have entered the cave. As it is, so it may be, or it may also be defeated. For the sake of Janamejaya's sacrifice, indeed for the purpose of destruction. Sūta said: Thus addressed, all the Kadraveyas gathered there. They deliberated there, the wise in the mind. Some there said, "We, having become the serpents, Will not allow Janamejaya's sacrifice to happen." Others, the learned and wise, said, "We will all be in agreement for this matter." He will guide us in all actions or decisions. There we will speak of how the sacrifice should be. He, the king, will consider us all wise. For the sake of the sacrifice, we will say it is not so. Seeing many faults, both here and beyond, By causes and reasons, let the sacrifice not be. Or, the teacher will be the one who will determine what will happen.

English: The serpents, listen! In that place, thus spoken. The wise traveler will become a great sage. Known as Jaratkāra, he is radiant and self-controlled. His son, Jaratkāra, will be born, a great ascetic. A sacrifice named Āstika will then be performed. There, the serpents who will be righteous will be liberated. The gods said: He, the foremost sage, Jaratkāra, the great ascetic, Who will give birth to a great soul? Brahmā said: In the name of Sanāmā, in the name of a maiden, the best of the twice-born, The gods will give birth to a powerful offspring. Thus, the gods spoke to him, the grandfather, saying: Having spoken thus, the gods departed, and he, the god, the grandfather. I see thus, O Vāsuki, your sister, Known as Jaratkāra, I will establish her. For the sake of the fearful, to calm the serpents, O sage of good vows, this liberation has been heard by me.

English: As the Lord Udra pierced the sacrificial deer in the sky, the one with the bow in hand followed, searching here and there. The deer pierced by him does not go to the forest while alive. Indeed, the deer that was pierced by the king was lost. The king, having been far away, was exhausted and thirsty, approached the sage in the forest. In the midst of the cows, having emerged from the mouths of calves, may the best of the milk be drunk by us. The king, with a firm vow, asked the sage, who was afflicted by hunger. O Brahman, I am King Parīkṣit, son of Abhimanyu. I have indeed lost the deer; have you seen it? The sage did not speak anything, remaining silent. The king, having placed a dead serpent on his shoulder, after throwing it aside, did not say anything to him, whether good or bad. The king, abandoning his anger, distressed, went to the city, and the sage remained there. The young son of that king, Bhūttigmateja, was a great ascetic.

English: He, having observed him to be emaciated and having spoken sweet words, asked, "How is it, father? Today, he who bears the burden of death is with me." The player said: "O father, the king, while engaged in the hunt, has been struck down by a serpent on his shoulder." "What wrong has my father done to that king, the wicked one?" "Tell me, you who see the truth, what is the strength of my penance?" The player said: "The king, while hunting, was struck by a single arrow from Parikṣit, and he fell, having been pierced by the bird." "And the king did not pursue another deer in that great forest. He asked his father, who was speaking with him." "That one, who is steadfast and remains, afflicted by hunger and thirst, repeatedly asked your father about the lost deer." The player said: "Then the king, having taken up his bow, shot an arrow at him." "Your father, who is devoted to the vow, is indeed like that. He too, the king, returned to his city, called Gajāhvaya."

English: In the seventh day, that sinful Tākṣaka, the best of serpents, is the leader of the house of Yama, which is extremely dreadful. The father was frightened by him, filled with anger. I have not done anything dear to you, O father; do not punish the ascetics. We reside in the realm of that king. We are protected by him according to justice; I do not like his sin. In every way, the king who is present must always be forgiven by us; for the son of Dharma, when killed, kills. If the king does not protect, then great suffering will come upon us. The son should not act against Dharma, as he wishes. We are protected, O father, by the kings with their branches. We wander in great Dharma; they have a share in it. By the poison of the surrounding, as his great-grandfather protects us, so the subjects must be protected by the king. Today, by that hungry and weary ascetic, this vow has been made without doubt, not knowing. Therefore, this was done by you suddenly in childhood; the king will not curse us, O son, in any way.

English: The world is indeed forgiving; therefore, practice forgiveness constantly. By being forgiving, you will attain the worlds that are immediately after Brahman. But I, having taken to calmness, will do what is possible today; I will send it to the king. You have been cursed by my son with a foolish mind; seeing this destruction of mine, O king, do not be angry. The charioteer said: Thus instructing the disciple, he sent him forth, being virtuous and a great ascetic, compassionate towards the king Parīkṣit. Instructing Kurāṭa about the work and the situation, he sent the one named Gauramukh, who was composed and virtuous. Approaching him quickly, the king entered the palace, as previously informed by the doorkeepers. Having been honored by the king, the brāhmaṇa Gauramukh then told everything to the king, being completely exhausted. The terrible words of the demon, as stated, were indeed spoken. O king, in the region of Shamik, there is a sage of supreme self-control, calm and peaceful, a great ascetic. You, O tiger among men, have been separated from life.

English: Determining the essence of the ministers, he constructed a secure pillar in the palace. He also provided protection there, along with the physicians and herbs, and the Brahmins invoked the perfected mantra from all sides. The one residing there, being a king, shone like his own jewels, surrounded by knowledgeable ones and well-protected from all sides. On the seventh day, the best of the twice-born approached the king to treat him. For he had heard that the best of kings, Tākṣaka, would not be taken to Yama's abode. "I will deal with the king of serpents, Tākṣaka, regarding the fever," he thought. That Tākṣaka, the king of serpents, was going along the path, becoming a twice-born, with a single mind. The king of serpents, Tākṣaka, approached the great sage, saying, "What work do you wish to accomplish quickly?" The speaker said: "The king born of the Kuru lineage, Parīkṣit, will be consumed by the great Tākṣaka, the best of serpents, with his fiery energy." The one bitten by the king of serpents, with that same fiery energy, was the king of the Pāṇḍavas, of immeasurable glory.

English: The sage said: Thus addressed, the great serpent approached the fig tree, having been seen by the great sage Kaśyapa. That tree, having been bitten by him, immediately blazed with great splendor. Having burned it, the serpent spoke again: "O best of the birds, revive this tree." Having turned the tree to ashes with the brilliance of the serpent king, he spoke the following words. "O serpent king, I will revive this tree, which is in this state of ashes; look at it, O serpent." Then the Lord, the best of the twice-born, revived the tree that had been turned to ashes with his knowledge. Thus, he, accompanied by the serpent, revived the tree with branches and leaves. The great sage Kaśyapa, seeing the tree revived, spoke to Takṣaka: "This is indeed wonderful for you." "O best of the brāhmaṇas, whatever you desire to be destroyed, whether mine or that of my kind, who do you wish to harm there, O ascetic?" "Whatever fruit you desire, I will give it to you, even if it is from the best of kings."

English: The king, protected by the mantra, contemplated then, "How can I deceive this prince through my illusion?" Then, in the form of a sage, he sent the serpents, taking the water from the leaf to the king, and thus Tākṣaka spoke. "Go, you who are untroubled, to the king to receive the water from the leaf." The charioteer said: They, instructed by Tākṣaka, did as the serpents did, and they brought fruits to the king. Thus, the king, the mighty one, received everything, and told them to go. When those serpents, disguised as sages, had gone, the king spoke to his ministers and friends: "Let you all eat these sweet fruits, which I have brought from the sage." Then the king, along with his minister, wished to take the fruits, and there a worm was found in the fruit taken by the king. A dark-eyed man of reddish hue, of the color of a red gem.

English: Thus, let them attain everything through my austerity. Let them be fulfilled in their desires. The fathers said: O blessed one, the one who desires to eat the flesh of others, cannot be freed from the consequences of austerity. Let us know the fruit of austerity, O best one, from the destruction of progeny, we fall into hell, impure. Here, let us not be ignorant, by which we do not recognize you, the renowned man in the world. O blessed one, the great fortune, who should be mourned by us, the very miserable. We, the sages named Yāyāvara, have fallen from the world due to our pious deeds, from the destruction of progeny. Our lost austerity is not present, there is indeed no progeny for us. There is one who is our progeny, but he is also not there. The unfortunate one, of little fortune, is indeed our relative. He is known as Jaradkaru, well-versed in the Vedas and their branches. The self-controlled great soul, with excellent vows and great austerity. Thus, we are indeed afflicted by the austerity. There is no son or relative of his.

English: As the moon grows in the Shungapakshe, so does he. Then, after a few hours, Jarātkaru, the great ascetic, having made the head of this one his resting place, slept, being exhausted. While he was asleep, the best of the brāhmaṇas, Savitā, approached him. At dawn, Brahman thought deeply. Vāsuki's sister, frightened by the loss of her strength, was distressed. What good deed may I have done that I may not be afflicted by this sorrow? How can I not be troubled by this offense? Is anger or the loss of virtue greater? Thus, the mind became agitated. I will raise him; who will create this unwavering anger? This will surely happen at the time of twilight. Thus, having resolved in his mind, Jarātkaru, the serpent, spoke to the sage, who was radiant and lying without loss. He spoke this sweet word: "Arise, O great one, the sun is setting. Worship at twilight, O Lord, for you are steadfast." Having been disturbed, the one who is the great ascetic, Jarātkaru,

English: The speech is dry from the mouth; with folded hands, the eyes are filled with tears. You do not deserve to abandon me, O knower of dharma. Established in dharma, always engaged in what is dear and beneficial. The reason for the donation, O best of the brāhmaṇas, is that I have obtained a poor one; what will Vāsuki say to me? O best one, afflicted by the curse of my mother, my relatives desire offspring from you. For by obtaining offspring from you, my relatives will have joy; this connection will not be futile for me, O twice-born. Wishing for the welfare of my relatives, I pray to you, O Lord; please accept this unmanifest form of mine. How can the great soul abandon me, desiring to connect with the unworthy? Thus addressed, he spoke to the sage; whatever is appropriate and logical, Jaradkaru, the ascetic, said. There is indeed a great one, O fortunate one, like you, the universal form; the sage is of supreme dharma, well-versed in the Vedas and their branches. Having spoken thus, the dharmic sage Jaradkaru, the great sage, went to perform greater austerities with determination.

English: Jarātkaru then spoke, comforting the tormented Vāsuki, the lord of serpents. Questioned about the reason for my son, that great soul with great austerity, he said, "Indeed, this is my fate." I do not remember anything false about him. O king, where will he speak of the future? There is no distress for you regarding the serpent; your son will surely rise like a blazing fire. Thus speaking, he went to the hermitage of his brother, where this great sorrow resides in your mind. Hearing this, the lord of serpents, Vāsuki, was filled with great joy, and he accepted that statement from his sister. With soothing words, gifts, and appropriate worship, the excellent serpent honored his sister. Then, the embryo of great radiance, like the sun, began to grow. In the same manner, she, the daughter of Brahmā, gave birth to a son, free from the fear of father and mother. He grew there in the abode of the king of serpents, and he mastered the Vedas and the sacred texts. A child of virtuous conduct, endowed with intelligence and qualities.

English: Hearing from you, indeed, in the anger of a father, I shall attain auspiciousness; never shall it be the opposite. The Sūta said: Then the great-souled one spoke this word, being questioned by that great soul, the wise one, knowing his own duty, to King Janamejaya. Thus, the great-souled one, the protector of the people, your father, was indeed as he was, that great-souled one. Having established the four varṇas in their own duties, he protected them; the king, knowing dharma, was indeed a warrior of dharma. He protected the earth, the goddess, the glorious one of unmatched prowess; he does not hate anyone, nor does he desire anything. He was equal towards all beings, like Prajāpati. The brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, and vaiśyas, and also the śūdras, were established in their own duties, being well-disposed towards the king, by that king's own conduct. He bore the burden of the helpless, the poor, and the wretched; he was like the moon among all beings. The prosperous one, endowed with truthfulness and great prowess, was a disciple in the science of archery, that king. Govinda was dear to him, your father Janamejaya, and he was dear to all the people, the great one of great fame.
