English: 176 Āstīkapaṃva In the Kurus, in the northern region, Parīkṣit was born; he was the son of Subhadrā. The king, skilled with the axe, was self-controlled and wise, served by the elderly. The great sage, knowledgeable in ethics and dharma, protected the people for sixty years. Then, having attained a certain fate, he was bitten by a serpent. Therefore, you, the best of men, should uphold dharma; this kingdom has come to the Kurus for a thousand years. You are still a child, a protector of your own kind. Janamejaya said: In this lineage, there has never been a king who did not act for the welfare of the people, especially considering the deeds of the great-grandfathers, who were devoted to the highest good. How did my father meet his end? Please tell me as it is; I wish to hear the truth. Sūta said: Thus addressed by the king, the ministers spoke to the king, devoted to the welfare of all. Your father became a hunter, O king, just like the great Bhīma, the best archer in battle.

English: As we are all angry with the king. Once, a hunter shot a deer with an arrow. The deer, struck, fled into the dense forest. The deer, bound by the hunter's arrow, could not escape; your father did not catch it. Exhausted and aged, he was sixty years old, afflicted by hunger, he saw a sage in the great forest. The king asked the sage, who was observing silence. The sage did not speak even when questioned. Then the king, filled with hunger, approached the sage, who was standing still, observing silence, and calm, immediately overtaken by anger. The king did not recognize the sage, who was observing silence. Overcome by anger, he struck his father. The dead serpent was lifted from the ground by the best of Bharata. The wise one did not speak to him, whether good or bad. He stood there, not angry, holding the serpent with his arm.

English: Father, having made a pact with you, shines like a flame. The one who, in the presence of the guru, releases the dead, that Nāga Taksaka, enraged, will strike with his brilliance. From the seventh night onwards, the sin has been a burden on my penance. Thus speaking, he went there where his father was. The six also informed the father of the curse. And that sage, having sent to your father, said, "You are cursed by my son, O king." Taksaka will strike you down, O great king, with his brilliance. Hearing those terrible words, your father Janamejaya was terrified of Taksaka, the best of serpents. Then, on the seventh day, he wished to go near the king. The king of serpents, having given him, made Taksaka act. The newly arrived king of serpents hurriedly went. "Why do you hurry, what work do you wish to accomplish?" Kāiyapa said, "Where the king, the best of the Kurus, is surrounded, he will surely be burned by Taksaka, the serpent."

English: Janamejaya said: "I wish to hear this, about the conversation of the king of serpents and Karayapa that took place in the solitary forest." "By whom has this been heard, and has it come to your ears? After hearing, I will establish the understanding of the serpent's end." The ministers spoke: "Listen, O king, how this was narrated before, about the meeting of the best of the twice-born and the king of serpents on the path." "In that tree, a certain man, seeking fuel, was searching for a dry branch of the plant." "While he was searching, the serpent-born twice-born was there in the tree." "Then, he was burned by that tree, and due to the power of the twice-born, the plant was alive, O king." "Thus, having gone, it was reported in this city." "All that happened, as it is, of the serpent and the twice-born." "This has been told to you, O king, as it was heard." "After hearing, O king, act as you desire." The sūta said: "After hearing the words of the ministers, King Janamejaya, suffering from grief, pressed his hand."

English: The sage said: Thus speaking, the illustrious one, having been approved by me, ascended the vow, the king Parthiva. At that time, the king Parīkṣit, who was a Brahmin by birth, was present. The king summoned the priest and the officiating priest of the earth. Whoever has killed my father, that wicked Tākṣaka, let them speak as they wish. If that deed is known to you by which I will obtain Tākṣaka, the serpent, I will do so with my relatives. As my father was previously burned by poison, I too wish to burn that sin, the serpent. Priests: O king, there is a great sacrifice for you, the divine one, which is known as the great sacrifice. There is no other king who can harm that sacrifice; thus, the ancient ones have said, and we also have this capability. The sage said:

English: Then the rituals commenced according to the prescribed method. The priests, having donned the garments of Krishna, with smoke-red eyes, offered the oblations as if they were the fire itself. They agitated the minds of all the serpents there; the priests offered the oblations facing the fire. Then the offerings were completed, and the blazing sacrificial fire, being wrapped up, called out to each other in distress. They were flashing and breathing heavily, and they covered the gas with their heads. The white, black, and blue ones, the aged ones, roared with the sounds of Bhairava, O Lord of the universe. Thus, hundreds of thousands of serpents, the best of the twice-born, were destroyed. Some were like the moon, others like elephants, and some were intoxicated like great elephants, large-bodied and powerful. Many were high and low, of various forms, fierce and resembling the club of a hammer, very powerful. They fell down, the serpents, tormented by the words of their mother.

English: CARA and the great Maudraka, the one with the fierce vow. Many others, including these, were external vow-takers. They were present as members in the sacrifice of Parīkṣit. At that time, the great Kato, while performing the sacrifice, was overwhelmed by terrifying creatures. The waters of the rivers, which are known as the Nāgas, were filled with fragrance and tumult. Let the sound of the falling Nāgas, who are established in the sky, be heard loudly. Tākhaka, the king of snakes, went to the abode of the king after hearing about the consecrated Janamejaya. Then, the great serpent narrated everything as it happened and went to the shelter of the fearful Purandara. Indra spoke to him, pleased: "O Tākhaka, do not fear here. The fear of the serpent sacrifice is not to be taken lightly." Previously, I was pleased for your sake, O grandfather. Therefore, you have no fear; let your mental fever depart. Thus reassured by him, the great serpent resided happily in the abode of Shakra. Vasuki, who was constantly falling into grief in the mountains, was troubled by minor faults.

English: Vasuki, the king of serpents, spoke thus. "I am your father's son, given by my brother for a purpose. This is the situation; do as you see fit." Āstīka said: "For what reason did your father give me to my maternal uncle? Please tell me the truth; having heard it, I will act accordingly." Sūta said: "She spoke thus to him, being a well-wisher of the relatives, the sister of the serpent king Jarātkaru." "The mother of all serpents is known as Kadru, as heard. By her curse, her son was born, so know that." "Uccaiḥśravā, the horse king, was not created by me falsely. For the sake of a humble offering, O sons, you will become servants." "In the sacrifice of Janamejaya, the wind-rider will burn you. There, having attained the fifth state, you will go to the realm of the dead." "Thus, having been seized, the grandfather of the world spoke. 'So be it,' he said, and he was pleased with that statement." "And Vasuki, having heard the words of the grandfather, went to the nectar churned, O father, to the abode of the gods." "All the perfected beings and the gods will attain the supreme nectar."

English: I will liberate you, O best of serpents, Vāsuki. Therefore, I will fulfill this promise to you. May you be free from fear, O noble serpent; indeed, you have nothing to fear. I will strive, O gentle one, for your well-being. My words are not false; how could they be otherwise, even in the morning? Going to that king, Janamejaya, who is initiated, I will please him with words filled with my essence, O mother. As that sacrifice will be fulfilled by the king, so shall it be. Thus, O great-minded serpent king, everything is possible for me. Your mind will never be false towards me. Vāsuki said: O Āstīka, my heart is filled with anguish; I do not know the fate of the people, being tormented by the rod of Brahman. Āstīka replied: You should not be troubled, O best of serpents; I will not let the fear born from the blazing fire harm you. I will destroy the terrible rod of Brahman, which is as fierce as the fire of time; you will not suffer any fear from me. Sūta said:

English: The sacrifice of Nṛga and that of Ajāmīḍha; as the sacrifice of Daśaratha the king. Thus is this sacrifice of yours, O Bhārata; may there be well-being for Parīkṣit and the dear ones. The sacrifice of Kṛṣṇa, the son of Satyavatī; where he himself performed the action. Thus is this sacrifice of yours, O Bhārata; may there be well-being for Parīkṣit and the dear ones. In the fire of your sacrifice, the one who is the destroyer of Vṛtra; how does it unite? Now, knowledge is to be known; to those who have given, let it not be taken away. There is no one like the ṛtviks in the worlds; this is determined by the Dvaipāyana. Indeed, the ṛṣis wander the earth; the priests are skilled in their own duties. The glorious one, the sun with its diverse rays; the one who consumes the offerings, O deity, is blazing. There is no other being in the world; equal to the king, the protector of the people. With determination and a joyful mind, I am always; you are either the king, Dharma, or Yama. You are indeed the one who is the protector of the people; in this world, there is no other householder in the sacrifice. The one who is like the great Yayāti; with the same influence as Māndhātṛ. The brilliance of the sun is like your brilliance; O Bhīṣma, as you shine, you are the one of great vows. Like Vālmīki, hidden in the forest; like Vasiṣṭha, who is ever controlled in anger. My opinion is that your power is equal to Indra's; and your radiance shines like that of Nārāyaṇa. As Yama is the one who determines dharma; Kṛṣṇa is endowed with all virtues.

English: 196 Āstīkapaṃva This one comes, O king, like a thunderbolt; A great roar is heard from him, terrifying like Bhairava. Surely, the serpent, having been freed from the grip of the thunderbolt, Is now in a state of confusion, losing its identity; the great serpent king breathes heavily. O king, it is indeed your duty to give a boon to the foremost of the twice-born. Janamejaya said: I wish to grant you a boon that is immeasurable in beauty; Choose what is in your heart, and I shall give it to you, even if it is difficult to grant. Sūta said: While the serpent king Takṣaka was falling, Āstīka urged him thus. If you grant a boon, I ask for a drink; Let your sacrifice not be disturbed by the serpents here. Thus addressed, King Parīkṣit was not overly joyful, And he spoke these words to Āstīka. Gold, silver, and whatever else you desire, O wise one, I shall give you a boon, let it not be turned back. Āstīka said: I do not ask for gold, silver, or anything else from you, O king.

English: Then the sound of the plough was heard, and the joyful Astīka was present. The king Janamejaya, son of the Pandava Parīkṣit, was filled with joy. To the priests and the assembled members who were present there, he gave wealth in thousands. To the red-eyed Sūta and the architect, the Lord spoke of the offering of the sacrifice. For the sake of the Brahman, he gave much wealth to him, and then he performed the ritual as prescribed. Astīka was sent to the well-treated home, and the king, with a joyful heart, honored the wise one. He spoke to him, saying, "You must return; you will be a member of my great sacrifice." Thus instructed, Astīka joyfully fled, having accomplished his task and pleased the king. Having gone, he was extremely pleased and approached his mother, Matṛ, and reported everything as it happened. Hearing this, those who were present, free from delusion, became joyful; they said to Astīka, "Choose a boon that you desire."

English: I am pleased with what you have told me, O father, about the great narrative. I will again cleanse you, O son of the charioteer, please narrate to me the story endowed with the wisdom of Vyasa. In that most difficult serpent sacrifice of the great souls, there are indeed stories that arise in accordance with the rules. There are wonderful stories that have arisen, which convey meanings as they are; I wish to hear them from you, O wise one. The charioteer said: In the various stories that are told, the tales based on the Vedas are indeed narrated; Vyasa constantly narrates the great Mahabharata. Shonaka said: The narrative of the Mahabharata, which brings glory to the Pandavas, was narrated by Krishna Dvaipayana to Janamejaya. He indeed narrated it properly in the various stories; I wish to hear that virtuous tale properly. O sage born from the ocean of the mind, please narrate the story of the virtuous, for I am not satisfied, O son of the charioteer. The charioteer said:

English: He who gave birth to Pāṇḍu, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, and Vidura, the great sage of the Kuru lineage. At that time, Janamejaya, the royal sage, entered the sacrificial hall accompanied by those well-versed in the Vedas and their branches. There, he saw the king seated, surrounded by many members, like the lord of the gods. Thus, with the sages and the rulers of various regions, the priests skilled in the divine rites performed the great sacrifice. Janamejaya, the best of the Bharatas, joyfully rose with his retinue upon the arrival of the sage. The lord, with the consent of the assembly, arranged a golden seat for him, like that of Brihaspati. There, the king worshipped the sage, who was seated and purified by the assembly of divine sages, with a focused mind. He offered water for washing the feet, the ceremonial water, and the cow according to the prescribed rites to his grandfather Krishna, as was fitting. Receiving that worship from Janamejaya, the son of Pāṇḍu, Vyasa was pleased and granted permission for the cow. After fully worshipping him, he sat down and, with a joyful heart, asked him about the name of the river. The Lord also, having seen him, skillfully responded.

English: 206 Worshipped by the members, he did not worship the members. Then, all the members honored Janamejaya. After this, with folded hands, he asked about the great deeds of the Kurus and the Pandavas. O twice-born, I wish to hear their stories as you narrate them. How did the great deeds of theirs come to be? How did that great war occur, leading to the destruction of beings? Among all the grandfathers, whose minds are filled with divine presence, O Bhagavan, are you well? Hearing his words, then Krishna Dvaipayana was seated near the sage. As there was a division between the Kurus and the Pandavas earlier, tell me all that you have heard in my intoxication. Obeying the words of the guru, then the sage began to narrate the ancient history. To that king and the members, and to all the Kshatriyas, he spoke of the division and the destruction of the kingdom of the Kurus and Pandavas. The descent of the original lineage.

English: The sage said: Having worshipped the guru with mind, intellect, and meditation, and having honored all the twice-born, as well as others who are knowledgeable. I shall speak the opinion of Vyāsa, the one of immense splendor, for the benefit of all in the world. Listen, O King, to this story of Bhāratī, which you have attained; the words of the guru resonate with joy and inspire me. Hear, O King, how it was between the Kuru and Pāṇḍava for the sake of the kingdom; thus the forest exile came to be. And how the war became a cause for the destruction of the earth, I shall explain to you, O best of the Bharatas, as you inquire. When your father died, the heroes came from the forest to their own abode, and soon the learned ones became skilled in the Vedas and archery. Thus, those endowed with beauty and valor, who were well-versed and approved by the people, did not envy the Pāṇḍavas, who were renowned and glorious. Then Duryodhana, the wicked, along with Karṇa and others, engaged in various actions to subdue them. The sinful one gave poison to Bhīma, the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, and that hero, with the help of food, overcame it.

English: 208 Adi Vamsha Avatarana In that place, Bhīma, having been bound by Gad, was thrown into the waters of the Ganges and went to the city. When the son of Kunti became aware, he cut the bonds and rose up, the great king Bhīma, free from pain. If he was asleep, struck by the venom of the serpent Krishna, he did not die, even in all the commands of the enemies. Among those wise ones, in those matters, Vidura became alert regarding their liberation and opposition. Just as the sweetener of sugar is beneficial for the living world, so too is Vidura always beneficial for the Pandavas. When various means were employed, even with the revealed ones, the Narakas, who were protected by divine beings, were killed. Then, with ten ministers like Duhshasana, having obtained permission from Dhṛtarāṣṭra, he ordered the house of the Pandavas. There, he made the Pandavas dwell, and did not burn them with fire again. By the words of Vidura, the miner was then instructed, and they were liberated through yoga, fleeing in fear. Then, in the great forest, there was a demon named Hidiṃba, whom Bhīma, enraged, killed with his great prowess. Then, the heroes, having made a pact, began to prepare the chariot.

English: Brahmarūpadharā Bhūtvā Mātrā saha Paraṃtapāḥ. There, they killed the mighty Baka along with the Brāhmaṇas and then went to the city of the Pāñcālas. Having obtained Draupadī there, they returned to Hastinapura, enraged after a full year. Thus spoke Dhṛtarāṣṭra and King Śāntanu, questioning how a conflict would not arise among brothers. We have a servant of yours, who has been thought of at Khāṇḍavaprastha. Therefore, go to Khāṇḍavaprastha, which is well-divided and has a great road. By their words, they went together to the city of Khāṇḍavaprastha, taking the Ralānyādāya. There, they stayed for many years, speaking with great prowess and defeating other kings. Thus, they were devoted to dharma, committed to truth, and arose without negligence, shining brightly. Ajaya, the son of Dhīmasena, was indeed mighty in the east; the brave Sāuno was in the north, and Nakula was in the west. In the south, Sahadeva conquered the enemy warriors. Thus, they all made this earth flourish.

English: 210 ~ € d Surya ~ With the five sons of the Sun, shining with the Sun, The earth was indeed illuminated by the Pandava, the one of true prowess. Then, at the appointed time, King Yudhishthira, Sent his brother Dhananjaya to the forest. He stayed there for a full year and one month. Then, at some point, he went to Dvaraka. There he met the beautiful-eyed Subhadra, Sister of Vasudeva, who spoke auspicious words. She was united with the Mahendra, Subhadra was pleased to marry the Pandava, the son of Kunti. Kunti's son offered the oblations in Khandava, Accompanied by the excellent Vasudeva, the best of kings. For indeed, the burden was not heavy for Partha, As he was aided by the resolute Vishnu in slaying enemies. He also took the excellent Gandiva bow, The chariot with the auspicious mark, and the inexhaustible arrows. He liberated the great demon there, And created a divine assembly, adorned with celestial beings. In that assembly, Duryodhana, the foolish one, Became greedy and devised a wicked plan against Yudhishthira. He sent the seven and five to the forest. The descent of the original lineage.

English: 212 Ādivaṃśāvataraṇapava When the wicked ones were calmed down, they were being used. 005 How did the one with the strength of a thousand serpents, Vṛkodara, manage to control his anger, O best of the twice-born? 006 How did Draupadī Kṛṣṇa, being tormented by the wicked ones, remain steadfast and not lose her composure? 007 How did the son of Madri, following the tiger among men, manage to overcome the wicked ones? 008 How did the best among the bearers of heat, the son of Ghaṭa, endure the unbearable, O Yudhiṣṭhira? 009 How did the numerous armies, with the Pandava and Kṛṣṇa as the charioteer, manage to lead them all to the realm of their ancestors, O Dhananjaya? 010 Tell me all this as it happened, O ascetic, regarding what the great charioteers did there and here. 011 Vāyasa said: I shall speak of the opinion of the great sage, the pure-hearted one, who is of immense radiance. 012 This thousand-fold gift indeed, is a great merit of sorrow, explained by the son of Satyavatī, the one of boundless brilliance. 013 Whoever, being learned, recites this, O TATA, will attain the place of the brāhmaṇas, equal to the divine. 014

English: This indeed is the pure and supreme assembly of the Vedas, the best among the audible, praised by the sages in the Purāṇa. In this great history of merit, wisdom is also the ultimate goal. Those who are devoid of faith, who are deceitful, and who are untruthful, should listen to this Veda. The sin of killing a fetus is indeed a great sin; without doubt, upon hearing this history, even a person of great misdeeds should listen to it, for it is called victory. One who conquers the earth conquers all enemies as well. This is the best Pumsavana, this is the great Swastyayana. It should be heard from the great kings. This supreme Dharma, the means of liberation, is proclaimed by Vyāsa, the one of great wisdom. Currently, they will narrate, and others will also tell. There are sons who are devoted to service and messengers who are dear doers. The sin committed by the body, by speech, and by the mind, all of it is quickly abandoned by a man who always listens. For the people of Bhārata, there is no fear of disease, nor any fear of the afterlife. Blessed are those with fame, longevity, and good fortune.

English: PME performed by the virtuous seeker. The fame of the great Pandavas is spread in the world, as well as that of other Kṣatriyas endowed with abundant wealth and splendor. Just as the ocean and the Himalayas are renowned, so is the Bharata declared. Whoever recites this, having purified himself, goes to the realm of Brahman, free from sin and victorious over heaven. And whoever recites this from the beginning, his ancestors are exalted and he attains immortality. Whatever a man does in ignorance, upon hearing this great Mahābhārata, he is liberated. The great birth of the Bharatas is called the Mahābhārata; whoever knows its meaning is freed from all sins. The sage Krishna-Dvaipāyana composed this excellent narrative of the Mahābhārata, arising from the three lineages. In righteousness, wealth, desire, and liberation, O best of the Bharatas, whatever exists here exists elsewhere; whatever does not exist here does not exist at all. The origin of the ancestral lineage.

English: Vērāmpāyana said: There was a king named Dhamanitya, the ruler of the earth, who once went hunting. He, the son of Vasu, the delight of Paurava, was to be captured by Indra, the king of the gods. The god himself, having taken the form of a sage, approached the king who was residing in the hermitage. Considering that the king was worthy of kingship due to his austerities, he directly inspired the king with his grace. Indra said: This dharma is not to be neglected on earth, O king of the earth. Protect this dharma, for it indeed sustains the world. You, being constantly engaged in righteous actions, will attain the eternal merits. You are my dear friend, residing in the land of the earth. May you, being virtuous and prosperous, enjoy the qualities of the land. This land is indeed filled with wealth and resources.

English: The king took the beloved daughter of Girikā. The wife of Vasa, Girikā, offered herself due to desire. On that day, the parents said to him, "You are like a deer." Remembering Girikā, the best of kings went hunting, not deviating from the command of his ancestors. She was exceedingly beautiful, like a goddess. His seed fell while wandering in the beautiful forest. The king thought, "Let my seed not fall in vain," and "Let the season not be unfruitful for her." The king, contemplating this, repeatedly thought about the infallibility of his seed. Seeing the wood for the offering of the seed, he approached Abhimanyu, who was standing there. Knowing the subtlety of the matter, he spoke to the falcon. "Take this seed, my gentle one, to my home quickly, and give it to Girikā."

English: 220 Grabbing it, the swift hawk took off, relying on supreme speed, the bird fled. Then, the hawk, having reached the other side, was immediately attacked by the fish-eating creature. In the battle of beaks, both engaged in a fierce struggle, and that also fell into the waters of the Yamunā. There, known as Adrika, the nymph, having received a curse from Brahmā, became a resident of the Yamunā. The fish, having lost its hawk-like feet, then approached Vāsava, saying, "O fish-shaped one, come quickly!" Once, the fish, having bound the fish-eater, when the month of Dāra arrived, then the best of the Bharatas. From Rudra, it was said that she was a human. Realizing the wonder, he reported to the king, "O king, these fish are indeed born as humans." Then, the king captured the male fish, who was named Rājāsīddhāmin, the true conqueror. The nymph, freed from the curse, immediately attained her form, as previously stated by the Lord, having fallen into a fortunate birth. Having given birth to a human, you will attain the release from the curse. The descent of the original lineage.

English: Then she, having given birth to a fish, abandoned the fish form and attained a divine form. The celestial nymph went to the path of the Siddhas and Charanas. That girl, the daughter of the fish, the fish-scented one, may you become the servant of the king Say. Endowed with the essence of beauty, she was adorned with all qualities. But she, named Satyavatī, due to the fish slaughter, was for some time a fish-scented one, smiling with purity. She was engaged in service, and she was in the water. Extremely endowed with beauty, even desired by the Siddhas, the wise one saw her, and the wise one, named Charudāsa, was captivated. The learned sage, the great sage, spoke to her, "O Bhagavān, how can there be a meeting with the sages who are situated in the sky?" Thus addressed by them, the Lord created a mist, by which the land became like a darkened place. The girl, astonished by the mist, was shy and full of spirit. Know me, O Bhagavān, as a girl always following the will of my father.

English: Due to your connection, my sinless maidenhood is tainted. If my maidenhood is also blemished, how can I protect it, O best of the twice-born? I wish to go home, but I am eager to stay, O wise one. Considering this, O Lord, please arrange what follows. Thus addressed, the most revered sage spoke to her, filled with affection: "You will become a maiden." Choose a boon, O timid one, that you desire, O beautiful one. My favor is indeed futile if it is not granted to the pure-smiling one. Thus addressed, she chose the most fragrant body. The Lord, pleased, granted her the boon of a beautiful form. Then, filled with joy and adorned with qualities of womanhood, she went along with the sage. Hence, her name became known as Gandhavati. Due to her fragrance, people on earth would sniff her out. Then, her name became known as Yojanagandha. Even the Lord himself went to his abode after announcing her. Thus, Satyavatī, delighted, received the excellent boon. Joined with Parāśara, she bore a son endowed with virtues. He was born on the banks of the Yamunā, the mighty Parāśara. She approached her mother, as if engaged in penance, and focused her mind. The descent of the ancient lineage has begun.

English: I will remember and will fulfill the duties, he said. Thus, the two were born from Satyavatī, and he who was abandoned became known as Dvāpāyana. The learned one, observing the lifespan and strength of the fish in each age, for the sake of the Brahmins and their welfare, taught the Vedas, thus he is remembered. He taught the Mahābhārata to Sūta, Jaimini, Pañcāla, Śuka, and his own son. Thus, the texts are classified separately for the Bharata. Similarly, Bhīṣma, the son of Śantanu, with immense radiance, was born from Vasu, a great hero of great fame. The ancient sage, known as Aṇīmandavya, was renowned. He had previously declared this dharma. With this knowledge, I have known since childhood, the Shakuntika. That sin, I remember not any other sinful act. Why then, with a thousand sacrifices, did I not conquer here? The killing of a Brahmin is the greatest sin of all. Therefore, you will be born from a lowly womb due to this sin.

English: 224 By that curse, Dharma was born in a Shudra womb. The wise one, in the form of a Brahmin, was indeed the sinless one. Saṅjaya, born of the sage, was the charioteer of Gavalgaṇa. In the Kuntī lineage, Karṇa, the great chariot warrior, was born. He, bearing the natural armor, with a face illuminated by earrings. For the welfare of the worlds, Vishnu, worshipped by the gods, appeared from Vasudeva's wife Devakī, endowed with great fame. The eternal, unchanging god, who is the lord of the universe, the imperceptible, the imperishable Brahman, the principal, without qualities. The self, imperishable, and the supreme nature, the person, the creator of the universe, the steadfast, the eternal. The infinite, unchanging god, the swan, the lord Narayana, the giver of immortality, eternal, is called the supreme imperishable. That person, the all-pervading one, the grandfather of all beings, was born for the protection of Dharma in the Andhaka-Vṛṣṇi lineage. The all-knowing, the great warrior, expert in archery, Sātyaki, and Kṛtavarmā, followed Narayana. From Satyakā, and also from Uddhīcā, were born the archery experts. From Bharadvāja's lineage, in the womb of Droṇī, Shukra was born. From the great sage, the one with great austerity, Droṇa was born. The descent of the original lineage.

English: Gautama gave birth to a pair, from the arrow of autumn. A mother, Kṛpa, and a great warrior were born. From Drona, the one adorned with blood, Aśvatthāmā was born. Similarly, Dhṛṣṭadyumna was born, directly manifesting the divine. From the fire of the sacrifice, Vaitāna was born. A hero, to destroy Drona, was born with a bow. Similarly, the radiant and auspicious Kṛṣṇa was born, Shining in form, possessing excellent beauty. Prahaḍa's disciple, and the well-formed Subala were born. From his lineage, due to the wrath of the gods, were born. The son of the king of Gāndhāra, the strong Bhṛṅgāra, And the mother of Duryodhana were born, both knowledgeable. From Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the lord of men, was born. In the field of the wondrous Vīya, the great warrior Pāṇḍu was born. From Pāṇḍu, five sons, equal to the gods, were born separately. Among the horses, the eldest, Yudhiṣṭhira, was born. From the wind, however, Bhīma was born. Indra's son, the glorious Arjuna, was born, the best among the strong. From the two horses, endowed with beauty, were born. Sahadeva, devoted to the service of the guru, was born.

English: Thus, Dhṛtarāṣṭra of great wisdom had a hundred sons; among them, Duryodhana and others were eager for battle. Abhimanyu was born to Subhadrā, the daughter of Vasudeva, and the great-souled Pāṇḍu. From the Pāṇḍavas, five sons were born to Kṛṣṇa, all endowed with beauty and skilled in all arts. From Yudhiṣṭhira, the son of Prativindhya was born; from Bhīma, Vṛkodara; from Arjuna, Śrutakīrti; and from Nakula, Śatānīka. Similarly, from Sahadeva, the valiant Śrutasen was born; and in the forest, Ghaṭotkaca was born to Bhīma and Hidimbā. Śikhaṇḍin was born as a daughter to Drupada, who later became a son; the Yakṣa desired her with great affection. In the battle of the Kurus, countless warriors assembled, ready to fight in the conflict of a hundred thousand kings. Their innumerable names cannot be counted, even in a hundred years. These are the main ones mentioned, to whom this narrative pertains. The descent of the original lineage has begun.

English: Janamejaya said: Those who are mentioned, O Brahman, and others not mentioned, I wish to hear them properly, as well as the words of other kings. As the great charioteers, born here, O great one, you are worthy to explain that to me. Vaśaṁpāyana said: This is indeed a secret, O king, we have heard about the gods. I shall tell you that, bowing to the Self-born. In ancient times, having created the earth with three-sevenths, Jamadagni performed austerities for the great Indra, the best of the winds. When the earth was created without kṣatriyas, The Brahmanas and kṣatriyas, O king, began to compete. With them, the resolute ones, who had taken vows, In the season of righteousness, not desiring anything false. From them, the kṣatriyas received great strength, Then, O king, kṣatriyas were born, endowed with valor. And also sons and daughters, again for the increase of kṣatriyas. Thus, from the resolute ones, kṣatriyas were born, Endowed with long life, established in righteousness.

English: 228 Ādivaṃśāvataraṇapava At that time, the four Vana became the best of the Bharata. The truthful woman approached, not desiring falsehood; likewise, other beings also, even those born in lower forms. The righteous ones, along with their wives, went forth, O best of the Bharata. Then, due to the heat, the hundreds of thousands of living beings were exhausted; those people, devoted to dharma, were on the earth. Freed from ailments and afflictions, the men were liberated. Then, GPR, the king of elephants, stood firm again in the Kṣatra, with the names of the great warriors. He governed the Kṣatra again, ruling this earth with dharma; the Brahmins and others then rejoiced greatly in the Vana. The kings, dispelling the faults of desire and anger, did not punish with the rod, but rather, with dharma, they guided the people. Thus, in the Kṣatra devoted to dharma, the thousand-eyed and hundred-sacrificer caused the people to flourish in their land and time. At that time, no child was dear to the king, nor did any youth attain the pleasures of life. Thus, with the long-lived ones, O best of the Bharata, this land, extending to the ocean, was filled.

English: In the great sacrifices, the Kṣatriyas are very generous; then the Brāhmaṇas are honored with offerings. At that time, Brāhmaṇas do not sell the Vedas, nor do the Śūdras chant them. They engage in agriculture with cows and other animals; they do not abandon the work of the land. Humans do not milk calves; they do not sell goods that are not properly weighed. The human tigers perform their duties; they follow righteousness and are devoted to their tasks. Those who are engaged in their own work are the rulers among men; thus, at that time, righteousness does not waver. In due time, cows give birth, and women also bear children; trees bear fruits and flowers in the seasons. Thus, in the Kṛta age, when everything was proper, the earth was filled with living beings. Then, in the world that arose, demons were born among the Kṣatriyas, the best of men. At that time, the Devas were defeated in battle by the Asuras, and they also became established on the earth. English: 230 The beings were born, O Lord, among those asuras. Among the cows and horses, O King, Among the flesh-eating beings, elephants, and animals. Here, the kings of the earth are born, Unable to bear the burden of their own selves. Then the kings, some accompanied by their retinues, The sons of Diti and Danu, thus fell from their positions. Those who were valiant and fierce roamed the earth, This ocean of milk was disturbed by the enemies. The brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, and vaiśyas, And other beings were tormented by their might. Terrifying and striking, they roamed the earth, Hundreds of thousands of beings. From the hermitage, the great sages, With their strength, were agitated. The non-brāhmaṇas, intoxicated with pride and strength, Thus, the earth was tormented by the might of those asuras. Tormented, the kings approached the brāhmaṇas. Indeed, the wind could not hold the earth, O King, Then, the earth was unable to bear the weight of the asuras. Then the earth, tormented by fear, Sought refuge in the Lord of all beings, the Father of all. The descent of the original lineage began.

English: The great one, surrounded by divine sages, addressed the eternal Brahmā, the sustainer of the worlds, along with Gandharvas and Apsarases, who were firmly established. Then, the earth, adorned with joy, was requested for the purpose of creation by the guardians of the worlds, all of them in the presence of Bhārata. Thus, the self-born one, knowing the duty of that earth, spoke of it as known to the Supreme Being. Why would the creator of the universe not be aware, O Bhārata, of the desires of the gods and demons in their entirety? The great king spoke to the earth, the lord of the earth, the omnipotent one, the lord of all beings, Śambhu, the progenitor. As you have reached me, O earth, for that purpose, I shall appoint all the celestial beings. Having spoken thus, the deity Brahmā, O king, released the earth and then commanded all the celestial beings to create. To relieve the burden of this earth, let it be borne separately by the portions of the earth, and thus it was said here. Similarly, gathering the groups of Gandharvas and Apsarases, the Lord spoke this excellent word.

English: The kings of the gods were born as they desired. The demons and the rakṣasas, as well as the gandharvas and serpents, and many other beings were born. The demons and the rakṣasas, as well as the gandharvas and serpents, were not defeated even in the presence of the best of the Bharatas. Janamejaya said: I wish to hear about the origin of the assemblies of the gods and demons, the gandharvas, and the apsarases, as well as all the humans and all the yakṣas and rakṣasas. I wish to hear the truth about the origin of all living beings. Vairāmpāyana said: Indeed, I will tell you, bowing down to Svayambhu, about the creation and dissolution of the worlds. The sons of Brahmā, known as the six great sages, are Marīci, Aṅgiras, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, and Vasiṣṭha. From Marīci, the son of Kaśyapa, these great beings were born, the three daughters of Dakṣa. Aditi, Diti, Danu, Kālī, Anayā, Siṁhikā, the sage, Krodha, Prāva, Ariṣṭā, Vinatā, and Kapilā were also born. Kaduśa, the mother of the tiger, was indeed the daughter of Dakṣa, O Bhārata.

English: Thus, these divine Gandharvas have been described. Therefore, I will describe other beings, O Bhārata, who are flawless and of the lineage of the beloved Aruṇa. The beautiful Anūpā was thus revealed. The Siddha, Gola, and the great renowned Pṛṇāśa, the celibate, the one with the quality of love, and also the seventh, Suparṇa. Viśvāvasu and Bhānu, and also Suchandra, are the tenth. Thus, these divine Gandharvas have been described. This lineage of the Apsarases, known for its auspicious qualities, was formerly revealed by the great goddess. Alambusā, with mixed hair, and the unblemished Tula, Aruṇā, and also the protected Rambhā, are of that kind, O Manoramā. Asita and Subāhu, and also Suvrata and Subhujā, and Supriyā, and the well-known Atibāhu, and Hahā and Huhū. Tumburu and these four are remembered as the best of the Gandharvas. The nectar, the cows of the Brāhmaṇas, and also the Gandharvas and Apsarases. The offspring of Kapilā has been described in the Purāṇa. Thus, the origin of all beings has been told by me, as it is properly counted, of the Gandharvas and Apsarases.

English: There are many sons of Atri, known as the lord of men. All are knowledgeable in the Vedas, accomplished, and of peaceful disposition, great sages. The demons, the sons of Pulastya, the monkeys, and the Kinnaras, as well as the animals of the Pūtahasa, lions, tigers, and Kimpuruṣas. The sons of the sacrifice are equal to the sacrifice, companions of the insects, renowned in the worlds, devoted to truth. Dakṣa was born from the right thumb of the lord sage, a Brahmin, the protector of the earth, a boon for those with sons. From the left thumb of that great soul, the sage gave birth to five daughters. Those daughters, with lotus-like eyes, were established by the lord of creatures, who had lost his son. By divine arrangement, O king, the thirteenth was born. The names of the righteous are to be known: Kīrtimān, Kīrtitakṣmī, Medhā, Kīrtitakṣmī, Dhṛti, Pūṣṭi, Śraddhā, and Kriyā. Buddhi, Lajjā, and Matī are also the daughters of Dharma; these are the doors of Dharma established by the self-born. The twenty-seven of the moon are well-known in the world; they are aligned with the eyes of time, the moon's daughters.

English: 240 Adi-Vamsha-Avatara The yogins of the stars are situated in the journey of the womb. The grandfather is the sage, the god, and the father of Prajāpati. I will describe his eight sons, the Vasus, in detail. Dharu, Dhruva, Soma, Aha, Anila, Anala, Pratyuṣa, and Prabhāsa are remembered as the eight Vasus. The son of Ghoomrāya is Dhara, the knower of Brahman, and Dhruva as well. The moon is from the mind of the powerful, and the breath of the breathers. The son of Rata is Aha, and the son of Śāṇḍilya is Hutaśana. Pratyuṣa and Prabhāsa are remembered as the sons of Prabhātā. The son of Dhara is Draviṇa, and Huta-Havyavaha as well. The son of Dhruva is the Lord Time, the creator of the worlds. The son of Soma is Vaca, the speaker, by whom one is born. The son of Manoharā is Prāṇa, and also Ramana. The son of Aha is remembered as Jyoti, and also as Śrama, the peaceful sage. The foremost son is Kumāra, the illustrious one of the Mandāra forest. His branch is Vidākh, and he is known as Kārtikeya due to the connection with the Kṛttikā stars. The son of Anila is Śivā, the swift one, and the unknown one is also a son of Anila. The son of Pratyuṣa is a sage named Nātha Devala. Devala has two daughters, Kṣamā and Vanta, who are wise.

English: Bṛhaspati's sister is a virtuous woman and a celibate; she, accomplished in yoga, wanders unattached throughout the world. The sister of Prabhāsa is known as Vasūtanāma. The great Vishvakarman was born as the Prajāpati of the Relpa. Among all ornaments, he is the best craftsman who created the divine aerial cars for the deities. Men sustain themselves by the craft of that great soul, whom they worship daily as the imperishable Vishvakarman. After breaking the right breast, the human form of Brahman emerged, bringing forth the Lord Dharma, who bestows happiness. He has three sons, all charming to the minds of all beings: Śama, Kāma, and Harṣa, who uphold the worlds with their brilliance. In the realm of desire, the attainment of Śama is the beloved; Nandī is the abode of Harṣa, where the worlds are established. The son of Marīci, the great one, was born as the king of the gods and demons; he is the source of the worlds. The Tvaṣṭṛ, the bearer of the sun, is the one who creates forms. The great one, who is free from envy, resides in the sky. The sons of Dādada and Vādite are led by Indra, the king of men.

English: 242 Where the sorrowful are established, there is the lower aspect of Viṣṇu. These are the three hundred deities; I will explain their lineage and groups. The lower aspect of Rudra, the Maruts, and the Vasus should be known as such. Vinatā's son Garuḍa is powerful, and so is the red one; Bhagavān Bṛhaspati is counted among the Ādityas. O King, know the hidden ones, the medicinal plants, and the animals; this group of deities sings your praises. One who sings is freed from all sins. The Lord Bhṛgu, having pierced the heart of Brahman, emerged; he is the son of Bhṛgu, the poet, the wise one, the son of the poet, the planet. For the purpose of the life journey of the three worlds, the self-born one is appointed and roams around the universe. The great teacher of yoga, endowed with great intelligence, was Bhṛgu; he was also wise among the gods, a celibate, and a vow-keeper. When he was appointed by the mighty one for the welfare of yoga, he produced another son, the unblemished Bhṛgu. Chyavana, the one of radiant austerity, the self-controlled thinker, who, being angry, fell from the mother for liberation, O Bhārata. The descent of the original lineage.

English: Āruṣī, the daughter of Manas, was the wife of the wise one; she gave birth to Mahāyaśa after breaking his thigh. Mahātapa, Mahāteja, a young one endowed with virtues. Ṛcīka's son was Jamadabha, and from Jamadagni, there were four sons of the great soul. Rāma was the most illustrious among them, endowed with incomparable qualities. There were a thousand sons of Jamadagni. Another daughter of a Brahmin, who stands with the characteristics of those who are established with Manu, is the one who is the creator and the ordainer in the world. The goddess Lakṣmī, the auspicious one residing in the lotus, is indeed their sister. From her, the sons are the horses that traverse the sky. The elder sister of Varuṇa, the goddess Śukrā, was born. Know her son as Bala, and also the divine Surā, the delight of the gods. Due to the mutual consumption of the desires of beings, he is known as the destroyer of all beings. From her, the sons of the dreadful ones, who are always engaged in sinful deeds, are born. There is great fear and also the fear of death, the ender of life.

English: Kākī, Śyenī, Bhāsī, Gṛtarāṣṭrī, and Śukī gave birth; Tāmra, the goddess, bore these five, renowned in the world. Kākī gave birth to Ulūkā, Śyenī to Śyena, and Bhāsī produced Bhāsā and Radhā, the lord of people. Gṛtarāṣṭrī gave birth to Hamsa and Kaṭa-hamsa, and all kinds of Chakravāka; she, the illustrious one, bore them. Śukī, the wise in dharma, gave birth to a son like a parrot, endowed with auspicious qualities and pure attributes. Women, even when born of anger, gave birth to self-born beings; also, the deer and the deer-like ones, and the auspiciously named Hari. Mātā Jīmutha gave birth to Śādūlī, a white one, fragrant, endowed with auspicious attributes, and also to Surasā, the illustrious one. All the offspring were deer, the deer-like sons of the best of men; bears and the deer-like ones, and also the deer. Then, the elephant-like Nāga, Bhadramana, was born; the son of that one was the great elephant. The offspring of the Haras and the swift Vanaras were born; indeed, the sons of the horses are called Bhadra. Then, the illustrious one gave birth to Śādūṭī, lions, and tigers, O Bhārata; there is no doubt about the great fortune of all. Then, the Mātā gave birth to the Mātanga offspring, O lord of men.

English: The white elephant named Dīrghāyus was born. Thus, the daughters of the king were born, including Rohiṇī and others. In Rohiṇī, cows were born, and in Gandhavatī, sons of the charioteers were born. From the son of Surasa, the daughter of Anala was born. English: 248 Ādivaṃśāvataraṇapava Isṛpā was the most powerful among those demons. Pāpajinna was a king known for his renowned valor on earth. 021 Ekacakra was a great demon known for his fame. Prativindhya was also known and became renowned on earth. 022 Virūpākṣa was a Daitya and a great warrior. Citravarma was known and resided on earth as a king. 023 Hara, the best of the demons, was a valiant one. Suvāstu was his name, and he was born as a human. 024 Ahar was a great luminary, the destroyer of the hundred wings. Bāhīka was a king who became renowned on earth. 025 Nicandra and Candravakra were the best of the demons. Muñjakerā was known and was a prosperous king. 026 Nikumbha, undefeated in battle, was born with great wisdom. Bhūma was remembered as the best of the earth's rulers, the lord of the gods. 027 Jhārabha was a great demon among those deities. Porava was a royal sage who became prominent among men. 028 The second was Śalabha among those demons. Prahāda was a Bāhīka who became a king among men. 029 Candra, the best of the Diti, was like the lord of stars. Ṛṣiko was a royal sage who became the best of kings. 030 Mṛtapā was known as the best of the demons.

English: Know the western king, the best of kings. The great and renowned Mahāsura, known as AeA, became a king on earth. The illustrious Mayūra, a great Mahāsura, became the king known as Viśca. The renowned Supaṇa, thus the lesser one, became known as Kālakiirti. The one known as Candrahante, the foremost of those, became the king named Śunaka. The destroyer of the moon, known as Vināśana, became the king named Jānakin. The long-tongued one, known as ALA, was mentioned as a demon. The renowned Kādirāja became the king of the earth. The one who gave birth to the planet, that one was the lion, Candrākamadana. The one known as Krātha became the king of men. The one who was short-lived among sons, the foremost of demons, became the king named Vikṣara. The second Vikṣara, the great king of men, became known as the king of the Pāṃsura kingdom. The renowned Balavīra, who was the best of demons, became the king known as Pauṇḍramatsya.

English: 250 Vṛtra, known as a great demon, was a king named Maṇimān, a royal sage. The one who killed in anger was a demon named Daṇḍa, a king on earth. Another, known as Krodhavadhana, was famous as Daṇḍadhāra, a lord of men. Among the sons of Kālaka, eight kings were born, powerful like lions. In Magadha, there was a glorious king named Jayatsena, a great demon among the eight. The second among them was a glorious king, known as Aparājita. The third was a great king, Mahābāhu, a great demon, known for his strength. The one known as the fourth was a royal sage, famous as Śreṇimāna. The fifth among them was a great demon, known as Mahojā, a great conqueror. The sixth was a wise one, a great demon known as Abhīrura. Abhīrura was known as a royal sage on earth.

English: Samudrasena, the king, was born from them in battle. Renowned, he was knowledgeable about the essence of heat on the earth by the sea. In their time, the great name was Parantapa. He became a king devoted to the welfare of his subjects. A group, known as Krōdhavaśa, was mentioned by the king. Then, the heroes, the kings of the earth, were born. Nandika, Kārṇaveṣṭha, Siddhārtha, Kīṭaka, Suvīra, and Subāhu, and the great hero ASA. Krōdha, the fierce one, the glorious one, and Nīla, the king of the earth. Vīradhāma, Kōravy, and the king of the earth were also known. Dantavakra and Ujaya were also known by name. Rukmī, the king of the Shādūla, and Janamejaya, the king. Āṣāḍha, the wind's speed, and Bhūritejā were also there. Ekalavya, Sumitra, Vāṭadhāna, and Gōmukha. Kārūṣaka, the kings, Kṣemaghūrti, and Śrutāyur, Uddhava, and Vṛhatsena were also there. Kṣemōgrathītha, Kuhara, and the king among Kalingas were renowned. Matimāṁśa, the king of men, and Īśvara were also known. Thus, due to the influence of the group, the royal lineage was established. Born long ago, the great king was Mahākīṭi, the mighty one. He was known as Devakō, the divine king, the lord of the gods.

English: Adivamśāvataraṇapava He was born as the king of men, the chief of the Gandharvas. Know that he was born from the great sage Vṛhaspati, from the lineage of Bhārata, as a part of Droṇa, born from the womb of Bhāradvāja. He, the best among archers, was the most skilled in all weapons, born with great radiance among men. He who is known by the learned as the master of archery and the Vedas, the foremost among them, Droṇa, the slayer of his own kin. From Mahādeva and Antaka, due to desire and anger, the great tormentor was born, who attained unity. Aśvatthāmā, the great hero, the valiant one with lotus-like eyes, was born as a king on earth. The eight Vasus were born in the Ganges as the sons of Śantanu, along with Vasiṣṭha and the sage, by the command of Vāsava. Among them, the foremost was Bhīṣma, the fearless one of the Kurus, wise, a master of the Vedas, and a destroyer of enemies. He who was known as Kṛpa, born from the sage, was a great warrior among the Rudras, born from the assembly of the gods. Know that he was the king of the great charioteers in the Dvāpara age, born as the slayer of enemies.

English: Sātyaki, the one who is united with truth, was born from the Vṛṣṇi lineage. From his side, the enemy of the gods, Maruta, was born. Draupada, the royal sage, also arose from that battle, the best among the human kings in this world, of the lineage of the Sṛbhṛtas. Then know that the one who was made is the king Janādhipa, born from actions that are not to be repeated, the best among the Kṣatriyas. From the group of Marutas, know the one known as the enemy of the gods, the royal sage named Virāṭa, who shines in the other kingdoms. The son of Ariṣṭa, known as Hansa, is renowned; he is the enhancer of the Kuru lineage. Known as Dhṛtarāṣṭra, even from Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana, he is of long arms and great radiance, the king with wise vision. From the anger of his mother, the blind one was born. Here, know the greatly fortunate son, the best among the wise, Vidura, in this world. From the fraction of Kali, the foolish Duryodhana was born, the one who is a great troublemaker among the Kurus. He who is known as the worst among all, the one who caused destruction to the world, is the lowest of men. By whom the great enmity was created, the one who causes destruction to all beings.

English: 254 Adi-vaṃśa-avataraṇa All the brothers of Pota were born among men here, the rulers of Duhśāsana and others, all of Kūrava's deeds. Dumukho and Duhsaha, and others who were not born in the proper way, those who are allies of Duryodhana, know them as the sons of Pota, the best of the Bharatas. Know the king as the royal warrior, Yudhiṣṭhira. Bhīma is the seat of Vāta, the king of the gods. The Ashvins are indeed unparalleled in form on earth. Nakula and Sahadeva are charming to behold. He who is known as Suvaca, the illustrious son of Soma, became the son of Abhimanyu, the son of Arjuna. Know the foremost part to be Dhṛṣṭadyumna, the great charioteer, and Shikhaṇḍi, know him as the rakṣasa. The five sons of Draupadī, know them as the best of the Bharatas, are indeed the divine beings. Karna, who was born with a divine armor, know him as the great charioteer, the best part of the sun. He who is known as Narayana, the eternal god of gods, his part among men was the illustrious Aśvattama. The part of the wrathful one is Baladeva, the mighty one, know Sanatkumāra as the great one among kings.

English: Thus, many portions of the divine beings were born from Vasudeva. The group of waters, which I have mentioned, was born from the command of the wine. Sixteen thousand goddesses were born in the human world, under the protection of Nārāyaṇa. The portion of wealth was born for the purpose of pleasure on the earth, from the daughter of Drupada, who was faultless in the middle of the altar. Not too weak, nor very great, with the fragrance of blue lotus, with lotus-like eyes, beautiful, and of dark complexion. Endowed with all auspicious signs, resembling a jewel, she captivated the hearts of five great men. The goddesses of success and determination, the mothers of the five, were Kuntī and Mādri, and the mind was the daughter of Subala. Thus, the descent of portions of the divine and the asuras, as well as the Gandharvas and Apsaras, has been described. Those kings born on earth, who are fierce in battle, great souls of the Yādavas, were born in a noble lineage. Blessed with fame, wealth, longevity, and victory, this descent of portions should be heard without envy. Hearing of the descent of portions of the divine, Gandharvas, and Rākṣasas.

English: No one was a sinner, nor was there fear of hunger or disease in that region. The people, like tigers among men, were engaged in service and enjoyment. The king, free from fear, was prosperous and powerful. The earth was rich and fertile, yielding crops and fruits. A young hero, endowed with extraordinary strength, lifted Mount Mandara. In the battle of bows and maces, he stood firm on the back of an elephant and a horse. He was equal to Vishnu in glory, like the sun in brilliance, and unmatched in strength. The king, being agreeable, was joyful and prosperous. People were aware of the situation and lived there.

English: Vaerāmpāyana said: Once, the mighty-armed one, possessing great strength, went to the deep forest like a horse on the way. With the heroic bearers of the red-hued weapons, the warriors who were like the hands of the great elephant, And the sounds of lions among the warriors, the sounds of the chariots, and the sounds of the great elephants, The mixed sounds of the roaring and the sounds of the trumpets were heard, and the earth trembled. The great palaces, adorned with the beauty of kings, beheld him, the great warrior, who was like the sun. The enemy was like a serpent, and the women there remembered him as a great hero. This man is a tiger among men, possessing extraordinary valor in battle, whose strength in arms does not allow friends to perish. Thus, speaking words of praise, they, with love, showered flowers upon the king. There, being praised by the best of the Brahmins from all sides, he went forth with great joy into the forest, desiring to hunt deer. Thus ends the narration.

English: Sundaramanujagmuṣṭa, the people of the city then, After that, permitted by the king. With a beautiful chariot, the lord of the earth, Filled the earth with a sound that reached the heavens. Surrounded by a fierce group of animals, Then, the man-tiger, with his retinue, Began to hunt various animals. With arrows reaching far, he struck down the tigers, And pierced them with his arrows. From a distance, the lion among men struck some, And others who approached were cut down. Some with arrows, others with strength, The mighty one, knowledgeable in the art of the mace, Roamed with great prowess. With the sages and the mace in hand, He roamed, striking down the wild animals there. With the king's wondrous valor and the warriors fond of battle, The great beasts of the forest were abandoned.

English: The king entered another forest due to the deer incident. Only one supreme strength, afflicted by hunger and thirst, reached the end of the forest and settled in a great lake. The king, having passed that, reached the excellent hermitage, which generates joy in the mind and is greatly esteemed. Accompanied by the cool breeze, he went to a great lake. With flowering trees, it was indeed filled with sweet sounds raised by the birds. Surrounded by the shade of the flourishing trees, it was adorned with the best of the best. No tree was without flowers, nor was there any fruit or thorns; in that forest, there was no lack of anything. The flowers raised by the birds were indeed very beautiful. Like a garden full of flowers, it was a delightful place. The great bowman entered the excellent forest. There, the flowers were scattered by the wind, and they rained down in a wonderful manner repeatedly. Touched by the sun, the trees there shone with various colored flowers.

English: 262 The birds are crying, accompanied by gentle sounds. There, in that region, many adorned with blooming flowers, surrounded by houses, enhancing the joy of the mind. Seeing this, the great radiance became delighted. The forest, adorned with flowering trees from the interwoven branches, shone like the flag of Indra. The fragrant breeze carried the scent of flowers, as if wandering through the forest, yearning. Thus, the king beheld the forest, endowed with qualities, resembling the lofty flag of the beloved, rising from the riverbank. That forest, protected and filled with well-placed birds, was a delightful ashram. Surrounded by various trees, ablaze with fire, it was filled with ascetics and their followers. With many flowers spread out, it shone exceedingly bright, like a great ocean. Around the lovely river, O king, filled with auspiciousness and desires, it was adorned with numerous flocks of birds, a delightful forest for asceticism. There, the gentle deer, having seen the path, attained joy. He too, the illustrious one, approached the ashram.

English: Devalokapratīkāśa, naturally delightful. He saw the river's hermitage, in the sacred waters, like a mother resting there among all living beings. The bank, embellished by the sacred recitations, And the splendid elephant-like trees, served by the great serpents. He then resolved to enter the hermitage associated with the river. At the beautiful shore of the island, adorned by the Narayana place, like the Ganges. He entered the great abode, filled with the sound of intoxicated elephants. Then the lord of men, approaching the renowned Chaitraratha, Spoke exceedingly virtuous and indescribable words. To see the great sage Kaśyapa and the ascetic Kanva. Having arranged the chariots and the assembly of foot soldiers, He spoke to the army at the forest gate. "I will go to see the sage Viraja, the ascetic. Let it be here until my arrival." Then the lord of men, having reached the renowned Nandana.

English: 266 She, with dark eyes, looked at the king Duṣyanta and quickly spoke, "Welcome!" while honoring him. After offering a seat and water for washing the feet, she asked the king, "What brings you here, O lord of men?" Having properly seated him, she then smiled and said, "What should be done?" The king then spoke to the sweet-tongued maiden, "I have come to worship the great sage Kaṇva; please tell me where he is." Shakuntalā said: "My father has gone to gather fruits from the hermitage; wait a moment, and you will see him coming here." Vairāmpāyana said: The king, seeing the sage, was told by her, and he beheld her, the beautiful maiden with a charming smile. The king spoke of her, adorned with beauty, youth, and austerity, saying, "She is indeed splendid." "Who are you, O beautiful one, and why have you come to the forest? With such beauty and qualities, from where do you shine?"

English: By the tenth, indeed, O auspicious one, my mind is afflicted by you. I wish to know you; please tell me, O beautiful one. Thus addressed, the maiden spoke this sweetly articulated sentence to the king in that hermitage, laughing. I am considered the daughter of the sage Kṇva, O Duḥṣanta, the daughter of the ascetic, the resolute, and the renowned knower of dharma. Duḥṣanta spoke: O great one, indeed, the blessed one is worshipped with offerings. From conduct, dharma should not waver, O steadfast one. How are you the daughter of that one, born of a noble lineage? My doubt is indeed great; you should dispel it for me. Śakuntalā spoke: As this is the arrival of wine, and as this was not before, Listen, O king, to the truth of how I am the daughter of the sage. A certain sage, having come here, urged me regarding my birth. To him, the Lord spoke; listen to that, O king. Once, indeed, the great ascetic Viśvāmitra was performing great austerities. He greatly tormented Śakra, the lord of the gods. By austerity, this one, of radiant valor, would cast me away from my place; Fearing that, Indra then spoke this to me.

English: In ancient times, where there was famine, the sage crossed the river, and then the Lord created the name. In that place, the one who was pleased performed the sacrifice; may you protect the moon from fear, O Lord of the gods. Angered by the lineage of the stars, he who possesses the starry wealth, causes the stars to tremble in the direction of Śravaṇa. I am greatly disturbed by the deeds of that one; may you command me, O Lord, so that I am not burned by the angry one. With brilliance, he would shake the earth with his foot; thus, he would shake the great Meru mountain. How can a girl like me, who is endowed with such austerity and is blazing like fire, desire to be like us? How can one like me, with a blazing face like the fire, be desired? Yama, Soma, and the great sages; all the deities and the universal beings, if they are disturbed by him, why should we not be disturbed by him? Thus spoken by you, how can I go near; I, the king of the gods, should think of protection for me; so that I may wander protected for your sake. May the wind grant me my desire to dwell there; may the god reveal the desired one; may my mind be engaged in that work, with your divine grace as a helper.

English: While enjoying as desired, on a certain day, the sage gave birth to Śakuntalā in the forest of Menakā, with the river Malinī flowing nearby in the beautiful Himalayas. Having abandoned her, the daughter of Menakā followed Malinī, then she went to the assembly of the gods. In the lonely forest, the birds surrounded the lion-like tiger, seeing her lying down. The flesh-eating creatures did not harm the young one, the birds protected the daughter of Menakā there. I went and saw her lying in the lonely wilderness, surrounded by birds. After bringing her, I arranged for her to be a daughter. The one who gives life, whose food is provided by the Jharīraka, In due course, the three fathers were mentioned in the righteous decision, and in the forest, she was protected by the birds. The name of this one is Śakuntā, and I have also done this. Thus, know this daughter of mine, my gentle Śakuntalā, and Śakuntalā thinks of me as her father, without blame. This I declare when asked, O great king, know that I am the son of Kaṇva.

English: The self is the friend of the self; the self is the goal of the self. The gift of the self is indeed the highest virtue. In brief, the eight types of marriages are prescribed by dharma: Brahma, divine, Prajāpati, and Asura. Gandharva, Rākṣasa, and Piśāca are considered the eighth. According to them, Manu, the self-born, declared the rules. TARA: Consider the full Brahman. Know the six types of Kṣatriya marriages as virtuous and blameless. For kings, the Rākṣasa marriage is also mentioned. Among the five, the two types of marriages are noted. The Piśāca and Asura marriages should not be performed under any circumstances. By this method, the path of dharma is understood. In Kṣatriya marriages, whether Gandharva or Rākṣasa, there is no doubt about their distinctness or mixture. O beloved, may you fulfill my desires. Śakuntalā said: If this is the path of dharma and if the self is the lord, grant me, O best of the Pauravas, the time for my request, O lord. Truly, let me promise you that I will speak of you in secret.

English: My son, who is to be born to me, will be after you. O Maharaja, this is the truth; please grant me this. If this is indeed so, may there be a union with me. Thus spoke the king, considering her words. Moreover, I will take you to my pure city. As you have said, O well-formed one, this is indeed the truth. Having spoken thus, the king took her, the blameless one, by the hand and dwelled with her. Trusting her, he repeatedly said, "I will send a well-equipped army to you." I will bring you to my pure residence. Thus, having promised her, the king Janamejaya, thinking in his mind, proceeded towards Kanyakubja. What will the blessed one, endowed with austerity, do upon hearing this? Thus contemplating, he entered his own city. After a moment, however, Kanva also arrived at the hermitage, but Shakuntala did not go to her father. Then, knowing her, Kanva, the great ascetic with divine knowledge, spoke to her with joy.

English: You have today, O king, been brought to me by your lineage. The Kṣatriya's marriage with a Gandharva is indeed considered the best. Then the great soul, Duḥṣanta, the best of men, approached the one whom you serve, Śakuntalā. The great soul born in this world is your son, O mighty one, who will enjoy the earth created by the ocean's feet. Moreover, the wheel of that great soul, who is intent on his purpose, will always remain unopposed like a wheel. Then, after washing her feet, she spoke to the resting sage, having placed the burden and fruits nearby. To him, who is my husband, that Duḥṣanta, the best of men, you should grant your favor. I am indeed pleased with him for your sake, O one of excellent qualities; accept the boon that I desire for him. Then, he chose righteousness, as well as the kingdom, for the sake of the welfare of the Pauravas, desiring the good of Duḥṣanta.

English: Sārva-daman, the prince, attained (his goal) with valor and strength. He was indeed a great man, destined for kingship, like Shakuntalā. Knowing this, Kaṇva spoke to Rishyaśṛṅga, "Quickly bring Shakuntalā and her son from the hermitage." Today, he shall be presented with all auspicious signs. A long stay of women does not please relatives; let us not delay. Thus instructed, they all quickly set out, bringing Shakuntalā and her son, accompanied by elephants. Taking the son, the lotus-eyed one, the auspicious one approached Dushyanta. Having approached the king, she entered with her son, like the young sun. After honoring him appropriately, Shakuntalā said, "This son of yours, O king, should be crowned as the future king." Indeed, this son, born of you, O king, is like a divine being. As previously arranged, this is the time you have set.

English: 278 Saṃbhavapava Remember, O great one, the path to the hermitage of Kaṇva. Upon hearing that statement, the king, even while remembering, said, "I do not remember you, O wicked ascetic." I do not recall the connection of desires with you. Go or stay, do as you wish. Freed from service, the noble lady, bashful and thoughtful, stood still, as if struck by sorrow. The fiery-eyed one, with lips quivering, cast a sidelong glance, as if to slay. Taking the form of a house, she was filled with anger, and at that time, she held the gathered radiance of austerity. After contemplating for a moment, afflicted by sorrow, she looked at her husband, angry. Knowing, O great king, why do you speak thus? I do not know, nor am I detached, just like any other mortal. Here, your heart knows the truth of both truth and falsehood. You are indeed a witness to the welfare of the self. He who perceives the self differently, what sin has he not committed, like a thief who steals the self? You think, "I am one," yet you do not know the ancient sage's heart. He who knows the actions of sin, you cause him distress.

English: He thinks that by committing sin, no one will say anything to him. The gods know him, as does the inner man. The sun, moon, wind, fire, earth, water, and Yama. Day and night, and the twilight; they know the conduct of a man. Yama, the son of Vivasvat, drives away the sinful deeds. He is the witness of actions, residing in the heart, and is pleased with the knower of the field. He is not pleased with the wicked man. Yama drives away the sinful deeds of that man. One who belittles himself, thinking otherwise, the gods do not grant him prosperity, even if he is self-sufficient. Do not abandon me, who is devoted to my husband. Why do you not move me, who is present? Why do you treat me like a common person in the assembly? Indeed, I am not a mere shadow; do you not hear me? If you do not fulfill the request of this one who is asking, O Duḥṣanta, you will reap the consequences today. The husband of the wife is born again from him. The poets know that the wife is called 'wife' because of her husband. From the one who has come, a son is born. He saves the ancestors from the lineage of the departed.

English: The son who brings prosperity to his father from hell is called a son, as stated by the self-born. The sister who is skilled in the household, the sister who is fruitful, the sister who is devoted to her husband, the sister who is chaste. The sister is the best friend of a man, the root of the threefold, and a friend of the one who is about to die. Those who are active and engaged in the household are joyful, and those who are endowed with wives are blessed. Friends who speak sweetly arise in solitude, while fathers are engaged in household duties, and mothers are in distress. Even in the forests, a man on his path finds rest; he who is trustworthy finds a higher destination. Even when wandering, the one who is single-minded in devotion to her husband always follows him. The first wife waits for her husband after death, and after the deceased husband, she follows the virtuous. For this reason, O King, the acquisition of a husband is desired, for what one attains in this world and the next is through the husband. A son born of one's own self is called a son; therefore, a man should tread the path of his mother as if it were a thread. The son born of the sister is seen as one's own face.

English: The one who is born is sent to heaven, having performed virtuous deeds. Burning with mental anguish, afflicted by diseases, men are distressed. Even if well-connected, a wise man should not speak unpleasant words, considering love, affection, and righteousness. The Kṣatriya born of oneself is eternal virtue, O Rāma. What power do the sages have over the offspring of Rāma? When the son is tightly bound by the mother's embrace, what more can be expected from the father? You, having attained this son of your desire, why do you belittle him with disdain? Ants carry their own eggs; they do not break them. How can you not carry your own son? Neither the garments, nor Rāma, nor the touch of happiness is the same as the touch of a son. The brāhmaṇa is the best among bipeds, the cow is the best among quadrupeds, and the son is the best among those who are worthy. May this son, dear to you, touch you. There is no touch more pleasurable than that of a son. In three full years, I have become this child, O King, the destroyer of your sorrow.

English: 282 Having been struck by the hundred-voiced Vājimedha, Thus spoke the charioteer to me in the sky before. Indeed, having raised the name, they have gone to Rāma's abode out of sorrow; People do not greet the sons of Mūdha. Even in the Vedas, the twice-born speak this mantra; Your son, O king, is also known as the gem of birth. From the heart, you are born from the womb; Your soul is the name of the son, and he lives through the autumn night. For I am indeed dependent on you, and my offspring is also eternal; Therefore, you live, my calf, happily for a hundred autumns. This one is born from your limbs, another man from a man; Like a lotus in the lake, I have a second son. As the sacrificial fire is kindled, so this one born from you is unique; You are the one who has been made. Indeed, having been pursued by the deer, I was approached, O king, by the maiden in my father's hermitage. Uvi, Pūvachitti, and Sahajanyā, along with Menakā; Viśvāchī and Ghṛtācī, the six foremost of the Apsarases. Among them, I, named Menakā, the Apsarā born from the outer womb, Having reached the heavens, gave birth to the world from Viśvāmitra. Born of the pure.

English: She, the celestial nymph Menakā, gave birth to me in the Himalayas. Having been cast away, I now dwell like a forsaken child. What sin did I commit in my previous birth, that I was abandoned by my kin in childhood and now by you? Having been forsaken by you, I shall return to my hermitage. However, I cannot abandon this path, nor my child. Duṣyanta said: I do not recognize you as my son, O Śakuntalā. Who will believe the words of a woman who speaks untruths? Menakā, your mother, is without compassion, having been cast away by the Himalayas like a flower. Your father, a Kṣatriya, is also without compassion, O Śakuntalā. Viśvāmitra, devoted to desire, is outside the fold. Your father is the best among the celestial nymphs, and the great sage. Why do you claim to be of their lineage? This statement is untrustworthy, as it is spoken in anger. Let the wicked ascetic come to me, if he dares. O great sage, you are like a celestial nymph, and Menakā is indeed so. Your son is of great stature, yet he has been brought low by a mere curse. How can he rise again?

English: When one sees a distorted face, he recognizes the other, not the self, as a person. The one endowed with great beauty does not despise anything; the one who speaks sweetly is indeed a charmer here. The foolish, upon hearing the words of men, both auspicious and inauspicious, accepts the inauspicious word like a pig accepts excrement. The wise, upon hearing the words of men, both auspicious and inauspicious, accepts the auspicious word like a swan accepts milk from water. One who speaks ill of others suffers, just as a wicked person is pleased when speaking ill of others. Respectfully greeting the elders, the good ones go to rest; thus, one who is good becomes at peace. Those who live happily are ignorant of faults, while the foolish are burdened by faults. Where the good ones are spoken of by others, they call them thus. Therefore, there is nothing more laughable than a little joke; where the wicked are, the wicked themselves speak. A person who is steadfast in truth and righteousness, even if he is an atheist, fights; what then of the theist? One who belittles his own son, having produced him himself, the gods fear him, and he does not attain the worlds.

English: 286 The ancestors indeed said to the son about the establishment of the family lineage: One should not abandon a son who is the best among the worthy. The lord of dreams, having bound five, spoke to Manu about the various letters that arose from the offerings. The sons, who are the bonds of affection for the minds of men, protect the fathers from the hellish births. You, O king, should not abandon your son; while upholding truth and righteousness, O ruler of the earth. O lion among kings, you are not unworthy. Better than this, better than that, better than the four, is the truth, the son of a hundred. A thousand horse sacrifices and truth have been upheld by you; indeed, truth is the most distinguished among the horse sacrifices. The acquisition of all Vedas and the immersion in sacred waters; When speaking truth, O king, it may or may not be equal. There is no dharma greater than truth, nor is there anything superior to truth; Indeed, nothing is more intense than falsehood here. O king, truth is the supreme Brahman, and truth is the ultimate time. Do not abandon the time, O king; may truth be united with you. If you do not believe in falsehood, then you do not believe in yourself. I shall go, for there is no connection with one like you. The pure possibility.

English: In you, O Duṣanta, even without, the son of mine will protect this maiden. Thus spoke the sage Vērāmpāyana. Having said this, Śakuntalā stood firm. Then, in the sky, the disembodied voice spoke to Duṣanta. The priest, the purohita, then covered the sacrificial offering. Well, the son born of the father and mother is indeed he. O Duṣanta, do not abandon Śakuntalā, your son. The son elevates the body, O king, from the death of the man. And you, O Śakuntalā, speak the truth about the bearer of the womb. The wife gives birth to a son, made of her own body in two ways. Therefore, O king, take Śakuntalā as your wife. This is the birth of a son, who is to be abandoned, living as a living being. O Porava, bear the great-souled Śakuntalā, the son of Duṣanta. This is the name you have given, therefore, let your son be named Bharata. Hearing this, King Porava, having been struck by the words of the divine messenger, spoke to the purohita and the ministers. Let those who hear this know the words of the divine messenger. I too know this son of mine.
