English: If I were to take this son, there would indeed be doubt in the world; thus, he would not be pure. Then the king, opposing him, joyfully and happily accepted that son from the divine messenger. Embracing him with affection, he fondly held him. Honored and praised by the servants, he was filled with great joy, the king. The righteous one, knowing the dharma, worshipped that mother. The king then spoke to her with comforting words. This relationship has been established in the world through you; therefore, this has been considered by me, O goddess. The world thinks you are connected; this son is indeed established in the kingdom, thus I have considered it. Whatever you have said in anger, dear one, I have taken it as dear to me. Thus, the king, having consoled the beloved queen, worshipped her with clothing and food. Then the king, Dushyanta, named the son Shakuntala and anointed him as the crown prince. Thus, the great soul's wheel began to turn.

English: Shining, divine, unconquered, and the great source of the world's sound. Having defeated the kings, he acted like a speaker. He roamed and attained the supreme fame of the virtuous. The king was a powerful Chakravartin, like the son of the Earth. He performed many great sacrifices like the Marutapati. Kṇva performed a sacrifice for him, like Dakṣa, the great and capable. He obtained the name Śrīmaṅgovitata, having performed the horse sacrifice. In which Kṇva gave a thousand lotuses to Bharata. From Bharata, the Bharati Kīrti, by which this Bharata lineage is known. Others who are also known as Bharata are the Puravas. Indeed, many great kings of divine nature arose from Bharata. Whose countless names are known to all. I will sing of them according to their prominence, O Bharata. The great fortunate ones, divine beings, devoted to truth.

English: The son of Dākṣāyaṇī, who is one of the thirteen, was born to Kaśyapa. The sons of Vivasvat, endowed with strength, include Indra and others. From Vivasvat was born Yama, the lord of the dead. Mātanga, the son of Yama, was also born, O king. From Mātanga was born the wise Manu, the lord. From Manu's lineage, the human race became well-known. From the Brahmins and Kṣatriyas, the human beings emerged. At that time, O king, they were united with external Kṣatriyas. The human beings of the Brahmin class held the Vedas. Vena, Dhṛṣṇu, and others were also born, as well as the eighth Milā. The Pṛṣadhra and others are said to be Kṣatriyas, devoted to their duty. From Nabhāga, the mighty sons of Manu were born. Fifty sons of Manu were born, and others also appeared on earth. Due to mutual distinction, they all perished, as we have heard. From Purūravas, the wise one reached the sky. Thus, she became his mother, and his father, indeed, we have heard.

English: Purūravāha, surrounded by the thirteen seas and islands, is a great hero with a glorious name. In his fury, he engaged in battle with the brāhmaṇas and seized their wealth. Sanatkumāra approached the king from the outer world and then he took him back, but he did not accept him. Then, he was cursed by the great sages and immediately became lost due to the power of greed and intoxication. He, indeed, was a great being residing in the fragrance, along with the earth, and he brought forth actions for the sake of the righteous. Six sons were born to him, including the mighty Ayu. Tṛṭāyu, Vanāyu, and Śrutāyu were among the sons. Nahuṣa, the aged and wise, is said to have sons named Raji and Rambhamana. Nahuṣa, the son of Ayu, is wise and possesses true valor, ruling the earth with great dharma. Nahuṣa struck down the fathers, gods, sages, brāhmaṇas, and the celestial beings, as well as the demons. After killing the band of robbers, he made the sages ride on his back like cattle. He caused the kingship to be established, overpowering the celestial beings. Thus, the pure one was born.

English: In valor, in austerity, and in prowess, Yayāti, the son of Nahusha, generated six sons. Yayāti, the king, was of true valor. He struck the earth with various weapons. With great effort, he always honored his father and the moon. Yayāti, undefeated, had sons of great prowess. From the celestial path, great kings were born, including Jhaminṣṭhā. From the celestial path, Yadu, Tuvansu, and others were born, as well as Purus and Śarmishṭhā. He ruled the subjects with righteousness for many years, and Nahusha, afflicted by old age, became a beautiful woman. The king, overwhelmed by old age, spoke to his sons: "O Yadu, Puru, and others, I wish to enjoy youth with young women." The son, Devayānī, said: "What is your work, O father, that you wish to do in youth?" Yayāti replied: "Let old age take me, and I will enjoy the pleasures of youth."

English: 294 Saṃbhavapava In the long sacrifice, While performing, the sage was cursed by the thief. PITA: My son is deprived by him. Let my body rule the kingdom alone. Then, the king, having anointed Purū, Eventually approached the great virtue of dharma.

English: 296 Saṃbhavapava The demons, hiding their own, did not revive the gods in the battle. The noble-minded Bṛhaspati did not revive them. Indeed, the wise do not know the knowledge that the poets know, the life-giving one; thus the gods fell into despair. Then the gods, having approached the poet, said to the eldest son of Bṛhaspati: "Those who are devoted, may you grant us excellent assistance, for the knowledge of glory resides in the one of immense radiance." "Bring that quickly, O Śukra, you will be the divider of fortune." "Near Vṛṣapava, a brāhmaṇa can protect the demons; there he does not protect the demons." "You are capable of worshipping that great soul's beloved daughter, the divine one, the poet of old." "There is no one else capable of worshipping you, except for the one skilled in the arts and the one who is restrained." "In the divine vehicle, indeed, in the state of satisfaction, you will surely attain that knowledge." Then, the son of Bṛhaspati, Kaca, proceeded. Having been summoned by the gods, he quickly went to the city of the demon king, and there he spoke to Śukra.

English: The wise one, having reviewed the situation, received knowledge from the guru. The learned one, having broken the womb, emerged. The beautiful Kaco, like the moon in the month of Phalguna, shone in the south. The Brahmin, having fallen, was raised by the Brahmanic energy. Having attained that perfected knowledge, Kaco then addressed the guru. Those who do not honor the guru, the giver of truth, will fall into disgrace. Sūrapāna (intoxicating drink) led to a dreadful situation; Kaco, having been seen, was also affected by the drink. The great one, having risen in anger, sought to punish the one who had caused the offense. This verse speaks against the drinking of intoxicating substances. The foolish Brahmin, from now on, who drinks out of delusion, will be condemned as a killer of Brahmins. I have established a limit for the wise Brahmins in all worlds. May all the gods and the wise Brahmins listen to the words of the great one. Having spoken this, the great one, the inexhaustible treasure of the sages, called the confused beings and spoke to them. I tell you, foolish demons, that the perfected Kaco will remain under my protection.

English: You are always worshipped, O daughter of the guru, by the beloved of the great soul Bhāgavata, with my life. As my father, the revered Śukra, weeps for me, you do not speak to me in the same way. The daughter of the guru said: You are not the son of my father, but you are worthy of respect and worship, O best of the brāhmaṇas. When the demons are being killed, remember the love that has been with you from that time onward. You know my supreme devotion in friendship and affection; you do not deserve to abandon me, who is innocent in devotion. Kacha said: In the unassigned duty, you are leading me in the auspicious vow. Be gracious, O auspicious one, for I am your disciple. Where you, O wide-eyed one, reside with a face like the moon, there I, O auspicious one, have dwelled in the poem's beauty. Sister, you have spoken thus to me, O auspicious-faced one; I am happy to have dwelled there, and my mind does not feel anger. I will ask you, and I will go on my path to auspiciousness; I am steadfast in the matter of dharma without opposition.

English: The ever-vigilant one, worship my guru. Devayāni said: If you are urged to reject me for the sake of dharma, desire, and wealth, then surely this knowledge of yours will not attain success. Kacha replied: As the guru's daughter, I speak without fault. Having been permitted by the guru, let this curse be as you wish. I, Devayāni, am not worthy of this curse, as I am not to be seized by desire today. Therefore, the desire that is not fulfilled will not be so in the future. No son of a sage will ever take your hand. Your knowledge will not succeed, as you have spoken to me thus. I will teach that which will indeed succeed in knowledge. Thus spoke the best of the twice-born, Kacha, to Devayāni, and swiftly went to the three-story mansion. Seeing him arrive, the gods, led by Indra, along with Brihaspati, honored him with great delight. What you have spoken to us is indeed wonderful.

English: Why do you, O Tel, become angry with me? For one who is devoid of good conduct, there will be no benefit for you. Śarmiṣṭhā said: Your father, who is seated and who is the father of my father, constantly praises and worships him, standing humbly below. You, O daughter, when asked, do not accept the praise offered to me, though I am being praised. Without weapons, you are agitated, O beggar; you will not receive a rescuer, for I do not consider you. Veraṁpāyana said: Having reached the divine abode, you are now powerful and reside there; then, having thrown into the well, he returned to his own city. Realizing that she was killed, the sinful one did not look back at the one who was filled with anger and speed. Then, the son of Nahuṣa, weary and thirsty, having entered that land, was exhausted and longing for water. He, Nahuṣa, seeing the water of the well, approached it. He asked the girl, who was like a celestial maiden, having consoled her, the best of kings, with a very sweet voice. The auspicious one.

English: What is your name, O copper-fingered, dark one with beautiful gem-like curls? Why do you meditate for a long time, O clever one, with a sharp arrow? How did you fall into this pit surrounded by grass, O brave one? Whose daughter are you? Tell me, O well-spoken one. Devayāna said: He who raises the fallen with knowledge, I am surely the daughter of Śukra, he does not understand me. This is my right hand, O king, with a copper-fingered nail. Lift me up, for you are indeed my choice. I know you, calm, full of valor and fame. Therefore, lift me up from this pit, O swan. Verāmpāyana said: Then, knowing the Brahmin woman, the son of Nahuṣa took her by the right hand and lifted her from the pit. If the king lifts her quickly from the pit, after calling the beautiful one, Yayāti went to his own city. Devayāna said: Quickly go to the house of the potter and tell my father everything. For now, I cannot enter the city of Vṛṣapavāṇa.

English: The sage Vērāmpāyana said: She, having quickly gone to the abode of the demon Ghūṇikā, spoke this poem, her mind filled with confusion. O great sage, tell me, was Devayānī killed in the forest? Hearing that his daughter was killed there, the poet, filled with sorrow, quickly sought his daughter in the forest. The poet, having embraced his daughter Devayānī in the forest, spoke sorrowfully. All people are bound by their own faults in happiness and sorrow. I think you have a bad character, for this is the punishment given. Devayānī said: Let there be or not be my release, listen to my plea. Truly, she said, you are the song of the demons. Thus speaks me, Śarmiṣṭhā, the daughter of Vṛṣapavāṇa, with harsh and sharp words, her eyes red like blood. When you are praised, O daughter, you do not accept the offerings of those who ask for you, nor do you accept the offerings of those who are being praised. Thus spoke Śarmiṣṭhā, the daughter of Vṛṣapavāṇa.

English: As a serpent sheds its skin, so is that man called. He who controls anger, who endures harsh words, and who, though heated, does not burn, gives the vessel of the essence. He who sacrifices tirelessly, month after month, is not more wrathful than the two of them. If the boys act without consciousness, let not the wise one act according to them; they do not know strength and weakness. The divine one spoke. I know, dear, even the young ones, what is here and what is beyond. In non-anger and in harshness, the Veda also knows strength and weakness. One should not tolerate the behavior of the unworthy, desiring to consume. Therefore, I do not like to dwell in the company of the unworthy. Men who criticize others based on their conduct and birth should not dwell among kings seeking welfare, for they are of sinful intellect. Those who recognize him based on conduct and birth should dwell among the good; that dwelling is said to be the best. The speech that is harsh and terrible, like the curse of a daughter, is not more difficult than this in the three worlds. He who worships the radiant glory of the dream, devoid of glory, drinks the essence. The pure one is born.

English: With a thousand maidservants, at that time with Rāma, she arrived there and roamed as she pleased. Accompanied by those friends, she was adorned with all her desires. Playing and enjoying, they drank the sweet honey and ate various foods and fruits. Then King Nāhuṣa, desiring to hunt, reached that very land, weary and seeking water. He saw Devayānī and the maidens, drinking and adorned with divine ornaments. He saw Devayānī seated, pure-smiling, unmatched in beauty among those maidens. Yayāti spoke. I ask you, O maiden, surrounded by a thousand maidens, about the lineage and names of the horses. Devayānī replied, "I will tell you my words, O king. Know that Śuka is the son of the guru of the demons." And this maidservant of mine, where I am, is the one who goes.

English: I am under your control, O friend, may you be my protector along with your wife, from the two thousand maidens. Yayāti said: O beautiful one, I do not deserve you, for kings are indeed unwed in your divine lineage. Devayānī said: The Kṣatriya is created by Brahman, and the Kṣatriya is united with Brahman. The sage and the sage's son, O Nahuṣa, carry me. Yayāti said: Though born from a single body, the different castes are like horses; the Brahmin is indeed the best among them. Devayānī said: The duty of the hand was not served by Nahuṣa in the past; I choose you, O hero, I take you. How can another man touch the hand of my strong-minded one, when it was taken by the sage's son or by you, O sage? Yayāti said: The learned man, like a furious snake, is more difficult to approach than a man who knows.

English: The gods spoke. How can one who is a great sage, with a blazing face, be more difficult to overcome? Thus spoke the best of men. Yayāti said: One who is a great sage kills even the unkillable. The sage, angered, destroys entire kingdoms. The great sage said: Therefore, my mind is firm on this matter. Thus, I will not marry you, O auspicious one, as my father has not given you. The gods spoke: You should carry me, O king, as I am bound by you. There is no fear for one who has been given and accepted. Verāmpāyana said: Quickly, the gods sent the message to the father. Hearing this, the Bharadvāja approached the king. Yayāti, the king of the earth, arrived and worshipped the Brahmin, bowing down with folded hands. The gods spoke: O king, Nahusha has taken my hand in marriage. Salutations to you, grant me, for I do not choose another husband in this world.

English: Śukra said: "By this woman, O hero, you are bound; accept this queen given by me, the daughter of Nahuṣa." Yayāti said: "May sin not touch me, O great one; I declare that you are outside the realm of sin." Śukra said: "I release you from sin; choose as you wish. In this marriage, I do not wish to bring you sin." "With your wife, the virtuous Devayānī, you will attain unparalleled happiness." "And this maiden, your daughter, is a precious gem; may you always honor her, O king." Thus addressed, Yayāti circumambulated Śukra and, pleased, returned to his city, having received permission from the great soul.

English: Thus, even when faced with difficulty, I do not hesitate to speak falsely. Rāma said: The king, having gathered, spoke: "He who is a husband is also a friend; they say that marriage is equal, you are my husband in friendship." Yayāti said: "My vow is that something should be given when asked; you too desire me, tell me what you wish me to do." Śarmiṣṭhā said: "By unrighteousness, you lead me away from righteousness; I, who have offspring from you, should uphold the highest dharma in the world." Three are indeed the wealthy, O king: a brother, a servant, and a son; whatever they attain, that is your wealth. I am the daughter of the gods, and I am your Bhārgavī; therefore, O king, serve me in the matter of marriage. Vairāmpāyana said: Thus addressed, the king, having acknowledged the truth, worshipped the goddess and upheld dharma. Having gathered and obtaining as desired, they worshipped each other and departed happily as they came.

English: Thus, the king asked the princes, "What is your lineage, O sons of the Brahmin father?" I wish to hear the truth from you. They expressed their doubts about the best of kings, and the children revealed their mother. Having spoken thus, they approached the king, but he did not rejoice at that time. The children then wept. The affection of those children was directed towards the king, and the wise goddess spoke this truth: "Why should I fear you, who have taken refuge in the wicked Asura?" Śarmiṣṭhā said: "What the sage has said is true, O charming one. I do not fear you, as I walk in accordance with righteousness and dharma." "Indeed, you are the king, and I was chosen by you. In truth, one becomes glorious through dharma." "You are worthy of my respect, and you are the elder and superior Brahmin. You are also the most worshipful to me; do you not know this?"

English: Hearing his words, Devayānī said: "O King, I will not stay here; you have done me harm." Seeing the dark one suddenly rise, with tearful eyes, the distressed Kāvya hastily set out. The king, confused, followed her from behind, but he did not lower his angered, red eyes. The beautiful-eyed queen, though unclean, soon arrived at the place of Kāvya. She stood before her father, having seen him, and immediately, Yayāti worshipped the sage. Devayānī spoke: "By unrighteousness, righteousness is conquered; I am the daughter of Vṛṣapavāṇa, born of a lowly mother." "Three sons were born to this king Yayāti; I tell you, O father, that I have two sons." "This king, known as Dharmajña, is the son of Bṛhugu; I will tell you this tale of Kāvya." Śukra said: "The righteous king, who does not act unrighteously, will soon age you, O king."

English: Yayāti said: O Lord, when I am requesting the season, I do not have any other intention. This has been done by me for the daughter of the king of demons. When a man is requested for the season, he does not give it; he is said to be a killer of the fetus, according to the sages here. The one who is desired by the beautiful Rad, when requested in secret, does not come forth, and he is said to be a killer of the fetus in righteousness. Considering these reasons, I, being frightened by the fear of unrighteousness, approached Shamiṣṭā. Shukra said: Indeed, I will observe you; you are under my control, O king. In righteousness, falsehood becomes theft, and thus it is not the way of Nahuṣa. Vairāmpāyana said: Cursed, Yayāti, the son of Nahusha, then abandoned his youth and immediately became old. Yayāti said: I am unsatisfied with youth; O Brahman, grant me favor in the path of the gods; do not let me be known.

English: I will enjoy the pleasures of youth with you. Having given up my youth, I will again become myself, along with old age and sin. Yayāti said: The wretched one, weakened by old age, saw the body that was full of life. Having been overwhelmed in the act, I do not desire that old age, along with the companions. Yayāti said: Since you do not grant me the youth that has arisen from my heart, your subjects will suffer as a result of the kingdom. You should take back your sin along with old age. I will enjoy the pleasures of youth, O son. Having given up my youth, I will again become myself, along with old age and sin. Yayāti said: I do not desire old age, O father, which is the destroyer of the pleasures of enjoyment and the killer of intellect and life. Yayāti said:

English: You do not grant me my own age, which has arisen from my heart. Therefore, your beloved desire will not be fulfilled. In the conduct of the wicked, in the actions of the foolish, you will become a foolish king. In the attachment to the teacher's house, in the lowly births, you will arise in the sinful conduct of animals. Thus spoke Vērāmpāyana. Thus, Yayāti, having addressed his son, spoke this word. Therefore, you should take the form that destroys old age, and give me back my youth. After a full thousand years, I will give back my youth, and I will take back my own, along with old age. Nārada spoke: Neither an elephant, nor a chariot, nor a horse, nor a woman, will be desired by the one who is old. Yayāti spoke: You do not grant me my own age, which has arisen from my heart. Therefore, your beloved desire will not be fulfilled. Where the celestial beings will always be, there will be a future.

English: You will attain the title of King Bhoja there. You should overcome the sin along with old age. I will wander for a thousand years in your youth. English: 004 The subjects, by righteousness, pleased Gal as they should. Yayāti ruled like Indra himself. 006 The king, a lion among men, youthful and in the realm of pleasures, enjoyed the highest happiness without opposition to righteousness. 007 Having attained auspicious desires, afflicted and distressed, the man-king remembered the thousand years of rain. 008 Counting, the wise one, strong in virtue, considered the full moon and spoke to Pūra. 009 As desired, with enthusiasm, and at the right time, the pleasures of youth were served to me by you, my son. 010 I am pleased, O auspicious one, accept this from your youth. And also accept this kingdom, for you are indeed my beloved son. 011 Then, King Yayāti, desiring youth, Pūra regained his own youth. 012 The Brahmins, led by the chief, spoke this word to the king, desiring to anoint Pūra, the younger son. 013 How, O Lord, will you give the kingdom to Pūra, the eldest son of Śukra, surpassing Yadu? 014 Your eldest son Yadu was born, and after him, Pūra, the son of Dhr̥tadhvaja, and then Pūra again.

English: How can a younger one claim the kingdom by surpassing the elder? This I convey to you, O Dharma. Yayāti said: Let the Brahmins listen to my words: the kingdom should never be given to the elder in any way. The elder, by Yadu's command, has not been upheld; he who is unfavorable to the glory of the father is not considered a son by the wise. The son who is angry at the words of the parents and is righteous is like a son to the father and mother. I, being disregarded, and you too, have been greatly disregarded by me. My word has been fulfilled, and especially honored; my younger heir, by whom I am held, is old. My desire has been fulfilled by the son in the form of a fulfillment. A boon given by Śukra, and by the poet himself, the son who follows you is the king of the earth. I request you thus: let Pūru be anointed as king. The nature spoke: He who is endowed with virtues and always beneficial to the parents is born pure.

English: The Brahmana, having lived in the forest, was content with fruits and roots, as he had gone to CMA. He, having gone to the abode of the gods, lived happily, but was again struck down by Śakra, not too long after. Having fallen, he was cast down to the earth, and he remained in the sky, as I have said. Thus, it is said that he again went to heaven, along with the king Vasumata and the valiant eight. Having gathered together with the assembly of the Kitsa, Janamejaya spoke. By whose actions did that king of the earth attain heaven again? I wish to hear all this in detail. You are speaking in the presence of the Brahmanas, O Brahmana. He was like the king of the gods, Yayāti, the lord of the earth, the enhancer of the Kuru dynasty, and like the shining sun. I wish to hear the story of his extensive fame and true glory, both here and in heaven. Vaśaṁpāyana said: Indeed, I shall tell you the story of Yayāti's descendants. Thus ends the translation.

English: 340 Saṃbhavapava Yayāti said: O king, if I have lost my strength due to the fragrance of the celestial forest, I wish to fall among the virtuous, devoid of the heavenly realm. 004 Indra said: O king, you have fallen among the virtuous; you have attained a higher status where you are honored. Knowing this, O Yayāti, you should not be disrespected by the virtuous. 005 Vairāmpāyana said: Then, having abandoned the celestial king's company, Yayāti, who had fallen, was addressed by the best of kings, who was a protector of righteousness. 006 Who are you, O youth, resembling Vāsava? You shine with your own brilliance like the sun. You have fallen into the darkness of the ocean; you are the foremost among the celestial beings. 007 And you, having fallen from the path of the sun, are accompanied by countless beings. Is it not true that all are bewildered, wondering why you have fallen? 008 And you, stationed on the divine path, are like the powerful forms of Indra and Viṣṇu. Today, all of us are eager to know the truth about you. 009 We cannot question you directly, nor do you ask us who we are. We inquire about you, desiring to know your form and the reason for your arrival. 010 Fear and sorrow should leave you; abandon the illusion of despair, O lord resembling the divine Indra. Your presence among the virtuous is indeed a source of strength. 011 The virtuous have a place in the realm of happiness, like the celestial beings among the righteous.

English: 342 Saṃbhavapava In various forms, many beings exist in the world; under the control of the gods, their efforts are lost. A wise person, having attained that, is not disturbed; considering it is destined, they remain steadfast. 006 If a being experiences happiness or even suffering; it is under divine control, not by their own effort. Therefore, thinking it is destined, a strong person should neither be disturbed nor rejoice at any time. 007 In suffering, they should not be scorched, nor should they rejoice in happiness; a wise person should remain equanimous. Considering it is destined, they should neither be disturbed nor rejoice at any time. 008 In fear, I am not deluded; at any time, there is no mental anguish for me. As the creator arranges for me in the world; thus, I think I will surely be. 009 Born from sweat, born from eggs, and those like serpents, insects, and fish; similarly, the grass and all beings worship their own nature in the destruction of destiny. 010 The transient nature of happiness and suffering; why should I endure suffering? What should I do, and what should I perform to not be scorched? Therefore, I will conquer suffering, being vigilant. 011 HER spoke II Those worlds that are primarily ruled by kings; which you have enjoyed, and how time is; O king, do not hide anything from me, as you are indeed knowledgeable. 012 Yayāti spoke: I am a king here, ruling over the earth; from there, I have attained great victory over the worlds. I remained there for a thousand years; then I approached the supreme world. 013 Then, I reached the beautiful city; extending a hundred yojanas. I remained there for a thousand years; then I approached the supreme world. 014

English: 344 Saṃbhavapava What is the reason for the predominance of the Kṛta age; having abandoned the earth, they wander? 001 Yayāti said: The relatives, friends, and kin of a person, when wealth diminishes; abandon the man whose merit has diminished, just as the gods abandon a man of diminished merit. 002 HER said II How do those of diminished merit come to be; my mind is exceedingly disturbed here? What is special about those who go to which abode; that is beyond my understanding. 003 Yayāti said: These men fall into this hell; all the celestial beings are distressed. They, like the Kṛtaghna, are diminished and do not attain growth. 004 Therefore, this action is to be avoided by men; it is wicked and to be condemned. I have told you, O king, if you ask now, what shall I say to you? 005 HER said II When those with sharp teeth are accompanied by age; how do the vultures and the sharp-beaked insects come to be? How do they come to be, how did they become; I do not hear of any other hell. 006 Yayāti said: Having risen from the body, they wander in the earth; these men fall into this hell; they do not see the many insects. 007 Sixty thousand fall in the sky; and eighty in the course of a year.

English: The beings strike the falling one; Bhīma, the mighty, the sharp-toothed demons. The sage spoke: By what means do they strike the falling one; Bhīma, the mighty, the sharp-toothed demons? How do they exist, how do they come to be; how do they become beings in the womb? Yayāti spoke: The essence, the seed, is adorned with flowers and fruits; it is created by that person. That essence, when it falls, is taken by the earth; it approaches the great being there. Plants and herbs enter; water, air, and the earth, as well as the sky. All beings, both four-footed and two-footed, thus become beings in the womb. HER spoke II Another womb is created here; or does it go by its own desire? Being afflicted, the human womb is created; tell me, I seek to understand this. From the body of the being, and the like, who gives the name to the eyes and ears? This truth, tell me all of it, being asked; I consider you, O father, to be the knower of the field. Yayāti spoke: The wind raises the great womb; the dead essence is adorned with the nectar of flowers. There, the essence, having the right to the subtle elements, gradually nourishes the womb here. Born, with limbs taken, a man with six faces; he hears the sound here with his ears. He sees all forms with his eyes.

English: 276 Saṃbhavapava By life, one perceives fragrance through the tongue; touch is felt through the skin, and the mind knows the essence. Thus, understand the gathering of the eight; of the great-souled, the life-breath resides in the body. 016 HER spoke II That man who is established, whether he gives or is buried, or is oppressed, having become non-existent, who makes himself aware of the self before that? 017 Yayāti spoke: Having abandoned the body, like a sleeping person, the chief, having performed good and bad deeds, following the wind, he worships the lion among kings. 018 The virtuous go to the virtuous womb; the sinful go to the sinful womb. Insects become sinful; I do not desire greatness. 019 Quadrupeds, bipeds, and six-legged beings; thus, those in the womb are born. This has been declared; why do you ask, O lion among kings? 020 HER spoke II What indeed do the worlds attain by performing austerities, or by knowledge? Tell me, as I have asked, how does one go to the auspicious? 021 Yayāti spoke: Austerity, charity, calmness, and self-control; the essence of compassion for one's own beings. Those who are overwhelmed by darkness are said to be men of the divine. 022 The learned, thinking themselves wise, who with knowledge harm others, they become unworthy; and he does not give that which is not his. 023

English: The possible pure one The one who lives by his own valor, free from sin; a giver, not a cause of distress to others. Knowing that night, one should strive to be established in the forest. 006 Two Pandavas and others; relatives with their own selves, together twenty-one. The forest-dweller performs good deeds; releasing the elements of his own body in the forest. 007 HER said II How many indeed, O sages, are the silent ones, and how many are there? Please tell us that, for we wish to hear. 008 Yayāti said: For one who dwells in the forest, a village exists behind; or for one who dwells in a village, the forest is behind him. 009 HER said II How indeed, does a village exist behind in the forest? Or for one who dwells in a village, how does the forest exist behind? 010 Yayāti said: One should not use the village, for a forest-dwelling sage will be; thus, when he resides in the forest, a village exists behind. 011

English: 350 Saṃbhavapava Yayāti said: The householder who is unattached, restrained in desires, lives in the village as a beggar, having gone to the better place of those two. One who, having not attained a long life, wanders in a distorted state, if he performs penance, he should wander after that; otherwise, he should perform penance elsewhere. What is cruel is said to be improper; he who serves with a mind of confusion, even a horse is without hope; thus, the king's meditation is the ultimate restraint. HER said II By whom have you been sent today, O king; a young woman adorned with a garland, with sweet words? Where have you come from, in which direction, or is there a place for the king? Yayāti said: This earth, O men, is a hell for one whose merit is diminished; I shall fall into the earth, having spoken thus; the Brahmins and guardians of the world are hurrying me. In the presence of the virtuous, the fall is indeed a descent; all those who are endowed with qualities are gathered. I ask you, do not fall into the fall; if there are sorrows, O king, here with me; if they are filled in the sky or in heaven, I consider you to be the knower of that dharma. Yayāti said:

Yayāti said: There is no one like us, O king; who dwells in the royal assembly. | As the gift is always given to the brāhmaṇas; so I have not given before, O king. TMA: The miser will never live; even if he is a hero, he may also be a coward. | I, who have taken the form of the past, will wander; what is good there, I wonder. Pratadāna said: I ask you, O desirable one; if I have worlds. | If they are in the sky or in heaven; I consider you to be the knower of that dharma. Yayāti said: There are many worlds, O king; even if there is one, there are seven, seven times. | The honey-dripping, ghee-soaked, sorrowless ones; they do not have an end, they declare. Pratadāna said: I give you those worlds; do not fall into the abyss; may those worlds of mine be yours. | If they are in the sky or in heaven; quickly overcome the delusion.

English: 352 Saṃbhavapava Yayāti said: One who desires the same glory as me should not desire the fruits of righteous actions; a king, being a king, should ensure the welfare of his subjects. By the command of the gods, a wise person, having faced calamity, does not blame the king. The righteous path, when followed with awareness, leads to fame; one should not neglect dharma. A mind like mine, which is not foolish, does not desire the wealth of others; what is the use of that which is not done by others? Thus speaking to the king Yayāti, the best of kings, Vasuśmana spoke. Chapter 088 Vasuśmana said: I ask you, O king, about the world beyond; if you are known in the sky, O great soul, I consider you to be the knower of dharma. Yayāti said: Whatever is in the sky, the earth, and the directions; whatever shines with the brilliance of the sun, all beings are established in the heavens; they do not perish, they protect. Vasuśmana said: I give you those who are my subjects; may your sorrows be removed.

English: Yayāti said: I do not remember any false sale; it is futile to hold on to what is not real. What should I do if others are not like me in their actions? Vasumānā said: You should take back what you have given, O king; if the purchase is not pleasing to you. I am not the one to take back, O king; may all beings be yours. Rivira said: I ask you, O Rivira, if I have any possessions here, dear one; If they are filled in the sky or in heaven, I consider you the knower of that dharma. Yayāti said: You do not speak with your heart, O king; desiring what is not yours, you do not stand firm. Thus, the countless worlds in heaven are filled with you; they are resounding with greatness. Rivira said: You should take back those worlds, O king; if the purchase is not pleasing to you. I do not wish to take them back here; wherever you go, you will worship those worlds. Yayāti said: As you are like Indra in your influence, so too are the countless divine beings. Thus today in this world, I do not rejoice in anything else; therefore, I do not delight in the gift.

HER said II Whose are these five golden chariots that shine like fire? Yayāti said: These five golden chariots will indeed be spoken of by you, O saints, shining like fire. HER said II Get up, O king, take the chariot, and proceed with speed. We too will follow when the time comes. Yayāti said: Now we must go together, we are indeed bound by the sound of the drums. English: Vaśaṁpāyana said: All the best kings mounted their chariots and, attacking, ascended to the heavens, enveloped by the virtue of Bhāma. I think I am the only one going; my friend Indra is indeed my great soul. Why did this one, who is a friend of the Shibira, go with all speed? Yayāti said: He gave the vehicle until he found the best. This son of Ujjinara is indeed superior to us, Shibi. Charity, penance, truth, and also glory, patience, and endurance; O king, these are not the qualities of a king; they are the qualities of a king who is established in righteousness. Thus, having been deprived of the lowly, Shibi departed with the chariot. Vaśaṁpāyana said: Then the eighth one again asked, "O king, I am curious, tell me about Indra's form; I ask you, O king, tell me the truth; from whom are you, and whose son are you?" What you have done, indeed, is not comparable; in the world, there is no other Kṣatriya or Brāhmaṇa like you. Yayāti said: I am Yayāti, the son of Nahusha; my father is Pururavas, the lord of the heavens. I speak to you about a secret matter; I am the grandson of your grandfather.

English: Bhūmanyu, the best of the Bharatas, was anointed as the prince. Then, from that great king, a son named Vitatha was born. Suhotra, Suhotā, Suhavi, and Suyajus were the sons of Mumanyu of the Mṛcīka lineage. Among them, the eldest, Suhotra, attained the kingdom of the earth. He performed the Rājasūya and Aśvamedha sacrifices with many horses. Suhotra ruled over the entire earth, filled with elephants and horses, abundant and crowded. The earth was indeed burdened by the weight of his greatness, like a heavily laden cart. At that time, Suhotra governed the people justly, and the land was filled with hundreds of thousands of people. The prosperous people shone along with Sahadeva. From Suhotra, the earth's king, were born Eṣvāka, Ajamīda, Sumīda, and Purumīda in Bharata. Ajamiḍha was the best among them, and in that lineage, six others were established. Rikṣa, Dhūmin, and Nīlī were born from the supreme Dhūṣanta, as well as others of the same lineage.

English: The kings of Bharata then offered everything to him. Having presented everything to the sages with proper respect and good words, the king himself chose the auspicious eighth day. Let your priest be devoted to our kingdom. Thus, Vasiṣṭha also spoke to Bharata. Then, it was heard that the entire kingdom of Paurava was under the rule of the great emperor. The land of Bharata was previously ruled by the best of cities, and it was filled with the glory of the earth. Then, having attained the earth, the mighty one rejoiced, like a great sacrifice, with abundant offerings. Then, from the gathering, the Kurus flourished, and the people, knowing dharma, were happy under his rule. By his renowned name, Kurujāṅgala became famous on earth. Kuruśetra became sacred through his great penance. The sage with the colorful chariot, and Janamejaya, renowned, were born to him. The five sons of the mighty one were born. Among them, Parīkṣit was valorous, Abhirāja was glorious, and Shalmalā was mighty.

English: Uccaiḥśravā, Bhadrakāra, and Jitāri are remembered as the eighth. Among these, the renowned ones are: Janamejaya and others, the seven mighty ones. All of them became Parīkṣit’s sons, all knowledgeable in dharma. Kakṣa, Senograsena, and the valiant Citrasenā, Indrasena, Suṣeṇa, and Bhīmasena are also mentioned. Janamejaya’s daughter is known as a great warrior, Dhṛtarāṣṭra is the firstborn, and Pāṇḍavīka as well. Niṣadha, the great one, and Jāmbūnada are strong, Kuṇḍodara, Padāti, and Vasāti are remembered as the eighth. All are devoted to the welfare of all beings. Dhṛtarāṣṭra was a king, and his son was Kuṇḍika, Hastī, Vitaka, Karātha, and Kuṇḍala are the fifth. Haviḥśravā, Indrābha, and Sumanju are also mentioned. Three sons were born to Pratīpa, the best of the Bharatas: Devāpi and Śantanu, both great charioteers. Devāpi, desiring to perform sacrifices, departed, Rāntanu and Bāhīka, both great charioteers. In the lineage of Bharata, many great charioteers were born, Numerous royal ones, endowed with strength, like the gods. Saṃbhavapava.

English: Aditi is the mother of Vivasvat. Vivasvat is the father of Manu. Manu is the father of Ila. Ila is the mother of Purūravas. Purūravas is the father of Ayu. Ayu is the father of Nahusha. Nahusha is the father of Yayati. The daughters of Ushanas are Devayani and the daughter of Vṛṣapavā, named Śarmishṭhā. Here begins the lineage. Devayani and Śarmishṭhā gave birth to children. There, in that lineage, the sons of Purū are Poravas. In the lineage of Purū, there is a name Kausalyā. In her, Janamejaya was born, who conquered the enemies. Viśvajitā entered the forest. Janamejaya indeed performed the sacrifice named Anantā. In her, Prācinvān was born. He conquered the east until the sunrise. Then he became known as Prācinvat. In her, Saṃyāti was born. Saṃyāti indeed gave birth to a daughter named Varāṅgī. In her, Ahaṃpātī was born. Ahaṃpātī indeed gave birth to a daughter named Bhānumatī. In her, Savambhoma was born. The lineage continues.

English: Sāvabhoma indeed defeated and took away Kekeyī and Sunandā. From her was born Jayatsena. Jayatsena indeed gave birth to Arācīna in Vedarbhī. Arācīna also gave birth to Mayādā, like Vedarbhī. Mahābhoma gave birth to Suyajñā through Prāsa. He who is a man of great sacrifice brought forth Ayutanāyi. Thus, he is called Ayutanāyi. Ayutanāyi gave birth to Bhāsā, the daughter of Pṛthuśravas. From her was born Akrodha. Akrodha gave birth to Karṇāḍu in Kālini. From him was born Devātithi. Devātithi gave birth to Mayodā in the Vedehī. From her was born Ṛca. Ṛca indeed gave birth to Sudevā in Aṅge. From her was born a son named Rakṣam. Ṛkṣa gave birth to Jvāla, the daughter of Takṣaka. From her was born a son named Matināra. Matināra indeed performed a sacrifice in Sarasvatī. After the sacrifice, he approached Sarasvatī and married her. From her was born a son named Tansu. Here is the lineage. Tansu gave birth to Matināra's son, and he gave birth to Kalinda, the son of Tansu. Ilin gave birth to many sons through Duhṣanta. Duhṣanta indeed took Shakuntalā, the daughter of Viśvāmitra. From her was born Bharata.

English: In the land of Magadha, Amṛtā was born. From her, Parīkṣit was born. From Suyaśa, Bāhudāma was born. From him, Bhīma was born. Bhīma was born to Kakeiyī, named Sukumārī. From her, Pyāśravā was born. They say he is named Pratīpa. Pratīpa was born to Rovyā, named Sunandā. From her, he produced sons, Devāpi and Śantanu. Devāpi entered the forest as a child. Śantanu became a king. Here is the lineage. Whoever touches the hands of the one who is happy, they say, becomes Śantanu. Thus, he is called Śantanu. Śantanu was born to Bhāgirathī. From him, Devavrata was born. They call him Bhīṣma. Bhīṣma, out of love for his father, married Satyavatī, who is also called Ghandakātī. From her, Kānīna was born. From her, the sons of Śantanu were born. Chitrāṅgada and Vichitravīrya. Chitrāṅgada was killed by a Gandharva at the time of youth. Vichitravīrya became the king. Vichitravīrya married the daughters of Kausalyā and the daughter of Karirāja, named Gambhīrā. Vichitravīrya, without offspring, attained the status of Videha. Then Satyavatī began to think.

English: There, Mādri ascended the chariot. She spoke to Kuntī: "By the carelessness of the two, it must happen." Then the five Pāṇḍavas, along with Kuntī, were brought to Hastinapura, as informed by the ascetic Bhīṣma and Vidura. Even there, they could not burn the Jatugṛha due to Vidura's warning. Then, having killed Hidiṃba, they went to Ekachakra. In that Ekachakra, having killed a demon named Baka, they reached Pāścālana city. From there, they found Draupadī and returned to their own place. The letters were produced. Yudhiṣṭhira was (the son of) Kunti. Vṛkodara was (the son of) Sutasoma. Ajuna was (the son of) Śrutakīrti. Nakul was (the son of) Śatānīka. Sahadeva was (the son of) Taha. Yudhiṣṭhira, however, in the svayaṃvara of the goddess Devikā, gave birth to a son named Yodheya. Bhīmasena also took a wife named Barudhara, who was of valor. From her, he gave birth to a son named Savega. Ajana, indeed, going to Dvāravatī, married the sister of Vāsudeva, named Subhadrā. From her, he gave birth to a son named Abhimanyu. Nakul, too, married a wife named Vai Kareṇuvatī. From her, he begot a son named Niramitra. Sahadeva also took Mādri in her svayaṃvara, marrying a wife named Vijayā. From her, he gave birth to a son named Suhotra. Bhīmasena, earlier, had a son named Ghaṭotkaca from the demon Hidiṃbā. Thus, these are the eleven sons of the Pāṇḍavas. From the daughter of Virāṭa, he married a wife named Uttarā. From her, a son named Parāśu was born.

English: The abode of her was raised by Maruta. Then the host of gods, with great speed, came together. The great sage, King Śaṅka, saw the river. The great sage, having been addressed by the Lord Brahmā, was born among mortals. Thinking thus, the king, along with the kings and the great sages, pleased his father with abundant words. The great sage, however, was to be taken by the river, which was not to be forsaken. She, being fearful of your form, was struck by the hand of the divine. While going on the path, the gods of the heavens were present. Thus, the river asked the best of the rivers, "What is this, O shapeless ones? Is there any welfare for the heavenly beings?" The gods replied to her, "We are indeed caught in the great river due to a slight offense caused by the great sage Vasiṣṭha." Indeed, we are all bewildered, concealed from the best of sages. In the evening, we saw Vasiṣṭha seated, and we were previously driven away by him. Therefore, out of anger, we are unable to be born. It cannot be otherwise, as stated by the great sage. You, having become human, should give birth to sons, O Vasu. We do not enter the womb of mortals, for we are inauspicious.

English: Thus spoke the Ganges to the sons of Vasu: "O best of men, who among you will be born?" The Vasu said: "The son of Pratīpa, the righteous king of Śantanu, will be born among men. What will happen to us?" Gadā said: "The gods also think like this; I will do what is dear to him, if you agree." The Vasu said: "You should not be born as a son; otherwise, there will be no release from the world." Gadā said: "I will do this; let the son be born according to that. There will be no futile connection with me." The Vasu said: "We will grant the strength of each one of us; through that strength, your son will be born as desired." He will not prosper among men, but your son will be strong. Therefore, a son will be born to you, who will be strong.

English: I do not desire another's wealth, O beautiful one. Know that I do not wish for anything else. Khyuvāca: I am not a serpent, nor should anything be spoken. Worship me, O king, worship the maiden. Pratīpa uvāca: This is what you have asked of me, which is dear to me. Otherwise, the one who is determined would not be destroyed. Having reached my southern thigh, you are the beautiful maiden. Let the seat be arranged for the daughters-in-law of the timid. On the left side, the part of the beloved is rejected by you. Therefore, I shall not act with desire towards you, O beautiful maiden. May you be well, O auspicious one; I choose you for the sake of a son. You are indeed the left thigh, having come and taken refuge. Khyuvāca: Even so, I shall be united with your son, O knower of righteousness. For your sake, I shall worship the renowned abode of Bhārata. Among those who are rulers on earth, you are the ultimate. I cannot express my qualities even in a hundred years. Saṃbhavapavaṁ

English: The one who has departed from the house is indeed the best among the excellent. One should not act in a way that is contrary to one's noble birth. Your son will attain his own through virtuous and beloved letters. Thus, having spoken, she vanished from the king's sight. The king, waiting for the birth of a son, held on to that. In this very moment, the Kṣatriya Pratīpa performed austerities for the sake of his son, O descendant of the Kurus. From them was born a son, the great Bhīṣma, who was born of Śāntanu. Remembering the sorrows conquered by his own actions, the noble one of the Kurus became a divine being. Pratīpa, the son of Śāntanu, then followed the youth. If she were to approach you secretly, she would be a daughter of excellent qualities. She should not be spoken of by you, who is she and whose is she? Whatever should be done, that should not be questioned by you, O sinless one.

English: The queen spoke to the king with a heart-melting voice: "I will be your devoted wife, O ruler of the earth." As for the king, whether it be the son of the king or the son of the noble, I will not be prevented from speaking what is dear to me. Thus, while speaking in this manner, I will remain with you, O prince, and I will abandon what is unpleasant. Thus, the queen was addressed by the king, and then the best of the Bharatas smiled, having received her. Approaching, Śantanu enjoyed her as he desired, thinking that he should not ask her anything, nor did he say anything to her. By her virtuous character and her beauty, she pleased the lord of the worlds. That divine goddess, Ganges, having taken a human form, became the most beautiful one. For the one desiring good fortune, she became the wife of the lion among kings, equal to the brilliance of the king of gods. He delighted the king as he delighted himself. The king, being attached to pleasure and endowed with excellent qualities, did not notice the passing of many years and seasons.

English: 378 Possible Purification The lord of the people, enjoying with her, gave birth to a son as desired. 043 As soon as she gave birth, she cast the child into the water, O Bhārata. I am pleased with you, she said, and with the strength of the mace, he was victorious. 044 Then, that which was dear to the king became a source of lamentation. The king, frightened by abandonment, did not speak to her at all. 045 Then, when the eighth son was born, as if smiling, the king, in sorrow, spoke to his son, wishing for him. 046 "Do not kill! Who are you? Why do you harm your sons? O son-killer, do not attain such a great sin; do not remain condemned." 047 He spoke: "I do not kill my son, O son of the best of sons. This is my dwelling, as it has been arranged. 048 I am Ganga, the daughter of Jahnu, served by the great sage. I have been born to you, along with you." 049 These eight Vasus, the great and glorious gods, have attained humanity due to the curse of Vasiṣṭha. 050 There is no other mother on earth besides you who can give birth to them. A mother like me does not exist here at all. 051 Therefore, for the sake of those sons, humanity has been attained. Having given birth to the eight Vasus, you have conquered the worlds, O imperishable one. 052

English: Varuṇa, the son of the ocean, once obtained the best of the Bharata lineage. The sage named Vasiṣṭha, renowned for his prowess, was also known as Āpava. His hermitage was sacred, accompanied by a multitude of deer and birds, adorned with flowers from the side of Mount Meru, the king of mountains. Varuṇa performed austerities there, O best of the Bharatas, in the forest rich with the fruits and waters of virtuous deeds. The daughter of Dakṣa, known as Surabhī, was greatly esteemed, and from her, the goddess Gāṁ was born. To bestow blessings upon the world, Varuṇa, the lord of the waters, brought forth the divine cow, the wish-fulfilling cow, Gāṁ. She resided in that forest of ascetics, served by sages, and roamed in the beautiful and righteous places, free from fear. Then, at that moment, the best of the Bharatas arrived. The Vasus, led by Prithvī, were present there. They, along with their wives, wandered in that forest, enjoying the delightful and pleasant places. In that forest, one of them, while wandering, gave a beautiful cow to the sage Vasiṣṭha, who was the best among those who fulfill desires. She, filled with wonder, possessed the wealth of character and virtue, and during the day, she revealed that cow to the bull-eyed Gāṁ. The pure one appeared.

English: The auspicious one with a beautiful face, endowed with excellent qualities, is connected to the divine Vasudeva. O king, in the past, there was a city known for its inhabitants. Then, the king spoke to that goddess, describing her beauty and qualities. This goddess is the most beautiful, with eyes like the Varuṇa. Whoever drinks her milk will live with youthful stability. Hearing this, the goddess, with a beautiful form, spoke to the excellent king. In the human world, I have a friend, a daughter of the gods, named Jinavatī, who is beautiful and youthful. O king, the daughter of the wise and truthful one is renowned in the world for her beauty. For her sake, bring my desired cow quickly, O best of the auspicious. As long as she drinks this milk, may she be the only one among humans, free from old age and disease.

English: 382 Possible Purity This is my great fortune, for I am not at all insulted by the great one. There is nothing dearer to me than this. Hearing these words from the goddess, desiring to please her, the Earth took away that village from the two. Then, appointed by the lotus-eyed one, the king could not see the sage's intense penance. That one was taken away by him; the waterfall was not to be reasoned about. Then, having reached the hermitage and having taken fruits, the Varuṇa did not go there to the best of the forest. Then he began to hunt in the forest, the one who was a great ascetic did not go to hunt that village. Knowing that it had been taken away, the divine seer, having compassion, cursed the Vasus. From whom the Vasus, having taken the cow, will be born among men. Thus, the Lord cursed the Vasus, the best of the sages, having received the wrath of the great one, O Bharata. And he, the great one, fixed his mind on penance. Thus, he cursed the king, the Vasus were lost, the ascetic. The great power of the Lord was accompanied by the anger of the gods.

English: Having reached the hermitage, the great-souled one was addressed by the sages, who said, "We know that you have cursed us." The Vasus, seeking to please the sage, did not reject the boon from the best of sages. The man-tiger, having torn apart the wind, spoke. He, the righteous one, said, "You seven, O Earth-dwellers, after a year, will attain liberation from the curse." But for the sake of which you have been cursed by me, he will live long in the human realm by his own actions. I do not wish for falsehood; I am angry with you for what you have said. The great-minded one will not be born among humans. The righteous one, skilled in his own weapon, will act for the welfare of his father and will enjoy the pleasures of companionship. Thus speaking, the sage departed. Then all the Vasus approached me and requested a boon, which I granted. Having been born, we are cast into the waters. Thus, I, having properly fulfilled the desires of the righteous, have acted for the liberation of the human beings. This is the only curse of the best of kings.

English: The one who is superior to all due to desire, thus established. Among these, the great one, Śantanu, the best of the Bharata lineage, there was no Kṣatriya equal to him in righteousness. Indeed, the present dharma is the best among all knowers of dharma; the kings anointed him, the great king of kings. Free from grief and fear, awakened from pleasant dreams, the earth's rulers approached the protector of the Bhārata. In the presence of Rāṇṭanu, the chief of the hidden, the kings then followed the rules, and the external affairs turned favorable. Brahman surrounded the Kṣatriya, and the Kṣatriyas followed the vow; those devoted to Brahman and Kṣatriya. He, residing in the beautiful Hastinapura, by breaking the shell of the Kurus, made the earth flow like the ocean. He, resembling the king of the gods, knowledgeable in dharma, truthful in speech, endowed with supreme asceticism and charity. Free from attachment and hatred, with a face like the moon, equal in speed to the wind. Like the earth in patience, he is the embodiment of death. The killing of animals and birds is indeed a fact; Rāṇṭanu, the king, does not engage in this in vain.

English: 386 Possible Purity In the northern region of Dharmabāhya, the self-controlled Śantanu ruled equally over all beings, free from desire. From that time, the rituals began for the deities and the ancestors. And by unrighteousness, no one among the wise was harmed. For the unhappy and the helpless in the lower forms of life, He alone became the father of all beings, the king. In that Kurupatishrī, with the king of kings present, Bharata spoke the truth with a steadfast mind. There were sixteen and eighty-four years, and also others, He became a forest dweller, having attained pleasure in women. Thus, of such form, such conduct, such behavior, and such fall, Gāṅgeya had a son named Devavrata, the Vasu. Skilled in all branches, he was also among the other kings, A great warrior, a great soul, a great charioteer. Once, having spotted a deer, following it along the river, Śantanu, the king, was pleased with the shallow waters of the Bhāgirathī. He thought, "What is this, O best of men? Is this river not flowing as it did before?" Then, desiring a cause, that great-minded one, Saw a young man, endowed with beauty, large, and with charming features. A divine weapon, like that of the god Indra, was prepared.

English: Peel, having surrounded the sharp arrows, stood firm. The king, astonished, saw the two rivers, Ganges nearby, enveloped by those arrows. Having just been born, that son of Śantanu was not remembered by the wise one to recognize his son. He then enchanted his father with illusion, and quickly disappeared from there. At that time, the king Śantanu saw something wonderful there. The Ganges, bearing a splendid form, took the boy in her right hand, adorned him. Adorned with the finest ornaments, she, though previously seen, was not recognized by Śantanu. He said: "You, O king, who were born as my eighth son, this tiger among men, take him to the house." He who is endowed with strength, versed in the Vedas and the branches, is like the king of the gods in battle. What is taught in the scriptures, that is the essence of the gods and demons, O Bhārata.

English: The son of Aṅgiras, honored by gods and demons, What is known in the scriptures is also established here. In you, O mighty-armed one, with great soul, The sage, invincible to others, is Jāmadagni, the valorous. What weapon is known in the Vedas, that is also established here. This great archer, knowledgeable in the ways of kings, I have given my own son, the hero, to you. Then, having obtained permission, Śantanu, With his son shining like the sun, went to his own city. Paurava, having gone to his city, resembling Indra's city, Thought of himself as fulfilled in all desires. Then, in Paurava, he anointed his son for the kingdom. The son of Paurava, the son of Śantanu, with great fame, Also delighted his father with his deeds, O Bharata. Thus, the king, enjoying with his son, Spent four rainy seasons with great valor. At one time, having gone to the forest, near the river Yamunā, The king, unseen, smelled the excellent fragrance. He wandered around, seeking the source of the fragrance.

English: He then bit the maiden, who was in the form of a goddess. He asked her, "O maiden with dark eyes, who are you and what do you desire?" "I am the daughter of the great king Dāsa, by the order of my father." Seeing her, King Śantanu desired the goddess-like maiden. He went to her father and asked for her hand, inquiring about her lineage. The king replied to Dāsa, "A daughter has just been born to me, to be given in marriage." "O Lord of men, if you desire this maiden from me, then listen." "If you wish for her, grant me a promise in truth." "At the right time, I will give you this maiden, for there is no one like you." Rāntanu spoke: "Having heard your promise, I will either give or not give." "If it is to be given, I will give her; otherwise, she shall not be yours." The wives spoke.

English: The son born to you will be the king of the earth; no one else should be anointed as king. Veraṁpāyana said: He did not wish to give that boon to Dāśa. Though burned by the intense grief, he was still in thought, O Bhārata. Then, the king, thinking of the Dāśa maiden, approached Hastinapura, afflicted by sorrow. At that time, seeing Śantanu in meditation, his son Devavrata approached and spoke to his father. "Your welfare should be ensured by your own sons; why then do you grieve here constantly, O distressed one?" "Why do you not speak anything, O king?" Thus addressed by his son, Śantanu replied: "Undoubtedly, I am absorbed in meditation, as I am, so I am." "Only you are our offspring, O great Bhārata; I lament the impermanence of life." "Somehow, O Gāṅgeya, there is no calamity for us." "Undoubtedly, you alone are the best son, even better than a boon." "And I do not wish to marry again; I desire well-being for the continuation of progeny."

English: Unmarried, they say, is the state of having no sons. The three Vedas and sacrifices are not harmed by the absence of offspring. Thus, among men, there is no doubt that where there is a wise son, there is no uncertainty for me. This is the eternal essence of the three ancient texts. You are a hero, always steadfast, O Bhārata; there is no other death for you, O sinless one. I am in distress, how can there be peace for you? Thus, the cause of sorrow has been stated by you in anger. Then, knowing that cause, the great-minded Devavrata, contemplating, went forth. He approached the aged minister, the father’s well-wisher, and asked him about the cause of the father’s sorrow. To him, the chief of the Kurus, he inquired appropriately. Then, Devavrata, accompanied by Kshatriyas, approached the king of the Dasa and sought the daughter himself. The daughters received him, duly honored according to custom, in the royal assembly, O Bhārata.

English: You are indeed the lord, O Tan, of the Jhaṭṭana. What shall I say to you, the best among sons? Who can desire the connection with the desired womb? Even the hundred sacrifices cannot surpass it. The offspring of Chaitadārya, who is equal to you in qualities, Whose son is the glorious Satyavatī. Thus, my father is greatly honored by you. Satyavatī, among all kings of Bharata. Even the sage Aśita was previously rejected by me, For Satyavatī was indeed the best among sages. Due to the girl’s fatherhood, I shall speak, O best of Bharata. I only point out the fault in the strong and capable. For if you are capable, whether of Gandharvas or Asuras, You will never find happiness, O Ma HSE, O Parantapa. This is indeed the only fault, no other king is like this. Know this, O blessed one, regarding the giving and receiving. Thus addressed, O Ma, he replied, To the listening kings, the father of Bharata. This is my opinion, take it, the truth of Satyavatī. Neither born nor born of a horse, I do not dare to speak. Thus is the possibility of birth.

English: Thus, I will do as you speak. The one who is born here will not be a king for us. Having spoken thus, the Dasā replied again, wishing to accomplish the difficult task for the sake of the kingdom, O best of Bharata. You alone are the lord of the son of Śantanu, and also the lord of the daughter, O great soul. This indeed is the word, O gentle one, listen to the task. I shall speak according to the character of the maidens. For you, who are devoted to truth and dharma, the promise made in the assembly of kings is indeed fitting for you. There is no doubt about this, O mighty-armed one; your offspring will be, but there is great doubt about that. Knowing this, the king, devoted to truth and dharma, then acknowledged the words of his father. Devavrata said: O Dasaraja, listen to this word of mine, O best of kings, for the sake of the rulers of the earth and for my father. The kingdom was indeed given up by me earlier, O king of men, and I will also make this decision for the sake of offspring. From today onwards, O Dasā, I shall observe celibacy. Even without a son, my worlds will be eternal in heaven.

English: Then, the wise Śāntanu was born to Satyavatī. By his valor, a hero named Citrāṅgada was born, who was known among men. Then, the lord again generated the great archer, the king Vichitravīrya, from Satyavatī. The king Śāntanu, who had not attained youth, approached the time of death. In heaven, Śāntanu established Bhīṣma and Citrāṅgada in the kingdom, as per the wishes of Satyavatī. But Citrāṅgada, the valiant one, did not consider any man equal to himself. As he was being thrown, the gods and also the asuras were equal in strength. Thus, a great war arose for him in Kurukṣetra. There, on the banks of the river Hirṇavatī, there was a battle between the two powerful ones. In that clash, amidst the shower of arrows, the mighty Gandharva killed the best of the Kurus. Having made an end of Citrāṅgada, the Gandharva ascended to heaven. In that, the husband of Sādhu was struck down, with great renown.

English: Bhīṣma, the son of Śantanu, had many daughters. When the names of the kings were being praised, Bhīṣma himself, the lord, then chose those daughters, O king. He spoke to the kings, the sound of his voice like thunder. Bhīṣma, the best of men, took the daughters in his chariot. Some offered a daughter along with a pair of cows. Others, with the wealth mentioned, offered various things. Some, in a state of excitement, approached, while others found their own. The eighth was the wedding, as remembered by the poets. The royal ladies approached the svayaṃvara, seeking to be chosen. They were said to be taken by the dharma speakers. These earth protectors, I wish to conquer by force. You should strive with all your might for victory or otherwise. I stand here, the protector of the earth, determined for battle. Thus speaking, the powerful king Bhīṣma took the daughters in his chariot. He quickly took those daughters. Then all the kings rose up, agitated.

English: The warriors, touching their own weapons, quickly released their arrows. The confusion became immense as they raised their bows. Like the shower of stars, it was for Janamejaya. With the ornaments and the auspicious ones, they shone. They adorned themselves with various armaments. The charioteers, having taken their positions, were ready with their weapons. As they advanced, they prepared for battle. Then, a great war arose between them and that of Bhārata. They hurled thousands of arrows simultaneously. And Bhīṣma swiftly cut down those who had not yet reached. Then all the kings surrounded from all sides. They rained arrows like a shower upon the mountains. That arrow-rain was everywhere. Then, the kings, having taken their positions, prepared for battle. They honored their own charioteers. The warriors also worshipped their own weapons. Thus, the battle commenced.

English: Having defeated the entire army in battle, the skilled warrior set out towards Dhārta, accompanied by maidens. Then, from behind, the great charioteer Śālva, with an immeasurable soul, attacked Bhīṣma, the son of Śantanu, in battle. As he struck the elephant in the thigh, the powerful leader of the troops, having received the signal, advanced. The king said to Bhīṣma, "Stand firm, stand firm!" Then, the mighty Śālva, urged by the enraged, powerful Bhīṣma, advanced. Then, that man-lion Bhīṣma, unperturbed by the great army, stood firm like a cloud ablaze with anger. Having taken his position in the battle, free from fear and confusion, the great charioteer advanced towards Śālva. Seeing him retreating, the kings were all astonished and exclaimed, "Well done, well done!" The warriors, like bulls, roared in the midst of the battle, engaging one another with great valor. Then, the best of men, Bhīṣma, was showered with thousands of arrows by the great king Śālva. The kings, having seen Bhīṣma previously attacked by Śālva, were astonished and exclaimed, "Well done, well done!" The warriors observed his lightness in battle.

English: The kings, delighted, honored Śālva with words. Hearing the words of the Kṣatriyas, Parapurañjaya spoke: "O Śāntanu's son Bhīma, stand firm!" Angered, he said to his charioteer, "Go where the king is, until I slay him like a serpent slays a bird." Then Kaurava skillfully harnessed the Varuṇa chariot, and with it, he took four horses from King Śālva. With weapons and armaments, King Śālva was defeated by Bhīma, who struck down his charioteer. With arrows and other weapons, he struck down the best of the steeds. For the sake of the maiden, Bhīma, son of Śāntanu, having conquered, sent away the best of kings alive. Then Śālva went to his city, O best of the Bharatas. The kings who were there, the self-chosen ones, also took their own kingdoms, O Parapurañjaya. Thus, having conquered, Bhīma, the best of warriors, went to Hastinapura, where the king was Kaurava. Before long, the king crossed the forests and rivers, various places of delight. Having made the unassailable ones retreat, he brought forth the sons of the ocean. The pure one has come.

English: As if they were Sūṣa, the virtuous souls, like sisters and their younger brothers, just as the daughters were received by the Kurus. They, endowed with all virtues, were brothers to the younger brother. Bhīma, the one of diverse prowess, bestowed the valorous ones. The righteous one, knowing dharma, arranged for the marriage of his brother, the one of diverse prowess. Having made a determination with Satyavatī, he was self-assured. The eldest daughter of Kāripati, wishing to arrange the marriage with Bhīma, spoke this word at that time. I, having been adorned by the former husband, am bound by him, and thus I am the daughter of my father. I was to be chosen by the one who is like a cloud in the self-choice, knowing this, you should act according to dharma. Thus addressed by her, Bhīma, in the assembly of the brāhmaṇas, was overcome with thought regarding the appropriateness of that very action. Having determined, the knower of dharma, with the learned brāhmaṇas, then arranged for the eldest daughter of Kāripati. To Ambikā and Ambālikā, the younger ones, Bhīma, the one of diverse prowess, gave them to the elder brother. Taking their hands, he, filled with youthful pride,

English: Thus addressed, the virtuous one replied: "This is indeed the answer to your question." Without doubt, the supreme dharma is known to you. You know the truth of the situation; I reaffirm my promise to you. I would abandon my kingdom or even the gods, but not the truth under any circumstances. One should abandon the earth, the fragrance, and the essence of water; one should also abandon light, form, and the qualities of air. One should give up the brilliance of the comet and the warmth; one should abandon sound and the coolness of the moon. Even if the slayer of Vritra were to act against dharma, I would not engage in any wrongdoing. Thus addressed by his son, the mother Satyavatī spoke to Bhīṣma thereafter. I know your position in truth, O one of great valor; wishing to create a beautiful form, you should shine with your own brilliance. I also know the truth of what you have said; in the face of danger, bear the burden of your ancestral duty. Let them act as they wish; may they not be defeated.

English: The earth was created by the three sevens, previously without kṣatriyas. Then, gathering together, the kṣatriyas spoke. The offspring produced by the brāhmaṇa with a controlled mind. It is determined in the Vedas that the son of the one who takes the hand is so. Establishing dharma in the mind, the brāhmaṇas approached them. In the world, the kṣatriyas are seen to act. Then, the renowned ṛṣi Utaṭhya was indeed wise. Mamatā was his wife, known for her supreme respect. Among the foremost of the Yavīyas of Utaṭhya, the great brilliance of Bṛhaspati approached Mamatā. Mamatā spoke to him, saying, "O divine one, I have been made to be with my elder brother." "This great fortune of mine is indeed in the womb of Bṛhaspati. Utaṭhya, the Veda is indeed here." "O Amogha, you too surely deserve to become." "Therefore, today, you should be elevated." Thus addressed, the great brilliance of Bṛhaspati could not control his desire for his own self. Then, the desirous one was born from her, while she, without desire, spoke to him.

English: Bhoṣṭāt, the maiden speaks: "O, it is possible! O, the unerring one, you have come here." Then, enraged, Bhṛhaspati spoke to Utaṭhya's son: "O, the Lord sage, you shall be reproached." When all beings desire, at that time, you will speak long words of darkness. He was born as the longest one due to the curse, like Bhṛhaspati, renowned for his greatness. He then begot sons, the great Gautama, for the increase of the sage Utaṭhya's lineage. Overcome by greed and delusion, those sons of Gautama cast him into the wood and abandoned him in the Ganges. They thought, "This blind old man should not be supported," and after contemplating, the cruel ones returned to their homes. Then, the sage, following the king, went to the abode of the blind one. The king, strong and wise, seized him, having come from the waters. The righteous one, Bali, of true valor, seized him, knowing him to be a man. For the sake of progeny, O great one, grant me honor.

English: 408 Saṃbhavapava To produce sons, O blind one, the great sage spoke thus. Thus addressed, the radiant one replied, "So be it." The king then sent his wife, Sudeṣṇā. Considering him to be blind and old, the queen did not go. But she sent her own daughter, Dhātrīyikā, to the old man. In the Shudra lineage, Kākṣīvata and others were born. The son of Kākṣīvata, having been addressed by the king, spoke to the sage, "I am he." The sage replied, "No, I am he," saying, "The Kākṣīvatas were born from me, a Shudra." Considering him to be blind and old, Sudeṣṇā, your queen, insulted me and gave me Dhātrīyikā. Then, having pleased the sage, she again sent her to him, the best of sages. The queen, with long limbs, spoke to him, "Your son will be radiant and truthful." There was a king named Ajlo born to Sudeṣṇā. Thus, many great Kṣatriyas were born on the earth. Born, they were supremely knowledgeable in dharma, powerful and valiant. Hearing this, you too, mother, do as you wish.

English: Bhīṣma said: For the sake of the Bharata lineage and the increase of descendants, I shall speak the truth, O Mother, listen to me. A Brahmin endowed with virtues, who is skilled in the sacred knowledge, should produce offspring in the diverse fields. Then, Satyavatī, smiling and speaking to Bhīṣma, said: Indeed, O mighty-armed one, as you say, I shall speak the truth regarding the lineage and descendants. It is not possible to remain unspoken about such matters. You are indeed our truth, you are the ultimate refuge; therefore, having heard my words, do as you deem fit thereafter. My father, who was righteous and virtuous, had once taken me there in my youth. Then, the greatest of the righteous, the supreme sage Parāśara.

English: Today I went to the river Yamunā. He, having approached the Yamunā, came to me then, the foremost sage, afflicted by desire, spoke sweetly. I, being afraid of the curse and fearful of my father, O Bhārata, cannot dare to refuse the boons that were easily granted. Having overwhelmed me, the great one took me, a child, with his brilliance, and enveloped the world in darkness, O Bhārata. The fish-scented one was previously repulsive to me; the sage gave me this auspicious fragrance. Then the sage spoke to me, having released me from the grasp of the great serpent, "You will be a daughter of this river." Parāśarya, the great yogi, became a great sage; he was previously known as Dvaipāyana, the son of a maiden. He who, through austerity, spread the Vedas, is the Lord sage; in the world, he attained the name Vyāsa and also the identity of Kṛṣṇa. The truthful one, self-controlled, an ascetic, having burned away sins, was appointed by me and you, O one of immense radiance. He will generate auspicious offspring in the fields of his brother. Indeed, he spoke to me there, "Remember me in your actions." I will remember him, O mighty-armed one, if you, Bhīṣma, wish it. The pure one is born.

English: Your son, O Anumata, will surely produce sons in the fields of Vichitravirya. The great sage Kīṭa spoke to Bhīma, the wise one. Desire and attachment are threefold, and they are distinct from one another. He who contemplates wisely and decides rightly is the wise one. This is indeed the righteous and beneficial path that you have spoken of, which pleases me greatly. Then, having made this promise, Bhīma, O scion of the Kurus, began to think of the sage. He, knowing the Vedas, contemplated what was known to the mother. In an instant, he appeared, known to the scion of the Kurus. At that time, he performed worship for the son, the one worthy of reverence. Embracing him with both arms, he anointed him with the sacred water, and he shed tears for his son. English: The one who knows Dharma, truth, and the supreme beyond, and the one who does not know Dharma, as your mind is directed towards Dharma. For a year, according to justice, it will be pure thereafter; no maiden who is unchaste will approach me. Satyavatī said: As soon as the goddess becomes pregnant, do so; in lawless kingdoms, there are no rain-giving deities. How can a kingdom be sustained, O Lord? Therefore, Bhīṣma will kill that one. Vyāsa said: If a son is to be given by me quickly, may this deformity be borne by her and also that of the other. If I can bear the fragrance, form, appearance, and body, let the goddess Kausalyā become pregnant. Vairāmpāyana said:
