English: Kausalyā, the deity is present today, and you will enter. The attentive one will arrive by waiting. Hearing that speech, the lying ones in the auspicious bed thought then of Bhīṣma and the other Kurupāṇḍavas. Then, in Ambikā, the truthful sage was first appointed. He entered the bed where the lamps were glowing. From Krishna's shining matted hair, the eyebrows and these eyes closed, O goddess. That night was born from her mother's dear wish. Out of fear, the daughter of Kāśi could not look at him due to anger. Then, having approached, the mother spoke to her son: "Even in this, the son will be virtuous; he will be a royal son." Hearing the words of the mother, the son, very wise, spoke, prompted by the divine knowledge. He who has the life of a thousand serpents, the best among the learned, will be very fortunate, very mighty, and will have great wisdom. And also, his sons will be very strong. However, due to the mother's bad qualities, he will be blind. Hearing that speech, the mother then addressed her son: "The king of the Kurus will not be blind, he will be a fitting son." The protector of the family lineage, the enhancer of the lineage of the fathers.

English: 416 Possible Purity You are worthy to give birth to the second king of the Kuru dynasty. Thus, having made that promise, the great ascetic departed. Kausalyā also gave birth to a blind son. Again, that goddess, having spoken, called the sage, just as before, the blameless one. By that very means, the great fortune came to her. Ambālikā also approached him, or she too was there. The Pandavas, resembling the color of the sky, became distressed. Seeing her frightened, resembling the Pandavas, and sorrowful, the son of Partha, Vyāsa, the son of Satyavatī, spoke this word. Since you have attained the pallor of the Pandavas, seeing me also deformed, this son of yours will indeed be pale. And his name will also be the same here, having a beautiful face. Thus speaking, the great sage departed. Then, having calmed down, Satyā spoke to her son. She praised the pallor of that child. The mother then requested another son. The great sage replied to her, "So be it." Then the goddess gave birth to a son, endowed with the characteristics of Pandu, shining like wealth.

English: The five Pāṇḍavas were born to him. At the time of the season, he arranged for the elder's marriage. She, contemplating the form and fragrance, did not heed the words of the goddess out of fear, resembling the son of the gods. Then, having adorned her with her own ornaments, she became like an Apsara for Kṛṣṇa, the son of Karipati. The maid, having approached the sage, bowed down and, having received permission, entered, having honored him. By indulging in sensual pleasures, he was pleased with her. "Arise, you will not be defeated; this is your auspicious path, the illustrious one has arrived." Then, he will be the best among all wise men. Vidura was born, the son of Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana, the brother of Dhṛtarāṣṭra and the wise Pāṇḍu. Dharma, in the form of Vidura, free from the curse of that great soul, was devoid of desire and anger. Having become free from debt to Dharma, he again entered the womb, having gathered there. Thus, the son of Dvaipāyana, of such diverse valor.

English: I asked the king about the situation of the ascetic. By which path did the robbers, the best of the twice-born, go? Let us go quickly, then. Thus, while the ascetic was speaking, the king did not fear, saying, "Do not be afraid, O king." Then the royal men searched for that hermitage and saw there the ascetic and the wealth of the moon. Then, the protector of the ascetics approached that sage and, having controlled himself, reported to the king. The king, along with the robbers, was advised to be cautious. The great ascetic, knowing of the impending danger, was pierced by a spear. Then, having raised the spear, the protectors of the sage returned to the king, taking away wealth as they pleased. Though he was starving, the sage did not succumb to death. He began to breathe and brought the sages along. While the spear was being heated by the great ascetic, the sages experienced great suffering. They, having become birds at night, surrounded him and asked the best of the ascetics as much as they could.

English: 420 Saṃbhavapava We wish to hear what sin you have committed. Then that sage's messenger spoke to the ascetics: "Who shall I go to for blame? No one else has offended me." Hearing this, the king, along with his ministers, pleased the sage, the best of ascetics, who was pierced by a spear. "Due to my delusion and ignorance, I have caused this, I offer my respects to you; you should not be angry with me." Thus addressed by the king, the sage granted his favor. The king, having received his favor, then descended. And as he descended, he saw the spear; he took the spear and broke it. Thus, the sage wandered with that spear, and through his penance, he conquered the worlds. It is said in the world, "Aṇīmaṇḍavya." Going to the abode of the brāhmaṇa, the supreme knower of dharma, he found the lord seated there, firmly established in dharma. What sin have I committed unknowingly, for which this result has come to me? Quickly tell me the truth; I am the strength of my penance.

English: The Kurus flourished in Kurukṣetra. The land became fruitful after the destruction, yielding crops and fruits. The vehicles were joyful, and the animals and birds were delighted. The merchants and artisans thrived in the cities, and the archers and learned men were happy. Some people, devoid of unrighteousness, were not troubled even in the regions of the kingdoms. Those engaged in charitable acts and devoted to sacrifices, united in mutual affection, protected the populace. People free from pride and anger, avoiding greed, supported each other. That great and prosperous city shone like a mountain adorned with clouds. Resembling the city of Indra, it was surrounded by palatial structures. In the rivers, forested areas, and beautiful gardens, the joyful people thrived. The Kurus to the north and the Kuravas to the south were in conflict, moving about in the pursuit of success. The pure and sacred emerged.

English: The wretched do not become prosperous, how can the widows? In that delightful city, many were created by the Kurus; there were wells, gardens, and Brahmin residences as well. Under the rule of Bhīṣma, the king was protected from all sides. It became beautiful, marked by the sacrificial post, and this land was adorned by foreign nations. The wheel of dharma was established by Bhīṣma. While activities were being performed, all the great souls among the princes became constantly festive. In the houses of the chief Kurus and the citizens, the words "Let it be given, let it be enjoyed" were heard. Pāṇḍu and Vidura, the wise one, were protected by Bhīṣma from birth like sons. They were cultured by rituals, engaged in vows and studies, and they reached youth through labor and exercise. In archery, wrestling, mace fighting, and swordplay, as well as in the art of elephant management, they excelled. In the histories and Puranas, and in various teachings, those knowledgeable in the Vedas and their limbs were diligent everywhere. In archery, Pāṇḍu was superior to other men.

English: Thus, it should be arranged by me and you, without enmity. It is heard that there is a suitable daughter of Subala's family, as well as the daughter of the king of Madra. The beautiful and the noble ones are indeed related to us, the Kṣatriyas. I think they should be chosen, as I consider the progeny of this lineage, or what Vidura thinks. Vidura said: You are the father, you are the mother, you are our supreme teacher. Therefore, consider what is beneficial for this lineage. Then, Śuka heard from the brāhmaṇas about Gāndhārī, the daughter of Subala, who worshipped the boon-giving god, the remover of the eyes of the world. Gāndhārī indeed has a hundred sons, which is auspicious. Thus, having heard this truly, Bhīṣma, the grandfather of the Kurus, then sent a message to the king of Gāndhāra. There, the consideration of Subala was not hidden; he observed both fame and conduct with wisdom. He sent Gāndhārī, the virtuous one, to Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

English: Amya, having vowed to his own son, the valiant one. He gave the maiden, named Agrajātā, to Kuntibhoja, his friend, for the sake of friendship. She was appointed in her father's house for the worship of the divine guests. With great determination, he performed the fierce external vow. He, with a hidden resolve, who was known as Duvāsasa, pleased the fierce one, who was self-controlled. He gave her, observing the auspicious signs, to the sage, who was afflicted by curses. Whichever deity you invoke with this mantra, by their grace, your son will come to be. Thus spoken by the Brahmin, she, out of curiosity, the virtuous maiden, invoked the glorious deity. She saw the sun, the sustainer of the worlds, approaching, and was astonished at that great wonder. Illuminating, the sun then placed a seed in her womb, and from that, a hero was born, renowned among the warriors. The illustrious one, adorned with the divine armor, was enveloped in glory. Holding the natural armor, with a face radiant like a jewel, a son was born, renowned in all worlds.

English: The girl was given to him again, he being the supreme one. Then, the best among givers ascended to heaven. Fearing the relatives, Kuntī secretly placed the well-formed son in the water. Then, the embryo was released, and the greatly famous one, Rādhābhata, was conceived as a son. The name of that child was to be given as he was born with Vasu, "May he be Vasuṣeṇa." While being killed, the strong one, endowed with weapons, approached the sun from behind. In that moment, the hero, who was chanting the truth, was not present in the external sounds of that great soul. Indra, becoming a Brahmin, for the sake of alms, the one who creates beings, sought the armor with great radiance. Taking the blood-dripping armor from his own body, Karṇa, cutting the earring, offered it with folded hands. He gave that to him, astonished, who spoke the words of the gods, demons, humans, Gandharvas, serpents, and Rakṣasas. In that, you will be thrown, and by this, it will not happen. Long ago, it was heard that his name was Suṣeṇa. Then, by the action of Vaikatanā, he became so. The pure one is born.

English: Vērāmpāyana said: Endowed with beauty, essence, and qualities, the great vow of Dharmarāja, the daughter of Kuntibhoja, was for the sake of her father in the svayaṃvara. In the midst of thousands of earth's heroes, he found Pāṇḍu, who had the lion's teeth, elephant's shoulders, and bull's eyes, and was very strong. With her, the son of Kuntibhoja, the Kurunandana, united, blessed with immense fortune, like Pulomā with Maghavan. Even with Devavrata, the daughter of Madra, renowned in the three worlds, was known as Mādri, the daughter of the king of Madra. Renowned among all kings for her beauty, she was sought after for the sake of Pāṇḍu with great wealth at that time. Bhīṣma arranged the marriage of the great-souled Pāṇḍu. The strong Pāṇḍu, with lion-like shoulders, elephant's shoulders, and bull's eyes, was admired by men on earth. Endowed with the strength of Pāṇḍu, he, desiring to conquer the earth, faced many enemies.

English: The warriors who were previously defeated in battle by the lion among men, Pāṇḍu, are now honored. Then, taking the army, Pāṇḍu advanced with the chariot of Nona, filled with numerous elephants, horses, and foot soldiers. The enemies of the valiant ones, who are the protectors of the earth, were defeated by the one who was killed in Rajagṛha. Then, taking the Kauravas, the vehicles and forces, Pāṇḍu went to Mithilā and defeated the Videhas in battle. Thus, in the battle of the Kauravas, with the strength of his own arms, he made the Bharata shine. The great flame of arrows, like the fire of Pāṇḍu, consumed the kings. They, with their armies, were destroyed by the powerful kings. All were defeated on the earth, all the rulers of the earth. They regarded him as the hero among the gods, like Purandara. All the kings bowed down with folded hands. They approached the wealth, taking various riches. Jewels, pearls, gold, silver, and various chariots and elephants.

English: The king of Nagpur seized that. Pandava, having taken that, again with the chariot of joy, will delight the kingdoms and the city with the help of elephants. The sound of the lost Kītija was revived by Pandu, of the wise Sāntanu and Bharata. Those who previously destroyed the Kauravas were made to pay by the lion of Nagpur, Pandu. Thus spoke the kings and the ministers gathered, their minds pleased, along with the townspeople and the subjects. They, having approached him, advanced like rivers, led by Bhīṣma. Surrounded by many kinds of people, they were joyful. With various vehicles, and also with elephants, chariots, and cows, they arrived. The Kauravas did not see the end upon reaching Bhīṣma. He bowed to his father's feet, the son of Kośalya, as I honored the townspeople. Having fulfilled the purpose of the neighboring kingdoms, Bhīṣma returned, having reached his son. He, with the great sounds of the drums of the assembled troops.

English: He spoke on the mountain tops and in the great forests. Pandava lived in the forest with Kuntī, like a mighty elephant in the midst of the herd. In Bharat, along with his brothers, the king skilled in supreme weapons, the valiant Vichitrakethu. This god is indeed wandering among the forest dwellers. Desiring pleasures and enjoyments, the men, always alert, were urged by Dhṛtarāṣṭra. Then he heard of the daughter of Devaka, the lord of the earth, endowed with beauty and youth. Then, having chosen her, the noble man arranged the marriage of the great-minded Vidura. And Vidura, the son of Kuru, produced sons endowed with good qualities. BRR STATS 107 dd qaqa spoke. Then, a hundred sons were born to Janamejaya in Gandhāra, and one son was born to Dhṛtarāṣṭra, surpassing the hundred.

English: The five sons of Pāṇḍu, the great charioteers, were born to Kuntī and others, having been offered to the gods for the continuation of the lineage. Janamejaya said: How was the son of the Kaurava born to Gāndhārī, the best of the twice-born? What was the duration of their lives and what else? How did the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra become one with a courtesan? How did he marry the virtuous Gāndhārī? While being favorable, Dhṛtarāṣṭra was very devoted. How did the great-souled Pāṇḍu, who was seized, give rise to the five great charioteers? This incident, which is known, should be narrated in detail, O ascetic, for I am not satisfied with what is being said about the relatives. Vyāsa said: Gāndhārī, who was in a state of distress, approached the sage Vyāsa and pleased him, and he granted her a boon. She chose a hundred sons for herself, and then she conceived through Dhṛtarāṣṭra. For a year, Gāndhārī carried the womb, but she then experienced great sorrow. The birth of the sons.

English: Hearing about Kuntī's son and the might of Bhāga, he contemplated the stability of his own belly. Unbeknownst to Dhṛtarāṣṭra, with great sorrow, Gāndhārī caused her brother to fall. Then, a muscle was born, tightly bound like iron. From the womb filled with poison, it began to move. Then, knowing the two-faced one, he quickly approached. He seized that fleshly form while chanting. Then he spoke, "What is this you desire?" And she, knowing the truth, praised the supreme purpose. Hearing about the elder Kuntī's son, who was like the sun, I have fallen into this belly with great sorrow. O Kīr, you have previously spread my sons. This fleshly form has been born for a hundred sons. Vyāsa said: Thus, this is the case, O Soubaleya; it would not be otherwise. My words are not false; where else could it be? Let a hundred pots filled with ghee be quickly prepared. Let them be sprinkled with cold water and this be consecrated.

English: She was being poured out like a stream then. Of the separate streams of the unblemished essence. A hundred and one full, as appropriate, O lord of the worlds. Then, in due course, the meat was served, O king, according to time. Then, in those pots, she poured out the essence. In the guarded vessels, she established protection. And the Lord, with the measure of the pot, Said, "These pots are to be broken." Thus spoke the Lord Vyasa and then arranged accordingly. He went to the ascetic Himavanta. Duryodhana, the king, was born from that action. By birth, the elder king Yudhishthira is the proof. When the son was born, Dhritarashtra was troubled. He gathered many Brahmins, Bhishma and Vidura alone. Yudhishthira, the royal son, the eldest among us, Has attained the kingdom due to his own qualities; there is nothing to be said against him. This one will also be a king after him. Indeed, this is my truth that will surely happen here. In the death of this statement, O Bharata, The flesh-eating, fierce beings and the terrible ones will arise. Having observed the ominous signs, they are terrible. The pure one will arise.

English: Vidura, the great sage, said: Your son will certainly be the one who brings about the end of your lineage. His peace will be great in abandoning the auspicious one. Let there be one less than a hundred sons for you, O king. With one, the Kuru will ensure the welfare of the world and the family. One should abandon for the sake of the family, and for the sake of the village, one should abandon the family. For the sake of the village, one should abandon the earth for one's own benefit. Thus, Vidura spoke, and all those who were wise agreed. But the king, attached to his sons, did not act accordingly. Then, within a month, a hundred sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra were born, and one daughter named Jātāghika was born. In Gandhāra, she was nurtured with care. Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the great king, was indeed blessed. In that year, the king Dhṛtarāṣṭra, of great fame, had a son named Yuyutsu, who was wise. Thus, a hundred sons were born to the wise Dhṛtarāṣṭra, and among the great warriors, there was one daughter named Duḥśalā.

English: Ugraśrava, the commander of Ashvasena, Tushparājaya. Aparājita, the learned one, with large eyes, difficult to conquer; strong-handed, with beautiful hands, and of swift speech. Adityaketu, Bahuśā, Nāgadanto, and the fierce one; Kavachī, Niṣadgī, and the staff bearer. Ugra, Bhīmaratha, the hero, with strong arms and restless; Abhayo, Rodrakama, and also Dhṛtaratha. Kundabhedī, Virāvī, with long eyes; Anādhrṣya, Kundabhedī, and Virāvī, with long eyes; Dīrghabāhu, Mahābāhu, with a golden banner. Kundāśī, Virajā, and also Duḥśalā, more than a hundred; this one, the daughter, is proclaimed, O king. Know the name and the order of birth, O king; all are your charioteers, all skilled in warfare. All are learned in the Vedas and proficient in royal sciences; all are adorned with the knowledge of various arts. All have suitable wives, O king of the earth; this was arranged by Dhṛtarāṣṭra at the appropriate time. In due time, the king gave Duḥśalā to the king of Sindhu, with the consent of Jayadratha.

English: Janamejaya said: The story of the Kauravas is indeed the best; it is inhuman among humans, O Brahman. Vairāmpāyana said: King Pandu, in the great forest, frequented by wild animals, During the mating season in the forest, he killed a herd of deer. That king, of great splendor, the son of a sage, engaged in austerities, Was united with his wife, taking the form of a deer. English: BYR possible wind Whether heedless or not, the one who is open is grasped by strength. Why do you hunt the deer? The deer said: I do not hunt, O king of deer, due to self-causation. But I shall wait for union with you. In the time of well-being for all beings, who indeed would kill a deer wandering in the forest? What you have done is false regarding the beloved of human effort. Among the sages of the Poravāṇas, who is there to match this? The great sin of human beings is condemned in the world. It is unworthy and unrighteous, O Bhārata. The one who knows the essence of scriptures and the nature of truth, is not like the divine, who is not to be harmed. By you, the sinful actions of humans are to be restrained, O best of kings, who are to be avoided by the three worlds. What have you done, O best of men, that you have caught me unawares? The sage who eats roots and fruits, disguised as a deer, O king. Always residing in the forest, ever devoted to peace. I have been harmed by you, therefore I shall not spare you.

English: The horse, having been enchanted by desire, will surely meet its end. I am indeed a sage named Kindama, unmatched in austerity, who has engaged in the act of mating among men. Having become a deer, I roam in the dense forest with other deer; this act of killing will not lead you to the sin of Brahma-hatya, as you do not know. Having taken the form of a deer, I am thus enchanted by desire. However, you will attain the fruit of this, for you will indeed enjoy companionship with your beloved, enchanted by desire. You too will go to the realm of the dead in this state. At the end, you will go to the beloved with whom you have associated, having reached the great difficulty of all beings. A devotee will follow you, being wise and superior in service. As you have brought me sorrow, so too will happiness come to you, and sorrow will approach you. Thus speaking, the deer, greatly afflicted by sorrow, detached from life, fell down in an instant.

English: The one who is covered by dust, without a place of refuge, residing at the root of a tree, indifferent to all that is dear and undear. Neither grieving nor rejoicing, equal in praise and blame, without hope, without salutation, without attachment, without possessions. Neither mocking anyone, nor desiring a hut, always with a cheerful face, engaged in the welfare of all beings. One who is free from all violence, equal to all living beings, always the same towards those who breathe. At one time, wandering as a beggar, whether in a family or among five, even if unable to obtain food, wandering without eating. Little by little, as much as can be eaten, by the gain of food, never exceeding the limit, in the absence of gain, filling seven. With one arm cut off, with one side adorned with sandalwood, neither auspicious nor inauspicious, meditating on both. Not wishing to live, nor acting like one who wishes to die, neither rejoicing in life nor hating death. Those who are alive, capable of performing actions of upliftment, they are all situated beyond the moment. In those states, abandoning all sense activities, having renounced all, with a pure mind, free from impurities. Freed from all sins, transcending one's own speech.

English: Not spoken by anyone, standing in the midst of the wind. With this continuous conduct, I will destroy fearlessly, having established myself. I do not walk on the path of the dog, unworthy of compassion. One who is engaged in any conduct with a desire for pleasure, he wanders the path of dogs. Veraṁpāyana said: Thus speaking, the king, deeply troubled, with a great sigh, looked at Kuntī and spoke to Mādrī. Kausalyā, Vidura, the king, and the relatives, along with Satyavatī, Bhīṣma, and the royal priest. The great-souled brāhmaṇas, drinkers of soma, and the aged Poruvas, who reside there, are our refuge. All should be spoken to, O Pāṇḍu, in the forest. Hearing the words of the steadfast one in the forest, Kuntī and Mādrī spoke the same words. There are also other hermitages that can be approached, O best of the Bharatas, along with the wives of the hermits, for great austerity. You alone will be the essence, even of heaven. The pure one.

English: In the practice of self-discipline, we shall perform great austerities, abandoning desires and pleasures. If you, O lord of the people, abandon us, we shall surely be defeated here. Pāṇḍu said: If this is determined, I shall follow the path of my father, adhering to the conduct of these two warriors. Abandoning the pleasures of life, I shall engage in great austerities, living on fruits and roots in the great forest. In the forest, both of us shall endure the hardships of hunger and thirst, and the weariness of the body. Enduring the cold, heat, hunger, and thirst, this body shall be worn down by severe austerities. Contemplating in solitude, I shall perform austerities with words dedicated to the ancestors and deities. Even for a hermit, the actions of the householders are not to be neglected; what to speak of those living in the village? Thus, I shall take on a more severe form of austerity in the forest. I shall remain steadfast in this body until its end. Vairāmpāyana said:

English: Thus, the king of the Kaurava lineage spoke. Then he gave the crown jewel and earrings. He also gave the fine garments and ornaments. After giving everything to the brāhmaṇas, Pāṇḍu spoke again. Pāṇḍu, having gone to the city of serpents, entered the forest. Abandoning all desires for wealth, pleasure, and the supreme bliss of the soul, the great Kurupūngava set out. Then, his attendants followed him. Hearing the various cries of compassion from Bharata's lion, they lamented, making a sound like Bhīma's lament. Shedding warm tears, they left the king behind and went to the city of Noga, taking grass with them. Hearing all this, the best of men, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, grieved for Pāṇḍu in the great forest as it happened. The prince, Pāṇḍu, who was eating the fruit of the Pāṇḍu tree, went to the mountain assembly with his wives. Having reached the Chaitraratha, he crossed the river Varuṇa and proceeded to the Himalayas, overcoming great obstacles, heading towards Gandhamādana. Protected by great beings and sages, the king then resided in all kinds of difficulties. Thus, the pure one was born.

English: The gardens of Kubera are similar and uneven; great rivers and mountains are also there. There are eternal snow and trees, and some great beings; some are unapproachable. No bird should transgress, for other animals do; the wind alone passes here, and the perfected ones are supreme. How can these enemies of the mountain king go? May they not suffer, O Bharatarṣabha. Pāṇḍu said: The great one without offspring does not see a wife. With debts combined, humans are born on earth. These, however, as they are, if a person does not understand, he has no worlds; thus, the knowledge of dharma is established. The sacrificer pleases the gods with study and austerity, and also with offerings to the ancestors, showing compassion to humans. I am released from the heat of the sages, gods, and humans; thus, I am liberated from the bondage of ancestors. In the destruction of the body, there is indeed destruction for the ancestors; hence, from here, the best of men are born for the sake of progeny.

English: As I was created by that great soul in my father's lineage, how can my offspring be born in this field of mine? There is indeed a divine and auspicious offspring of yours, O king, born of the sinless lineage, seen with divine vision. A man, wise and ungrasped by the fruits of actions, attains what is destined for him by the gods. In that case, O father, you should not hesitate; you will attain a virtuous offspring that will bring you joy. Hearing this from the ascetic, Pandu became absorbed in thought, knowing the action that had been obstructed. He spoke to Kuntī, the illustrious wife, about the means of producing offspring in times of distress. In the world, offspring is known as the establishment of dharma. Thus, Kuntī, the wise, understood the eternal dharma from the beginning. What is desired, given, performed as penance, and followed by rules, all of it is not considered pure without offspring here. Knowing this, I shall proceed with a pure smile, thinking that I will not attain the auspicious offspring.

English: Due to the curse of the deer, my progeny is lost, indeed, of the unselfish. O coward, just as the slain are thus. These are the relatives and heirs, O team of Dharma, listen to me, O Pṛthī, the six heirs. From the self-sacrifice, the son who is well-formed and the one born of a free woman. The one who is given, the one who is artificial, and the one who approaches himself, and the one who is born of a lowly womb. Considering the absence of the eastern and western, he should seek the son. The best and the worst of men desire a son in calamity. The righteous, who yield the fruit of Dharma, find the offspring. Even from the self-sperm, Manu, the self-born, spoke. You are indeed devoid of progeny, O TASES. You, O illustrious one, are either similar or superior in glory. Listen, Kunti, to this tale regarding Śāradaṇḍāyani, which is about the birth of the hero's offspring, appointed by the teacher. With flowers, having bathed at night, Kunti at the crossroads, having chosen the accomplished brāhmaṇa, having performed the fire sacrifice for progeny. When she was engaged in her duties, she dwelled there with her husband. There, she gave birth to three sons, the great charioteers. The birth is possible.

English: In that sacrifice, the divine beings, including Indra, approached the great soul, the righteous one. Indra, with the moon and the southern winds, performed the sacrifice. The king, Vyūṣitāśva, shone like the sun, surpassing all beings in brilliance. Having conquered and taken hold, the best of kings ruled over the eastern, western, and southern regions. In the great Ashvamedha sacrifice, the powerful Vyūṣitāśva became a king, accompanied by a host of elephants. The ancient scholars sing of Vyūṣitāśva, who conquered the land up to the ocean. He protected all his sons, like a father. The patron of the great sacrifice gave wealth to those outside. He also brought forth many excellent offerings. His sister, Kākṣīvatī, was of supreme beauty, resembling the goddess Bhadrā among men. The two desired each other, as the scriptures say. In that desire, he became afflicted with illness. The pure one was born.

English: He soon went to the setting sun like a wooden figure. In that corpse, the king of men was distressed by grief. The childless man-eater weeps, as we have heard. O king, know that the fortunate one is greatly afflicted. A woman who is knowledgeable in the highest dharma, without a son, lives without her husband; she does not live, she is distressed. Without a husband, I wish to go, O best of Kṣatriyas; please be gracious and lead me. Without you, I cannot bear to live even for a moment. O king, grant me your favor and lead me quickly. I will follow you from behind, through all difficulties. I, O best of men, will go where you go. Like a shadow, I will always speak, O king, remaining devoted to the welfare of the beloved. From today onwards, O king, the painful heart-wrenching will overwhelm me, without you, O lotus-eyed one. Surely, I am unfortunate; I have been separated from my companions. The connections are either due to the wise or the royal bodies. This is the result of sinful actions accumulated in previous bodies. The suffering that has come to me, O king, is due to your absence.

English: Thus addressed by her, the king spoke again to that goddess: "This is indeed the best speech, free from faults." Thus, Kunti, having been addressed, performed a great deed, As you have said, O auspicious one, he indeed became like an immortal. Now I shall speak of this, so listen to me: The ancient sages have described this as the supreme truth. In ancient times, the beautiful ones were unrestrained, Enjoying pleasures, free with their eyes like horses. Among those wandering maidens, the fortunate ones had husbands; There was no sin in their union, for he was indeed of ancient lineage. And those who were born of the people of the city, Even today, they are still engaged in desires, avoiding faults. This dharma, as seen in the ancient texts, is revered by the great sages. In the northern regions, the fame of Ramba still exists; He is indeed the eternal dharma, a benefactor of friends. In this world, soon, by me, this pure smile was established; From which it is to be elaborated. There was a sage named Udalaka, as we have heard; His son was known as Śvetaketu, who became a sage. This was done by me, as we have heard, for human beings; O lotus-eyed one, understand the reason for this.

English: 458 Saṃbhavapava Once, the Brahmin caught the hand of Śvetaketu in front of his mother and father, saying, "Let us go." The son of the sage, having become angry, forcibly took his mother away. The father, seeing him angry, spoke to Śvetaketu, "Do not be angry, my son; this is the eternal dharma." Indeed, all beings are not covered by the same qualities; just as cows stand in their respective colors, so do the progeny. The son of the sage then looked at Śvetaketu and spoke to him, "This is a sin for men of great fortune; it is not so for other beings." From that time onward, it has been heard that this is how it will be. The sin of killing a fetus will bring unhappiness from today onward. Regarding the unmarried girl, the celibate, when the unmarried girl is separated, it will indeed become a sin for the devoted wife. The one appointed by her husband and the one who is a devoted wife will not do this; this will indeed happen. Thus, the fearful one was established by the son of Uddālaka, Śvetaketu.

English: Yeo possible purity Thus addressed, Kuntī spoke to Pāṇḍu, the conqueror of enemies: "Speak, O noble one, who is devoted to the welfare of the beloved." "I, a girl, am engaged in the worship of the invited guests, there I serve the fierce one, the external vow." "Concealing the determination, they know that it is a difficult task; I, having a determined mind, did not please him." "That which is mixed with malice, the Lord revealed the boon; He granted me the mantra, just as the ocean does to me." "Whichever deity you will summon with this mantra, whether desiring or not desiring, that is yours." Thus I spoke then to the father of the Vedas, O Bharata; the Brahmin spoke the truth, and this Kato has arrived." "By your permission, O deity, I shall summon; by this mantra, O king, may our subjects be prosperous." "I summon which deity, tell me, O best among the wise; I am waiting for your instruction, standing in this place." Pāṇḍu spoke: "Today, O noble one, strive according to the proper method; surely summon the auspicious one, for he is indeed a share of the virtuous among the gods." "By unrighteousness, our righteousness shall not be joined at any time."

English: In the middle of the day, the sun is worshipped on the auspicious date. Kuntī, endowed with prosperity and fame, gave birth to a son at the right time. There is no doubt that he will be the greatest among the righteous. He is known as Yudhiṣṭhira, the first son of Pāṇḍu. He will become a renowned king, famous in the three worlds, endowed with strength and virtuous conduct. Having obtained that son, Pāṇḍu then spoke again: "Choose a son who is the strongest among the Kṣatriyas." Then, as spoken by her husband, she invoked the wind, and from that, the mighty Bhīma, the one of great prowess, was born. He was born as a powerful child, and it was declared that he is the greatest among all the strong. This was indeed wonderful; as soon as he was born, he shook the earth, causing the stone to crumble. Kuntī, having given birth, was astonished and did not realize that her son was born. Then, the son, like a thunderbolt, fell to the ground, and with that fall, his body was shattered into a hundred pieces. That stone, which was shattered, was a source of wonder to Pāṇḍu.

English: In that very day, Bhīma was born, the best of the Bharatas. Even the wealth of Duyodhana was born there, the lord of the earth. When born in the womb of Vrikodara, Pāṇḍu thought again, "How can my son, the best among men, become the greatest?" In the deeds of the gods and men, this indeed is established. There, the god is enjoyed according to the prescribed time. Indra is indeed the king of the gods, as we have heard. He is immeasurably strong and powerful, with great might. Having pleased him with austerity, I shall obtain a mighty son, Whom I shall give, he will be my son, he will be the most excellent. By action, mind, and speech, therefore, I shall perform great austerity. Then, the great-splendor Pāṇḍu, having taken me in his mind, Ordered Kuntī to perform a virtuous vow for a year. And with his own self, the mighty-armed one stood on one leg, Performing fierce austerity with supreme meditation. He worshipped the lord of the three worlds. Sūrya, with his own self, approached Bhārata. Then, with a great voice, Vāsava spoke, "I shall give you a son renowned in the three worlds." To the gods, the brāhmaṇas, and friends, the achievers, I shall give you a son, the best, who will destroy all enemies.

English: The king Kaurava, thus addressed by the great Vasava, spoke to Kuntī, remembering the words of the lord of the gods. The great-souled one, endowed with wisdom like the sun, is difficult to overcome and possesses a remarkable intellect. O virtuous one, give birth to a son of noble lineage, endowed with the valor of kṣatriyas, having received the grace of the lord of the gods, the pure-smiling one. Thus addressed, the illustrious Kuntī called upon Śakra, and then the lord of the gods arrived to grant her a boon. As soon as the boy was born, the voice of the incorporeal one resounded in the sky with a great and profound sound. Kuntī, equal to the Kātavīrya in valor, will give birth to one who will be renowned like Śakra. As the affection of Aditi for Viṣṇu was established, so will Arjuna increase the affection for you. This one, having made an alliance with the Madras and the Kauravas, will bring prosperity to the Kuru lineage. By the strength of his arms, the one who carries the sacrificial offerings will satisfy all beings with his abundance. Having conquered the kings of the earth, the mighty one, along with his brothers, will seize the wealth of the brave.

English: Jāmadagnya is equal to Kunti, equal to Vishnu in valor; he will be the greatest among the valorous in the future. Thus, he will bring forth all divine and celestial weapons; he will restore the lost glory of the Brahmins. Kunti's son spoke this wondrous speech, which the wind carried to the sky, and Kunti heard it. Hearing the speech of the ascetics, there arose great joy among the hosts of the hundred. Thus, there was a tumultuous sound of drums from the divine sages and the celestial beings. A great uproar arose, covered by a shower of flowers, as the assembled gods honored Partha. The Kadraveyas, the Vainateyas, and the Gandharvas, along with all the great sages, Bharadvāja, Kaśyapa, Gautama; Viśvāmitra, and Jamadagni; and he who was invoked by the sun, he too came here. Marīci, Aṅgiras, and Pulastya, Dakṣa, the Prajāpati, and the Gandharvas. The Apsarās, adorned with divine garlands and garments, sang and danced around Bhīma. Accompanied by the illustrious Tumburu, he sang.

English: The place of the sacrifice is the ghee, and the universe is also the offering. It is known as Uṣo, and it is called FSA and SAT. The killer, the friend, Varuṇa, Bhagā, Indra, Vivasvān, Pūṣa, Tvaṣṭa, and Savitā. Pajān̄jaya and also Viṣṇu, the Adityas, and the fire, standing in the sky, are killing the glory of the Pāṇḍava. The deer hunter and Bae, the great ones, Ajekapāda, Hivundhya, and Pinākī, the scorcher. Dahana, the lord, and Kapālī, and faa, the lord, and the great god, standing there. The Ashvins, the eight Vasus, and the great mighty Maruts, and the world gods and the Sādhya, were all present there. Kakotaka, AIA, Vāsuki, the serpent, Kacchapa, Apakunda, and Takṣaka, the great serpent. They were endowed with great energy, very angry, and very powerful. Many other serpents were also present there. Tārṣya, Ariṣṭanemi, Garuḍa with the black flag, and Aruṇa and Aruṇi, the sons of Vena, were present there. The great wonder astonished the best of the sages. The Pāṇḍavas were then engaged in their activities.

English: Let there be your grace upon me, and may it also be beneficial for you. Indeed, I am like a pillar due to my attachment to Kunti. If you are pleased, then inspire her yourself. Pāṇḍu said: This is always changing for me, O Mādrī. I cannot speak to you with the intention of what is desirable or undesirable. Knowing your opinion, I will strive for the utmost. I believe that what I say will be fulfilled. Then Pāṇḍu again spoke to Kuntī in solitude: O Kuntī, please make my progeny dear to the world. And for the destruction of my enemies, and for my own sake, O auspicious one, do the utmost good. When you perform the difficult task, you will attain sovereignty through Indra's sacrifices, which are desired by the worthy. Thus, the wise brāhmaṇas, through austerity, approach the gurus for fame, O beautiful one. Thus, all the kings and the brāhmaṇas, the ascetics, performed the difficult task for fame. May I, like a boat, save Mādrī, the blameless one.

English: By the division of offspring, may you attain the highest glory. Thus, having spoken to Mādrī, she thought of the deity. Therefore, your offspring will undoubtedly be suitable. Then, considering Mādrī, she went to the Ashvins in her mind. Upon their arrival, she gave birth to the twins. Ae, with Sahadeva, unparalleled in form on earth. Likewise, the twins also spoke with a body. Endowed with form, essence, and qualities, they shine with the wealth of beauty. They named them, the residents of the Jātash, and also with devotion, they honored the lord of the twenty-one. They called the eldest Yudhishthira, the middle one Bhīma, and the third Ajauṇa, thus imagining the sons of Kuntī. The former was Nakula, and thus Sahadeva, and the sons of Mādrī were spoken of by the pleased brāhmaṇas. Even after a year, you are born, O best of the Kurus. Then Kuntī again urged, "What is this?" The wise Pṛthā, always speaking the secret of kings, said to him. She said, "I am deceived by this, having once been told." I fear the fate of women. The birth is auspicious.

English: YOR possible winds With Palāśa, Tirakeśa, and Champaka, with Paribhadraka; And others with many trees, with the abundance of flowers. In the water place, adorned with various lotuses; Seeing the Pāṇḍava, Manmatha arose in the heart. There, delighting in the mind, like an immortal, He approached him, wearing a beautiful garment. Observing him, he, of that youthful form, His desire grew, like a rising sun in the deep. The king, with a secret heart, with lotus-like eyes, Could not control that desire, overpowered by the force of desire. Then the king forcibly seized her, who was hidden, With the goddess, shining forth as per her strength. He, with a heart filled with desire, did not understand that curse, Going towards Mādrī, in the act of love, like a force. At the end of life, the Kaurava, blessed by Manmatha, Leaving behind the fear of Rāpa, went away. His desire-filled mind was directly bewildered by time; Overcoming the group of senses, lost along with the mind. He, united with her, O Kurunandana, Pāṇḍu, with a supreme soul, engaged in the duty of time. Then Mādrī, embraced, approached the king, whose mind was gone.

English: Kuntī said: I am the eldest wife, my eldest is the fruit of dharma. O Bhāva, do not abandon me, the daughter of Madrī. I will search for my husband who has gone to the abode of the dead. Arise, and leave this child behind. Māgā said: I will follow my husband who has fled. Indeed, the eldest among desires should not be abandoned. And this one, weakened by desire, is coming to me. How can I cut off his desire? Nor will I remain without distinction among your sons. I will live in this manner, thus I will be. Therefore, O Kuntī, my sons should be treated as your own. This king, desiring me, has gone to the abode of the dead. With the king's body, I too am dead. Make this beloved one well concealed. Let there be no negligence towards the children, and may they be well. Therefore, I will not speak of anything else. Thus spoke the wife of the king.

English: Vardhamānapuradvāramāsasād Yāsvinī Hearing the arrival of thousands of Charanas and sages, a wonder arose among the people of Nāgapura. At the moment the sun rose, all the residents of the city, devoted to dharma, observed the auspicious sight. The assemblies of the Kṣatriyas and the groups of vehicles were gathered, along with the women of the Brāhmaṇas who accompanied them. Thus, there was a great disturbance among the groups of lightning, and none of the wise with dharma consciousness acted. Thus, Bhīṣma, the son of Śantanu, Somadatta, and Bāhika, along with the wise sage Vidura himself. And the goddess Satyavatī, along with the illustrious Kausalyā, surrounded by the royal ladies, and Gāndhārī also. The heirs of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, led by Duryodhana, adorned with a hundred ornaments, took their positions. Having saluted the great sages with their own words of respect, all the Kauravas, along with their priests, entered. Similarly, bowing down to the ground with their heads, they all entered, along with the people of the various janapadas. Understanding the crowd as if it were a great roar, Bhīṣma presented the kingdom and the nation to the great sages.

English: The eldest among them, having risen, with matted hair, knowing the command of the great sage, spoke this. He, the king of the Pāṇḍavas, having abandoned sensual pleasures, went away from here with a hundred peaks. For one who observes celibacy, by divine cause, a son was born to him, Yudhiṣṭhira. Thus, from the powerful one, the great-souled king, Mātariśvā gave birth to a son named Bhīma, the mighty. From Puruhūta, in Kuntī, the one of true valor was born, whose fame will conquer all enemies. But from Mādrī, the best of the Kurus, the two man-lions were born, who stood firm like tigers among horses. While wandering in the forest, always adhering to righteousness, this lineage of Pāṇḍu is renowned. The birth of sons, their growth, and the study of the Vedas, were constantly observed by Pāṇḍu. Having attained the fruit of virtuous conduct, he went to the world of ancestors after seventeen days. Knowing that he had departed, Mādri, having left her life, entered the fire.

English: The virtuous king, Pandu, who is worthy of praise, is not to be mourned; he has five heroic sons, comparable to the sons of the gods. Then, Vidura, having spoken thus, along with Bhīṣma, performed the rites for Pandu, who was enveloped in great sorrow. Then, from the city, the offerings of grass and clarified butter were prepared. The fiery Pāṇḍavas were slain by the royal priest. Then, adorned with various ornaments, he was covered with a beautiful canopy. That canopy, adorned like a garland, was surrounded by great wealth, and the ministers, relatives, and friends stood by. The lion-man, adorned with supreme ornaments, was accompanied by the chief of the musicians, well-covered with fine cloth. With white and large umbrellas, and with fans made of peacock feathers, they made a great sound. Taking up many hundreds of weapons, the men fled from the Pāṇḍavas, who were there in their bodies. Then, the auspicious white umbrellas and large ones were raised. The priest, adorned with a beautiful garment, went ahead, shining brightly.

English: Brahmins, Kṣatriyas, courtesans, and Śūdras, countless in number, wept, tormented by grief, and followed the king. All the Pāṇḍavas, along with Bhīṣma and Vidura, cried out in the beautiful forest by the banks of the Ganges. They placed that truthful Shibikā, the wife of Nṛsiṃha, in the chariot of Pāṇḍu. Then, his body, fragrant with all kinds of scents, was bathed with pure water and anointed with the main bath. With the water of the sacred pot, quickly filled with pure water. With sandalwood and the main ingredient, they anointed him with the essence of time and the essence of the lofty. Then, they covered him with a garment, like a lion among men. The man-lion, a great tiger among men, was properly laid to rest. Having been permitted by the officiating priest, he was engaged in the funeral rites, anointed with ghee, along with his own ornaments. With the mixture of the lofty lotus and fragrant sandalwood, and with various other scents, they burned him with a gentle fire. The pure essence.

English: Then, having entered the bodies of both of them, the illusion of SBT took hold. "Alas, my son!" cried Kausalyā, and she fell suddenly to the ground. Seeing his mother fallen, the people of the city and the countryside wept loudly, along with the king's loyal subjects, who were accompanied by Kṛpa. Exhausted by the sound of the wind, all beings, including humans and those in lower forms of life, cried out. Thus, Bhīṣma, the son of Śantanu, and Vidura, the wise one, along with all the Kauravas, were deeply pained. Then, Bhīṣma, Vidura, and the king, along with their relatives, performed the water rites, as did all the women of the Kuru clan. Having taken the ashes of the Pandavas, the hundreds of followers of their command, by nature, began to pour out the water. Just as the Pandavas slept on the ground with their relatives, so did the citizens, the king, and the brāhmaṇas. That city, which was devoid of joy and health, became like a great ocean of sorrow for the Pandavas.

English: The sage said: Then the king and the mighty Bhīṣma, along with their relatives, performed the śrāddha for the Pāṇḍavas, which was filled with the essence of their own nectar. After feeding the prominent Kauravas and many others, they also gave to the village leaders. Then the citizens of Vāraṇāvatī took the Pāṇḍavas, the best of the Bharatas, into the city. The people, always remembering the great Bharata, mourned as if they had lost their own kin. At the end of the śrāddha, seeing that distressed person, Vyāsa spoke to the grieving mother. The times of happiness have passed, and the dreadful times have arrived; each day is worse than the previous one for the world. Overwhelmed by various troubles and filled with many faults, a terrible calamity will arise due to the neglect of righteous actions. Go, taking to renunciation, and stay in the forest of austerities; do not witness the terrible fate of this family. Thus, having received permission, she set out, O Sūshāmā, for the son of Ambikā, who is indeed a great Bharata. The birth of the pure.

English: When the fruits of the trees are being plucked, Bhīma shakes the tree with his foot. Struck by the force of the blow, the branches, filled with fruits, fall down. Then, the renowned Dhātara, knowing Bhīma's strength, became filled with wicked thoughts. From the sinful thoughts of this wicked one, a desire arose due to greed. This Bhīma, the son of Kuntī, is the strongest among the mighty. Let him be restrained by the eldest, Yudhishthira, among the sons of Pāṇḍu. Thus, having made this wicked determination, Duryodhana then constantly plotted against the great Bhīma. Then, for the purpose of water sports, he arranged various grand and colorful games.

English: The place of the proof is approached by someone, and at the end of the game, all of them, adorned with their own ornaments, slowly enjoyed the abundant food. At the end of the day, exhausted after their play, the heroes took rest in the pleasure houses. However, distressed by excessive exercise, the mighty one, having carried the young ones who had come to play, the one seeking residence in the place of proof fell asleep there. Feeling cold, having gathered his clothes, the exhausted Pandava, intoxicated and bewildered, lay motionless like a dead man. Then, Duryodhana, bound by the desire, caused the deep, swift water of Bhīma to fall. Then, awakened, the son of Kuntī, having cut all bonds, rose from the water and struck Bhīma, the best of warriors. And also, having been asleep, he was bitten by the sharp fangs of the great poison. Angered, they bit him, and all the flesh was struck down. The teeth of the biting ones fell upon him, but they did not pierce his skin due to the thickness of his broad chest. Awakened, Bhīma struck all of them with his fists, and he also struck his charioteer, his beloved, with that blow.

English: While hunting, a certain warrior of King Śantanu encountered a pair in the forest. The bow and arrows, as well as the black deer skins, were prepared for the archery expert. He then presented the pair to the king, accompanied by Kṛpa. Taking the pair, he came home, saying, "These are my sons." Then he performed the necessary rituals and ceremonies. Gautama, having arrived, also became involved. Due to the bond formed by the two boys, the king established their lineage. Gautama, being there, found the truth through austerity. Upon arriving, I revealed my lineage and other details. Various types of archery were described in four divisions. With this, I revealed all the secrets. Soon after, he attained the status of a great teacher. Then all the great charioteers, including the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra and the mighty Pāṇḍavas, went to learn archery. The Kauravas and other kings from various regions also gathered. The end of the story.

English: Bhīṣma spoke. Then Bhīṣma, with great anger, addressed the sons of Pāṇḍu. The great sage Bharadvāja, while performing a sacrifice, saw the celestial nymphs directly. The wind, having arisen, carried away her garment. Then the sage Droṇa took hold of her essence. In that moment, a great battle arose, and he, the wise one, taught the Vedas and their branches completely. The illustrious Bharadvāja, having been honored, then offered the fire oblation to the best of the strong. That sage, knowing the truth, then honored the best of the Bharatas. There was a king named Pṛṣata, a friend of Bharadvāja. His son was named Drupada.

English: He regularly went to the hermitage and played with Drona, engaging in study as well. Then, after some time, King Drupada emerged, a great warrior among men. Bharadvāja also ascended to heaven at that time, and then, due to attachment to his son, the highly renowned one was appointed by his ancestors. Then Drona found Kripi, the sister of Jarādvatī. He who is always engaged in righteousness and self-control, and is devoted to the good, is indeed Ashvatthama. As soon as he was born, a horse was born as well. Hearing the sound of the horse, he who is in the sky spoke. As the horse went to the place of the river, this boy Ashvatthama will be known by that name. With that son, Bharadvāja was very pleased, and there, he became a master of the Vedas. He heard of the great soul, the son of Jamadagni, who was a great warrior, and he was surrounded by Brahmins. Then Bharadvāja spoke to Rama, who was about to set out into the forest, saying, "Know that Drona is coming, desiring wealth." Rama said, "It is possible."

Receiving all of that, the best of the twice-born, pleased with his dear friend, went to Drupada.

English: 492 Saṃbhavapava Then, having approached Dṛupada, the illustrious Bhāradvāja spoke to the king, his friend, "Know me." Draupadā said: "Your wisdom is not appropriate for this; you have not made me your friend in a fitting manner." Indeed, among kings, no one becomes friends with a low-minded person who is devoid of glory and wealth. Let them decay over time; may you have previously been bound by strength. In this world, friendship is never seen with the imperishable; desire plays and anger drives it. Thus, let us establish a new friendship; you have been my bond of wealth, O best of the twice-born. Neither the poor nor the wise have a friend; what will remain of friendship if it is not based on prior bonds? Friendship and marriage are not between those who have equal wealth and lineage, but between those who are prosperous and impoverished. Neither the unlearned has a friend in the learned, nor the charioteer in the king; what will remain of friendship in the king's garage? Vairāmpāyana said:

English: Draupadī thus addressed the mighty Bhāradvāja. He contemplated for a moment, filled with anger. Having firmly resolved in his mind, the wise one went to the city of the Kurus, called Nāgasāhya. The princes, having emerged, gathered at the place of the elephant, joyfully playing there. That Vīṭā fell into the well while they were playing, and they did not return to rescue her. Then Drona, having performed the PARKA, spoke slowly with cunning. Alas, how lamentable is the strength of the Kṣatriyas! Woe to you who have failed to rescue Vīṭā, born in the lineage of Bharata! This fist of mine, empowered by the mantra of the weapon, behold its valor, for there is none like it. I shall know Vīṭā through the mantra of the weapon, and through another, I shall unite with her in my grasp. Then the princes beheld her, astonished and with eyes wide open, having discovered the Vīṭā, they approached the Vīṭā-keeper. We salute you, O Brahman; this is not known to others. Who are you? What do we know of you? What shall we do?

English: Drona said: "Please tell me about Bhīṣma's form and qualities. He is indeed very wise and will soon take charge." Vaśampāyana said: "Thus, all of them replied to Bhīṣma, our grandfather, saying that the words of the Brahman are true, and that action is like a curse." Hearing the words of the princes, Bhīṣma recognized Drona, thinking, "He is indeed a capable teacher." Then, having brought him there, Bhīṣma, the best among those wielding bows, respectfully inquired of him. In response to the reason for his arrival, Drona conveyed everything. "From the great sage's neck, I have come here, O infallible one, to learn the science of archery." The celibate, self-controlled, and matted-haired one, remained there for a long time, desiring to learn archery. The son of the king of Pañcāla, Yajñasena, very powerful, was engaged in the service of the teacher, being attentive with me. He was my friend there and was also helpful and dear to me. Thus, I remained happily associated with him for a long time. In childhood, we studied together.

English: 496 Saṃbhavapava Thus addressed by Dronapāla, Bhīṣma, filled with anger, went to the Kurus, endowed with virtues. Bhīṣma received him along with the sons of Pāṇḍu, taking the grandsons and various Vasu deities. He gave the king the name Rīṣya according to the prescribed method, and he, the great archer, received the Koravas. Receiving them, Drona spoke the following words: "One who is truly devoted and has performed the necessary rites." "What is my task? Please tell me, as I am surrounded by many." "Those who have been armed, let them speak the truth." Hearing this, the Koravas, desiring to rule the world, all pledged their allegiance to the great conqueror. Then, embracing the unyielding one repeatedly with joy, he wept with delight. Then Drona took various weapons from the sons of Pāṇḍu, both divine and human, endowed with valor. The royal sons and others, gathering together, approached Drona, the best of the twice-born, with half of the weapons. The Vṛṣṇis and the Andhakas, as well as various other kings, came together. The son of the charioteer, Rādhā, also went to Drona at that time.

English: Drona, having seen Arjuna, once again engaged in battle with chariots and elephants, and even on the ground, displayed his martial skills. In the mace fight, he demonstrated his prowess with the tomara and prāsa weapons, and in the fierce battles, he challenged the Pandavas. The kings and princes, witnessing his skill, gathered in thousands. Then, the son of the Nishada king, with a golden bow, approached the great king Drona. He did not seize him, thinking him to be a Nishada, and observed them with a keen eye. But the son of Drona, having reached the forest, struck Drona on the head. At that time, firmly established in the teacher's conduct, he engaged in archery with great discipline. With utmost faith and through supreme yoga, he attained the lightness of being, leading to liberation. Then, once permitted by Drona, the Kurus and Pandavas, skilled in hunting, set out. There, a man, with some equipment, went alone, taking a dog with him to the Pandavas. As they wandered there, they desired to achieve various things.

English: The dog, foolish, went to Nishada in the forest. Seeing Krishna, whose body was smeared with filth, wearing a black deer skin in the forest, the dog barked and stood near him. Then, the dog, barking, released seven arrows from its mouth, as if it had let go of tenfold lightness. That dog, having approached the Pandavas, the heroes, caused them great astonishment. The lightness and sharpness of sound, then, protected it, and the bashful ones praised it. Then, searching for it, the Pandavas, residing in the forest, saw it, O King, constantly releasing arrows. They did not recognize it then, in that distorted form. Then they asked it, "Who are you, and whose path do you follow?" Ekala vyasa said: "O hero, son of the lord of Nishada, the one with the golden bow, Drona's disciple, I am the one who has been burdened by the weight of wealth." Hiranyapayana said: Knowing him thus, the Pandavas returned and told Drona everything that had happened. O King, remembering the one who was to be remembered, the son of Kunti.

English: Upon meeting Drona, I spoke this affectionate word: "Having embraced you, I shall not be separated from you." Then why should I, who am strong, be less than anyone in the world? There is another disciple of yours, the son of the chief of the Nishadas. After contemplating for a moment, Drona made a decision, Taking Savyasāchin, he went towards the Nishada. Ales, with his body smeared with mud, Was constantly holding a bow, like a dense cloud. However, Ekalaavya, approaching Drona, Humbly bowed down to the ground. After worshipping Drona properly, the son of the Nishada, Having introduced himself, stood with folded hands before him. Then Drona spoke this word to the king: "If you are my disciple, let the fee be grass." Hearing this, Ekalaavya, pleased, spoke: "What shall I give, O Lord? Let my Guru command me." Indeed, I have nothing to give to my Guru, the knower of Brahman. He said, "Let the right hand be given to me, which is covered with dust." Hearing Drona's harsh words, Ekalaavya, always devoted to protecting his promise, remained steadfast in truth.

English: Thus, having taken away the face, the mind became agitated. Cutting through the doubt, he gave it to Droṇa, who was like a lump of flesh. Then, however, Naiṣādī began to pull like a wild animal. He was not as swift as the previous king. Then Arjuna, with a pleased mind, became free from fever. And Droṇa was indeed truthful; no one else became like him. At that time, Droṇa's disciple, especially worthy of the mace, was Duryodhana, and Bhīma approached the Kauravas. Aśvatthāmā was superior in all secrets. Thus, he was like a man among men, both Sārūka and Yamajā. Yudhiṣṭhira was the best of charioteers, and everywhere was Dhanañjaya. In the ocean, the charioteer of the chariot troop was present. In the enthusiasm of wisdom, the Pāṇḍava was in all aspects. In the love of the blood, he became a hero, equal in the teachings of blood and valor. Alone, Arjuna became a great charioteer. More than life, Bhīma was knowledgeable, and Dhanañjaya was wise. The wicked ones, the kings, were envious. They gathered all the warriors, firmly established in all sciences. Droṇa, knowledgeable in weaponry, was curious about the best of men.

English: Drona, displeased, said, "This cannot be achieved by you, you are merely mocking." Then, Duryodhana and others, with great fame, inquired about the situation. Others, including Bhīma and others from different regions, were also mocked. Then, Drona, smiling, spoke to Dhananjaya, "You should aim at this target now." "Your aim should be to hit the target, son of Madayā, stay there for a moment." Thus instructed, the left-handed one, with desire, stood ready, urged by his teacher's words. After a moment, Drona spoke to him, "Look at this target, it shines brightly." Arjuna replied to Drona, "I do not see the tree or you." Then, pleased, Drona again spoke to him, "Look at the target of the Pāṇḍavas." "Do you see the target? Speak again." Arjuna replied, "I do not see the target clearly."

English: Drona, thus addressed, with a joyful body, released Partha, saying "Let go!" without hesitation. Then, the Pandava, with a sharp sword, struck off the head of that one who was in the city. In that action, having succeeded, he embraced Phalguna, and thought of Ud as defeated with a connection. At some point in time, the best of the Angiras, having gone to the Ganges, Drona, having submerged, was seized by a powerful being, urged by time. Though capable of liberation, he did not urge the Rishis. Having killed the seizer, he hastened, saying "Liberate me!" That statement, however, was met with a piercing arrow from Bhīma. With five seizers, he struck the great being, the one who was like a mother. The others, however, bewildered, fell here and there. Drona, seeing him engaged in action, did not consider the Pandava, and there arose affection for his own disciples. He was like a broken arrow, and the seizer attained the fifth state, having abandoned the great soul. Then, the great chariot warrior, having newly arrived, said "Take this, O mighty-armed one, it is very difficult to bear."

English: In the presence of Gāṅgeya, Vyāsa, and Vidura, the princes, knowledgeable in the scriptures, arrived, and with your permission, O King, they will impart their teachings. Then the great king spoke, filled with joy in his heart: "O best of the brāhmaṇas, what great work has been done for you by Bhāradvāja?" When you think of the wood in which the body is, as it is, so you should command me for the arrangement. I desire today, out of weariness, to see my sons, who are of great valor. The teacher Dururācārya will be so, O Kuru, for I do not think that such a beloved one will be like a righteous one. Then, following Vidura, the king went outside, and the great sage Bhāradvāja measured the earth. In that place, the earth was established, with the water flowing around it. In that place, the earth performed a sacrifice, worshipped by the moon and stars, and it was also proclaimed in the city for that purpose. The TAT Bags were arranged properly, and the artisans worked there. The king, equipped with all weapons, and the women too. The people of the villages were made to perform the rituals there. The fire of the house of the Jatugṛha was purified.

English: 508 Jatugṛhadāhapavaṁ Then the mighty ones, bound by their bodies, with their arms bound, like the bulls of Bharata, shot arrows with great force. The elder brother Yudhiṣṭhira and the others followed him there, these great heroes, the sons, were truly wonderful. Some, fearing the arrows, looked at the sky with astonishment. They were targets, struck by various arrows, and they released diverse arrows from their bows. There, the group of princes, having taken hold of the bow, saw the city of the Gandharvas and were filled with wonder. Suddenly, there were hundreds of thousands of men there, with eyes wide open in amazement, saying "Well done, well done!" Having taken their bows, they repeatedly struck the elephants and the backs of the horses in battle. Having taken hold of the sword, they struck again and again. The lightness and beauty of the firm grip of the sword was evident in the use of the sword and shield by all. Then, the ever-strong Suyodhana and Vṛkodara, descended, with their maces in hand, like two lions. The mighty one, bound by his arms, stood firm in valor.

English: This is Partha, the great king, Phalguna, the son of Pandu. FTE said: I am indeed blessed, I am protected, O great-minded one, by the Pandavas, who are like the rising sun. Veraṁpāyana said: In that arena, when it was somewhat established, the terrible Vibhatsu unleashed a fierce attack. The foremost released the water, the Varuṇa released the water, the Vāyavya released the wind, and the Pāñcajanya released the sound. The earth was entered by Bhoma, and the Pāvate released the winds, and in the end, AT was again hidden. In an instant, the momentary one, the swift one, and the one driven by the chariot, in a moment, stood in the middle of the chariot and in a moment, seized the earth. The delicate one and Ben, and also the beloved of the teacher, united with the arrow of the two kinds. While wandering, the foremost of the boar, in the forefront of the inquiry. He released five arrows, unconnected, like a single arrow. The great hero dug deep, with many arrows.

English: The man with the dazzling eyes entered the vast stage, like a conqueror of enemies. He wore a natural armor, his face illuminated by shining earrings, like the wind that moves swiftly. PART: The one with great fame, broad eyes, and sharp rays, is the enemy-slayer of the Kauravas. He is equal to the lion, the elephant, and the king of beasts, shining like the sun and moon combined. The young one, golden in hue, is the slayer of lions, possessing countless virtues, born from the essence of Bhāskara. The mighty-armed one, observing the grand stage, bowed down to Drona and Kripa, as if he were a humble servant. The entire assembly was still, with steady gazes, wondering who had arrived, filled with curiosity. He spoke with a voice like a cloud, addressing his unknown brother, the one seated on the throne of Savitṛ. What you have done, I will do, without anger; behold, the wonder of men is within me. As soon as he finished speaking, the crowd, as if startled, quickly rose in all directions.

English: 514 Jatugṛhadāhapavaṁ And the tiger among men, Duryodhana, was touched by affection. He spoke to Bhīma, the terrible one. Then, having been permitted by Droṇa, the beloved one always, What was done there by Partha, the great warrior. Then Duryodhana, there with his brothers, O Bhārata, Embracing Karṇa with joy, spoke these words. Welcome to you, O mighty-armed one, you have arrived as a guest. And I too, let the Kuru kingdom be enjoyed as you wish. Karṇa spoke: All has been done by another for me, and you have become my friend. I wish to engage in battle with Partha, O Bhārata. Duryodhana spoke: Ah, the pleasures I have enjoyed with my relatives. Let all the Kurus be united, O fool, let the feet of the enemy be crushed. Vērāmpāyana spoke: Then, considering himself as if thrown away, Partha spoke, Like a mountain standing firm in the midst of the brotherhood. Those who are uninvited and come without invitation, Those people, O Karṇa, you will face as I have encountered them. Karṇa spoke:

English: Your birth, O King, is also destined. How will a deer give birth to a tiger-like being? This one is worthy of the earth's kingdom, O Lord of Men. With this strength of arms and my ignorance, This action of mine is not to be tolerated by any man. Let the charioteer take away the lustful one. Then there was a great uproar from all the spectators, Connected with the praises of the good, and the sun set. Then Duryodhana, holding onto a corner, The light was made to shine from that stage. The Pandavas along with Drona and the Kauravas, All of them went to their respective abodes with Bhīṣma. Some said "Ajuna," some "Karna," and some "Duryodhana," Thus speaking, they set out. Recognizing Kunti, the one with divine features, The joy of Gāra was concealed. Then, having approached Duryodhana, Karna, Fearful of Arjuna's command, quickly disappeared. And that hero, having been made weary by the battle, Spoke to Suyodhana with great effort.

English: Thus speaking, he laughed and then said again: "Do not fear for your life, O king; we are capable." In the hermitage, what was done by you in childhood with me, by that, you have been nurtured, O Kṣatriya. This friendship has been established by you, O best of men; I grant you a boon, O king, of the lowest rank in the kingdom. A king should not be a friend of kings; therefore, I have made efforts in the kingdom, O Yajñasena. You are a king on the southern bank; I am on the northern bank of the Bhāgirathī; recognize me, O Pāñcāla, if you think so. Darapad said: This is not surprising, O Brahman, among great souls; I love you, and from you, I desire eternal affection. Veraṃpāyana said: Thus addressed, Droṇa liberated him, O Bhārata; having honored him, he joyfully returned to his kingdom. On the banks of the Ganges, in the city of a hundred villages, he resided, with a mind disturbed, in the excellent city of Kāmapiḷya. The river flowing southward is the Pāñcālā; Remembering the wealth, Droṇa was filled with emotion.

English: The king has attained the kingdom, how can he not become a ruler? Thus, Bhīṣma, the son of Śāntanu, the one who is true to his vows and has great austerity, having renounced the kingdom long ago, will never accept it. We shall anoint the eldest of the Pāṇḍavas, the young one, the wise one, the one who is compassionate and knows the truth. He will indeed worship and unite with his son, the one who knows righteousness, Bhīṣma, and Dhṛtarāṣṭra. Hearing these words, Duryodhana spoke to those who were attached to Yudhiṣṭhira. The wicked-minded one, tormented, could not bear their words and, being envious, approached Dhṛtarāṣṭra. Then, having worshipped his father, who was without a protector, he spoke this in anguish for the people. I have heard the words of the people, O father, during the day; they desire you, Bhīṣma, and wish for the Pāṇḍava as their lord. This is Bhīṣma's opinion; he does not desire the kingdom. However, the people in the city wish to inflict great suffering upon us. Having attained the kingdom from our father, due to the qualities of the Pāṇḍavas, you too, due to the association with the unworthy, will not attain the kingdom. If the Pāṇḍava obtains the inheritance of Pāṇḍu, his son will surely attain it, and another will also be born to him.

English: The king's father, especially with assistance. The strength of the sons and grandsons of Pāṇḍu is always supported. The people of Paurava were honored by Pāṇḍu. How can they not kill Yudhiṣṭhira along with his relatives? Duryodhana said: Thus, O father, I have perceived this fault within myself. The natures of the people are indeed aligned with this. Surely, your allies will primarily be those who are with us. He will soon expel the Pāṇḍavas from the city of Vārāṇavat. When the kingdom is established with me, O king, Kuntī will return with her sons to Bhārata. Ghaṭotkaca said: Duryodhana, I too do not wish to reveal the sinful nature of this intention. Neither Bhīṣma nor Droṇa nor Kṣatta nor Gautama will support the Kauravas when they are being expelled. Indeed, this is the age of the Kauravas, O sons.

English: Some ministers, summoned by Dhṛtarāṣṭra, spoke of the beautiful city of Vārāṇasī. This society is indeed the most beautiful on earth, present in the city of Vārāṇasī under the lord of poetry. Thus, stories were narrated based on Dhṛtarāṣṭra's words. While speaking in the beautiful city of Vārāṇasī, the Pandava princes were mentioned by the king. When the king expressed curiosity about something else, the son of Ambikā, the Pandava, spoke. These men always tell me repeatedly that Vārāṇasī is the most beautiful city in the world. O father, if you think of celebrating in Vārāṇasī, go with your entourage and enjoy like the gods. To the brāhmaṇas and singers, give as desired, like the gods. Some, having enjoyed the festivities, experienced great joy. This is indeed Hastinapura, where the happy will return. Understanding Dhṛtarāṣṭra's desire, Yudhishthira replied to him about his own helplessness.

English: Purōcana, having brought the chief of the Bharata, spoke to his minister after taking him by the right hand. This land, full of wealth, is indeed my Purōcana. Just as my father protects it, so do I wish to protect it. Indeed, there is no one else for me who is more trustworthy than you. You are the ally by whom I can achieve my desires. Protect me, O father, and rescue me. Do what I wish with a clever means. The Pāṇḍavas, sent by Dhṛtarāṣṭra, will enjoy themselves in Vāraṇāvata under the rule of Dhṛtarāṣṭra. You, with the chariot drawn by donkeys, should go to Vāraṇāvata today as you wish. Having gone there, establish the four corners of the house, which is well fortified, and make it a great treasure by taking shelter in the storehouse. Among the various materials, some of which are made of shānasa and other substances, you should offer those that are suitable for the fire. Mixing ghee with the clay and also with the red lac, you should apply the paste in the huts. Ghee from the shānā tree, wood, and various instruments, in that place, you should place all of them around.

English: The Pāṇḍavas, having mounted their chariots, approached like the wind. Ascending, they grasped the feet of Bhīṣma. To the king Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the great-souled Drona, and the elders Vidura and Kṛpa, Thus, having saluted all the aged Kurus, the resolute ones, they also saluted the assembled ones. With their mothers behind them, they performed circumambulation and all the natural ones proceeded towards the abode. Vidura, the great sage, and other Kurus of noble lineage, along with the townspeople, followed the men, afflicted by sorrow. There, some Brahmins, trembling, lamented for the Pāṇḍu sons, greatly distressed, O best of the Bharatas. The king, enveloped in darkness, was in a difficult situation; Dhṛtarāṣṭra, of poor intellect, was violating dharma. Indeed, the Pāṇḍava, or Bhīma, the strongest of the strong, or Kuntī's son, would not delight in sin. What indeed will the great sage, the son of Mādrī, do? That kingdom, obtained from the father, is not to be despised by Gṛtarāṣṭrī; Bhīṣma, however, approves of the lowest of the low. While being exiled, the sons of Kuntī, O best of the Bharatas, are in a difficult position.

English: 532 Jatugṛhadāhapavaṁ Indeed, the king is like a father to us, having previously been a peaceful protector. The valorous king, Pāṇḍu, is a joy to the Kuru lineage. In that man, the tiger among men, when the destined time has come, The sons of the king, the young ones, do not suffer from Gṛhatarāṣṭrī. We do not suffer from this; we shall leave our homes and go where Yudhiṣṭhira goes. Thus speaking to the distressed citizens, the righteous king Yudhiṣṭhira, filled with great joy, addressed them. The father is to be honored, the teacher is the best, as said by the lord of the earth. We do not doubt that we are to be honored by him. You, our friends, having made a circumambulation of us, Return to your homes with blessings as we depart. But if your work is to be done, may your prosperity and welfare be achieved. Then you shall do what is dear to me and beneficial. They, having made that promise and having circumambulated, With blessings, they indeed went to the city. When the citizens had returned, Vidura, the knower of dharma, Spoke this word to the best of the Pāṇḍavas. The wise one, knowing the essence of wisdom, Understands how to escape from calamity.

English: He who knows does not harm those who are hostile. He who protects himself does not get burned. One who does not see the path does not find fear. A man who takes what is not given becomes free from the fire. One who moves knows the directions like the stars. By making a decision, Vidura, with the Pandavas' permission, went home. When Vidura returned, Kunti spoke to Bhīṣma and the people. If a statement is made in the assembly, we know it is true. If it can be heard by us without fault, I wish to hear all the conversation between you and him. Yudhiṣṭhira said: Vidura told me that sorrow must be understood, and that no one knows the path.
