English: The machine and the bow were also artificially created. With that machine, King Get obtained gold. Darapad said: This bow is strung; with this arrow, whoever pierces the target is my son. Then King Drupada himself proclaimed it. Hearing that, all the kings gathered there, O Bharata. The great sages, with the intention of the svayamvara, Duryodhana and the Kurus, along with their followers, And the blessed Brahmins from various regions came. They were honored by the great-souled Drupada with royal gifts. Then all the townspeople, with the sound of the ocean, reached the city of Ridyumāra and settled there, along with the kings. In the auspicious part of the city, in the northern part, The assembly courtyard shone, surrounded by houses on all sides. Enclosed by walls and a fence, adorned with gates and arches, Covered all around with a beautiful canopy. Decorated with sandalwood water and garlands, it was splendid. The svayamvara of Draupadī.

English: Draupadī's Swayamvara Achutājī, adorned with all ornaments. Taking the valorous Kānsa, adorned with gold. The priest of the Somakas, pure and knowledgeable, then performed the ritual with clarified butter. After offering to the Brahmins, he proclaimed auspiciousness and restrained all musical instruments from all sides. In silence, then, the king of the Vishāmpates, with a deep voice, spoke. He uttered this excellent statement. "Listen, O kings, to this target; let it be known to you all. By surpassing the target with an arrow, you shall attain the bird." This task is indeed difficult; one who is endowed with strength and form. Today, my sister, Krishna, will not be in vain. Thus addressed, the son of Drupada then spoke to Draupadī, "With lineage and action, let us unite with these kings."

English: Dhṛṣṭadyumna said: Duryodhana, difficult to conquer, Duhśasana, and Vivinśati, along with Vikṇa, are present. Yuyutsu, with the speed of a lion, and Bhīma, the wielder of great strength, as well as Ugrāyudha, Balākī, and Kanakāyur, and Virocana. Sukundala, Chitrasena, and Kanakadhvaja, along with Nandaka, the strong-armed, and Kuṇḍaja, the fierce. These and many others, the mighty sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, have arrived with Karṇa. A hundred of the great-souled, renowned Kṣatriyas. Rākuni and Bala, as well as Vṛṣaka and Bṛhadvaṭa, all the sons of the king of Gāndhāra have gathered. Aśvatthāmā and Bhoja, along with the best of warriors, have assembled, great-souled ones, adorned with glory. Vṛhanta and Maṇimāṃsa, and the valiant Danda-dhara, along with Sahadeva, Jayatsena, and Meghasaṃdhi. Virāṭa, along with his sons, and Radhaghnī, and Vārthakṣemi, Suvaca, and Senācīndu, the king. Abhibhū, with his son, and Sudāma, with good speech.

English: Draupadī's Svayaṃvara Struck by the arrows of Kandu, the hearts of the kings were filled with sorrow at Krishna's arrival. The chariot of Drupada's daughter was adorned with gems and friends were also present there. Then, the celestial beings arrived in their aircraft; the Rudras, the Ādityas, the Vasus, and the Aśvins. All the Sādhya beings and the Maruts, along with Yama and the Lord of Wealth, were honored. The great serpents and the Gama, along with the Guhyakas and the celestial musicians, and the foremost Gandharvas accompanied by Apsaras. There were also the mighty Kauravas and the Vrishnis, as well as the prominent ones among them. They stood there, as per Krishna's wish. Those resembling the king of elephants, with five lotus-like faces, were like the fire-covered ones, and the Yadava heroes were present. Rāma, Yudhiṣṭhira, Bhīma, Jīṣṇu, and the hero Yama were there. Observing them, Rāma felt pleased with Janārdana. Others, however, were various sons and grandsons of kings; with Krishna's arrival, their minds were not at ease. They were troubled, with their teeth bared and their faces turned red. The mighty Yama was not a great personality, and so were the broad-armed Pāṇḍavas; Yama and the mighty ones were there. At that time, all were struck by the arrows of Kandu, and Draupadī was lost. The divine fragrance of the Gandharvas was present, adorned with divine garlands and surrounded by the Nagas and Siddhas. The great sound of the dundubhi echoed; that assembly filled the sky. The aircraft were bound together, and the sound of the veena resonated throughout.

English: The strength of the bow is indeed great. How can one, with a weak bow, achieve success in archery? Brahmins will be mocked in this kingdom, if the work is not accomplished and is done carelessly. If one is weak in archery or due to Brahminical carelessness, let them not proceed to shoot the bow. We will not be mocked, nor will we be established in weakness, nor will we attain knowledge in the world of kings. Some say that the illustrious one is like a serpent king, with broad shoulders and strong arms, like the mighty Himāvat. This work seems possible due to enthusiasm. The power of great enthusiasm does not allow the incapable to proceed. And nothing is known in the world that is impossible for Brahmins in the three realms of existence. The wind-eaters and fruit-eaters are chanting. The weak are indeed stronger, for the learned ones possess the brilliance of Brahman. A Brahmin should not be disregarded, acting with faith and devotion. Happiness and sorrow, great or small, whatever comes, Thus, various voices of the Brahmins lament. The archer stood firm like a mountain. The contest of Draupadī's swayamvara.

English: He, having circled that bow, performed the circumambulation; bowing his head, the joyful Parantapa seized it. With a twinkling eye, he swiftly grasped the ten arrows; he shot at the target, piercing it with a sudden strike through the ground. Then, in the sky, there arose a great sound among the assembly; divine flowers rained down, as the god aimed to slay the enemies of Partha. The sounds of the arrows and the cries of the wounded fell all around; there rained down a shower of flowers from the sky. The sounds of the conch and the drums resounded; the groups of charioteers and bards sang praises there with sweet voices. Seeing him, the mighty Nishūdana was pleased; he quickly approached Partha for assistance. When that great sound arose, Yudhiṣṭhira, the foremost of the righteous, swiftly went to the abode, accompanied by the two supreme beings. Observing the target, Kṛṣṇa, looking at the image of Pāṭha, took the dry garland of flowers and went, smiling at the son of Kṛntī. He, having taken her and defeating the sound, was worshipped by the Brahmins; he then released the arrow, which was inconceivable, and she too followed him.

English: The sage said: To that great soul Brahmana, desiring a daughter, There was anger among the kings, seeing each other closely. He wishes to give the daughter, Draupadī, to the Brahmana, having disregarded us and treating us like grass. Let him not think that he can kill this wicked one; For killing does not bring honor, nor does it enhance the qualities of the aged. Let him be killed along with his son, the wicked one; For he has indeed called us and honored us, the kings. Having gained qualities, he then later speaks ill of us. In the assembly of enemies, like the gods in a gathering. What is this similarity? I have not seen such a king. Nor is there any right among the Brahmanas regarding the choice. The self-choice is indeed well-known among the Kshatriyas. Or if this girl is not here... Let her be cast into the fire, as the kings of the realms. If a Brahmana or a child has done this, It is not to be killed in any way by the king. O Brahmana, indeed we do not desire the kingdom, life, or wealth. Draupadī's self-choice is pure.

English: The son and grandson are asking for something that is dense. Due to fear of humiliation and to protect one's own flesh, let there be no fate like that of others in the svayaṃvara. Thus spoke the king's courtiers, delighted, with their arms like clubs, ready to strike. Seeing the angry kings who had taken up their arrows, the frightened Trapa fled. The son of Pāṇḍu, mighty and swift, was perceived as a great enemy. Then, the armed ones rose up; the kings, with their fingers bound, aimed to kill the sons of Kuru, attacking Bhīma. Bhīma, of great strength, like a thunderbolt, uprooted a single hero, as an elephant would. Taking that tree, the enemy's destroyer, the fierce one, stood near the lion-like man, the son of Pritha. This statement was made by Dāmodara, who is like a brother to Jṣhṭa, with a mind beyond human comprehension. This one, who is equal to the mighty bow, causes great pain; this is Arjuna, there is no doubt about it, for I am Vasudeva. This tree, suddenly stopped in the king's transformation, is not another; how can the wolf be capable in this world?

English: The elephant, frightened, approached like a wild elephant. The kings, desiring to kill, spoke harsh words; indeed, the killing of a twice-born is seen in battle. Then, Kṛṣṇa swiftly went to Arjuna, as an elephant goes to another elephant for battle. The mighty Shalya, lord of the Madras, who is like Bhīma, along with others, gathered with Duryodhana. In the battle, the one who was not fighting, shot arrows at the one who was falling with three arrows. Kārṇa, with his intellect, pulled the bowstring with great strength. With the speed of their sharp arrows, the radiant ones, Rādhā's son, bewildered, fled. Both of them, desiring victory, fought fiercely against each other. In response to the challenge, I shall show my strength and prowess. Thus, they spoke to each other. Then, knowing the unmatched strength of the arms of the one who was not fighting, he prepared for battle. With arrows released by Arjuna, the army was struck down, and they honored him.

English: Karna said: "I am pleased with you, O foremost of the brāhmaṇas, in the battle of strength. And also with the lack of despair and the conduct of the conch-blowing." "Are you indeed the great sage Dhanurveda, or Rāma, the best of brāhmaṇas? Or are you directly the great horseman, or directly Viṣṇu, the infallible?" "For the purpose of concealing my self, I rely on the strength of my arms. Having assumed the form of a brāhmaṇa, you then fight against me." "For in battle, no man can directly challenge me, the son of the Sun, whether he is a warrior or the one with the crown, the son of Pāṇḍu." Vaśampāyana said: Thus addressed, Phalguna replied: "I am not a particle of the science of archery, nor am I Rāma, the glorious." "I am a brāhmaṇa, the best among warriors, a great boon." "Standing firmly under the instruction of my teacher, I am here to conquer you in battle, O hero, be unwavering." Thus addressed, the son of Rādhā, Karṇa, fell into battle, thinking that his splendor would conquer the great chariot-warrior. The battle raged there, the king's army like a wolf, with warriors madly charging, and with the trees and the wind. They were mutually challenging each other like great elephants in madness.

English: Then Bhīma, lifting Shalya with his arms in battle, struck him down, the best of the weak. There Bhīma, the son of Kuntī, performed a great deed. What Shalya, the mighty, fell to the ground, was not struck down by the strong Bhīma. When Bhīma had struck down Shalya, Karṇa was also in doubt. All the kings were frightened. They said there, "Who can fight against the son of Rādhā?" Who indeed can fight against Duryodhana in battle? Similarly, against the Madra king Shalya, the best of the strong. Let a vow be taken by us, united with the Brahmins in this war. Then, having considered Bhīma's action, Krishna, the son of Kuntī, was in doubt. He thought, "The king should not be bound by dharma."

English: Thus, the warriors, skilled in battle, returned, astonished, as they went to their respective places. The superior Brahman, adorned with the western attire, departed, and those who were present there also left. However, the Brahman, concealed, wept with the horsemen, and with difficulty, Bhīma and Dhanañjaya went there. Freed from the crowd of people, accompanied by Kṛṣṇa, the noble ones shone there. Their mother contemplated various forms of destruction, fearing for her sons, who were in danger. The Kurus, unaware of the plot, would not be the cause of the downfall of the Dhārtarāṣṭras. Accompanied by fierce demons, they were like a mirage. Thinking contrary to the great sage Vyāsa, Pṛthā, accompanied by her sons, reflected thus. Then, enveloped by dense clouds, the great one appeared there, preceded by Jṣhṇu.

English: Having gone to that Bhāgavata assembly; the great one reached the earth. He then informed Yājñaseṇī, greatly pleased, to beg. Having gone to the hut, the sons did not see; they all said, "Eat." Later, Kuntī, seeing the maiden, said, "I have spoken harshly." Being afraid of the same dharma, lamenting; Yājñaseṇī, greatly pleased. Kuntī, taking her hand, approached Yudhishthira and spoke this word. "This maiden is the daughter of King Drupada; she has been given to you two. As appropriate, my son, I have also spoken; together, do not neglect the king." "How could I have spoken untruth today; O best of the Kurus, listen. The son of the King of Pāñcāla, dharma would not approach." After a moment's thought, King Yudhishthira; comforting his mother, the best of women. To Kuntī, the hero of the Kurus, Dhananjaya spoke this word. "By you, the daughter of Yājñaseṇī is conquered; by you, the princess will be pleased. Let her be ignited, let her be called, take the hand of this one according to the ritual." Ajana said: "Do not, O king, make me a sinner; do not let the dharma be desired by others." "Then you will be placed first; Bhīma, the great-armed, is inconceivable." "I am then Nakula; after me, the son of Mādrī, Sahadeva, is lowly. I am Vṛkodara, and Yama, and the king, all the maidens are yours." Thus, whatever is to be done here; consider what is dharmic, which is dear to the King of Pāñcāla, all are under your control.

English: There sat the broad-armed one; Krishna, along with Rāuhineya, saw Ajaṭaśatru and those seated, shining like moving lights. Then, the divine Vāsudeva approached Kuntī's son, the foremost among the bearers of dharma; pressing the foot of Yudhishthira, the king, he said, "I am Krishna." Thus, Rāuhineya also praised him, and the Kurus too rejoiced; the sons of the fathers, the Yadavas, took hold of the feet of the chief of the Bhārata. Ajaṭaśatru, the hero of the Kurus, asked Krishna, "How is it that we, O Vāsudeva, who are hidden, are known to all?" Vāsudeva spoke secretly, "Even if hidden, O king, this valor of the Pāṇḍavas is known; who else among men possesses such?" By good fortune, you all, the Pāṇḍavas, are freed from the fire; by good fortune, the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, along with his maternal uncle, would not have been desirous. May you be well; it is established that you should strive like a blazing fire; let not the earthly ones among you be aware of this until the time of the camp. Thus permitted by the Pāṇḍava, the imperishable glory was quickly granted by Baladeva.

English: Draupadī's Svayaṃvara Dhṛṣṭadyumna, the son of the Pāṇḍavas, followed behind the Kuru princes as they went to the abode of Bhāgavata. Not knowing the men around him, he was not able to kill them; he was seated in the abode of Bhāgavata. Then Bhīma, the slayer of enemies, and Jaya, the great one, having performed their deeds, informed Yudhiṣṭhira, the one of humble nature. Then Kuntī, the noble lady, spoke at the right time: "O blessed one, give alms to the Brahmins and take the lead among the Kurus." "Those who desire food, give to them; those who are determined, let them be around you." Then quickly dividing the rest, they gave honey to the four and to my own self. "Give to Bhīma, O blessed one; he who is equal in form to me, this young man, strong and capable, is indeed a hero who enjoys much." She, like a beautiful maiden, spoke her words; and as it was rightly said, they all accepted the food. The son of Madri, Sahadeva, made a bed for the Kauravas; all the heroes, having performed their own duties, slept soundly. Agastya's command was indeed in that direction; the Kauravas, the best of men, were there. Kuntī was in front of them; and Kṛṣṇa was also there. The earth was made a bed for the Pāṇḍu sons; there was no sorrow there, nor did it seem to be a burden.

English: They were there, the heroes, speaking; the tales were strange, of the Pṛtanādhikara. Divine weapons and chariots, and also the serpents, the conch shells, and the axes. The tales of them were being recounted; at that time, the son of the Pāścāla king. He heard about Kṛṣṇa and also about those seated; and all of them looked at the humans. The prince, however, was troubled; the entire story of them was told at night. He quickly went to inform King Drupada; The king of Pāñcāla, in a sorrowful form, not finding the Pāṇḍavas, asked the great soul; where has Kṛṣṇa gone, and who has taken him? Not by a lowly person; nor by a courtesan, nor by a servant. Is there not some place where my son is not found; is there not a garland fallen in this place? Is there not a distinguished man; even if of a different color? Is there not a left foot of mine; today, my son has been made dear to Kṛṣṇa. Is there not a great being, who is supremely revered; united with Partha, the best of men? Is there not a great victor, who has taken my daughter? Is there not a son of the Kaurava hero, who bears the strange name; or is it that Partha, the more powerful, has struck down the target with an arrow?

English: The kings were asleep, and Krishna was their support; they lay on the earth, resting on the beds of the Dabhājināga. They were like clouds of time, and their stories were wondrous. Those tales are not of courtesans or lowborn; nor do the heroes speak of the twice-born. Without doubt, those Kṣatriya chiefs tell of war, O king. Indeed, this hope is manifestly prosperous; for we hear of the pearls from the burning of the path. As they speak to each other, the paths are concealed and they wander. Then King Trapada sent for the priest and spoke thus: "May you have knowledge." The minister, having received the king's words, went and praised them, speaking the king's words as they were. The lord of the earth wishes to know you; the king of the Pāñcālas, Drupada, is a boar. He is determined to strike the target; he does not see the end of the joy. Therefore, knowing the lineage, you should strike at the heads of the enemies. My heart is troubled by the king of the Pāñcālas and his followers. Pāṇḍu was a dear friend of King Drupada, equal to himself. This desire of King Drupada is always present; if Arjuna, with his long arms, were to find my daughter.

English: 684 Drauḍī's Svayaṃvara Thus spoke the priest; the king, observing him, stood humbly. Let Bhīma, who is nearby, be offered the foot-wash and the gift. 020 The respected priest of King Drupada, having been employed, performed the worship more than necessary. Bhīma also performed that worship, counting it in multiples. 021 Seated comfortably, the priest was addressed by Yudhiṣṭhira as "the external one." The daughter of the Pāṇḍavas was released according to her own desire. 022 The fee was paid by King Drupada; the brave one followed suit. There was no distinction made among the varṇas; neither in life nor in lineage. 023 With the bowstring drawn by the skilled archer, aimed at the target, This Krishna was indeed victorious among the assembly of kings. 024 The king of the Somakas, not moving, was troubled by great sorrow. As for the desire of King Drupada's daughter, he too would prosper among the kings. 025 The daughter of the king, indeed, was not attainable; I think, O Brahmana, That it cannot be arranged by that strong man; thus it is. 026 Neither by the unformed nor by the inferior can it be struck down. Therefore, I, the king of the Pāñcālas, do not know what to do regarding the daughter. Nor can I bear the thought of her being struck down by another. 027 Thus speaking to Yudhiṣṭhira, another man approached near King Drupada. He quickly arrived there, intending to present the prepared food. 028

English: The messenger said: The food was prepared by the king for the wedding; it was also well-cooked. The bridegroom, having been honored, Krishna would not stay there long. These chariots are adorned with golden lotus designs; they are equipped with excellent horses, the lords of the earth. All these are for the residence of the king of the Pāñcālas. Then the Kurus set out; first they approached the priest. They took their great vehicles; Kuntī and Krishna also went along. Hearing the words of the priest, Dharmarāja, the son of Kunti, inquired about the various goods he had collected. Fruits, garlands, well-prepared dishes; also chairs and other items for the feast. In addition, there were other vehicles; all were gathered there for the purpose of play. The king collected all of them. Chariots and horses were splendid; the great chariots were beautifully adorned. Bows and arrows were also prominent; they were adorned with gold. The spears, swords, and all other weapons were also present.

English: Draupadī's Svayaṃvara The best seats and various thrones were there. Kuntī, having taken hold of Kṛṣṇa, entered the inner quarters of Drupada. The women, along with the sons of the Kauravas, were filled with compassion. Those with lion-like movements, adorned with the best garments, were there; the great heroes with long arms and powerful bodies. The king, all the ministers, and the sons of the king, as well as friends, all gathered there. The heroes sat on the highest seats, without any doubt, and entered the assembly of the princess, not astonished by the great honors. Delicious food was served in golden vessels, and the servants and maidservants were well-dressed; even the Bhojas provided food. There, the great heroes, having freed themselves, were pleased according to their desires. They enjoyed all the wealth there, entering the assembly of the brave. Seeing that, the sons of the king, along with all, were joyful, having come together, and they were delighted with the sons of Kuntī and the princes. STATS 187 Vairāmpāyana said.

English: Thus, calling the Pāñcāla prince Yudhiṣṭhira, with the acceptance of the Brahman, the great luminary was pleased. The soul, afflicted by thirst, asked the son of Kuntī, "How shall I know your noble lineage?" Whether endowed with qualities or born of a Śūdra lineage, or having taken refuge in illusion, they who are accomplished are indeed self-illuminated. For the sake of Kṛṣṇa, those who have not arrived, let the lord speak to us; indeed, the doubt here is not great. At the end of our doubts, may our minds find satisfaction here; may auspicious things be ours, O scorcher of foes. Desiring, speak the truth; you shine in truth, O king; thus, it should be said with offerings, not falsehood. Hearing your words, O immortal one, I shall certainly engage in marriage according to the prescribed rites. Yudhiṣṭhira said: "Do not be troubled, O king; may you have affection for the Pāñcāla. This desire of yours has indeed come to fruition." "We are indeed Kṣatriyas, O king, sons of the great-souled Pāṇḍu; know me as the eldest, and this is Kuntī's son, Bhīma, and Arjuna." "By whom your sons, O king, have been conquered in the royal assembly."

English: Yama, O king, where Kṛṣṇa is established, May your mind be free from sorrow, O Kṣatriyas, O best of men. This is the truth, O great king, I convey all this to you. Indeed, you are our supreme guru and refuge. Then, King Drupada, with eyes troubled and agitated, Was unable to respond to Yudhishthira. But the great warrior, having seized that joy, Then spoke appropriately to Yudhishthira. He asked him, "How were you, O son of Pāṇḍu, in the past?" The Pāṇḍava narrated everything to him in order. Hearing this, King Drupada criticized the son of Kuntī, At that time, he rebuked Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the lord of men. He consoled Yudhishthira, the son of Kuntī, And Drupada vowed to grant him the kingdom. Then Kuntī and Kṛṣṇa and Bhīma and others, And Yama, instructed by the king, entered the great palace. There, they were honored by the royal sacrifice. Then the king spoke to them along with his sons.

English: Upon rising, the great soul Krishna was worshipped with great devotion. He then sat on a golden seat, his mind serene. All were permitted by Krishna, the one of immense radiance, to sit on the grand seats. Then, after a moment, the sweet voice of the sage was heard. The great soul Drona, the husband of the princess, asked him, "How can one be among many, and not be a part of the whole? May the Lord reveal this to us as it is." Vyasa spoke: "In this matter of separation, which contradicts the Vedas, I wish to hear whatever each one thinks." Rapa spoke: "This is my opinion: this unrighteousness contradicts the world and the Vedas. There is no doubt that many of the twice-born are not aware of this. Nor have the great souls acted in accordance with this before. Nor is righteousness to be practiced in many ways, it is eternal." "Therefore, I do not engage in such actions, for doubt in righteousness indeed arises in me." Gṛṣṭyusna spoke:

English: How can the younger brother Bhāya be superior? Brahman is indeed exalted. Brahman is indeed exalted; the good are indeed established. We do not know how the essence of dharma is established; adharma cannot be considered as dharma. I will not engage in that which is not established; may the five queens be Krishna, in some way. Yudhiṣṭhira said: My speech is not false; my mind does not dwell on adharma. Indeed, my mind here does not engage in adharma at all. It is heard in the Purāṇas that there is a sage named Gotamī, who is the best among the seven bearers of dharma. The words of the guru are said to be the best among those who know dharma. Among all gurus, the mother is the supreme guru. She also spoke the words, "Let the beggar be fed." Therefore, I consider this to be dharma, O best of the brāhmaṇas. Kuntī said: Thus, Yudhiṣṭhira, the follower of dharma, speaks; how can I be freed from the intense fear of falsehood? Vyāsa said: The self-choice of Draupadī...

English: Draupadī's Svayaṃvara Then the people became numerous; they were afflicted by the passage of time and death. Then the Shakas, Varuṇa, Kubera; the Sādhyas, Rudras, and Vasus, along with others, gathered there, the lord of the world, Prajāpati. Then they spoke to the teacher of the Tattvas; there is no fear for humans, therefore, desiring happiness, all should proceed to the abode. Brahmā said: What fear do you have, O immortals, from humans? Let there be no fear from the assembly of the wise at any time. The gods said: There is no particular fear; those who have come here are not distinguished. Brahmā said: The son of Vivasvat is engaged for the sake of the sacrifice; therefore, these humans do not die. In that focused state of action, that is their destined end. The body of Vivasvat is also endowed; by your strength, it is used. The end of them will be in the final moment; the strength will be in men. Vyāsa said: Then, having heard the words of the gods, the gods who are worshipped, they sat together, the mighty ones; in the Bhāgirathī, they are like lotuses.

English: The seers were astonished; Indra, the hero, went there. He saw the woman with the brilliance of fire, where the Ganges flows continuously. There, the woman, weeping and flowing with water, stood holding the goddess Ganges. From her tears, a moon fell; then there was a golden lotus. Seeing that wonder, he asked the woman nearby, "Who are you, why do you weep, and for whose sake? I desire to know the truth." She spoke: "You will know me here, O king; for this reason, I weep, unfortunate one. I will go ahead; you will see me weeping for what I have done." Vyasa said: "As she was going, he saw a young man with a beautiful form, seated on a throne, accompanied by a maiden, like a mountain king. The king of the gods then said, 'You should know this; the whole world is established in me. I am indeed the one who is angry and very much intoxicated.'" Seeing Shakra angry, the god laughed and looked at Shakra with a slight smile. The king of the gods became still, like a pillar, gazing at him. When the water was filled with the creature, then he spoke to the weeping goddess, "Bring her here, for I have not yet known her." Then Shakra, touched by her, fell into the earth. There, the divine one, with his grace, said, "Thus, O Shakra, do as you wish."

English: Draupadī's Svayaṃvara The great king, with unmatched strength and valor, is revealed; where those like you, shining like the sun, reside. Seeing that great mountain peak, he observed others equal to him. Seeing them, he became sorrowful; "Will I not be like these?" Then the god Girīśa, with a thunderbolt in hand, angrily spoke with open eyes. "Enter this, O hundred-eyed one; for I was abandoned in my youth." Thus addressed by the mighty king of the gods, he was greatly agitated by the wind. With folded hands and a humble face, he spoke suddenly, "O Bhagavān, you are the seer of the remaining." He, with a fierce bow, laughing, said, "Such beings do not express anger here." "These too will become like this; therefore, let this Draupadī be revealed." There is no doubt that anger will also arise in you; all beings will be born human. There, what will you do to endure; having caused many others to perish? The arrivals are honored by their own deeds; I have spoken this thus; other duties must be done. The former gods said: "We shall go to the human realm, where liberation is prescribed. Let us not be abandoned; righteousness, the wind, and the great one are to be considered." Vyāsa said:

English: This text appears to be a mix of verses and prose, but it contains many references to characters and events from the Mahabharata. Here are the translations for the provided snippets: 1. Hearing this, the one with the thunderbolt spoke again; the best of the gods said this: "By my power, I have created this man, born of my essence." 2. Among them, the Lord with the fierce bow; the males are as stated. "And also among them, the beloved wife of these women, who is dear to me, was struck among mortals." 3. Thus, the deity went to the immeasurable Narayana; and he too, having been struck, became all. "Then all became the bearers of the burden." 4. He too, Keshava, the bearer of Rudra; and also Krishna. "And Keshava, the one who is the wealth of the Yadus, Rohini, and Devaki." 5. Among them, one became Baladeva; Krishna, the second, Keshava, was born. 6. Those who were previously restrained in the form of Indra; in that compassion of the wind, the northern one. "Indeed, you Pandavas, the mighty ones; the portion of the Shakya, the Pandava, the one with the left-handed bow." 7. Thus, these Pandavas were born; O king, they became like Indra. "They were instructed to be like Indra; the divine form of Draupadi, who is dear." 8. How indeed, at the end of actions, does the earth rise; it arises by divine fate from elsewhere. "Whose form is like that of the moon, shining; the fragrance of which is like that of a hundredfold." 9. This I give to you, O king, as a wonderful boon; indeed, it is divine. "See the sons of Kunti with divine eyes; they are endowed with divine forms." 10. Then Vyasa, the most generous, pure Brahmin, by the austerity of that king. "Gave them divine sight, and they saw the divine forms as they truly are."

English: Draupadī's Svayaṃvara Then, adorned with a divine diadem, like Indra, he who is the fire, the sun, and the forest; the young ones bound by the form of the great ones, the sky was covered by the sound of the conch. Paresh: Shining with golden garlands, endowed with great fortune; directly the Vasus or the divine ones, endowed with all virtues. Seeing them, the king Drupada, delighted and astonished. Having attained that divine illusion, immeasurable; and that form resembling prosperity, endowed with beauty; the king of the earth, with their beauty, splendor, and fame. He, having grasped the great form of the son of Satyavatī; with a cheerful mind, spoke to him. Vyāsa said: There was a maiden of great virtue in the forest of the sage; she, being beautiful and chaste, did not approach a husband. She pleased the lord with her penance, and the pleased lord himself said, "Choose your desire." Freed from service, the maiden desired a husband endowed with virtues, again and again. Then the lord of gods granted her that boon, saying, "Five excellent husbands will be yours." She, having pleased the god, spoke again: "I desire one husband endowed with virtues from you."

English: As I greet you, O lady, adorned with the beauty of youth, So too shall I greet again the son of the charioteer, endowed with virtues. Then, the one who is the rescuer sent to the Pandavas, Gave them various ornaments, adorned with pearls and gold. Madhava has splendid garments from various regions, And auspicious blankets made of deer skin and other materials. There are various grand couches and vehicles, And vessels adorned with designs like thunderbolts. With beauty, youth, and grace, Kṛṣṇa, the one of many forms, is surrounded by thousands. The elephants, well-trained and auspicious, And the horses, adorned with their own decorations, are there. He who is the source of countless gold, The one with immeasurable self, sent forth the mighty Kṛṣṇa. All this was received by Dharmarāja Yudhishthira, Filled with great joy, desiring the company of Govinda.

English: Then King Duryodhana, along with his brothers, with Karṇa, with Mātuṭa, with Kaṇa, and with Kṛpa. Having been dismissed, the white chariot of Drauḍpadi was then approached by Duhśāsana like a dullard. If that Drauḍpadi were not to be seen, no one would know the truth about the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra. I consider the supreme god to be the ultimate, but manliness is indeed futile, for the sons of Pāṇḍu bear that manliness here. Thus conversing and criticizing Pūrocanā, they entered Hastinapura, dejected and bereft of consciousness. Having lost their resolve, the distressed ones, freed from the sacrificial rites, were united with Darupadā. Dhrṣṭadyumna and others, thinking thus, and also Śikhaṇḍin, and the sons of Drupada, all skilled in warfare. Then Vidura, having heard of the Pāṇḍavas, who were ashamed and had come to Dhṛtarāṣṭra, and the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, who were distressed and had come to drink. Then, with a pleased mind, King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, addressed the Kurus, astonished, saying, "They are killing." The king, having heard this from Vidura, spoke with great delight, "What a wonderful thing, O Bharata!" He thinks indeed that the son, the eldest, is with the daughter of Drupada.

English: Duryodhana, the one who knows the self, saw the Lord. Then he ordered Draupadī to bring many ornaments. At that time, he called his son Duryodhana. Then Vidura spoke about the Pandavas who were surrounded by the valiant and purified by Drupada. Among them and others related, many were endowed with strength. Gṛtārāja said: Just as the sons of Pāṇḍu are, so too are my sons superior. This is what I consider to be superior. The Pāṇḍavas, who are valiant and have friends, are indeed skilled. Who, having reached Drupada, would not desire a friend who is related? No one would wish for a king who has lost his glory. Then, while he was speaking thus, Vidura replied: May your intellect be ever present, O king, for it is the nature of kings. Then Duryodhana and Rādhēya approached Gṛtārāja and spoke these words: In the presence of Vidura, we are unable to speak, for we are isolated. What is it that you wish to accomplish?

English: The sons of this one should be tempted, as well as the entire lineage of ministers. Abandon the king, the son of Kuntī, Yudhishthira. Let them enjoy their residence there. Let them describe the faults of these individuals separately. The Pandavas, being divided, should focus their minds there. Or some skilled men, adept in means, may separate them from one another due to attachment. Let them either awaken Krishna, for it is indeed easy due to the multitude, or let them frighten the Pandavas in that situation. Let death be arranged for Bhīmasena or for the king, for he is indeed stronger than them. But when the king is slain, the valiant one will be killed, for they will not strive for the kingdom; he is indeed their refuge. Unconquerable is Arjuna in battle, like a wolf guarding the rear. Without Bhīmasena, Falguna will not have a share in the battle against Rādheya. They, knowing of Bhīmasena's death, will surely destroy us, knowing us to be weaker. In the presence of the sons of Pārtha, we shall act, O king, in accordance with the commands, not in disbelief. Or let them be tempted by the pleasures, let each of the sons of Kunti be separated, and then let Krishna be abandoned.

English: Vidura's Arrival You are not able to express your misfortune; it is indeed destined for you. The paths of the ancestors are marked, and the desires are also under control. There is a division among them, and it is possible to separate them. Those who are attached to one do not break apart from each other. Nor can Kṛṣṇa separate them from others. What can be said about those who are surrounded by the dust? The desired quality of women is to have many husbands. Kṛṣṇa, who has attained that, does not find it easy to separate her. The king of the Pāñcālas is not dear to wealth. Surely, no one will give up the kingdom, O Kaunteya. Thus, his son is virtuous and attached to the Pāṇḍavas. Therefore, I think it is impossible to achieve them in any way. This is indeed within your capacity, O best of men, as long as the Pāṇḍavas are not rooted. Let your valor be pleasing to us, as long as they are not taken away. Our side is indeed great; as long as the Pāñcāla is light, let the attack be made upon them; do not deliberate. There are many vehicles and numerous friends. As long as they are not in Gandhāra, let your valor be swift. As long as the king of the Pāñcālas does not turn his mind towards the Kurus.

English: 014 As long as the son of Vāsudeva does not arrive, 015 the prowess of the Pāṇḍavas is indeed great. 016 Various enjoyments and the kingdom are solely for the sake of Krishna; 017 there is no abandonment of the earth for the sake of the Pāṇḍavas. 018 By valor, the earth has been attained by the great-souled Bhārata; 019 by valor, Pāka's throne has been seized. 020 The Kṣatriya's valor is indeed praised by the wise; 021 for it is the valor of the king that protects the arrows. 022 With great strength, we shall quickly bring the Pāṇḍavas down. 023 Indeed, the Pāṇḍavas cannot be subdued by force, gifts, or division; 024 therefore, they must be subdued by valor alone. 025 By valor, we shall conquer this entire earth; 026 I shall now speak the means to achieve this, O lord of the people. 027 Hearing the words of Rādhya, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the illustrious one, 028 after honoring him, then spoke this statement. 029 This statement is indeed fitting for you, O great sage, 030 endowed with valor.

English: Thus, by righteousness, you attain the kingdom; they too have attained the kingdom, this is the opinion. Let the kingdom be given to them as sweet; this is indeed for the benefit of the tiger among men and all people. If otherwise done, it will not be beneficial; your fame will also be completely lost. Let fame be protected; this is the greatest strength. The life of a man is remembered as lost when fame is lost. As long as a man does not lose his fame, he lives; when fame is lost, he perishes. Establish this righteous act, O mighty-armed one, suitable for the Kurus; it is appropriate for the self of the former ones. By destiny, those heroes bear; by destiny, Pṛthā lives; by destiny, the sinful one, the evil-doer, has gone away. From that time onward, in Gandhāra, no one will be able to look upon you. In the world of living beings, someone has heard of Kuntī, who has come. Nor does the world go to the evil-doer because of a fault; just as, O tiger among men, the world goes to you because of a fault. Therefore, this life of theirs is your cleansing of sins; it should be considered, O great king, as the destruction of the Pandavas' sins. Nor do the heroes among them live, O descendant of the Kurus.

English: The appropriateness and affection of yoga should also be described. Again and again, the son of Kuntī comforts Mādri's son. May the auspicious golden ornaments be given to you, O king, as per your words. Thus, for all the sons of Drupada, for all the sons of the Bharata lineage, and for all the Pāṇḍavas, those associated with Kuntī. Thus, the Pāṇḍava, united with the comforting Drupada, should be heard after this is said regarding their arrival. Let the valiant Duhśāsana and Vikarna take the Pāṇḍavas to the beautiful place. Then, those who are always honored by you, O king, will remain in their positions with the consent of the nature of the people. Thus, O great king, I think that among your sons, the conduct is suitable with Bhīṣma. Karna said: Having been united with those two, in all matters, what is more wonderful than this, if they do not consult you? The one who, with a wicked mind, speaks secretly from within, how can he say what is the highest good for the virtuous? Friends, in difficulties, or for the sake of welfare, whether it is happiness or suffering, indeed, for everyone, it is according to the rules.

English: 716 Vidur's Arrival The wise and the unwise, the child and the elder, all beings find their own everywhere. Indeed, it is heard that there was once a king in the royal house of the Magadhas. That king, devoid of strength, was the supreme ruler, and he was established in all affairs. His minister, the great Kaniṣṭha, was previously known as a powerful lord. The king took possession of the enjoyable and valuable wealth, and he himself became foolishly wealthy. Taking away the gains of the greedy, he desired the kingdom for himself. Even the one who is weak and the one who is the supreme ruler, it is said, could not achieve that kingdom. What else is hidden in that manliness? If the kingdom is destined for you, O lord of the wise, it will remain in you. Otherwise, if it is otherwise destined, striving for it will not succeed. Thus, the wise should be cautious in their dealings, and the words of the wicked should be understood.

English: Vidur's Arrival And you, O King, are equal to the sons of Pāṇḍu. In righteousness, O King, and in truthfulness, O Bhārata, Neither have they spoken anything superior, nor has anything unfavorable been done by you. These two, O King, are like tigers among men; how can your greatness be diminished? The wise ones among men, O best of men, do not speak anything unworthy due to you. Thus, my thoughts, O descendant of Kuru, are directed towards you. And they will not speak anything against the purpose, for this is indeed the highest good for you, O Bhārata. The sons of Duryodhana and others, O King, are like that. Similarly, the sons of the Pāṇḍavas, O King, are also in doubt. If they wish for anything good among them, They do not see any good due to their anger. But, O King, in their hearts, there is a drought; The good is certainly within them, revealing itself. Thus, O King, these great souls with great splendor, Do not reveal anything, nor is there any certainty from you.

English: The one who is like a lion among men, how can the Pandava, the illustrious Savyasāchin, be defeated even by the mighty king? How can Bhīma, the great-armed one with the strength of a thousand serpents, be defeated in battle, even by the immortal? Similarly, how can Yama, the son of Yama, be defeated in battle while wishing to live? In whom there is restraint, patience, truth, and valor, how can the best of the Pandavas be defeated in battle? What can be said of those whose supporter is Rāma, whose minister is Janārdana? What can be said of their victory in battle, where Sātyaki is on their side? Those who have their father-in-law and brothers-in-law as warriors, how can they be defeated? Knowing their strength, O Bharata, act in accordance with the rightful path. This is a great act of valor, done with the favor of them, O king, for the purification of the self. Even the one who is weak, if he acts rightly, can gather strength, O king, against his own side. The strong ones and many others fall.

Those who live by destiny, Pṛthā lives by destiny; the great charioteers have obtained the daughter of the three-footed one by destiny. All are peaceful, O Purōchana, regarding the great distress that has come upon me by destiny. Then Vidura went, under the command of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, to the Yajñasena and the Pāṇḍavas, O Bhārata. Having gone there, he, well-versed in the lineage, approached the king Dṛupada justly. He also took hold of Vidura by dharma, and he acted according to justice, as per the agreement with the Kurus. He embraced the Pāṇḍavas and Vāsudeva there, and then he asked them about their well-being. With great intelligence, he was purified in due course, by the words of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, again and again. He asked the king about the Pāṇḍavas, and then he also gave various gifts and wealth. As for the Pāṇḍavas, Kuntī, and Draupadī, and the sons of Dṛupada, as given to the Kauravas.

English: 722 Vidur's Arrival Then, with humility and respect, Amitamatī spoke: "Near Darpaḍa are the sons of Pāṇḍu and Kṛṣṇa." "Let my words be heard by the minister and his sons. Dhṛtarāṣṭra, along with the minister and relatives." "King, repeatedly pleased, with unadorned hair, you too, O king, are dear to me by relation." Thus, Bhīṣma, the son of Śantanu, along with his companions, inquires about your well-being, O great sage." "Bharadvāja, the great archer, and Droṇa, your dear friend, having approached you, inquires about your well-being." "And Gṛhitarāṣṭra, along with the Pāñcālas, believes himself fulfilled, as do all the Kauravas." "However, their attainment of the kingdom is not considered as pleasing as the relationship gained with you, O Yajñasena." "Knowing this, you should establish the Pāṇḍavas, for the Kauravas are greatly eager to see the Pāṇḍa heirs." "These noble men have been long exiled, and they too, like Pṛthā, will be eager to see the city." "Even Kṛṣṇa and Pāñcālī are waiting to see, the city and the matter concerning us."

English: Vikāṇa and the great archer Citraseṇa, Drona the supreme archer, Gautama, and Kripa. The heroes surrounded, shining like great charioteers, then gradually entered the city of Hastinapura. The city appeared as if it were being given away with curiosity, where those tiger-like men were afflicted by grief and sorrow. Those high-sounding words were uttered by the Pandavas, who were dear to those who wished for what is dear. This man, the tiger among men, returns again, the knower of dharma, who protects us and our heirs with righteousness. Today, the king of the Pandavas, beloved like a forest to the forest-dweller, has come here wishing for us. What indeed has been done today that is the greatest joy for all of us, since the brave sons of Kunti have returned? If what is given or taken is known, or if we have any austerity, let the Pandavas remain in the city for a hundred years. Then, the great-souled Dhṛtarāṣṭra and Bhīṣma, and others, performed the foot salutations. Having done this, all of them entered the houses under the rule of Dhṛtarāṣṭra. The great souls, resting, performed some great deeds.

English: Ahūta by Dhṛtarāṣṭra and King Śāntanu. Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: "Listen to this word of mine, O Kuntī's son, with your brothers. Do not let the conflict arise again in the Khaṇḍava forest. No one among you has the power to disturb those who are being protected, without the three worlds. Having attained the kingdom, let the Khaṇḍava forest be established. Vairāmpāyana said: Having received that word, all bowed to the king and then they entered that terrible forest, those men resembling humans. Having attained the kingdom, let the Khaṇḍava forest be established. Then the Pāṇḍavas, going there with Kṛṣṇa in the lead, made the city flourish like a celestial abode. Adorned with walls resembling the ocean, it stood prosperous, enveloped in the sky. Illuminated by pale clouds and resembling the snow, the city of Nāgebhogavatī shone beautifully.

English: The victorious ones, great sages, devoted to truth and righteousness, attained supreme joy there, the sons of Pāṇḍu. Then, all the great souls seated there, Narada, the divine sage, arrived by chance. Yudhishthira offered a pleasing seat to him. As Narada was seated properly, Yudhishthira respectfully offered him clarified butter and other items. Receiving that worship, the sage was filled with joy and, having honored him, spoke to him. Having been permitted, King Yudhishthira sent for Krishna, who was present. Draupadi, having become pure, also went there where Narada was with the Pāṇḍavas. Having saluted his feet, the divine sage, the one who acts properly, was greeted by her with folded hands, and she stood there, the daughter of Drupada. He, the virtuous one, spoke various words of truth to the sons of kings, Narada. He said, "Let her go," addressing the blameless one.

English: As they were going, Krishna spoke to Yudhishthira, who was leading the Pandavas. The sage Bhagavān said to them in a secluded place. O Dharma's wife, Yarasvini, you are the only wife of the five, so let there be no distinction among you; thus, let the rules be established. Sundopasundau, the two brothers, are renowned in all three worlds for being invincible. In a single kingdom, in a single home, with a single seat and food, let the best of sesame seeds be the reason for their mutual conflict. Let the brother be protected, as there is mutual recognition; therefore, let there be no conflict here, so do this, Yudhishthira. Yudhishthira said: Whose son is Sundopasundau, O great sage? How did the distinction arise, and how did they come to fight each other? Is Tilottama an Apsara or a daughter of the gods? By whose desire were they both killed by each other? I wish to hear all this in detail, as it happened, O ascetic; for we are indeed curious.

English: Due to the power of their austerities, the Vindhya released smoke for a long time, as if it had become something extraordinary. Then the gods, frightened by Bhīma's austerities, caused obstacles. They were terrified and repeatedly cried out, but they could not break the great vow of those two. Then the divine beings, having great power, created an illusion. The sisters, mothers, and relatives of those two were also frightened. Terrified and pursued by the demon with a trident, they took refuge in the forest, clad in the garments of the forest. Then they cried out for help, but they could not break the great vow of those two. When neither of them caused any disturbance, the women and all beings became invisible. Then the grandfather, directly approaching the great demon, granted a boon, the grandfather of all worlds. Then the beautiful Sundopasunda, the brothers with great prowess, saw the grandfather, the god, and stood there, wise at that time. O Lord, if the grandfather is pleased with our austerities, then let him be with us. The illusionists, those skilled in the art of deception, are powerful and take on forms of desire.

English: If both are pleased, then the lord will be favorable; otherwise, not. Grandfather said: Except for immortality, nothing else will be. The decree of death is the same for the immortals. This great penance, which you will perform, is for the purpose of naming your immortality. By this reason, I will not fulfill any desire. Sundopasundāvr̥catuḥ: In the three worlds, whatever exists, whether stationary or moving, There should be no fear from each other, O grandfather. Grandfather said: As it has been stated, I now give this desire to you. This decree of death will be as it is for you. Nārada said: Then, after giving this boon, the grandfather returned to the realm of Brahmā, And both of them, having received all boons, went to their own abode, invincible in all worlds.

English: With the mace held by the one who supports the earth, accompanied by the great demon army, he set out with his righteous companion. Praised by hymns, they departed with great joy. The demon, having risen into the sky, went to the abode of the gods, ready for battle. Knowing of their arrival and the boon granted to them, the gods left Triviṣṭapa and went to the world of mortals. Having conquered Indra's realm, they defeated the groups of Yakṣas and Rākṣasas, as well as the beings that fly in the sky. After defeating the serpents that had reached the earth, those two great demons conquered the ocean-dwelling beings. Then, all the earth began to tremble as they prepared for battle, summoning their troops and speaking sharp words. The great sacrifices of the kings increase the strength and power of the gods. Thus, with all the demons united, the task of killing them was to be accomplished by all of us together. Having gathered together, they set out towards the cruel shore of the great ocean.

English: Those who perform sacrifices and those who are twice-born, let them be strong and prosperous. | 013 | In the hermitages, the offerings of the sages are made by the soldiers who are well-prepared. | 014 | Those who are ascetics and who are blessed by the great ones do not fall into the curse. | 015 | When the arrows are released, the twice-born abandon their vows and flee like stones. | 016 | On earth, those who have attained perfection through austerities and are peaceful, fear not the serpents like Vena. | 017 | In the hermitage of Mātṛ, the world was as if struck down by a wooden stick. | 018 | The royal sages and the great demons, having made a decision, engaged in battle. | 019 | Becoming like elephants, they entered the fortresses and were not defeated. | 020 | The lion and the tiger, having become fierce, both attacked each other. | 021 | With the cessation of sacrifices and studies, the earth became desolate and devoid of kings. | 022 | Having become fearful, the market of the withdrawn was in chaos.

English: Chandrāditya, Dharma, the Supreme Being, and Budha. The Vekhanasa, the Watakhilya, the Vanaprastha, and the Marīcipa. The Ajā and the Avimūṭaḍhā, the Tejogabhāsa, and the ascetics. The sages worship the Supreme Ancestor. Then, approaching together, the great sages praised everything about Sundopasundaya. As it was created and as it was done, they presented everything to the Supreme Ancestor in order. Then all the divine beings, indeed, with great doubt, approached the Supreme Ancestor. Then the Supreme Ancestor, having heard all their words, contemplated how to decide on the matter. Having directed their attention, the Supreme Ancestor commanded the creation of the universal gem. Let the great ascetic create the Prāthanyī. Having bowed to the Supreme Ancestor, they spoke that word, thinking of the divine woman, they became agitated. In the three worlds, whatever is moved, whether stationary or mobile, they brought together in that way. The Korirāśa also, the Rallāni, were placed on her body.

English: She, who is adorned with the form of a goddess, was created from the assembly of the Rāḍha. By the great effort of Viśvakarman, she became unparalleled in beauty among women in the three worlds. There is no GAARA for her, where the wealth of beauty is not suitable for the one who gazes upon her. She, endowed with the form of beauty, captivated the eyes and minds of all beings. The grandfather, having gathered the gems, named her Tittottama. The grandfather spoke: "Go, with the beautiful and the very beautiful, and create a charming allure with your exceptional beauty." "For your sake, with the power of beauty, there should be no opposition, just as they should act mutually." Nārada spoke: "Thus, having made a promise and bowing to the grandfather, she created a circle there for the worship of the deities." "On the southern side, the Lord Mahādeva, and on the northern side, the gods, while the ṛṣis were present on the western side." "But she, there, made the circle and circumambulated it."

English: Indra and the Lord Śiva, having taken their positions. The face that emerged from the southern side was adorned with feathers. The face that emerged from the western side of the one that turned around. The face that emerged from the northern side of the one that departed. From the eyes of Mahendra, there arose a thousand red, large ones from the back, front, and sides. Thus, the four-faced great deity was born before, and the thousand-eyed one became the powerful food. Thus, the faces of the assembly of gods and sages also turned towards the supreme one, by which the excellent Tilottama travels. Having fallen on her body, they, the great ones, all became the supreme father of the gods, except for the king of the earth. Then all the gods and the great sages went, thinking that the work was done, endowed with beauty. At that time, the one who creates the worlds, having gone to Tilottama, defeated the assembly of gods and sages.

English: Narada said: Having conquered the earth, the demon, free from sorrow, became accomplished. Taking the celestial beings, the Yakṣas, and the Nagas, they attained great satisfaction. When there is no obstruction from the guardians, some here become inactive, like the immortal ones. With friends, Bhīma, and the fragrant ones, they enjoyed various drinks and food with great delight. In the inner palace, in the garden, and in the desired places, they became like the immortal ones. Then, at some time, on the flat ground of the mountain, they went to play among the blooming flowers. In the divine gardens, where all desires are fulfilled, they joyfully sat on the best seats. Then, with the sound of musical instruments, they approached, filled with joy and praise. Then, the best among them, while gathering flowers in the forest, Wearing a garment thrown aside, adorned with red, they became radiant. Ajuna, residing in the forest.

English: The beings born on the riverbank, searching for Kārṇikāra, went to that land where those two great demons were. Then, having drunk the boon of wine, intoxicated by the red drink, they beheld that boon-giving woman, and being disturbed, they became agitated. Leaving the seat of their birth, they went where she was situated, both being desirous and both seeking her. In the right hand, the beautiful one seized her heavy arm, while the handsome Upasunda also grasped the excellent Tilottamā with his left hand. Intoxicated by the boon of wine, both of them, with strength and the intoxication of wine, were filled with desire for each other. The beautiful one spoke, "My sister is your teacher," while the handsome Upasunda said, "My sister is your wife." "She is not yours, nor is she mine," thus anger entered there. Due to the cause of that woman, Bhīma and both of them did not seize her. Then, seizing Bhīma's mace, he was enchanted by her desire. "I am the elder, I am the younger," they struck each other. Then, struck by the mace, Bhīma fell to the ground. Covered in blood, the two were like a blazing fire in the sky. Then, the demon host was not there.

English: 744 Ajunavanavāsapava Then the grandfather, along with the great sages, arrived there, pure in spirit, to worship the excellent Tilottamā. The one who was adorned with boons, pleased by Brahmā, was addressed by the grandfather with affection. "O Bhāminī, you will wander in the path of the sun; no one will harm you with their brilliance." Thus, having granted her the boon, the grandfather, having taken Indra to the realm of Brahmā, departed. Thus, having become united, they both struck each other for the sake of Tilottamā. Therefore, I will go to you, O friends, for the sake of the Bharata's greatness. As there should be no division among you, let it be for the sake of Draupadī. Thus, may good come to you all. Having been addressed in this way by the great sage Nārada, the great souls decided to meet each other. In the presence of that divine sage Nārada, of immense energy. If anyone among you speaks ill of Draupadī, let him live as a celibate in the forest for twelve years.

English: The cow is killed by the lowly and deceitful, who are devoid of self-control; the Pāṇḍavas rush from this place. The offering of a heedless brāhmaṇa is lost. The lowly one attacks the empty cave of the Jādūla. When the brāhmaṇa is taken away, the thief is lost in wealth. When I am weeping, let the blood be held. The Pāṇḍava heard those words, the son of Kuntī, Dhananjaya. Upon hearing, the great-armed one spoke to that brāhmaṇa. Where the weapons of the great-souled Pāṇḍavas were. There, King Yudhiṣṭhira was with Kṛṣṇa. The Pāṇḍava was eager to enter and to go; he was repeatedly urged by them. There, Kuntī's son, distressed, began to think. In that wealth, the ascetic's tears were to be shed. If I do not protect the great king while he weeps, what protection will I provide? In the protection of all, may there be no lack of faith; let there be no lowly one in this world. Ajuna's forest dwelling is pure.

English: There is no doubt that if I leave without asking the king, it will be unpleasant for me. The king's entry will lead to my exile, or death will be great for me in the forest. Even for the body, dharma is superior. Thus determined, the son of Kuntī, Dhanañjaya, entered and asked the king, the lord of the world. Taking up his bow, he joyfully spoke to the brāhmaṇa, "As long as the thief seeks your wealth." We will not be far from you, O lowly ones, until I go today and take your wealth from the thief's hand. Following him, the mighty-armed archer, having vanquished the thieves, took that wealth. Having taken the glory of the brāhmaṇa and having drunk it, the hero Savyasāchi, the scorcher of foes, arrived in the city. Having bowed to all the teachers and also being honored in return, he spoke to Dharmarāja, "Let this boon be granted to me." The time has passed; I will go to the forest as you have commanded. Thus spoken, Dharmarāja suddenly said an unpleasant word.

English: As he proceeded, the mighty-armed one, the fame-bringer of the Kauravas, was followed by the great-souled Brahmanas, well-versed in the Vedas. The learned ones, knowledgeable in the Vedas and their branches, as well as those engaged in spiritual contemplation, and the devotees of the Lord, along with the Puranic bards, and others such as the royal sages and forest-dwelling ascetics, and the sweet-voiced twice-born who recite divine narratives, were accompanied by many others, the son of Pandu, surrounded like Indra by the Maruts. The beautiful forests, lakes, and rivers, as well as the oceans and regions of Bharat, and the holy places and sacred waters, were seen by Bharata's best, who, having reached the gate of the mace, made his abode there. There, listen to the wondrous deeds of that pure-souled charioteer of the Pandavas. When the son of Kunti was settled there among the Brahmanas in Bharat, the learned ones performed many sacrifices. As they were being awakened, burning in the sacrificial fires, with flower offerings made, and having entered the riverbanks, the king, having been anointed, shone exceedingly, surrounded by great souls on the righteous path.

English: Thus, in the water tank, the son of the Pandu, Kuntī's son, prepared for the anointing, and the conch was blown. After performing the anointing there, he, having worshipped the grandfather, was eager to perform the task. Having been rejected by the daughter of the great serpent king, the great king was desiring the one who was in the womb. There, the ten Pandavas were well gathered at the house of the Kaurava and the serpent. There, Kuntī's son performed the task, and he was struck by the one who was not pleased with the stars. Then, having done this, the son of Kunti, smiling, spoke this word. "What is this audacity, O timid one, that you have done, O beautiful one? Who is this fortunate land, and who are you, the daughter of whom?" Ulūpī said: "Born in the lineage of Airāvata, I am a Kaurava named Pannaga. I am the daughter of the serpent named Sal." "I have seen you, O Kuntī's son, while I was going to the ocean for the anointing, and I was enchanted by your beauty." "Please make me happy, O Kuru's son, by granting me a boon, for I am devoted to you." Ajuna, the son of Pandu.

English: Ajana said: O auspicious one, this vow of celibacy has been given to me by Dharmarāja; I am not a suitor. I wish to know how dear you are, O water-dweller. I have never spoken a lie, nor have I ever said anything at any time. How can there be a lie, and how can you be dear? My dharma would not be disturbed, nor would it be like a serpent. Ulūpī said: I know, O son of Pāṇḍu, how you traverse the earth, and how your guru has instructed you in this vow of celibacy. Regarding the daughter of Drupada, who is present, if one does not enter into delusion, he is not twelve years old. In the forest, one should observe celibacy; this is the time for you. This is for the sake of Draupadī, the mutual departure has been arranged; dharma does not fail here for the sake of warmth. And how can there be a failure of dharma for the sake of the broad-eyed ones? By ensuring my protection, your dharma does not perish. If there is even a slight transgression of this vow, then your dharma would indeed be the one to give up my life.

English: From the sacred fig tree of Agastya and the wind of Vasiṣṭha, the son of Kunti, having fulfilled his desires, gave a thousand cows to the twice-born at the holy places and shelters. Having bathed in the holy place of Hiranyabindu, the best of men, he praised the holy places of Pavatashṛṣṭha. The best of men, having traveled to the eastern direction, went to the sacred place of Alāta. Having seen the holy places in succession, the best of the Kurus, went to the beautiful river Utpalanī and the forest of Nemiṣa. He also visited Nandā, Aparanandā, Kaurikī, and the great river Gayā, and even the Ganges in Bhārata. Thus, having visited all the holy places, he gave wealth for the purification of his soul to the Brahmins. He went to all the holy places and shelters where some meritorious deeds were done. He also gave wealth according to the rules. In the houses of the Kaliyuga, the Brahmins, followers of the Pāṇḍavas, having been permitted, approached the son of Kunti, O Bhārata. Then, having been permitted by them, the son of Kuntī, Dhanañjaya, with a few brave companions, set out towards the ocean.

English: In the age of Kali, the Lord, observing the beautiful places, went to the abode of the sages. He went to Mahendraparvata, adorned by the ascetics, by the seashore. There, having visited all the holy places and sacred abodes, the mighty-armed Bhīma approached the lord of the intoxicated. The king of Maṇalūre, Dharmarāja, with the beautiful chariot. His daughter named Citrāṅgadā, with a lovely face, was seen wandering in the city by him. He approached her, the excellent one, and informed the king of his purpose. The king then spoke to him, pacifying him with these words. The king named Prabhāṅkara was born in this lineage. Without a son, he performed great austerities. By his severe penance, Lord Śiva, the Lord, was pleased with him, Mahādeva, the consort of Umā. To him, the Lord granted a single boon: that in this abode, there would always be one birth. From each birth, sons were born to all of them, my previous ones. But a daughter was born to me, surely the one who produces offspring of this abode.

English: The ascetic then asked the Kurunandana, "Why are these sacred places mentioned by the Brahma-advocates?" The ascetics replied, "The five Grahas reside here and take away the ascetics' power. Therefore, these sacred places are mentioned, O Kurunandana." Hearing this, the mighty-armed one, the great ascetic, went to see those sacred places, the best of men. Then, the son of Subhadra, the great sage, having bathed, performed the ritual with great speed. Then, that great man, the tiger among men, caught the son of Kunti, Dhananjaya, in the water. Taking him, the son of Kunti, who was shining with matted hair, the mighty-armed one, the best among the strong, stood up. Indeed, that Graha was excellent, and it was adorned by the glorious woman, beautifully decorated with all ornaments. Shining with splendor, the king, divine in form, was enchanting. Then, the wonderful Dhananjaya, the son of Kunti, spoke this word, filled with great joy.

English: What are you, O auspicious one? Where do you reside, O ascetic? Why did you commit this great sin in the past? I am an Apsara, O mighty-armed one, wandering in the celestial forest. I am always desired by the lord of wealth, known as Vaga, the great strong one. I have four other friends, all auspicious, who are also desirous of pleasure. With them, I will properly establish the guardians of the worlds. Then we shall proceed to the Brahmana, who is endowed with great strength, beautiful, and who wanders alone in solitude. By his austerity, the king's radiance was covered, shining like the sun in that land. By his austerity, he attained a wonderful vision. We descended to that land, wishing to disturb his penance. I, along with Sorabhayī, went to that sage through the path of yoga, O Bharata. Singing and laughing, they enchanted that Brahmana, yet he did not act against us, O hero, in any way. The great radiant one does not tremble, standing in penance. That Brahmana, angry with us, said: "You Kshatriyas, who have been caught in the water, you shall wander for a hundred years."

English: A hundred and the universe are indicators of one's own destruction. A hundred is the measure, but this is not an indicator of destruction. By the word of Kṛṣṇa, they indeed made that mountain, And the men prepared food and offered it.

English: The Pandavas, having received permission, along with Vāsudeva, saw the dancers. Having taken them to their own place, the great luminary went to the divine bed that was honored. He narrated the stories of the holy places and the rivers, as well as the forests of the earth. While narrating these stories, Janamejaya, being tired, was in a state of sleep, and the son of Kunti was engaged in his own meditation. With a sweet song and the sound of the lute, he was awakened and understood the praises of the bards. Having spoken words of praise, he was welcomed by the son of Vasudeva and went to the city of Dvārakā in a golden chariot. The city of Dvārakā was adorned, and Janamejaya was honored even in the small huts of the son of Kunti. The people of Dvārakā, eager to see him, came in thousands, like grass. In the sight of women, there were hundreds of thousands, and a great assembly of Bhojas, Vṛṣṇis, and Andhakas was present. Thus honored, he was greeted by the sons of Bhoja, Vṛṣṇi, and Andhaka. Having greeted and reciprocated with everyone, he was honored with respect. The hero was honored with respect and greetings. Ajuna, the son of Kunti, was in the forest.

English: 764 Subhadrā-haraṇa With their retinues and followers, the kings arrived in thousands. Then Haladhara, along with Revati, the lord, was followed by the Gandharvas in that place, O Bhārata. Similarly, the powerful king Ugrasena of the Vṛṣṇis, was being sung about by the Gandharvas, accompanied by the sound of their instruments. Rokṇi's son and Samba, along with Kṣīva, the two great warriors, were adorned with divine garlands and garments, like the immortals. Akrūra and Sārana, along with Gada, Bhānuvindratha, Niṣṭha, Śvārudeśṇa, and the mighty Prithu, were also present. Satyaka and Sātyaki, along with Bhāṅgakāra, were there as well. These were surrounded by women, each of them distinct, and they made the festival at Revati's place splendid. At that time, amidst the great auspiciousness, Vāsudeva and Pāśa arrived together. There, while moving about, Vāsudeva's son, the auspicious one, was adorned among the friends, making Bhadrā shine. At that moment, the god of love, seeing the beauty of Arjuna, was born in his heart. Then, laughing, the lotus-eyed one said, "What is this, O Bhārata? Is the mind of the forest dweller being stirred by desire?"

English: My sister is the sister of Pāṭhaṃ Sāraṇa. If you wish, I will inform our father myself. Ajana said: The daughter of Vasudeva and the sister of Vāsudeva, endowed with beauty, should not enchant like a creeper. Indeed, all that is auspicious is mine, if my daughter-in-law is your sister. If a means is obtained, I will rely on that, if it can be done by a man. Vasudeva said: The svayaṃvara of kṣatriyas is a marriage of men, and it is uncertain due to the nature of Pārtha. Forceful abduction is also praised among kṣatriyas. The wise know that it is for the purpose of marriage that the brave act. You, O Ajuna, have a beautiful sister. Who knows what is desired in her svayaṃvara? Then, Ajana and Kṛṣṇa, having determined this, quickly sent men to the city.

English: Then, that man-tiger, taking the pure-smiling one, set out towards his own city in a chariot like a bird in the sky. Seeing Subhadrā being dragged, the army of men rushed towards the city, all around her. They, having reached together, surrounded the assembly hall and spoke of the prowess of Pāthava. Hearing this, the assembly hall sounded the great conch, beautifully polished like the Jāmbūnada. With that sound, the Bhoja, Vṛṣṇi, and Andhaka clans, having given up food and drink, then left the assembly. Then, the Jāmbūnada's limbs shone like the bright jewels of the sky. The great charioteers of the Vṛṣṇi and Andhaka clans, like blazing fires, sat on hundreds of thrones. Among those seated, like the gods in assembly, the assembly guardian, along with his followers, narrated the deeds of Jīṣṇu. Hearing that, the Vṛṣṇi heroes, with eyes like red lotuses, unable to contain themselves, rose up in pride. "Quickly bring the chariots, and also the weapons and great bows," they said, "and let the large arrows be prepared."

English: Some shouted to the charioteers, and some adorned the horses themselves. When the chariots were being brought, there was a great distress among the heroic men due to the armors and flags. Then the one with a garland, resembling a lion, clad in blue and intoxicated with pride, spoke this word. What is this, O Kurus, that you are desiring, unaware of the essence of this matter? This is the opinion of the wise one; let it be known that whatever is pleasing to him, you should act accordingly. Then, upon hearing those words, the beings, having taken the form of the plow, were all satisfied, saying, "It is good." The wise Baladeva said, "Let the words be equal," and all sat down again in the assembly. Then, the one who protects desires spoke to Vāsudeva, the great scorcher, "Why are you sitting quietly, observing the people?" You are honored for our sake, and we are not ungrateful for that worship. Who indeed has eaten the food that is to be broken? Thinking thus, the man was born. Desiring the relationship that was previously established, Subhadra was taken away.

English: The Pandava thinks that the swayamvara is not to be seen. Who would dare to take the bride's hand? Who would want to buy the son? Kunti's son has seen these faults, this is my opinion. Thus, the Pandava, having been pleased, took the maiden by virtue. The relationship is appropriate, and Subhadra is auspicious. Who would desire the son of Kuntibhoja, born in the lineage of Bharata and the great soul of Śantanu? I do not see anyone who could defeat Partha in valor. Who among all the warriors is equal to him? By pacifying him with the highest wisdom, let us turn back, my opinion is supreme. If Partha, by force, were to take his own city, he would immediately bring glory, not defeat. Hearing this, Vasudeva and the king of the Chakrus, Arjuna, then performed the marriage there. After staying there for a year, Kunti's son, the lord, spent time in the lotuses.

English: In the twelfth year, at Khāṇḍavaprastha, the king approached with humility. Having approached the king, Partha went to Draupadī. Draupadī replied to the Kurunandana with affection, "Go there, Kaunteya, where she, the daughter of the Satvata, is." Even the well-bound Bhāra was previously bound. Thus, Dhananjaya, who was of many kinds, consoled her and repeatedly showed patience. In haste, he sent Subhadrā, who was red-eyed and had a beautiful form, to the cowherd. With that form, she was adorned and became the best among the beautiful maidens. Pṛthutāmra, the glorious and renowned, worshipped her. Then, quickly approaching, the one with a full moon-like face worshipped Draupadī, saying, "I am here." Rising, Kṛṣṇa addressed his sister, "May your husband be without a rival." Thus, the delighted Bhadrā spoke to her, "Let it be so." Then, the great charioteers, the sons of Pāṇḍu, were filled with joy.

English: Kuntī, very pleased, became joyful upon hearing of Janamejaya. Hearing that Pundarīka-eyed Kṛṣṇa had arrived at his best city, Indraprastha, where Arjuna, the foremost of the Pāṇḍavas, was. Kṛṣṇa, the pure-souled one, arrived with Rāma, along with the great heroes of the Vṛṣṇi and Andhaka clans. Surrounded by brothers and sons, and hundreds of warriors, the great warrior Parantapa came with a mighty army. There, the great and renowned Akrūra, the commander of the Vṛṣṇi heroes, arrived. Uddhava, of great glory and unmatched brilliance, also came, a direct disciple of the Lord. Sātyaki and Sātyaki, along with Kṛtavarmā, and the sons of Śrī, such as Pradyumna and Sāmba. Chārudeṣṇa, the valiant one, and Jhilī, and the great-armed Gada, the best among the wise. These and many others from the Vṛṣṇi, Bhoja, and Andhaka clans arrived, bringing much wealth to Khandavaprastha. Then King Yudhishthira, upon hearing of Madhava's arrival, prepared to receive Kṛṣṇa. That which was received from them, the great wheel of fortune, entered Khandavaprastha, adorned with flags and banners.

English: The path, adorned with flowers, is moistened and beautiful. It is served by the cool essence of sandalwood, fragrant and pure. In every region, it burns with a strong scent, Adorned by well-gathered people and merchants. Mahābāhu, along with Rāma, approached, The supreme person, surrounded by the great Bhoja of the Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas. Worshipped by countless beings, He entered the palace of the king, resembling the abode of Indra. Yudhiṣṭhira, too, approached Rāma as was fitting. Embracing him with his arm, Kṛṣṇa, pleased, honored him with humility. He duly worshipped Bhīma, the tiger among men. Yudhiṣṭhira, the king of dharma, received them with respect, As was appropriate according to the ritual. He worshipped like a guru, as if desiring something. Some spoke with great reverence, while others greeted him. Then Vāsudeva gave the best wealth for the sake of the people, The great fame of Subhadrā's kin was to be taken. Of the chariots, adorned with golden limbs, Entangled in the net of skillful arrangements, They were endowed with four yokes.

English: Kṛṣṇa gave a thousand cows and the best of them. The noble ones of Mathurā, the two-horned ones, of the virtuous words, and the white ones of the Vṛṣṇi clan, like the moon.
